get.description:
Returns the build that the answering server runs. Behind a load balancer, `hostname` in the response tells you which server replied. To check the API's dependencies rather than its build, use `GET /health`.

Without a token, the response carries only `apiversion`, `git-commit`, `hostname`, and `current-time`. With a valid token it also carries the full commit hash, the branch, the build date, and the PHP and framework versions. No token is needed. You can still send one (a bearer access token, an API key, or the `ns_access_token` cookie) to get the longer response. Any valid token works, whatever its scope. A token that is sent but is invalid or expired is refused with `401`, and an API key that is not valid with `403`; you do not get the shorter response instead.

`current-time` is `YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm:ss` with no offset, not RFC 3339. Takes no parameters.

200.description: Build information for the server that answered. The optional fields are present only with a valid token.

schema.description: Build information for the server that answered. Without a token, only `apiversion`, `git-commit`, `hostname`, and `current-time` are present.

apiversion.description: The API package version, such as `46.0.1234`. `development` on a server without a version stamp.

git-commit.description: The short hash of the Git commit the build came from, 7 characters. `null` when it cannot be determined.

git-commit-full.description: Only with a valid token. The full hash of that commit. `null` when it cannot be determined.

git-branch.description: Only with a valid token. The Git branch the build came from, such as `master-v46.0`. `null` when it cannot be determined.

build-date.description: Only with a valid token. When the package was built, in RFC 3339 UTC with a `Z` suffix, such as `2026-08-28T18:04:11Z`. `null` on a server without a build stamp.

hostname.description: The hostname of the server that answered. Behind a load balancer, it tells you which server replied.

current-time.description: The server's current time as `YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm:ss`, in the server's PHP time zone, which is normally UTC. It carries no offset and is not an RFC 3339 date-time.

php-version.description: Only with a valid token. The PHP version, such as `8.5.3`.

library-version.description: Only with a valid token. The framework version, such as `5.1.4`.

401.description: A token was sent but is invalid or expired. The message is `Invalid Token [APP011]`, `Expired token`, or `Invalid Token`. Get a new token and retry, or send no token for the shorter response.

403.description: An API key was sent but is not valid, such as `Invalid APIkey [Type 3]`. Check the key, or send no token for the shorter response.

get.description:
Checks the dependencies of the server that answered: the cache, every configured database connection, and the message bus. Load balancers and monitoring services can call it without a token.

Without a token, the response carries only `status`, `timestamp`, `hostname`, and `app_version`. With a valid token it also carries `environment`, `php_version`, and `checks`, the result of each dependency. No token is needed. You can still send one (a bearer access token, an API key, or the `ns_access_token` cookie) to get the longer response. Any valid token works, whatever its scope. A token that is sent but is invalid or expired is refused with `401`, and an API key that is not valid with `403`; you do not get the shorter response instead.

The HTTP status is always `200`. Read `status`: `healthy` means every check passed, and `degraded` means at least one failed. Results are cached for 15 seconds per server, so a failure can take up to 15 seconds to show, and repeated calls in that window do not repeat the checks. The `X-Health-Cache` response header is `hit` when the result came from that cache and `miss` when it was just computed. Takes no parameters.

200.description: The health report. The HTTP status is `200` whether the server is healthy or degraded.

4.summary: With a valid token, a database is down

X-Health-Cache.description: `hit` when the result came from the 15-second cache, `miss` when it was just computed.

401.description: A token was sent but is invalid or expired. The message is `Invalid Token [APP011]`, `Expired token`, or `Invalid Token`. Get a new token and retry, or send no token for the shorter response.

403.description: An API key was sent but is not valid, such as `Invalid APIkey [Type 3]`. Check the key, or send no token for the shorter response.

post.description: Runs an OAuth grant and returns a JWT access token and JWT refresh token instead of the opaque tokens that `POST /tokens` returns. It is the same call as `POST /netsapiensjs`. No bearer token is needed. The request must arrive over HTTPS. Send the `client_id` and `client_secret` of an OAuth client in the body, or as HTTP Basic credentials in the `Authorization` header. It accepts the same `grant_type` values as `POST /tokens`, including `password` and `authorization_code`. When the user still needs MFA, the response carries `scope` `mfa_required` and a limited `token`: send it as `access_token` to `POST /tokens` with `grant_type` `mfa`. The response also sets the `ns_access_token` and `ns_refresh_token` cookies. A plain HTTP request returns `403`. Missing or invalid client credentials return `401`.

200.description: Grant accepted. The body holds `token` and `refresh`, or a limited `token` with `scope` `mfa_required`.

400.description: Missing `grant_type`, an unsupported `grant_type`, or a missing grant field such as `username`.

401.description: Missing or invalid client credentials, or an expired authorization code. Check `client_id` and `client_secret`.

403.description: The request did not arrive over HTTPS, or the login name or password is wrong. Resend over HTTPS with valid credentials.

405.description: The user's domain requires single sign-on. Use an SSO grant instead.

post.description: Links a single sign-on (SSO) identity to an existing user, so the user can later log in through that identity provider. No bearer token is needed. Send the provider's token in `idtoken`, the provider in `vendor`, and the user's `username` and `password` to prove the account is theirs. `vendor` is `google`, `apple`, `office`, or the `provider_id` of an enabled OIDC provider. The user's domain must have single sign-on enabled, and the email in the provider's token must be allowed for that user. The email is added to the user's email list. A `202` means the link was published, not yet applied. Wrong credentials return `401`. An invalid provider token, an unsupported vendor, a domain without SSO, or a disallowed email returns `409`.

username.description: Login name of the user to link. Ignored when `user` and `domain` are both sent.

password.description: Password of the user to link. Proves the account is theirs.

vendor.description: Identity provider: `google`, `apple`, `office`, or the `provider_id` of an enabled OIDC provider.

idtoken.description: Token from the identity provider. An ID token for `google`, `apple` and OIDC providers. For `office`, a Microsoft Graph access token.

user.description: Extension of the user to link. With `domain`, replaces `username` as `user@domain`.

domain.description: Domain of the user to link. Used with `user`.

real_subscriber_login.description: Login name to check the password against, when it differs from `username`.

account_setup.description: Set during first-time account setup on a domain that requires SSO only. Skips the password check.

202.description: Link published. It applies once the event is processed.

400.description: Missing `idtoken` or `vendor`, or the change could not be published.

401.description: The login name or password is wrong, or an OIDC-path token is missing required claims.

409.description: The provider token is invalid, `vendor` is not supported, the domain does not have SSO enabled, or the token's email is not allowed for this user. Check the domain's SSO settings.

post.description:
Issues an OAuth access token and refresh token. One endpoint serves every grant, and `grant_type` picks it. No bearer token is needed. Send the `client_id` and `client_secret` of an OAuth client in the body, or as HTTP Basic credentials in the `Authorization` header. The response also sets the `ns_access_token` and `ns_refresh_token` cookies.

### Password login
Send `grant_type` `password` with the user's `username` (matched against the login name) and `password`. A wrong login name or password returns `403` by default. A domain that requires single sign-on returns `405`: use an SSO grant instead.

When the user has MFA enabled, or the domain requires an authenticator app, the response has `scope` `mfa_required`, an `access_token` that expires in 600 seconds, and no `refresh_token`. Finish the login with **Complete MFA**.

### Complete MFA
Send `grant_type` `mfa`, the limited `access_token`, the 6-digit `passcode` from the user's authenticator app, and `ns_id_type`. The server reads only those fields for this grant, and client credentials are optional. The passcode is checked with a tolerance of about 60 seconds either way. A wrong passcode returns `401`. An unknown limited token returns `400`: start again with the password grant. The limited token is single-use: once a passcode has been accepted for it, any further `mfa` grant with the same token returns `401` `Pre-MFA token already used`, and a limited JWT that carries no `jti` returns `401` `Invalid pre-MFA token`.

### Refresh
Send `grant_type` `refresh_token` and the `refresh_token`. It can be the opaque token from this endpoint or a JWT refresh token from `POST /authCode`. A JWT refresh token is revoked after one use by default, and the claim is atomic: if two exchanges of the same refresh token race, exactly one succeeds and the other returns `401` `Refresh token already used`. An opaque refresh token stays valid until it expires, 4 days after issue by default. An unknown refresh token returns `400`, and an expired one returns `401`: log in again.

### Other grants
`grant_type` also accepts `authorization_code`, `google`, `office`, `apple`, `oidc`, `masquerade`, `delegated`, `guest` and `chat_guest`. Any other value returns `400`.

client_id.description: ID of your OAuth client. You can send it with `client_secret` as HTTP Basic credentials instead. A Super User creates OAuth clients with `POST /oauth-clients`.

client_secret.description: Secret of the OAuth client named by `client_id`. Keep it on your server.

client_id.description: ID of your OAuth client. You can send it with `client_secret` as HTTP Basic credentials instead. A Super User creates OAuth clients with `POST /oauth-clients`.

client_secret.description: Secret of the OAuth client named by `client_id`. Keep it on your server.

access_token.description: The limited token from a password login whose `scope` is `mfa_required`

passcode.description: 6-digit passcode from the user's authenticator app

ns_id_type.description: Which MFA record to check: `subscriber` for API and Portal logins, `level1` for Admin UI logins

client_id.description: ID of your OAuth client. You can send it with `client_secret` as HTTP Basic credentials instead. A Super User creates OAuth clients with `POST /oauth-clients`.

client_secret.description: Secret of the OAuth client named by `client_id`. Keep it on your server.

schema.description: `grant_type` selects the grant. The three most common grants are shown.

200.description: Token issued. When `scope` is `mfa_required`, the token is only good for **Complete MFA**.

400.description: A required field is missing, `grant_type` is not supported, the client credentials are invalid, or a refresh or limited token is unknown. The message names the problem.

401.description: The MFA passcode is wrong, a refresh token or limited JWT is invalid or expired, or a single-use token was already spent (`Refresh token already used`, `Pre-MFA token already used`, `Invalid pre-MFA token`). Ask for a fresh passcode, or log in again; never retry a spent token.

405.description: The user's domain requires single sign-on. Log in through the domain's SSO provider instead.

500.description: The server could not check the client credentials. Try again, then contact support.

get.description: Lists the API keys in your scope. With an OAuth or JWT token, a Super User sees every key, a Reseller sees keys in their territory and in its domains, and lower scopes see keys in their domain that are assigned to their own user. With an API key, the list holds only the keys that key created. The secret `key` is never returned. An empty list is `[]`.

200.description: API keys in your scope, as an array.

401.description: Missing or invalid token. Get a new access token, then retry.

403.description: The API key is invalid or used from a disallowed address, or a Reseller token has territory `*`.

post.description: Creates an API key and returns its secret `key` once. Store it securely: it is never shown again. With an API key, the calling key must have `can-create-keys` set to `yes`. With an OAuth or JWT token, you need Reseller or Super User scope, and you cannot create a key above your own scope. Reseller keys cover a whole territory, so their `domain` and `user` are set to `*`. Office Manager and Call Center Supervisor keys need a `domain`. User-level keys need a `domain` and a `user`. The key is published to every node, so allow a moment before it authenticates everywhere. `Site Manager` and `No Portal` scopes return `400`. A scope, territory or domain you cannot grant returns `403`.

description.description: Purpose of the key, shown in listings. At least 12 characters on create.

reseller.description: Territory the key can reach. `*` for Super User keys. A Reseller key needs a specific territory.

domain.description: Domain the key can reach. `*` for Super User and Reseller keys. Required for Office Manager scope and lower.

user.description: Extension the key acts as. `*` when the key is not tied to one user. Required for user-level scopes.

user-scope.description: Scope that sets the key's permissions. A custom scope name is also accepted. `Site Manager` and `No Portal` are not supported. Required on create.

ip-address.description: Comma-separated IPv4 or IPv6 addresses and CIDR ranges the key can be used from. `*` allows any address. A request from any other address returns `403`.

readonly.description: `yes` limits the key to read, list and count actions, and any other action returns `403`. `no` allows every action the scope permits.

can-create-keys.description: `yes` lets the key create keys and update the keys it created. `no` blocks both. Revoking does not need it.

anyOf.description: A string with a specific model or "*" for all.

items.description: A string with a specific model or "*" for all. The specific models reference the API's scope defintions stored in the DB.

allowed-models.description: Objects the key can access. `*` allows every object. On create or update, send a string or an array of object names; reads return an array unless the value is `*`. A request for any other object returns `403`, but the key can always read itself. Object names come from the scope definitions and can differ from path names.

200.description: Key created. The body includes the secret `key` and a `notes` reminder. This is the only response that ever shows `key`.

example.notes: This key needs to be kept secure and secret and will not be shown again so please note it down now!

400.description: A required field is missing, `description` is shorter than 12 characters, `user-scope` is missing or not supported, or the territory, domain or user does not fit the scope.

401.description: Missing or invalid token.

403.description: The caller cannot create this key: the calling API key lacks `can-create-keys`, your scope is too low, or the territory or domain is outside yours.

404.description: The `domain` does not exist.

500.description: The server could not generate a unique key. Retry.

get.description: Returns one API key by its key ID. The secret `key` is never returned. The key must be in your scope: a Super User can read any key, a Reseller can read keys in their territory and its domains, and lower scopes can read keys in their domain assigned to their own user. Use `~` as the key ID to read the key you are calling with. A key outside your scope returns `404`, the same as a key that does not exist.

parameters.name: key_id
parameters.description: Key ID of the API key: the first 12 characters of the key, such as `nsr_EXAMPLE1`. The prefix shows the tier: `nss_` for Super User or NDP, `nsr_` for Reseller, `nsd_` for Office Manager or Call Center Supervisor, and `nsu_` for user-level scopes. Use `~` for the calling key.

200.description: The API key.

401.description: Missing or invalid token.

403.description: The API key is invalid or used from a disallowed address, or `~` was used with an OAuth or JWT token.

404.description: No key with this ID in your scope. The body is {"code": 404, "message": "Resource not found."}.

put.description: Changes the `description`, `ip-address` or `allowed-models` of an API key. Every other field is ignored: to change scope or access rights, create a new key and revoke this one. With an API key, the calling key must have `can-create-keys` set to `yes`, must be the key that created this one, and cannot update itself. With an OAuth or JWT token, the key must be in your territory, and in your domain below Reseller scope. Nobody can update a key above their own scope. Super User scope skips the ownership, territory and domain checks. A `202` means the change was published, not yet applied. An unknown `key_id` returns `404`.

ip-address.description: Comma-separated IPv4 or IPv6 addresses and CIDR ranges the key can be used from. `*` allows any address. A request from any other address returns `403`.

A request for any other object returns `403`, but the key can always read itself. Object names come from the scope definitions and can differ from path names.

400.description: The stored key has no scope, or the change could not be published.

404.description: No API key has this `key_id`.

delete.description: Revokes an API key. The key stops working on each node once the revocation is applied there, and a `202` means the revocation was published. With an API key, the calling key must be the key that created this one. With an OAuth or JWT token, the key must be in your territory, and in your domain below Reseller scope. Nobody can revoke a key above their own scope. Super User scope skips the ownership, territory and domain checks. Keys that this key created stay active unless you send `revoke_child_keys`. An unknown `key_id` returns `404`.

parameters.description: Key ID of the API key: the first 12 characters of the key, such as `nsr_EXAMPLE1`. The prefix shows the tier: `nss_` for Super User or NDP, `nsr_` for Reseller, `nsd_` for Office Manager or Call Center Supervisor, and `nsu_` for user-level scopes.

parameters.description: Set to `no` to also revoke every key this key created. Any other value, or leaving it out, revokes only this key.

get.description: Returns the API key you are calling with: its scope, territory, domain, restrictions and timestamps. Use it to check what a key can do. The secret `key` is never returned. It works even when the key's `allowed-models` leaves out `apikey`. Calling it with an OAuth or JWT token instead of an API key returns `403`.

401.description: No `Authorization` header. Send the API key as a bearer token.

get.description: Decodes the JWT in the `Authorization` header and returns all of its claims, plus the `apiversion` of the server that answered. Any valid JWT can call it, and no scope check applies. Use it to find a token's `jti` before revoking it, or to check `exp` and `user_scope`. The registered claims follow RFC 7519, section 4.1. An expired token or an API key returns `401`.

200.description: The token's claims.

401.description: The bearer token is missing, invalid or expired, or is not a JWT.

post.description:
Issues a JWT access token and a refresh token. One endpoint serves four grants, and the fields you send pick the grant. Every grant requires HTTPS; a plain HTTP request returns `403`.

### Password login
Send `grant_type` `password`, the user's `username` and `password`, and your OAuth client credentials, in the body or as an HTTP Basic `Authorization` header. No bearer token is needed. A wrong username or password returns `403`. A domain that requires single sign-on returns `405`: use the SSO flow instead.

If the user has MFA enabled, or the domain requires an authenticator app, the returned `token` has the `user_scope` claim `mfa_required`. It expires in 5 minutes and is good only for **Complete MFA**. The `refresh` token from that response cannot be used.

### Complete MFA
Send `grant_type` `mfa`, the pending token as `access_token`, the 6-digit `passcode` and `ns_id_type`. Also include `password`, because this endpoint picks the grant by that field, although this grant does not check its value. A wrong passcode returns `401`: ask the user for a fresh code. An expired pending token returns `401` `[OA080]`: log in again. The pending token is single-use: once a passcode has been accepted for it, any further `mfa` grant with the same token returns `401` `Pre-MFA token already used`, and a pending token that carries no `jti` returns `401` `Invalid pre-MFA token`.

### Refresh
Send `refresh` on its own. No client credentials are needed. The refresh token you send is revoked on use, so keep the new `refresh` from the response. The revocation is an atomic claim: if two exchanges of the same refresh token race, exactly one succeeds and the other returns `401` `Refresh token already used`. The new token picks up changes to the user's email, avatar or department since login. A token issued while MFA was pending returns `401`.

### Delegated (API key)
Send an API key as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`, and name the user with `user` and `domain`. The key must be allowed to create tokens and must have update rights on the user. A Super User key can issue tokens for any user; any other key only for its own user or a user with a lower scope. The issued token records the key's ID in its `mask_chain` claim. A JWT bearer instead of an API key returns `403`.

2.description: Finish a login that returned an mfa_required token

4.description: Issue a token for user 1001 with an API key bearer

200.description: A JWT access token and its refresh token. After a password login that still needs MFA, `token` is a 5-minute pending token.

400.description: A required field is missing, `grant_type` is not supported, or a delegated request names a user the key cannot act for. The message names the problem.

401.description: OAuth client credentials are missing or invalid (`[OA100]` to `[OA104]`), the MFA passcode is wrong, the refresh or pending token is invalid or expired, or a single-use token was already spent (`Refresh token already used`, `Pre-MFA token already used`, `Invalid pre-MFA token`). Check the message, then retry or log in again; never retry a spent token.

403.description: The username or password is wrong, the API key is missing, invalid or not allowed to create tokens, or the request was not sent over HTTPS. The bad-credentials status is configurable and is `403` by default.

405.description: The user's domain requires single sign-on, so the password grant is refused. Use the SSO flow.

delete.description: Revokes the JWT in the `Authorization` header so it can no longer authenticate. Requires a JWT bearer token whose scope can delete `oauth` objects. By default Basic User, Call Center Supervisor, Office Manager, Reseller, and Super User can. The revocation applies on this server at once and on the rest of the cluster shortly after. The call also clears the `ns_access_token` and `ns_refresh_token` cookies. Your refresh token stays valid. To revoke it, call `DELETE /jwt/{jti}` with its JTI.

202.description: The token is revoked. The status comes from `NsHttpStatusCodeSuccessDelete`, which is `202` in the shipped configuration.

401.description: The bearer token is missing, invalid or expired, is not a JWT, or has no `jti` claim.

403.description: Your scope does not have `oauth` delete rights.

delete.description:
Revokes JWTs by user or by token. The value in the path picks which, by its format: 40 lowercase letters and digits is a JWT ID (`jti`), and anything else is a user as `user@domain`. Revocation applies on this server at once and is published to the rest of the cluster. The call also clears the caller's `ns_access_token` and `ns_refresh_token` cookies.

### Revoke one token by JTI
Send the token's `jti` claim, which `GET /jwt` returns. It works for access and refresh tokens. It requires a bearer token and `oauth` delete rights. An unknown JTI still returns success.

### Revoke all tokens for a user
Send the user as `user@domain`. Every JWT issued to that user before this call is revoked, on every server. Tokens issued afterward stay valid, so this signs the user out everywhere without locking them out. Authenticate with an API key (`Authorization: Bearer <key>`): a JWT bearer returns `403`. The key must be allowed to create tokens and must have `oauth` delete rights over the user.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: A JWT ID (40 lowercase letters and digits) to revoke one token, or a user as `user@domain` to revoke all of that user's tokens

202.description: The tokens are revoked. The status comes from `NsHttpStatusCodeSuccessDelete`, which is `202` in the shipped configuration.

401.description: The bearer token is missing, invalid or expired.

403.description: Your scope has no `oauth` delete rights. For a user, also: the bearer is not an API key, or the key may not create tokens or has no rights over the user.

post.description: Issues a JWT that expires 30 seconds after issue, to hand to another application such as a WebSocket server or a third-party validator. It copies every claim of your current JWT and adds an `application` claim set to the value you send. No refresh token or cookie is returned. Requires a JWT bearer token: an API key or an OAuth access token returns `400`. No scope check applies. The request must use HTTPS.

200.description: The application JWT.

400.description: `application` is missing or has characters other than letters, digits, hyphens and underscores, or the bearer is not a JWT.

401.description: The bearer token is missing, invalid or expired.

403.description: The request was not sent over HTTPS.

post.summary: Log in and set session cookies
post.description: Authenticates a user and returns a JWT access token and refresh token. It also sets them as `HttpOnly` cookies, so a browser app can make later calls without handling the tokens itself. No access token is needed. Send your OAuth client credentials as `Authorization: Basic` or as `client_id` and `client_secret` in the body. The request must use HTTPS. The cookies are `ns_access_token`, which lasts 1 hour, and `ns_refresh_token`, which lasts 30 days. Both are `Secure` and `SameSite=Strict`. If the user has MFA enrolled, the response carries a limited `token`, `scope` `mfa_required` and no refresh token, and no cookies are set. Ask for a passcode and call this endpoint again with `grant_type` `mfa`. The limited token is single-use: once a passcode has been accepted for it, any further `mfa` grant with the same token returns `401` `Pre-MFA token already used`. If `mfa` is `mfa_required_setup`, the domain requires MFA but the user hasn't enrolled yet. Wrong user credentials return `403`, bad client credentials return `401`, and a domain that requires single sign-on returns `405`. To refresh the session later, use `/oauth/refresh`, and to end it, use `/oauth/logout`.

200.description: The user is authenticated. If `scope` is `mfa_required`, MFA is still pending: the token is limited and no cookies were set.

400.description: `grant_type` is missing or unsupported, or a field that the grant needs is missing

401.description: Client credentials are missing, malformed or invalid (`[OA100]` to `[OA104]`), or the limited MFA token was already spent (`Pre-MFA token already used`). Check `client_id` and `client_secret`, or log in again.

403.description: The request didn't use HTTPS (`Forbidden`), or the username or password is wrong (`Invalid User Login`). Your administrator can change the status code for wrong credentials.

405.description: The user's domain requires single sign-on, so password login is refused. Use an SSO grant instead.

post.description: Ends the current session. It clears the `ns_access_token`, `ns_refresh_token` and `ns_masquerade_token` cookies and revokes the access and refresh tokens. No authentication is required. By default, the endpoint revokes the tokens in the cookies. To revoke other tokens, send them as `token` and `refresh_token` in the body. The endpoint also ends every masquerade session that the logged-in user opened, on any device. The response is always `200`, even if a token couldn't be revoked, because the cookies are cleared either way.

token.description: Optional. An access token to revoke instead of the one in the `ns_access_token` cookie

refresh_token.description: Optional. A refresh token to revoke instead of the one in the `ns_refresh_token` cookie

200.description: The cookies are cleared. The response is the same whether or not revocation succeeded.

message.description: `Logged out successfully`

post.description: Returns the identity of the user who holds the access token. Use it when your app starts, to find out whether the user is logged in and who they are. Send the token in the `ns_access_token` cookie or as `Authorization: Bearer`, and the cookie wins when both are present. `GET` works the same way. `avatar`, `email` and `department` come from the subscriber record at request time. During a masquerade session, the response describes the masqueraded user and sets `masquerading` to `true`, with the admin's identity in `real_user`. If the masquerade has expired, it is cleared and the response describes the admin with `masquerade_expired` set to `true`. A missing, invalid or expired token returns `401`: call `/oauth/refresh` or log in again.

200.description: Identity of the token holder

401.description: No token was sent, or the token is invalid or expired. The body is `{error, message}`, not `{code, message}`.

message.description: Why the token was refused

post.description: Issues a new access token and refresh token from the `ns_refresh_token` cookie and sets both as cookies again. The endpoint reads only the cookie, and any request body is ignored. No access token is needed. A JWT refresh token produces JWTs, which are returned **only** in the cookies, and the body carries the user's identity. An opaque refresh token produces opaque tokens, which are also returned in the body as `access_token` and `refresh_token`. A token issued while MFA is still pending can't be refreshed. A missing, invalid or expired refresh token returns `401`: send the user back to log in. A JWT refresh token is single-use and the claim is atomic: if two refreshes with the same cookie race, exactly one succeeds and the other returns `401` `Refresh token already used`. For apps that hold tokens themselves, use the `refresh_token` grant on `/netsapiensjs` or `/jwt` instead.

200.description: New tokens are set in the cookies. The body describes the user.

uid.description: User ID in `user@domain` form

user.description: User part of `uid`

domain.description: The user's domain

territory.description: Territory that the user's domain belongs to

scope.description: The user's scope, for example `Basic User`

client_id.description: OAuth client that the session belongs to, if known

token_type.description: `Bearer`. Present when the tokens are JWTs.

access_token.description: New opaque access token. Present only when the refresh token was opaque.

refresh_token.description: New opaque refresh token. Present only when the refresh token was opaque.

400.description: The opaque refresh token wasn't found (`Token refresh failed`). Log in again.

401.description: The `ns_refresh_token` cookie is missing, invalid or expired, the token was issued while MFA was pending, or a JWT refresh token was already spent (`Refresh token already used`). Log in again. The body is either `{error, message}` or `{code, message}`.

message.description: A readable description of the error

get.description: Starts an OpenID Connect (OIDC) login by redirecting the browser to the provider's authorization endpoint. Open it in the browser; don't call it with `fetch`. No authentication is required. The endpoint adds the provider's `client_id` and `scope`, plus `response_type=code`, `state`, `redirect_uri` and, if you sent one, `nonce`. The authorization endpoint comes from the provider's configuration or its discovery document. Without `redirect_uri`, the provider returns the user to `https://{host}/auth/oidc/callback`. An unknown or disabled provider returns `404`, and so does a provider whose IP allowlist excludes the caller, so that the response doesn't reveal which providers exist. To list the providers a login page can offer, use `/oidc-providers/public`.

parameters.name: provider
parameters.description: `provider_id` of an enabled OIDC provider. Required.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Opaque value that the provider returns unchanged to your callback. Generate a random value per login and check it on return. Required.

parameters.name: redirect_uri
parameters.description: Callback URL that the provider sends the user back to. It must be registered with the provider. Defaults to `https://{host}/auth/oidc/callback`.

parameters.name: nonce
parameters.description: Value that the provider includes in the ID token, to prevent replay

302.description: Redirect to the provider. The `Location` header holds the provider's authorization URL with the query parameters filled in.

400.description: `provider` or `state` is missing

404.description: The provider doesn't exist, is disabled or doesn't allow the caller's IP address

500.description: The provider's discovery document couldn't be fetched, or no authorization endpoint is configured. Check the provider configuration.

post.description: Generates a new time-based one-time password (TOTP) secret and a QR code URL that an authenticator app can scan. No authentication is required. Nothing is saved: pass the returned `secret` as `mfa_key` to `/oauth/mfaVerify` to test a code, then to `/oauth/mfaEnroll` or `/oauth/mfaEnrollWithToken` to save it. The `qrCodeUrl` points to a third-party QR service (`api.qrserver.com`) and carries the secret in its query string. If you don't want the secret to leave your app, build the QR code yourself from `secret`. A missing `tag` returns `400`.

200.description: The generated secret and QR code URL

secret.description: Base32 TOTP secret, 16 characters from `A-Z2-7`. Pass it as `mfa_key` to the verify and enroll endpoints.

title.description: The `title` you sent, or `null` when you omitted it

applicationName.description: The `tag` you sent, used as the account label in the authenticator app

qrCodeUrl.description: URL of a 200 × 200 QR code image for an `otpauth://totp/` URI. The image is served by `api.qrserver.com`, and the URL contains the secret.

apiversion.description: Build version of the API that answered, or `development`

400.description: `tag` is missing or empty. Send a non-empty `tag`.

post.description: Removes an authenticator app enrollment. Send an access token in the `ns_access_token` cookie or as `Authorization: Bearer`. Without `ns_id`, the endpoint removes the token holder's own enrollment, and any user scope can do that. To remove another user's enrollment, send that user's `ns_id`. This requires Super User, Reseller, Office Manager or Site Manager scope, and other scopes get `403`. The call is idempotent: it returns `200` even when no enrollment matched, including when `mfa_vendor` or `mfa_type` doesn't match the stored values. The removal is published to the platform and takes effect once it is applied.

200.description: The removal was accepted. Also returned when nothing matched.

status.description: `success`

message.description: `MFA disabled successfully`

apiversion.description: Build version of the API that answered, or `development`

400.description: `mfa_vendor` or `mfa_type` is missing

401.description: No token was sent, or the token is invalid, expired or has no subject. Log in again to get a new token.

403.description: `ns_id` names another user and your scope can't manage other users' MFA

500.description: The removal couldn't be published (`Service bus communication error`). Try again later.

post.summary: Enroll in MFA with username and password
post.description: Saves an authenticator app as the MFA method for a subscriber, using the user's login credentials instead of an access token. Use it in a login flow before the user has a full token, for example after `/netsapiensjs` reports `mfa_required_setup`. The server checks `username` and `password`, then checks `mfa_passcode` against `mfa_key`, and saves only when both pass. The enrollment is published to the platform and takes effect once it is applied, so a login made immediately afterwards may not see it yet. Wrong credentials return `409`, and a wrong passcode returns `401`: ask the user for a fresh code and try again. If the user already has a token, use `/oauth/mfaEnrollWithToken` instead.

200.description: The enrollment was accepted

status.description: `success`

message.description: `MFA enrollment successful`

apiversion.description: Build version of the API that answered, or `development`

400.description: A required field is missing. The message names it.

401.description: `mfa_passcode` does not match `mfa_key` (`Invalid Passcode`). Ask for a new code from the authenticator app.

409.description: `username` or `password` is wrong (`Invalid User Login`)

post.summary: Enroll in MFA with access token
post.description: Saves an authenticator app as the MFA method for the user who holds the access token. Send the token in the `ns_access_token` cookie or as `Authorization: Bearer`, and the cookie wins when both are present. During a masquerade session, the masqueraded user is enrolled. The subscriber comes from the token, never from the body. The server checks `mfa_passcode` against `mfa_key` before it saves. The enrollment is published to the platform and takes effect once it is applied. A wrong passcode still returns `200`, with `status` `error` and `valid` `false`, so check `status` rather than the HTTP code. A missing or invalid token returns `401`.

200.description: Outcome of the enrollment. Check `status`: `success` means it was accepted, and `error` means a wrong passcode or a failed publish.

status.description: `success` when the enrollment was accepted

message.description: `MFA enrollment successful`, `Invalid passcode` or `MFA enrollment failed`

enrolled.description: Present on success (`true`) and on a failed publish (`false`)

valid.description: Present only for a wrong passcode, and always `false`

apiversion.description: Build version of the API that answered, or `development`

400.description: A required field is missing. The message names it.

401.description: No token was sent, or the token is invalid, expired or has no subject. Log in again to get a new token.

post.description: Checks a 6-digit passcode from an authenticator app against a TOTP secret. No authentication is required, and nothing is saved. Use it during enrollment to confirm the user scanned the QR code correctly before you call an enroll endpoint. The response is always `200`: branch on `valid`, and read `message` for the reason. Codes from 1 time step before or after the current one are accepted, which is 60 seconds of clock drift either way. The only supported pair is `mfa_vendor` `google` with `mfa_type` `authenticator`.

200.description: Verification result. Always returned, including for missing parameters and wrong codes. Check `valid`.

post.description:
Starts a masquerade session in which you act as another user, and returns its `session_id`. It authenticates with the `ns_access_token` cookie set at login and ignores the `Authorization` header, so browser apps call it. Your scope must be able to update the target user, and you must outrank them. Nobody can masquerade as a Super User, and only a Super User can masquerade as a Reseller. An Office Manager target needs Reseller or Super User. A Call Center Supervisor or Site Manager target needs Office Manager or higher.

Send `X-Masquerade-Session: <session_id>` on later requests to act as the target user. The session and its token stay on the server. The response's `mask_chain` lists who masqueraded, starting with you. If you send `X-Masquerade-Session` for a session you own, the new masquerade nests inside it, up to 5 levels by default. Send `force_new_session: true` to open a separate session instead. By default you can hold 5 sessions at once. Hitting either limit returns `403`.

End sessions with `POST /oauth/masquerade/end`, or step back one level with `POST /oauth/masquerade/pop`. Error bodies carry `error` and `message`, not `code`.

parameters.name: X-Masquerade-Session
parameters.description: Optional. The ID of a masquerade session you own. The new masquerade nests inside it, unless `force_new_session` is `true`

mask_uid.description: The user to act as, in the form `user@domain`

force_new_session.description: If `true`, opens a separate session even when `X-Masquerade-Session` is sent

200.description: The session started. Send `session_id` in `X-Masquerade-Session` to act as the target user.

400.description: `mask_uid` is missing or is not in the form `user@domain`.

401.description: The `ns_access_token` cookie is missing or invalid. Log in again.

403.description: You lack rights over the target user or do not outrank them, the session named in `X-Masquerade-Session` belongs to someone else (`session_not_owned`), or you hit the depth or parallel-session limit. Close a session and retry.

404.description: The target user does not exist.

post.description: Ends one of your masquerade sessions, or all of them, and returns you to your own identity. It authenticates with the `ns_access_token` cookie, not a bearer token. To end one session, send its ID in the `X-Masquerade-Session` header or as `session_id` in the body. If you send both, they must match. If you send neither, the call ends every masquerade session you own, and it still succeeds when there are none. You can end only sessions you started. The call also clears the legacy `ns_masquerade_token` cookie.

parameters.name: X-Masquerade-Session
parameters.description: Optional. The ID of the session to end

session_id.description: Optional. The ID of the session to end, as returned by `POST /oauth/masquerade`

200.description: The session or sessions ended. `end_mode` says which.

400.description: The header and body name different sessions (`session_id_conflict`), or the named session does not exist (`Not currently masquerading`).

401.description: The `ns_access_token` cookie is missing or invalid, or the session's token cannot be decoded.

403.description: The named session belongs to another user (`session_not_owned`).

post.description: Steps a masquerade session back one level, or back to a named user in its chain, and returns the identity now in effect. It authenticates with the `ns_access_token` cookie, not a bearer token. Choose the session with the `X-Masquerade-Session` header or with `session_id` in the body. If you name no session, `target_uid` picks the one session that contains that user, and without `target_uid` your most recent session is used. When you name no session and `target_uid` is already a session's effective user, nothing changes and the response has `noop` set to `true`. Stepping back past the first masquerade ends the session and returns you to yourself: `masquerading` is then `false`. Send `end_later_sessions: true` to also end every session you opened after this one.

parameters.name: X-Masquerade-Session
parameters.description: Optional. The ID of the session to step back

session_id.description: Optional. The ID of the session to step back, as returned by `POST /oauth/masquerade`. You can send it in the `X-Masquerade-Session` header instead.

target_uid.description: Optional. The user in the session's `mask_chain` to return to, as `user@domain`. If omitted, the session steps back one level. `mask_uid` is accepted as an alias.

end_later_sessions.description: Optional. If `true`, also ends every masquerade session you opened after the selected one

2.summary: Return to a user in the chain

200.description: The identity now in effect. The response shape depends on whether you are still masquerading, returned to yourself, or nothing changed (`noop`).

400.description: One of these errors: `session_id_conflict` (the header and body disagree), `not_masquerading`, `target_not_in_chain`, `target_in_multiple_sessions` (name a session; `matching_sessions` lists them), `target_not_in_any_chain`, `target_user_invalid` (that user no longer exists) or `invalid_state`.

401.description: The `ns_access_token` cookie is missing or invalid, or the session's token cannot be decoded.

403.description: The session belongs to another user (`session_not_owned`).

get.description:
Returns the number of territories you can see, as `total`. Super User and Super User Read Only count every territory. A Reseller counts only its own, so its `total` is `0` or `1`. Every other scope gets `403`.

Filter with `reseller` to check whether one territory exists. Use `GET /resellers` for the territories themselves.

parameters.name: reseller
parameters.description: Count only the territory with this name. Send `~` for your own. A Reseller naming another territory gets `403`.

200.description: The number of territories that match.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired, or invalid. Get a new token and retry.

403.description: Your scope cannot count territories, or you are a Reseller and filtered on another territory. The message names the missing privilege. Ask a Super User for access.

example.message: Reseller not found or access denied: scope 'Office Manager' has no 'territory_list' privilege on object 'reseller'

get.description:
Returns territories with their SMTP settings and live totals: domains, users, and active calls. A territory is the configuration record that a Reseller's domains belong to, and `reseller` is its name.

Super User and Super User Read Only see every territory. A Reseller sees only its own, as a one-item array. A Reseller that filters on another territory gets `403`, and so does every other scope.

Filter with `reseller`. Page with `start` and `limit`, 100 territories by default, and sort by `reseller` or `description`. Use `GET /resellers/count` for a total, and `GET /resellers/list` for names and descriptions only.

The totals are counted on every read. `users-total` leaves out system users. `email-send-smtp-password` is masked. Super User can send `include-secrets=yes` for the plain text. SMTP settings that are not set are left out.

parameters.name: reseller
parameters.description: Only the territory with this name. Send `~` for your own. A Reseller naming another territory gets `403`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of records to return. Defaults to `100`. Use it with `start` to page.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Number of records to skip before the first one returned. Defaults to `0`. Use it with `limit` to page.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort order: `reseller` or `description`, each optionally followed by `asc` or `desc`, comma-separated. Defaults to `reseller asc`. Any other field returns `400`. The totals cannot be sorted on.

parameters.name: include-secrets
parameters.description: Send `yes` to get `email-send-smtp-password` in plain text instead of masked. Only Super User can send it, and each use is recorded in the audit log. Any other scope gets `403`.

200.description: The territories you can see, possibly an empty array. `email-send-smtp-password` is masked unless you sent `include-secrets=yes`.

400.description: `sort` names a field other than `reseller` or `description`, or a direction other than `asc` or `desc`. Fix the value and retry.

example.message: Bad Request. 'sort' must be reseller or description, optionally followed by asc or desc.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired, or invalid. Get a new token and retry.

403.description: Your scope cannot list territories, you are a Reseller and filtered on another territory, or you sent `include-secrets=yes` without Super User. The message names the reason.

example.message: Reseller not found or access denied: scope 'Office Manager' has no 'territory_list' privilege on object 'reseller'

post.description:
Creates a territory, the configuration record that a Reseller's domains belong to. Send its name in `reseller`, and optionally a `description` and SMTP settings for the email its domains send.

Requires Super User. Every other scope, Reseller and Super User Read Only included, gets `403`.

The name is 1 to 64 letters, digits, spaces, `.`, `-`, and `_`. It cannot start or end with a space or be only dots. Any other name returns `400`, and a name that already exists returns `409`.

A `202` means the territory was published over the service bus (SBUS), not yet created. Each core server writes it when the event arrives, so a read straight after the `202` can still return `404`. Assign a domain to the territory with the domain's `reseller` field.

get.description:
Returns how many phone numbers are assigned to a domain. Every user scope can read the numbers of its own domain. A Reseller reads the domains in its territory, and Super User and Super User Read Only read every domain.

parameters.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

parameters.description: Counts only the numbers routed to this destination, exact match. Prefix a service code with `lookup:` to match every user in the domain that has that service code, for example `lookup:system-queue`. A `lookup:` that finds no user matches no number.

parameters.description: Counts only the numbers routed to this destination host, exact match.

put.description:
Changes where calls to a phone number go, or its other settings. Name the number in the body with `phonenumber`. It is the same change as `PUT /domains/{domain}/phonenumbers/{phonenumber}`, with the number in the body instead of the path. Requires Site Manager, Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User scope. Scopes below Reseller change only their own domain, and a Reseller only the domains in its territory.

The request is a partial update: a field you leave out keeps its value. A `202` means the change is accepted and applied shortly after, so a read made right away can still show the old values.

A Reseller or Super User can name a number that is not assigned to any domain. The change assigns it to the domain in the path. A Super User can also name a number assigned to another domain, and the change moves it to the domain in the path, so check the path before you send.

A number that has only an SMS assignment can be changed too. Send only `sms-*` fields to change the assignment, or `dial-rule-translation-destination-user` to give the number a dial rule.

If an Office Manager sends `dial-rule-translation-destination-host`, it must be its own domain, except with the `to-connection` and `to-single-device` applications, or the request answers `403`. A number in neither place answers `404`: add it with `POST /domains/{domain}/phonenumbers`.

### Send to a user

Set `dial-rule-application` to `to-user`, `dial-rule-translation-destination-user` to the user's extension, and `dial-rule-translation-destination-host` to your domain.

### Send to a call queue

Set `dial-rule-application` to `to-callqueue` and `dial-rule-translation-destination-user` to the queue's extension.

### Use another application

Set `dial-rule-application` to any other application, such as `to-connection-add-header-update-cdr-by-user` for an off-net number. Put a header the application adds in `dial-rule-parameter`.

### Move back to available

Set `dial-rule-application` to `available-number`, the destination user and host to `[*]`, and `dial-rule-parameter` to `<NULL>`. The number stays in this domain, ready to assign again.

### Change other fields

Leave `dial-rule-application` out and send the fields to change: `enabled`, the description, the destination, the caller ID name, or the `sms-*` fields. Send `sms-enabled` `false` to remove the SMS assignment.

A body without `phonenumber` answers `400`.

`hostname` is the host of this API's NDP database connection, or this server's own name when that connection is local. `name` is always `ndpConfig`, and `port` is always `5060`. Any method other than `GET` returns `405`.

200.description: This API instance's NDP connection.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired, or invalid. Get a new token and retry.

403.description: Your scope cannot read this resource. Use a Reseller, Super User, or Super User Read Only token.

405.description: Only `GET` is allowed on this path. Resend the request as `GET`.

get.description:
Lists brand default rows: the per-brand vendor parameters that the Endpoints server (NDP) writes into device configuration files. Requires Super User or Super User Read Only scope.

Each row is keyed by `default-brand`, `default-server` and `default-name`. Without `default-server`, only the `default` tier is returned; `default-server=all` returns every tier. Domain and site defaults share the storage but are never listed here: use `/domains/{domain}/provisioning-defaults`. Sending both `default-brand` and `default-name` reads one row: the response is a single object, or `404` when the row does not exist. Append `/count` for a total, or `/list` for the rows without their values. Reads come from the NDP database this API server is connected to.

To find which brands have defaults, use `/brand-defaults/brands`.

parameters.name: default-brand
parameters.description: Lowercase brand slug, such as `polycom`, or `*` for the general defaults. `domain` and `site` answer `400`.

parameters.name: default-server
parameters.description: The server tier to read. Omitted means `default`. `all` returns every tier.

parameters.name: default-name
parameters.description: Exact vendor parameter name. Combined with `default-brand`, the response is one object, or `404`.

parameters.name: default-description
parameters.description: Exact description to match.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum rows to return. Default `1000`.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Number of records to skip before the first one returned. Defaults to `0`. Use it with `limit` to page.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: `default-brand`, `default-server`, `default-name`, `default-description` or `default-timestamp-datetime`, each optionally followed by ` ASC` or ` DESC`. Separate several with commas. Default `default-brand,default-server,default-name`.

200.description: The matching rows, or one object when `default-brand` and `default-name` are both sent.

400.description: The request failed validation. `message` names the parameter and the reason. Correct it and retry.

401.description: The bearer token is missing, expired or invalid. Get a new access token and retry.

403.description: The token is not Super User or Super User Read Only. Use a token with one of those scopes.

404.description: `default-brand` and `default-name` were both sent and no row matches. Check the brand, server tier and name.

post.description:
Creates one brand default row and publishes it to every Endpoints server (NDP) over the service bus (SBUS). Requires Super User scope.

Send `default-brand`, `default-name` and `default-value`, and optionally `default-server` (default `default`) and `default-description`. A `202` means the change was published, not yet applied: each NDP server applies it when the event arrives. Add `synchronous=yes` to wait until this API server's NDP database shows it.

A row with the same brand, server tier and name answers `409`: pass `overwrite=yes` or use `PUT`. A named server that is not in `/phones/servers` answers `404`. The brands `domain` and `site` answer `400`: use `/domains/{domain}/provisioning-defaults`.

parameters.name: overwrite
parameters.description: `yes` replaces a row that already exists instead of answering `409`.

parameters.name: synchronous
parameters.description: `yes` waits after publishing until this API server's NDP database shows the write, then answers `200` with a one-row report whose `default-applied` is `yes` or `no`. `no` means the write was not observed within the budget, not that it was rejected. Other NDP servers are not checked.

200.description: Returned instead of `202` when `synchronous=yes`: one row whose `default-applied` says whether this API server's NDP database showed the write.

202.description: Published to every NDP server over the service bus (SBUS). The change is applied when each server receives the event, so a read straight after may still show the old value.

get.description:
Lists the domain's provisioning options, one object per option, in the order the Endpoints server (NDP) reads them. Super User, Reseller and Office Manager can read and change these defaults. Super User Read Only, Office Manager Read-Only, Call Center Supervisor, Route Manager and Site Manager can read them. A Reseller is limited to domains in its territory, and other scopes to their own domain.

NDP stores these options as one `key="value"` string per domain and server tier; this resource splits it into options so each can be validated. Without `default-server`, the `default` tier is returned; `default-server=all` returns every tier. The result is what is stored for that tier, not the merged set a device receives. NDP applies site options first, then the domain row for the device's server, and uses the `default` tier only when that row is absent. A domain with no options on the tier returns an empty array. Add `option-name` to read one option. Append `/count` for a total, or `/list` for option names without values.

For the stored string, use `/domains/{domain}/provisioning-defaults/{server}/raw`.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

parameters.name: default-server
parameters.description: The server tier to read. Omitted means `default`. `all` returns every tier.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: `option-name` or `server`, optionally followed by ` ASC` or ` DESC`. Omitted keeps the stored order, which is the order NDP reads the options.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum rows to return. Default `1000`.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Number of records to skip before the first one returned. Defaults to `0`. Use it with `limit` to page.

parameters.name: option-name
parameters.description: Reads one option by name, for a name the path cannot carry. The response is then a single object, or `404` when the option is absent. With `default-server=all` it is an array with one row per tier that holds the option.

200.description: One object per option, or a single object when `option-name` is sent.

400.description: The request failed validation. `message` names the parameter and the reason. Correct it and retry.

401.description: The bearer token is missing, expired or invalid. Get a new access token and retry.

403.description: The token cannot read this domain's defaults. A Reseller sees only domains in its territory, and other scopes their own domain.

404.description: The domain does not exist. Check the path. With `option-name`, the option is not on the row.

post.description:
Adds one provisioning option to the domain's row for `default-server` (default `default`), creating the row if needed, and publishes it to every Endpoints server (NDP) over the service bus (SBUS). Requires Super User, Reseller or Office Manager scope. A Reseller is limited to domains in its territory, and an Office Manager to its own domain.

Send `option-name` and `option-value`, and optionally `default-server` and `default-description`. The option is checked against NDP's own parser first, so a value the API accepts is one NDP will read. A `400` names the reason: a double quote, the literal text `SPACE`, `EQUALQUOTE`, `EQUALINVALUE` or `<null>`, a character NDP cannot parse, or a row that would exceed 2,000 options. A `202` means the change was published, not yet applied: each NDP server applies it when the event arrives. Add `synchronous=yes` to wait until this API server's NDP database shows it.

An option that already exists answers `409`: pass `overwrite=yes` or use `PUT`. A named server that is not in `/phones/servers` answers `404`.

parameters.name: overwrite

parameters.name: synchronous
parameters.description: `yes` waits after publishing until this API server's NDP database shows the write, then answers `200` with a one-row report whose `default-applied` is `yes` or `no`. `no` means the write was not observed within the budget, not that it was rejected. Other NDP servers are not checked.

parameters.name: synchronous-timeout

404.description: The domain does not exist. Check the path. Or the named `default-server` does not exist in `/phones/servers`.

get.description:
Lists the site's provisioning options, one object per option, in the order the Endpoints server (NDP) reads them. Super User, Reseller, Office Manager and Site Manager can read and change these defaults. Super User Read Only, Office Manager Read-Only, Call Center Supervisor and Route Manager can read them. A Site Manager is limited to its own site and gets `403` for any other. The site must exist in the domain, or the call answers `404`.

NDP stores these options as one `key="value"` string per site and server tier; this resource splits it into options so each can be validated. Without `default-server`, the `default` tier is returned; `default-server=all` returns every tier. The result is what is stored for that tier, not the merged set a device receives. Site options have the highest precedence: NDP applies them before the domain's. A site with no options on the tier returns an empty array. Add `option-name` to read one option. Append `/count` for a total, or `/list` for option names without values.

For the stored string, use `/domains/{domain}/sites/{site}/provisioning-defaults/{server}/raw`.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

parameters.name: site
parameters.description: The site name within the domain. It must exist in the domain, or the call answers `404`. It cannot contain `|`.

parameters.name: default-server
parameters.description: The server tier to read. Omitted means `default`. `all` returns every tier.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: `option-name` or `server`, optionally followed by ` ASC` or ` DESC`. Omitted keeps the stored order, which is the order NDP reads the options.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum rows to return. Default `1000`.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Number of records to skip before the first one returned. Defaults to `0`. Use it with `limit` to page.

parameters.name: option-name
parameters.description: Reads one option by name, for a name the path cannot carry. The response is then a single object, or `404` when the option is absent. With `default-server=all` it is an array with one row per tier that holds the option.

200.description: One object per option, or a single object when `option-name` is sent.

401.description: The bearer token is missing, expired or invalid. Get a new access token and retry.

403.description: The token cannot read this site's defaults. A Site Manager can read only its own site.

404.description: The domain does not exist, or the site does not exist in the domain. Check the path. With `option-name`, the option is not on the row.

post.description:
Adds one provisioning option to the site's row for `default-server` (default `default`), creating the row if needed, and publishes it to every Endpoints server (NDP) over the service bus (SBUS). The option is checked against NDP's own parser first, so a value the API accepts is one NDP will read. An option that already exists answers `409`: pass `overwrite=yes` or use `PUT`. A named server that is not in `/phones/servers` answers `404`.

A Site Manager may change only its own site: another site, or a token whose site cannot be resolved, answers `403`. The site must exist in the domain, or the call answers `404`.

The delete is published over the service bus (SBUS); a `202` means published, not yet applied. Add `synchronous=yes` to wait until this API server's NDP database no longer shows the row.

A tier with no row answers `404`.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

parameters.name: site
parameters.description: The site name within the domain. It must exist in the domain, or the call answers `404`. It cannot contain `|`.

parameters.name: server
parameters.description: The server tier: a server name from `/phones/servers`, `default` for the fallback tier, or `*` (stored as written, treated by NDP like `default`). A named server that does not exist answers `404`, and `all` answers `400`.

parameters.name: synchronous
parameters.description: `yes` waits after publishing until this API server's NDP database shows the write, then answers `200` with a one-row report whose `default-applied` is `yes` or `no`. `no` means the write was not observed within the budget, not that it was rejected. Other NDP servers are not checked.

parameters.name: synchronous-timeout
parameters.description: How long `synchronous=yes` waits, in milliseconds, 0 to 5000. Defaults to `2000`. A larger value returns `400`.

200.description: Returned instead of `202` when `synchronous=yes`: one row whose `default-applied` says whether the row was gone from this API server's NDP database within the budget.

202.description: Published to every NDP server over the service bus (SBUS). The change is applied when each server receives the event, so a read straight after may still show the old value.

400.description: The request failed validation. `message` names the parameter and the reason. Correct it and retry.

401.description: The bearer token is missing, expired or invalid. Get a new access token and retry.

403.description: The token cannot change this site's defaults. A Site Manager can change only its own site, and only when its site can be resolved.

404.description: The domain does not exist, or the site does not exist in the domain. Check the path. Or the site has no row on this tier, so there is nothing to delete.

post.description:
Creates the button layout for one phone, identified by its MAC address, in the domain. It has the same fields as a phone template, and is often a copy of one.

`phoneconfiguration-mac-address` is required: 12 hexadecimal digits with no separators, such as `00005E005301`. A phone that already has a configuration in the domain returns `409`.

Every button you send is saved, and the buttons belong to this configuration in this domain only. The button types and features a model supports come from `GET /deviceprofiles/{brand}/{model}`, in `devicemodel`.

Two button features also write a dial rule. It goes in the dial plan of the user on the first `line` button, or in the domain's dial plan when there is no `line` button. A `queue_status` button toggles the user's call queue availability: its target is ignored, and reads return it empty. A `timeframe_status` button toggles a time frame: its target is the time frame name, and `Default` means the default time frame. Add `targetUser` to the button's `phoneconfiguration-extra` to toggle another user's time frame. The dial rules appear with the dial plan's other dial rules.

`phoneconfiguration-domain` in the body is ignored: the domain comes from the path. A `202` means the change is accepted and already applied.

Requires Office Manager scope or above for your own domain, Reseller scope for the domains in your territory, or Super User scope.

A Reseller sees the subscriptions in its own territory, except the ones a Super User created, and can narrow to one of its domains. Every other scope sees the subscriptions its own scope created in its own domain, and user-level scopes see only their own and domain-wide ones. Naming a domain you cannot see returns `403`.

`post-url` comes back in full only when you can change the subscription. Otherwise its user-info, query string, and fragment are masked.

| `agent` | Call center agent status changes, matched on the call queue |

A host that does not resolve is refused too. Each refusal is a `400` that names the rule. An installation can allow private addresses with the `NsSubscriptionAllowPrivateUrls` setting. The `id` is derived from the model, scope, territory, domain, user, `post-url`, and `subscription-geo-support`, so creating the same subscription twice returns `409`. The call waits up to 5 seconds for the new subscription to be stored and then returns it with `200`. Delivery starts within about 5 seconds after that.

get.description:
Returns the SIP servers a domain's clients connect to, in the order to try them, with the WebSocket URI for web phones and the DNS SRV records for each transport. Every user can read the servers of their own domain, and Resellers the domains in their territory.

How the list is built:

1. The preferred server is the `provisioning.preferred-server` domain setting, read from the domain, then the reseller, then the system. When none is set, the legacy portal setting is used, then the platform default.
2. The other servers in the preferred server's geographic group follow, if they allow backup. When the `provisioning.redundancy` setting is `none`, the list holds the preferred server alone.
3. `servers` is sorted by `priority`, lowest first. The order is not by distance: the API has no location for a browser.

`srv` lists the `_sip._tls`, `_sip._tcp`, and `_sip._udp` names of each server group with their resolved records. `preferred-srv` is the entry for the `provisioning.preferred-transport` setting, or `tls` when it is unset.

The answer is cached for up to 5 minutes, so a change can take that long to show.

post.description:
Creates a user (an extension) in a domain. Requires Site Manager, Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User scope.

Send `user`, `name-first-name`, and `name-last-name`. The other fields are optional:

- A field you leave out takes the value from the user's site, then from the domain, then from the platform defaults.
- `login-username` defaults to the extension and domain, such as `1001@example.com`.
- `directory-name-number-dtmf-mapping` is computed from the last name.
- A `site` that does not exist is created.
- Send `password-hash` to set a password, and `voicemail-login-pin` or `passwordLength` to set the voicemail PIN.

The new user starts with a default answering rule.

The response is `202`: the user is accepted and created shortly after. With `synchronous=yes` the call waits up to about 2 seconds and answers `200` with the new user, including the voicemail PIN in full. This is the only response that shows a generated PIN. If the user is not created in time, the response is `202`.

The named examples show a minimal create, a create in a site with a PIN, and a create that waits for the result.

The voicemail PIN is masked unless you send `include-secret=yes`. `moh=yes` adds whether the user's site and domain have their own music on hold and hold message.

Use `~` for `domain` and `user` to read the user your token belongs to. `GET /domains/~/users/~` does the same.

put.description:
Changes a user. Send only the fields to change. A field you leave out keeps its value. Send an empty `site`, `department`, or `email` to clear it.

A Basic User token changes only its own user. Site Manager, Office Manager, Reseller, and Super User tokens change the users in their domains.

Some changes have conditions:

- **Your own password or email.** Send `current_password` with your current password. Without it, when a password is already set, `password-hash` and `email` are not changed. A wrong `current_password` is a `403`.
- **Scope.** You can give a user your own scope or a lower one. A higher scope is a `403`.
- **Email for scopes below Reseller.** When the domain does not allow users to edit their primary email, changing `email` from a scope below Reseller is a `403`.
- **A new password** signs the user out everywhere and sends the user a security notification. An empty `password-hash` resets the account: it removes the user's single sign-on links and signs the user out.
- **The masked PIN.** Sending back the masked `voicemail-login-pin` from a read leaves the PIN unchanged.

The response is `202`: the change is accepted and applied shortly after.

The named examples change a name and caller ID, move a user to another site, change your own password, and clear a department.

Deletes a user and everything that belongs to it. Requires Site Manager, Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User scope.

The delete also removes the following:

- the user's devices, answering rules, time frames, voicemail reminders, contacts, and conferences
- the user's emergency addresses, call recording settings, scheduled CDR reports, and call queue email reports
- the user's video host, multi-factor enrollment, avatar, and personal settings

The user's phone numbers and SMS numbers return to the domain's inventory. The delete cannot be undone.

The response is `202`: the delete is accepted and applied shortly after.

Returns the product image stored for a phone brand and model, as raw image bytes with the stored `Content-Type`.

No token is needed. Only `GET` is accepted; any other method returns `405`.

The response carries an `ETag` computed from the image itself, and expires after 24 hours. Send the `ETag` back in `If-None-Match` to get `304` with no body while the image is unchanged; a replaced image gets a new `ETag`. A brand and model with no stored image returns `404`. `GET /deviceprofiles/{brand}/{model}` returns the profile, including this image's URL.

get.description:
Returns devices across domains: every device on the platform for a Super User or Super User Read Only, or every device in its own territory for a Reseller.

Requires Reseller, Super User, or Super User Read Only. Other scopes get `400` or `403`: read devices per domain with `GET /domains/{domain}/devices` instead.

To keep a platform-wide read fast, the provisioning fields from the Endpoints server and the owner's name and login are left out. Send `ndp=yes` to include them, at the cost of reading every phone and user row. Page with `start` and `limit`; without `limit` every device is returned. Order with `sort`, by SIP registration URI by default. Filter with `device-sip-registration-state` and `filters`. Credentials follow one rule: your own devices come back in plain text, and everyone else's are masked, the first 2 and last 2 characters around asterisks, or all asterisks for a value of 8 characters or fewer. A Super User can send `include-secrets=yes` to get them in plain text, and that read is audit-logged; any other scope that sends it gets `403`. Lists carry `device-provisioning-password` but not `device-sip-registration-password`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Most devices to return. There is no default: without `limit` every matching device is returned.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Number of records to skip before the first one returned. Defaults to `0`. Use it with `limit` to page.

parameters.name: filters
parameters.description: `video` leaves out web phone, data, and video bridge devices: any SIP registration URI containing `wp`, `data.`, or `video.bridge`.

parameters.name: ndp
parameters.description: `yes` adds the provisioning fields and the owner's name and login to each device. This reads every phone and user row on the server, so page with `limit`.

parameters.name: include-secrets
parameters.description: Super User only. `yes` returns device credentials in plain text instead of masked, and the read is audit-logged. Any other scope that sends `yes` gets `403`. A device's own user always gets its own credentials in plain text and does not need it.

parameters.name: device-sip-registration-state
parameters.description: `registered` returns devices whose registration has not expired, plus devices with push enabled. `unregistered` returns the rest. `registered_endpoint`, the stored value, is the same as `registered`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort order: comma-separated field names, each optionally followed by `asc` or `desc`. Allowed fields: `device`, `device-sip-registration-uri`, `user`, `domain`, `device-sip-registration-state`, `device-sip-registration-user-agent`, `device-sip-registration-ip-address`, `device-sip-registration-contact`, `device-sip-registration-datetime`, `device-sip-registration-expires-datetime`, `device-sip-registration-expiry-seconds`, `device-sip-registration-transport`, `device-sip-latency-seconds-current`, `device-sip-latency-seconds-average`, and `created-datetime`. Any other value returns `400`. Defaults to `device-sip-registration-uri` ascending.

200.description: The devices, possibly an empty array.

device.description: The device identifier which forms the first part of the device-sip-registration-uri and can be used to retrieve specific device information.

device-sip-registration-uri.description: Read-only. The complete SIP URI for this device, typically in the format sip:[device]@[domain].

device-sip-registration-state.description: Read-only. The current registration status for the device. The value will be 'registered' if the device is within the valid time window.
