Creates a SIP device for the user and, when you send a MAC address and model, links it to a phone on the Endpoints server.

Requires Basic User for your own devices, or Site Manager, Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User for the users you administer. A Basic User or other user-level scope can create devices only for itself, and a Site Manager only for users in its site; anyone else gets `403`.

Only `device` is required. A bare name is qualified with the path domain; a full SIP URI naming another domain returns `404`. Settings you leave out come from the domain's and territory's device defaults, and a flag you send wins over the default. If you send no `device-sip-registration-password`, a random 16-character password of letters and digits is generated. A password that looks like a mask, such as `********`, returns `400`. To link a phone, send `device-provisioning-mac-address` with `device-models-model`, and optionally `device-provisioning-line`, which defaults to `1`. A model of `Manual or Softphone` links nothing.

The change is published over the service bus (SBUS) and applied shortly after, so the answer is `202`. With `synchronous=yes` the API waits up to 2 seconds for the device to appear and answers `200` with it. If it has not appeared by then, the answer is still `202`.

A device name that already exists returns `409`.

parameters.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

parameters.name: user
parameters.description: User's extension, such as `1001`. `~` means the user your token belongs to.

user.description: User who owns the device, such as `1001`. `domain` for a device no user owns.

domain.description: Domain the device belongs to.

device-sip-registration-uri.description: SIP address the device registers as: `sip:<device>@<domain>`. Read-only.

device-sip-registration-state.description: `registered` while the device's last registration has not expired, allowing about 2 minutes of grace. Otherwise `unregistered`. Read-only.

device-sip-registration-password.description: SIP password the device registers with. Returned on single-device reads, not on lists. In plain text only when your token is the device's own user; every other caller gets it masked: the first 2 and last 2 characters around asterisks, or all asterisks for 8 characters or fewer. A Super User gets it in plain text with `include-secrets=yes`, and that read is audit-logged. On create, a random 16-character password of letters and digits is generated when you send none. post.description:
Creates a site. Send its name in `site`, and any settings the site's users should share, such as `dial-plan`, `caller-id-number`, `time-zone`, or `emergency-address-id`.

Requires Office Manager in the domain, Reseller for a domain in your territory, or Super User. Site Manager, Basic User, Super User Read Only, and every other scope get `403`.

The name is the site's key and cannot be changed later. Use letters, digits, spaces, and `.`, `-`, `_`, `'` only. The create accepts other characters, but a site named with them cannot be read, updated, or deleted by its path. Avoid `*`, which scope checks read as a wildcard. The name shares the domain's extension namespace:

- a name another site uses returns `409` `Site already exists`
- a name a user or other extension uses returns `409` `Extension already exists`
- a login already in use returns `409` `Login already exists`, naming the extension that holds it

The login defaults to `<site>@<domain>`. Set `login-username` to choose another. Check a name first with `GET /domains/{domain}/sites/count?site=<name>`.

Settings you leave out are copied from the domain's defaults. A user created later with `site` set copies the site's dial plan, dial policy, caller ID, time zone, area code, limits, language, and emergency address, unless the request sets them. Creating a user with a `site` that does not exist also creates that site.

A `202` means the site was published over the service bus (SBUS), not yet created, so a read straight after it can still return `404`. With `synchronous=yes`, the call waits up to 2 seconds. It returns `200` with the site once the site appears, or `202` if it has not appeared yet.

Deletes a site: the system extension that holds its settings, and the records that extension owns.

Requires Office Manager in the domain, Reseller for a domain in your territory, or Super User. Site Manager, Basic User, Super User Read Only, and every other scope get `403`.

A site that still has members is refused with `409`, and the message gives how many. Members are the users, call queues, and other extensions filed under the site. Move them first, or send `force=yes` to clear the site from every member and then delete it. Members keep their own settings, including values they copied from the site when they were created, and their devices are not touched.

Deleting the site also removes what its own extension owns: its devices, time frames, emergency addresses, contacts, conferences, recording settings, and CDR schedules, among other records. Phone numbers routed to the site's extension return to inventory. The site's group chat is archived last, after everything else succeeds. The site's provisioning defaults are not removed.

A `202` means the change was published over the service bus (SBUS), not yet applied. Each core server applies it when the event arrives, so a read straight after the `202` can still show the old state. `DELETE /domains/{domain}/sites`, with no name in the path, returns `405`.

Requires Office Manager, Call Center Supervisor, Route Manager, Reseller, or Super User. Site Manager can create a queue at its own site: a create without `site` is assigned to the Site Manager's own site, and another site returns `403`. Other scopes get `403`, including Office Manager Read-Only and Super User Read Only.

`callqueue` and `description` are required. `callqueue` takes letters, digits, `.`, `-`, and `_`, and `list`, `count`, and `all` are reserved; anything else returns `400`. `callqueue-dispatch-type` defaults to Call Park when left out, so send it for a queue that dispatches to agents. `202` means the change was published over the service bus (SBUS), not yet applied. Send `synchronous=yes` to wait up to 2 seconds and get the created queue back with `200`. A queue that already exists returns `409`. A `phone-number` that is not in the domain's number inventory, or belongs to another domain, returns `422` before anything is created. A value too long for its field returns `400`.

A call counts as abandoned when the caller hung up in the queue, or the call left the queue unanswered by a transfer, a retrieve, or no answer. Calls that went to voicemail are not counted. Calls count when they entered the queue between `datetime-start` and `datetime-end`, both included. Rows are ordered by the hour the call entered the queue. `queue_list` limits the queues.

parameters.description: Shifts both ends of the window by a relative amount, for example `-5 hour`. Kept for older integrations: give the offset in `datetime-start` and `datetime-end` instead.

The last period runs to `datetime-end`. While the window has not ended yet, it runs to now instead and is marked `open`, with `end-datetime: null`.

Basic User, Simple User, Advanced User and Call Center Agent read only their own timeline, in their own domain; any other agent or domain is `403`.

get.summary: Read 15-minute, hourly or daily call queue history
get.description:
One point per bucket over the range, oldest first. Each point gives every covered queue's statistics for that bucket and a domain-wide `*`. A queue absent from a point has no history for that bucket.

The queues covered are the ones the caller may see in the other call center statistics, narrowed by `queue_list`. A Site Manager sees only the queues of its own site. Agent-level scopes (Basic User, Call Center Agent and the like) may read only their own agent statistics and get `403` here.

Available when the platform has call center reports enabled; `404` otherwise.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

parameters.name: period
parameters.description: Bucket size, not case-sensitive. Omitted or blank is `hour`. `15m` gives quarter hours aligned to :00, :15, :30 and :45 UTC, and reaches back only as far as the server keeps its raw queue samples (about two days by default; `oldest-available` says where it starts).

parameters.name: range
parameters.description: How far back to go; the allowed values depend on `period`. For `hour`: `24h` (default), `7d` or `14d`. For `day`: `30d` (default), `7d` or `90d`. For `15m`: `24h` (default) or `48h`. Omitted or blank is the period's default.

parameters.name: queue_list
parameters.description: Comma-separated queue extensions. Narrows the queues covered; a queue the caller may not see is left out, not refused.

200.description: The history

400.description: An unsupported `period` (`Invalid period. Use hour, day or 15m.`), a `range` the period does not allow (`Invalid range for period <period>. Use one of: ...`), or no domain (`Please provide a domain`)

401.description: Missing or invalid token

403.description: The scope may not read call center statistics, or may read only its own agent statistics (`Access Denied: scope '<scope>' may only read its own agent statistics`)

404.description: Call center reports are not enabled on this platform (`Resource not found.`), or the domain does not exist

get.summary: Read per-minute call queue gauges for the last hour or two
get.description:
One point per minute, from `range` ago up to the current (partial) minute, oldest first. Each point gives every covered queue's values for that minute (the highest it reached during the minute) and a domain-wide `*`.

The queues covered are the ones the caller may see in the other call center statistics, narrowed by `queue_list`. A Site Manager sees only the queues of its own site. Agent-level scopes (Basic User, Call Center Agent and the like) may read only their own agent statistics and get `403` here.

Each core server keeps its own samples, so the read asks every core and, per queue, takes the larger of the cores' values. A core that does not answer is left out and named in the `X-NS-Fanout-Missing` response header; the values then cover the other cores only, and the response is still `200`.

Available when the platform has call center reports enabled; `404` otherwise.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

parameters.name: range
parameters.description: How far back to go. Omitted or blank is `1h`.

parameters.name: queue_list
parameters.description: Comma-separated queue extensions. Narrows the queues covered; a queue the caller may not see is left out, not refused.

200.description: The per-minute series

X-NS-Fanout-Missing.description: The core servers that did not answer, when any did not.

400.description: An unsupported `range` (`Invalid range. Use one of: 1h, 2h.`), or no domain (`Please provide a domain`)

401.description: Missing or invalid token

403.description: The scope may not read call center statistics, or may read only its own agent statistics (`Access Denied: scope '<scope>' may only read its own agent statistics`)

404.description: Call center reports are not enabled on this platform (`Resource not found.`), or the domain does not exist

get.summary: List call queue statistics per queue
get.description:
Returns call center statistics for each call queue in the domain, over a time window. Requires Office Manager, Call Center Supervisor, Site Manager, Reseller, or Super User scope. A Reseller reads the domains in its territory.

The response is a map from call queue extension to that queue's statistics, with the queue's description in `name`. Only queues with statistics turned on (`callqueue-calculate-statistics` is `yes`) are included. `queue_list` limits the queues.

Calls count when they entered the queue inside the window, from `datetime-start` up to but not including `datetime-end`. There is no limit on the window length, but long windows are slow. `fields` picks the statistics; it defaults to `VOL,CH,ATT,AC,AAS,SL`. Units follow each field's name except `calls-after-call-work-avg-duration-seconds`, which is in minutes without `interval`. `unit` changes the units.

With `interval`, the response is a map from bucket to rows. Bucket keys are RFC 3339 for `minute`, `hour`, and `day` (`2026-09-01T14:00:00+00:00`), `YYYY-Www` for `week` (`2026-W36`), and `YYYY-MM` for `month` (`2026-09`). Buckets are in UTC unless `datetime-start` names a bracketed time zone. `all` and `all-queues` in place of `per-queue` return the same map.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

parameters.name: datetime-start
parameters.description: The start of the time window, RFC 3339 with an offset, for example `2026-09-01T00:00:00-07:00`. The window includes this moment. `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` (read as UTC) and `YYYY-MM-DD` (start of that day, UTC) are also accepted. To group `interval` buckets by local time, add the IANA time zone in brackets after the offset, for example `2026-09-01T00:00:00-07:00[America/Phoenix]`. The offset must match the zone.

parameters.name: datetime-end
parameters.description: The end of the time window, RFC 3339 with an offset, for example `2026-09-02T00:00:00-07:00`. It must be later than `datetime-start`. `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` (read as UTC) and `YYYY-MM-DD` (end of that day, UTC) are also accepted.

post.summary: Create the default call center codes
post.description:
Creates the recommended dispositions and call reasons for each type the domain has no codes of yet, or only for `type`. Nothing runs it automatically. A type that already has any code (inactive included) is skipped and its codes are not changed, so calling it again is safe. Each created code has `seeded` `yes`, a `description`, and `sort-order` in the order below starting at `0`; every disposition has a `classification` and every call reason `none`. POST only. Requires the Office Manager, Call Center Supervisor, Reseller or Super User scope.

**Dispositions**
| name | direction | system-applied | classification | description | |---|---|---|---|---| | Resolved | both | no | positive | The caller's issue or request was fully handled on this call. | | Follow-up Required | both | no | neutral | Not finished; someone needs to act or call back later. | | Callback Scheduled | both | no | positive | A time was agreed to call the customer back. | | Escalated | both | no | neutral | Passed to a supervisor or specialist team to handle. | | Transferred | both | no | neutral | Sent on to another agent, queue or department. | | Left Voicemail | both | no | neutral | No answer; a message was left. | | Wrong Number | both | no | negative | The caller or number reached the wrong business. | | Not Interested | outbound | no | negative | The contact declined the offer or conversation. | | Abandoned in Queue | inbound | yes | negative | The caller hung up before an agent answered. | | No Answer | both | yes | negative | The call rang out with nobody picking up. | | Line Busy | outbound | yes | negative | The number was busy. | | Call Failed | both | yes | negative | The call could not be connected (network or number error). |

**Call reasons** (all `system-applied` `no`, `classification` `none`)
| name | direction | description | |---|---|---| | Sales Inquiry | inbound | A prospect asking about products, pricing or availability. | | Sales Outreach | outbound | Calling a prospect or customer to sell or upsell. | | Order Status | both | Checking where an order, shipment or delivery is. | | Billing or Payment | both | Invoices, charges, refunds or taking a payment. | | Technical Support | both | Help with a product or service that isn't working as expected. | | Appointment or Scheduling | both | Booking, moving or cancelling an appointment. | | Complaint | inbound | The customer is unhappy and wants it put right. | | General Information | inbound | Hours, locations, policies and other general questions. | | Collections | outbound | Following up on an overdue balance. | | Survey or Feedback | outbound | Asking the customer about their experience. |

post.description:
Creates a dial rule in a dial plan. Requires Basic User, Site Manager, Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User scope. A Reseller reaches only domains in its territory; every other scope reaches only its own domain.

Send at least `dial-rule-matching-to-uri` and `dial-rule-translation-destination-user`. The dial plan and domain come from the path. Send `synchronous=yes` to wait up to 2 seconds and get `200` with the created rule instead.

A rule with the same match fields already in the plan returns `409`. To change a rule's match fields later, delete it and create a new one: `PUT` updates only the other fields.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

parameters.name: dialplan
parameters.description: Dial plan name. `~` means the domain's own dial plan, which is named after the domain.

synchronous.description: `yes` waits up to 2 seconds for the rule to be applied and returns `200` with the rule. `no` (the default) returns `202` straight away

dial-rule-matching-to-uri.description: Destination pattern the rule matches, as a SIP URI. `?` matches one character and `*` matches anything, so `sip:611@*` matches 611 dialed to any host

enabled.description: Whether the rule is used for matching. A disabled rule is skipped

dial-rule-matching-from-uri.description: Caller pattern the rule also requires, as a SIP URI. `*` matches any caller

dial-rule-matching-day-of-week.description: Days the rule applies: one digit from `0` (Sunday) to `6` (Saturday), or a range in brackets such as `[1-5]`. `*` matches every day

dial-rule-matching-start-date.description: First day the rule applies, as `YYYY-MM-DD`. `*` means no start date

dial-rule-matching-end-date.description: Last day the rule applies, as `YYYY-MM-DD`. `*` means no end date

dial-rule-matching-start-time.description: Time of day the rule starts applying, as `HH:MM` from `00:00` to `23:59`. `*` means all day. Uses the time zone of the user the call passes through, when there is one

dial-rule-matching-end-time.description: Time of day the rule stops applying, as `HH:MM` from `00:00` to `23:59`. `*` means all day. Uses the time zone of the user the call passes through, when there is one

dial-rule-parameter.description: Extra setting for the application in `dial-rule-application`. Its meaning depends on the application. Empty by default

dial-rule-translation-destination-scheme.description: URI scheme of the destination. `[*]` keeps the scheme of the incoming request and is correct in most cases. `sip:` sets it to SIP

dial-rule-translation-destination-user.description: Where a matching call goes, read together with `dial-rule-application` and `dial-rule-translation-destination-host`. A user, a call queue, or an off-net number, depending on the application

dial-rule-translation-destination-host.description: Host of the destination: usually a domain, or a connection name for off-net routing. `[*]` keeps the incoming host

dial-rule-translation-source-name.description: Caller ID name passed on. `[*]` keeps the incoming value. Add text around it to change it, for example `sales_[*]`

dial-rule-translation-source-scheme.description: URI scheme of the caller. `[*]` keeps the scheme of the incoming request and is correct in most cases. `sip:` sets it to SIP

dial-rule-translation-source-user.description: Caller ID number passed on: the part of the caller's SIP URI before `@`. `[*]` keeps the incoming value. `<OwnCidNmbr>` substitutes the user's caller ID number

dial-rule-translation-source-host.description: Host part of the caller's SIP URI, after `@`. `[*]` keeps the incoming value. `<OwnDomain>` substitutes the user's domain

dial-rule-description.description: Free-text description of the rule

patch.description:
Copies a voicemail message into the `new` folder of another mailbox, and emails that user the new-voicemail notice. Your copy stays where it is. The recipient's copy shows who forwarded it in `voicemail-forward-from`: the user, or `user@domain` when the message came from another domain.

Name the recipient in `voicemail-forward-new-destination`: a bare user (extension) such as `1002` means that user in the path's domain, and `user@domain`, such as `1002@acme.example.com`, names a mailbox in that domain. The mailbox the message is in cannot be the recipient.

Any user may forward a message from its own mailbox to any mailbox in its own domain. Otherwise your scope must be able to change both mailboxes: Site Manager within its site, Office Manager and Route Manager within their own domain, Reseller and Route Manager Reseller within their territory, and Super User anywhere. So a recipient in another domain needs Reseller (a domain in its territory) or Super User. Anything else returns `403`. Office Manager Read-Only and Super User Read Only never forward.

The copy and its metadata are written on the server that handles the request and copied to the other servers over the service bus (SBUS) file journal. The call answers `202`. Each forward is recorded in the compliance access log as a disclosure of the message to the recipient. Only `PATCH` and `PUT` are accepted.

A missing or malformed recipient, or the message's own mailbox, returns `400`. A recipient that does not exist returns `404`, one without voicemail returns `409`, and one without room for the message returns `507`. A message that is not in the folder returns `404`.

Streams one voicemail message, or the PDF or JPEG image of a fax in a voicemail folder, so a browser or an `<audio>` element can play it.

Call it one of two ways:

- **With a session.** Send a bearer token, or let the browser send its session cookie. The access is the same as for reading the file. Every user can play their own mailbox, and Call Center Supervisor only its own. Site Manager can play the mailboxes of users at its own site, and Office Manager, Office Manager Read-Only, and Route Manager any mailbox in their domain. Reseller and Route Manager Reseller can play any mailbox in their territory, and Super User and Super User Read Only any mailbox. Any other mailbox answers `403`.
- **With a signed link.** Every read of the file returns `file-access-url`, which is this path with `expires` and `signature` added. Anyone holding the link can play that one file, with no token, until it expires (24 hours by default). Treat the link like the file itself.

The message is found in any folder, so a link still plays a message that was saved or moved to the trash after the link was made.

Without `download`, the file is sent inline and a single range request (`Range: bytes=...`) is answered with `206`, so a player can seek. A range that starts past the end of the file answers `416`. The response is never cached by a shared cache.

Each play or download of a voicemail or fax is recorded in the compliance access log, once per listen: seeking within the same message adds no entries. A play through a signed link is recorded with the listener unknown. A fax document is always recorded as a download.

post.description:
Adds a voicemail greeting for the user, from an uploaded file, a base64 file, or text to speech. It takes the next free index unless you send `index`; an `index` that is already used is overwritten, and `index` `0` replaces the user's recorded name.

Send `synchronous=yes` to get `200` with the stored file instead. With `synchronous=yes` the call waits up to 2 seconds for the file to appear. Every upload is converted to 8 kHz, 8-bit, mono mu-law WAV. Audio that cannot be converted returns `400` and nothing is stored.

**Upload a file.** Send `multipart/form-data` with the audio in the `file` part (`File` also works). The part's `Content-Type` picks the decoder: `audio/mpeg` or `audio/mp3` is decoded as MP3, `audio/ogg`, `audio/webm`, `video/ogg`, `video/webm` and `application/ogg` as Ogg or WebM, and anything else is read as WAV. put.description:
Replaces the audio of the MoH file at `index` with an uploaded file or a base64 file, or changes only its description. The index does not change.

Any user can change their own MoH. Site Manager can change the MoH of users in their own site, Office Manager and Call Center Supervisor any user in their domain, a Reseller any user in its territory, and Super User any user. Read-only scopes get `403`.

The file is written on the server that handles the request, before the response, and copied to the other servers over the service bus (SBUS) file journal. The call answers `202` by default. Send `synchronous=yes` to get `200` with the stored file instead. Every upload is converted to 8 kHz, 8-bit, mono mu-law WAV. Audio that cannot be converted returns `400` and nothing is stored.

**Upload a file.** Send `multipart/form-data` with the audio in the `file` part (`File` also works). The part's `Content-Type` picks the decoder: `audio/mpeg` or `audio/mp3` is decoded as MP3, `audio/ogg`, `audio/webm`, `video/ogg`, `video/webm` and `application/ogg` as Ogg or WebM, and anything else is read as WAV.

**Description only.** Send JSON with `file-script-text` and no file. Only the description changes: the audio stays as it is and nothing is spoken, so text-to-speech fields are ignored. A request with neither audio nor `file-script-text` changes nothing and still answers `202`. To replace the audio with text to speech, `POST` to the same index on `/domains/{domain}/users/{user}/moh` instead; a `POST` with an index that is in use overwrites it.

An index with no file returns `404`. Add a file with `POST` on `/domains/{domain}/users/{user}/moh`.

put.description:
Changes the order MoH files play in by renumbering them.

Any user can change their own MoH. Site Manager can change the MoH of users in their own site, Office Manager and Call Center Supervisor any user in their domain, a Reseller any user in its territory, and Super User any user. Read-only scopes get `403`.

List the current indexes in `ordinal-order` in the order you want. The listed files are renumbered into the same set of indexes, sorted: `[3, 1, 2]` moves the file at `3` to `1`, `1` to `2`, and `2` to `3`. Files you leave out keep their index. Every listed index must be a distinct whole number with a file: a repeated or non-numeric index returns `400`, and an index with no file returns `404`; either way nothing moves. The files are renamed on the server that handles the request before the response, and copied to the other servers over the SBUS file journal. The call answers `202` by default, which here means applied on this server.

Reordering does not close a gap left by a delete: `[1, 3]` keeps `1` and `3`. To fill a gap, update the file at the free index.

get.description:
Streams one of a user's music on hold (MoH) files, so a browser or an `<audio>` element can play it.

Call it one of two ways:

- **With a session.** Send a bearer token, or let the browser send its session cookie. The access is the same as for reading the file. Basic User, Advanced User, Simple User, and Call Center Agent can play only their own files. Site Manager, Call Center Supervisor, Office Manager, Office Manager Read-Only, and Route Manager can play any user's files in their domain. Reseller and Route Manager Reseller can play files in the domains of their territory, and Super User and Super User Read Only in every domain. Any other file answers `403`.
- **With a signed link.** Every read of the file returns `file-access-url`, which is this path with `expires` and `signature` added. Anyone holding the link can play that one file, with no token, until it expires (24 hours by default). Treat the link like the file itself.

Without `download`, the file is sent inline and a single range request (`Range: bytes=...`) is answered with `206`, so a player can seek. A range that starts past the end of the file answers `416`. The response is never cached by a shared cache.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

parameters.name: user
parameters.description: The user (extension) whose music on hold (MoH) you play, such as `1001`. Use `~` for yourself. A user that does not exist answers `404`.

parameters.name: index
parameters.description: The index of the MoH file, as `ordinal-order` shows it in a list, such as `2`. Digits only. The file is `moh-02.wav`. With a token, leading zeros are ignored, so `02` names the same file. A signed link must use the index exactly as `file-access-url` gives it, or it answers `403`.

parameters.name: expires
parameters.description: The expiry of a signed link, in Unix seconds. Copy it from `file-access-url`; never set it yourself. Leave it out when you call with a token or a session cookie.

parameters.name: signature
parameters.description: The signature of a signed link, from `file-access-url`. With it the call needs no token, and it plays only the file the path names until `expires`. An expired link answers `403` with `Link has expired`; a changed path or expiry answers `403` with `Invalid signature`. Leave it out when you call with a token or a session cookie.

parameters.name: download
parameters.description: `yes` sends the file as a download (`Content-Disposition: attachment`) and turns off range requests. Left out or blank, the file is sent inline so a browser or an `<audio>` element plays it.

parameters.name: convert
parameters.description: Transcodes the audio before it is sent: `aac` (`audio/aac`) or `ogg` (`audio/ogg`). Left out, the stored WAV file is sent (`audio/wav`).

200.description: The MoH file's bytes. The body is the file: `audio/wav`, or `audio/aac` or `audio/ogg` with `convert`. It is binary, so there is no example.

Content-Disposition.description: `inline`, or `attachment` with `download=yes`, plus the file name.

Cache-Control.description: Always `private, no-store`: the file is personal data and is never cached by a shared cache.

206.description: The byte range the `Range` header asked for, with `Content-Range` giving the range sent and the full size.

Content-Range.description: The range sent and the full size.

404.description: No MoH file exists at this path, or the user or domain does not exist. The message is `Audio file not found`.

416.description: The `Range` starts past the end of the file. `Content-Range` gives the file size as `bytes */<size>`.

put.description:
Changes the order of the hold messages by renumbering them.

Basic User, Advanced User, Simple User, and Call Center Agent can change their own hold messages. Site Manager can change the hold messages of users at its own site. Office Manager, Call Center Supervisor, Route Manager, Reseller, and Super User can change any user's. The read-only scopes get `403`.

List the current indexes in `ordinal-order` in the order you want. The listed messages are renumbered into the same set of indexes, sorted: `[3, 1, 2]` moves the message at `3` to `1`, `1` to `2`, and `2` to `3`. Messages you leave out keep their index. Every listed index must be a distinct whole number with a message: a repeated or non-numeric index returns `400`, and an index with no message returns `404`; either way nothing moves. The files are renamed on the server that handles the request before the response, and copied to the other servers over the SBUS file journal. The call answers `202` by default, which here means applied on this server.

Reordering does not close a gap left by a delete: `[1, 3]` keeps `1` and `3`.

parameters.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

parameters.name: user
parameters.description: User (extension) whose hold messages you work with, such as `1001`. `~` means yourself. A user with no record returns `400` `Invalid User` on a read and `404` `User not found` on a write.

500.description: `Unable to reorder the files`: a rename failed. Files already staged are put back where possible. List the messages before retrying.

get.description:
Streams one of a user's hold messages, so a browser or an `<audio>` element can play it.

Call it one of two ways:

- **With a session.** Send a bearer token, or let the browser send its session cookie. The access is the same as for reading the file. Basic User, Advanced User, Simple User, and Call Center Agent can play only their own files. Site Manager, Call Center Supervisor, Office Manager, Office Manager Read-Only, and Route Manager can play any user's files in their domain. Reseller and Route Manager Reseller can play files in the domains of their territory, and Super User and Super User Read Only in every domain. Any other file answers `403`.
- **With a signed link.** Every read of the file returns `file-access-url`, which is this path with `expires` and `signature` added. Anyone holding the link can play that one file, with no token, until it expires (24 hours by default). Treat the link like the file itself.

Without `download`, the file is sent inline and a single range request (`Range: bytes=...`) is answered with `206`, so a player can seek. A range that starts past the end of the file answers `416`. The response is never cached by a shared cache.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

parameters.name: user
parameters.description: The user (extension) whose hold messages you play, such as `1001`. Use `~` for yourself. A user that does not exist answers `404`.

parameters.name: index
parameters.description: The index of the hold message, as `ordinal-order` shows it in a list, such as `1`. Digits only. The file is `msg-01.wav`. With a token, leading zeros are ignored, so `01` names the same file. A signed link must use the index exactly as `file-access-url` gives it, or it answers `403`.

parameters.name: expires
parameters.description: The expiry of a signed link, in Unix seconds. Copy it from `file-access-url`; never set it yourself. Leave it out when you call with a token or a session cookie.

parameters.name: signature
parameters.description: The signature of a signed link, from `file-access-url`. With it the call needs no token, and it plays only the file the path names until `expires`. An expired link answers `403` with `Link has expired`; a changed path or expiry answers `403` with `Invalid signature`. Leave it out when you call with a token or a session cookie.

parameters.name: download
parameters.description: `yes` sends the file as a download (`Content-Disposition: attachment`) and turns off range requests. Left out or blank, the file is sent inline so a browser or an `<audio>` element plays it.

parameters.name: convert
parameters.description: Transcodes the audio before it is sent: `aac` (`audio/aac`) or `ogg` (`audio/ogg`). Left out, the stored WAV file is sent (`audio/wav`).

Cache-Control.description: Always `private, no-store`: the file is personal data and is never cached by a shared cache.

206.description: The byte range the `Range` header asked for, with `Content-Range` giving the range sent and the full size.

404.description: No hold message exists at this path, or the user or domain does not exist. The message is `Audio file not found`.

416.description: The `Range` starts past the end of the file. `Content-Range` gives the file size as `bytes */<size>`.

get.description:
Speaks the text in the `file-script-text` query parameter and returns the audio, without storing it. It works like `POST /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/voices`, for players that can only fetch a URL.

Office Manager Read-Only and Super User Read Only get `403`. Synthesis also needs text to speech enabled (`PORTAL_VOICE_TEXT_TO_SPEECH`) for the user in the path, or the call returns `400`; the voice service answers for that user, and refuses with `403` when its settings do not allow text to speech.

get.description:

get.description:
Counts the call detail records (CDRs) that match across domains, and totals their talk time. Requires Super User, Super User Read Only, or Reseller scope. A Reseller sees only its own territory's domains. A Super User sees every domain unless you narrow the request with `domain` or `reseller`.

Send `datetime-start` and `datetime-end`: unlike the list, a count has no default window, and without them it returns `400`. The filters are the list's, and rows hidden with `hide-from-results` are left out unless you send `showhidden`. `minutes` rounds up month by month, so it can exceed `seconds` / 60 by up to 1 per month. Refused scope returns `403`.

parameters.description: Start of the window, matched on `call-start-datetime`. Use RFC 3339, such as `2026-09-01T00:00:00+00:00`. Also accepted: `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` in UTC, a date alone (from 00:00:00), and a time zone name in brackets after the time, such as `2026-09-01T00:00:00-05:00[America/Chicago]`, which reads the clock time in that zone and shows the response times in it. A numeric offset, such as `-05:00`, moves the window the same way and sets the offset of the response times. An offset that cannot be read returns `400`. Required: without both `datetime-start` and `datetime-end` the request returns `400`.

parameters.name: datetime-end
parameters.description: End of the window, exclusive, in the same forms as `datetime-start`. A date alone means 23:59:59 that day. It must be later than `datetime-start`. Required.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Only calls of one kind: `Inbound` is `call-direction` `1` or `2`, `Received` is `1`, `Missed` is `2`, `Outbound` is `0`, `On-net` or `Ext to Ext` is `3`, and `Off-net` is anything below `3`. A number matches `call-direction` exactly. Names match exactly, so `inbound` is refused: any other value returns `400`.

parameters.name: reseller

parameters.description: Only calls whose dialed number, `call-orig-to-user`, contains this value. `dialed` is accepted as the same parameter.

parameters.name: caller
parameters.description: Only calls whose caller's From URI, `call-orig-from-uri`, contains this value.

parameters.name: site
parameters.description: Only calls filed under this site. The rows then use the site shape, `CdrG`, with `grp` and `grp_type`. A Site Manager must name its own site.

parameters.name: group
parameters.description: Only calls filed under this department. The rows then use the site shape, `CdrG`. `department` is accepted as the same parameter.

parameters.name: showhidden
parameters.description: `yes` includes rows whose `hide-from-results` is `1`. They are left out otherwise. Any non-empty value works.

200.description: How many CDRs match, and their talk time.

get.description:
Returns call detail records (CDRs) across domains, newest first. Requires Super User, Super User Read Only, or Reseller scope. A Reseller sees only its own territory's domains. get.description:

get.description:
Returns the audio quality of each leg of one call: MOS, jitter, and packet loss in both directions, with links to the quality monitor that captured it. Requires Super User, Super User Read Only, Super User CDR, or Reseller scope, and a Reseller reads only calls that involve a domain in its territory. An empty array means the call exists but has no quality data: it predates quality scanning, scanning is off on this cluster, or the call ended less than about 30 seconds ago. A metric that was not measured is left out rather than reported as `0`, and the `rtcp-*` metrics are left out until RTCP capture is on. get.description:
Counts one domain's call detail records (CDRs) that match, and totals their talk time. Requires Office Manager, Office Manager Read-Only, Call Center Supervisor, or Route Manager scope for your own domain, Reseller scope for a domain in your territory, or Super User or Super User Read Only scope. A Site Manager reads its own site by adding `site`.

Send `datetime-start` and `datetime-end`: unlike the list, a count has no default window, and without them it returns `400`. The filters are the list's, and rows hidden with `hide-from-results` are left out unless you send `showhidden`. `minutes` rounds up month by month, so it can exceed `seconds` / 60 by up to 1 per month. Refused scope returns `403`.

parameters.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

parameters.description: Start of the window, matched on `call-start-datetime`. Use RFC 3339, such as `2026-09-01T00:00:00+00:00`. Also accepted: `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` in UTC, a date alone (from 00:00:00), and a time zone name in brackets after the time, such as `2026-09-01T00:00:00-05:00[America/Chicago]`, which reads the clock time in that zone and shows the response times in it. A numeric offset, such as `-05:00`, moves the window the same way and sets the offset of the response times. An offset that cannot be read returns `400`. parameters.name: datetime-end
parameters.description: End of the window, exclusive, in the same forms as `datetime-start`. A date alone means 23:59:59 that day. It must be later than `datetime-start`. Required.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Only calls of one kind: `Inbound` is `call-direction` `1` or `2`, `Received` is `1`, `Missed` is `2`, `Outbound` is `0`, `On-net` or `Ext to Ext` is `3`, and `Off-net` is anything below `3`. A number matches `call-direction` exactly. Names match exactly, so `inbound` is refused: any other value returns `400`.

parameters.description: Only calls whose dialed number, `call-orig-to-user`, contains this value. `dialed` is accepted as the same parameter.

parameters.name: caller

Returns one domain's call detail records (CDRs), newest first. Requires Office Manager, Office Manager Read-Only, Call Center Supervisor, or Route Manager scope for your own domain, Reseller scope for a domain in your territory, or Super User or Super User Read Only scope. A Site Manager reads its own site by adding `site`.

Set the window with `datetime-start` and `datetime-end`, matched on `call-start-datetime`. Without both, or when the start is not before the end, the window is about the last 60 days, from 00:00 UTC through the end of today. The offset you send moves the window and sets the offset of the response times.

Page with `start` and `limit`, 100 rows by default. `limit` also picks the response shape:

- `limit` of 100 or less, or `raw=yes`: the expanded shape, with the full call record merged into each row
- `limit` over 100, or `0` for no limit: the base shape, without `id`, the SIP Call-IDs, `core-server`, and about 60 other fields

The expanded shape costs one extra lookup per row. `call-parent-cdr-id` is on every row, and it is the id the keyed paths and `/quality` take.

The same path takes these forms. Each is a named example:

- **Search:** `dialled` matches part of the dialed number and `caller` part of the caller's From URI

post.description:
Creates a CDR export schedule for one domain. At each `schedule-next-run-datetime`, the CDR export service collects the calls that ended between `schedule-last-run-datetime` and `schedule-next-run-datetime`, keeps the directions the `export-*-calls-enabled` flags select, writes a CSV, and delivers it by `export-method`. It then moves both times forward by `schedule-repeat-interval`. Requires Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User scope. Basic User, Call Center Agent, and Site Manager can create one for themselves only: the schedule is stamped with their own extension, and a `user` naming someone else returns `403`.

`schedule-preset` is required. `Daily`, `Weekly`, and `Monthly` set `data-lookup-window` and `schedule-repeat-interval` for you. `Weekly` needs `schedule-weekly-day-of-week` and `schedule-start-time`, `Monthly` needs `schedule-monthly-day-of-month`, and `Custom` needs `time-zone` and `data-lookup-window`. Send `schedule-next-run-datetime` in RFC 3339 (`2026-09-02T09:00:00-04:00`) or as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` in `time-zone`. It is stored in UTC, and leaving it out means now. With `Daily`, `Weekly`, or `Monthly`, only its date is used: the time comes from `schedule-start-time`, or is midnight for `Monthly`. The owning reseller is filled in from the domain when you leave `reseller` out. A `reseller` that does not own the domain returns `400`. `schedule-user-export-scope` is set from your scope and cannot be sent.

The schedule was published over the service bus (SBUS) and is created when each server applies it. The body is `{"code": 202}`. Read the schedule back to confirm it.

A name already used anywhere on the platform returns `409`. A missing or invalid field returns `400` naming it, including an unknown `time-zone`, an unparseable date, a bad `schedule-start-time`, a name that breaks the pattern, `export-method` `scp copy`, and a masked-looking `export-password`.

parameters.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

get.description:
Downloads the CSV file (`text/csv`) of one export of a CDR schedule.

Call it one of two ways:

- **With a token.** Send a bearer token. Office Manager, Office Manager Read-Only, Call Center Supervisor, Route Manager, Reseller, Super User, and Super User Read Only can reach the exports of any schedule in the domain. Every other scope can reach only the exports of a schedule it owns in its own domain. A schedule you cannot see, or one that belongs to another domain, returns `404`.
- **With a signed link.** Every list or read of an export returns `file-access-url`, which is the system-wide form of this path with `expires` and `signature` added. Anyone holding the link can download that one file, with no token, until it expires (60 minutes by default). Treat the link like the file itself.

The file is kept on the server that ran the export. When you call a different server, it answers `302` with a short-lived signed link to the server that holds the file; follow the redirect.

Every download is recorded in the access log. The response is never cached by a shared cache.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

parameters.name: schedule_name
parameters.description: Schedule name. Names are unique across the whole platform, not per domain.

parameters.name: export_id
parameters.description: The export's `export-id` from the list: the start of the export window in UTC, as `YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ`.

parameters.name: expires
parameters.description: The expiry of a signed link, in Unix seconds. Copy it from `file-access-url`; never set it yourself. Leave it out when you call with a token.

parameters.name: signature
parameters.description: The signature of a signed link, from `file-access-url`. With it the call needs no token, and it downloads only the export the path names until `expires`. An expired link answers `403` with `Link has expired`; a changed path or expiry answers `403` with `Invalid signature`. Leave it out when you call with a token.

200.description: The export's CSV file (`text/csv`), sent as an attachment. It is the file the schedule wrote, so there is no example.

302.description: The file is on another server. `Location` is a signed link to it there, valid for 5 minutes. Follow it; most HTTP clients do so automatically.

Location.description: Signed download link on the server that holds the file.

400.description: `export_id` has the right shape but is not a real date and time, such as month `13`. Copy `export-id` from the list.

401.description: No signature was sent, and the access token is missing, expired, or invalid. Get a new token and retry, or use `file-access-url`.

403.description: Your scope has no rights on this domain's schedules, or the domain is outside your territory. The message names the missing privilege. Or the signed link has expired (`Link has expired`) or does not match the path (`Invalid signature`); read the export again for a fresh `file-access-url`.

404.description: The domain has no schedule with this name that you can see, or the domain does not exist. Or the schedule has no export with this `export-id`, or its file is no longer on the server (`File no longer available`).

503.description: The file is on another server, and a link to it could not be signed. Retry later.

A share link needs no token, is read-only, and stops working when the share expires or is revoked. A share stored on another server of the cluster is opened by adding `location`.

**What is included.** The trace follows transfers, forks, and conference bridges from your call IDs and adds those calls; `sql` lists every call ID it covered. The window is widened to cover the whole of every call found. A trace holds both parties' numbers, every hop's address, and the raw SIP messages, so treat it as call metadata. In `cradle_to_grave`, steps outside your scope are removed: by territory for a Reseller, and by domain for the other scopes below Super User.

- `type=csv&download=yes`: a CSV file (`text/csv`, `trace.csv`)
- `type=call_trace&download=yes`: the SVG diagram (`image/svg+xml`, `sipflow.svg`)
- `type=call_trace_html`: an HTML viewer page (`text/html`); add `download=yes` for `sip_flow.html`

A long call can take a minute or more to build.

- Ladder diagram: `GET /sipflow?start_time=2026-09-01T14:30:00+00:00&end_time=2026-09-01T14:34:10+00:00&callids=0f1e2d3c4b5a69788796a5b4c3d2e1f0@192.0.2.10&type=call_trace`

- Cradle to grave: `GET /sipflow?start_time=2026-09-01T14:30:00+00:00&end_time=2026-09-01T14:34:10+00:00&callids=0f1e2d3c4b5a69788796a5b4c3d2e1f0@192.0.2.10&type=cradle_to_grave`

parameters.name: margin
parameters.description: Seconds added before `start_time` and after `end_time` when reading events. A whole number. Defaults to `10`.

parameters.name: ds
parameters.description: Event sources to read, comma-separated: `diag` for the SIP servers, `ncs` for the conferencing servers. Defaults to `diag`. A conference bridge found on the way adds its conferencing server.

parameters.name: show_attendees
parameters.description: `yes` to follow a conference bridge and include every attendee's legs. Defaults to the platform setting, `no` unless changed. An ad hoc monitor bridge is always followed.
