400.description: A required field is missing (`Please provide a "start_time"`, `"end_time"`, or `"callids"`), or `Invalid "start_time" or "end_time"`. Send all three in a form the API can parse, or send `k`.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired, or invalid. Get a new token and retry. A share link (`k`) needs no token.

403.description: Your scope does not hold the call-trace privilege. Call with an Office Manager, Reseller, Super User, or Super User Read Only token.

404.description: No call in your scope matches the call IDs and window, or the share key is unknown, expired, or revoked, or `location` is not a known server. Check the call IDs and widen the window, or ask for a new share link.

get.summary: Get call trace by CDR ID without domain
get.description:
Builds the trace of one call from its CDR and returns it in the rendering you pick with `type`. The default is `call_trace_details`, with no `event` envelope. The path names no domain, so the call only has to be in your scope.

Super User and Super User Read Only see every trace. A Reseller sees calls that have a party domain (originating, terminating, or `by`) in its territory. Office Manager and the other domain-tier scopes see calls that have their own domain as a party domain. User-tier scopes see only calls where their own user is the originating or terminating party. A call outside your scope answers the same `404` as a call that does not exist. A scope without the call-trace privilege gets `403`; by default Office Manager, Reseller, Super User, and Super User Read Only hold it.

The documented response is JSON. The other renderings answer a file of their own media type:

- `type=csv&download=yes`: a CSV file (`text/csv`)
- `type=call_trace&download=yes`: the SVG diagram (`image/svg+xml`)
- `type=call_trace_html`: an HTML viewer page (`text/html`); add `download=yes` for `sip_flow_<id>.html`
- `type=call_trace_text`: plain text (`text/plain`)

In `call_trace_text`, each block header shows its time as `YYYY-MM-DD_HH:MM:SS` in UTC, and `csv` rows show the same form, with the millisecond Unix time in `UnixTsm`.

Prefer `GET /domains/{domain}/cdrs/{id}/sipflow`, which names the domain. `event` is not an ID here: `POST /sipflow/event` injects an event.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID of the call's CDR, as `id` in `GET /domains/{domain}/cdrs`. Letters and digits only.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Rendering to return: `call_trace_details` (the default), `call_trace`, `call_trace_html`, `call_trace_text`, `cradle_to_grave`, or `csv`.

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: Month the call was made in, as `YYYYMM` or any date, to pick which monthly CDR table to search first.

parameters.name: download
parameters.description: `yes` to receive the rendering as a file attachment.

parameters.name: show_attendees
parameters.description: `yes` to follow a conference bridge and include every attendee's legs.

200.description: The trace, in the rendering `type` asked for, with no envelope.

400.description: `date` is not `YYYYMM` or a date. Fix it and retry.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired, or invalid. Get a new token and retry.

403.description: Your scope does not hold the call-trace privilege. Call with an Office Manager, Reseller, Super User, or Super User Read Only token.

404.description: No CDR has this ID in the months searched, the CDR does not name the domain in the path, the call is outside your scope, the CDR has no call IDs, or no server logged the call. Send `date` for an older call, or check the ID.

get.summary: Download shared call trace as text
get.description:
Returns a shared call trace as plain text (`text/plain`): the raw SIP messages and log lines in time order, separated by dashed lines. Each block header shows its time as `YYYY-MM-DD_HH:MM:SS` in UTC, with no offset. The link ends in `.txt` for tools that accept only a file URL, such as an AI assistant you paste it into.

Needs no token: the share key in the path is the credential. A share link is read-only and expires; after that, or once it is revoked, the answer is `404`. Until then, anyone with the link can read the trace, including other parties' numbers and the raw SIP messages, so pass it only to people who should see the call.

This is `GET /sipflow?k={k}&type=call_trace_text`, and the route fixes `type`. Send `download=yes` to receive it as `sipflow.txt`. For a share stored on another server of the cluster, add `location`. Create a share with `POST /domains/{domain}/cdrs/{id}/sipflow/store`. Only `GET` is served on this path; any other method gets `405`.

parameters.name: k
parameters.description: Share key, the `key` a share answer gave: 8 digits, then 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters.

parameters.name: download
parameters.description: `yes` to receive the text as a `sipflow.txt` attachment.

parameters.name: location
parameters.description: Base64 of the `store-location` hostname the share answer gave, when the share is stored on another server of the cluster. A hostname that is not a known server of this cluster answers `404`.

200.description: The trace, as `text/plain; charset=utf-8`.

404.description: The share key is unknown, expired, or revoked, or `location` is not a known server. Ask whoever shared it for a new link.

405.description: The path serves `GET` only. Use `GET`.

post.description:
Writes one event row into a call's trace, so another application can place what it knows about the call in the same timeline as the SIP messages: an IVR choice, a media decision, or a push notification. The event appears in every rendering of the trace except `cradle_to_grave`.

Requires Super User scope. Super User Read Only gets `403`, because this is a write.

The row is written right away to the event log of the server you call; it is not published to the cluster. `201` means it is stored. A trace is read from the event logs of the servers its CDR names, so call the server that handled the call, or the event does not show. The day's event table is created by the SIP server, never by the API: an `event_time` whose day has no table returns `409`. A trace that has already been built is cached and does not show a new event until the cache expires, so write events before the trace is first viewed.

Stamp `event_time` when the event happens, not when you send it, as RFC 3339 with an offset (converted to UTC) or `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` in UTC, and include milliseconds. The trace sorts on that time, so a delivery delay cannot move the event. The answer's `event-time` is RFC 3339 in UTC, to the second; the milliseconds are in `event-ts`.

1.description: A menu selection, stamped when it happened.

value.event_text: push apns call alert="call" from="Front Desk" aor=sip:1001@example.com devices=2

2.description: A push-notification row, drawn on its own push lifeline.

201.description: The event is stored on the server you called. The answer is the row as written.

400.description: A required field is missing or blank, a field is too long or holds control characters, `event_time` is not a valid date and time (an impossible date included), or `event_ts` is not a number of milliseconds. The message names the field.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired, or invalid. Get a new token and retry.

403.description: Your token is not Super User scope. Call with a Super User token.

409.description: The server you called has no event table for that day. The message names the tables it looked for. Check `event_time` and `hostname`, and call the server that handled the call.

example.message: No event table for 2026-09-01. Looked for: event_20260901, core1_example_com_event_20260901.

500.description: `Unable to inject trace event`: the insert failed. Retry; if it fails again, contact support.

get.description:
Searches the raw event rows that call traces are built from. Where the other trace endpoints render one call, this one returns matching rows as they were logged: by call ID, by text inside the event (a SIP header, a number, an IP address), by event type, or by time alone.

Each core server keeps only its own events. By default every core server is searched at the same time and the rows are merged into one list, newest first. Set `hostname` to search one core server. Each row's `server` says which server it came from.

Requires Super User or Super User Read Only scope. The rows are raw SIP messages from every domain.

The search is limited so it cannot overload the event database:

- **Window**: at most 6 hours. With no `datetime-start` or `datetime-end`, it covers the 30 minutes before the request. A longer window returns `400`; it is never shortened for you.
- **Query time**: each server stops its search after 10 seconds.
- **Request time**: the whole request, including collecting rows from every server, stops after 15 seconds. A server that has not connected within 2 seconds, or answered within 15, is left out.
- **Rows**: `limit`, 1000 by default and 10000 at most, across all servers. When there are more matches, `X-NS-Result-Truncated` is `true`.

When some servers do not answer, you still get `200` with the rows from the ones that did, and `X-NS-Fanout-Missing` names the ones left out. When none answer, you get `504` if they all ran out of time, otherwise `502`.

parameters.name: datetime-start
parameters.description: Start of the window, inclusive. RFC 3339 with an offset (converted to UTC), or `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` in UTC. Defaults to 30 minutes before `datetime-end`.

parameters.name: datetime-end
parameters.description: End of the window, exclusive. Same formats as `datetime-start`. Defaults to now. Must be after `datetime-start` and no more than 6 hours later.

parameters.name: hostname
parameters.description: Core server to search. Leave blank or set `all` to search every core server and merge the rows. Any other value must be the name of a core server in this cluster.

parameters.name: callid
parameters.description: Call IDs to match, comma-separated, up to 50. A row matches when its `orig-callid` or `served-callid` is one of them.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Text to find anywhere in `event-text`, up to 255 characters. Matched as written, including `%` and `_`.

parameters.name: event-type
parameters.description: Event types to match, comma-separated, up to 20.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Most rows to return, 1 to 10000. Defaults to 1000.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: `desc` for newest first (default) or `asc` for oldest first.

200.description: Matching rows, possibly none. The headers state the window searched, which servers answered, and whether rows were left out.

event-index.description: Row number within that day's event table on the server you called. Not unique across days or servers.

event-time.description: When the event was logged, RFC 3339 in UTC, to the second.

event-ts.description: The same moment in milliseconds since the epoch. Traces sort on this.

hostname.description: Server name the event was logged under.

event-type.description: Kind of event, for example `sip` for a SIP message.

orig-callid.description: Call ID of the call leg the event belongs to.

served-callid.description: Call ID of the leg it was served on. Often the same as `orig-callid`.

event-text.description: The raw event: a full SIP message, or a server log line.

server.description: Core server whose event log the row came from.

value.event-text:
Received 1024 bytes from 192.0.2.10:5060
INVITE sip:1001@example.com SIP/2.0
Via: SIP/2.0/UDP 192.0.2.10:5060;branch=z9hG4bK776asdhds
From: <sip:2125550100@192.0.2.10>;tag=1928301774
To: <sip:1001@example.com>
Call-ID: 0f1e2d3c4b5a69788796a5b4c3d2e1f0@192.0.2.10
CSeq: 1 INVITE

X-NS-Window-Start.description: Start of the window searched, RFC 3339 in UTC.

X-NS-Window-End.description: End of the window searched, RFC 3339 in UTC.

X-NS-Result-Truncated.description: `true` when more rows matched than `limit` allowed.

X-NS-Fanout-Servers.description: Servers whose rows are included, comma-separated.

X-NS-Fanout-Missing.description: Servers that were asked and did not answer, comma-separated. Present only when some are missing; their rows are not in the list.

400.description: The window is longer than 6 hours, `datetime-start` is not before `datetime-end`, a date is not valid, `limit` is outside 1 to 10000, `sort` is not `asc` or `desc`, a filter has too many values or is too long, or `hostname` is not a core server in this cluster. The message names the problem.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired, or invalid. Get a new token and retry.

403.description: Your token is not Super User or Super User Read Only scope.

500.description: `Trace event search failed.`: the event database returned an error. Retry; if it fails again, contact support.

502.description: No server answered, and at least one failed for a reason other than time. The message names each server and why.

504.description: The search ran past 10 seconds, or the request past 15 seconds, on every server asked. Narrow the window or add a filter, and retry.

get.description:
Exports a call's trace as a file: the ladder diagram as SVG, or the event rows as CSV. Name the call by its SIP call IDs and a time window, as in `GET /sipflow`, or send a share key `k` for a stored trace. It takes the same fields as `POST /sipflow/export`, as query parameters, so a link can embed the diagram: `GET /sipflow/export?k=<key>` renders a shared trace as an image.

Super User and Super User Read Only see every trace. A Reseller sees calls that have a party domain (originating, terminating, or `by`) in its territory. Office Manager and the other domain-tier scopes see calls that have their own domain as a party domain. User-tier scopes see only calls where their own user is the originating or terminating party. A call outside your scope answers the same `404` as a call that does not exist. A scope without the call-trace privilege gets `403`; by default Office Manager, Reseller, Super User, and Super User Read Only hold it. Every call ID you send must match a CDR in your scope inside the window; the rest are ignored, and if none remain the answer is `404`. A share key needs no token and exports read-only; with a token, the stored call must be in your scope.

The answer is a file in the media type `export_format` picks:

- `image` (the default): the SVG ladder diagram, `image/svg+xml`, sent inline
- `csv`: the event rows with a header row, `text/csv`, as an attachment
- `base64`: base64 of the PHP-serialized raw rows, `text/plain`. The cluster's servers use this format with each other; integrations should use `csv`. Times in CSV and base64 rows, and in the `call_trace_text` block headers, are `YYYY-MM-DD_HH:MM:SS` in UTC (an underscore, no offset); the millisecond Unix time is the `UnixTsm` column.

For JSON renderings, use `GET /sipflow`.

**Example requests**

- SVG diagram: `GET /sipflow/export?start_time=2026-09-01T14:30:00+00:00&end_time=2026-09-01T14:34:10+00:00&callids=0f1e2d3c4b5a69788796a5b4c3d2e1f0@192.0.2.10`
- Shared trace as SVG: `GET /sipflow/export?k=202609019f86d081884c7d659a2feaa0c55ad015`

parameters.name: start_time
parameters.description: Start of the window to search, RFC 3339. A legacy `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` value is also accepted. Required unless `k` is sent.

parameters.name: end_time
parameters.description: End of the window. Same forms as `start_time`. Required unless `k` is sent.

parameters.name: callids
parameters.description: Comma-separated SIP call IDs. Each must match a CDR in your scope inside the window; the rest are ignored. Required unless `k` is sent.

parameters.name: export_format
parameters.description: `image` (the default) for SVG, `csv` for a CSV file, or `base64` for the raw rows the cluster's servers exchange.

parameters.name: k
parameters.description: Share key. Exports the stored trace with no token, read-only; the search fields are then ignored.

parameters.name: search_callids
parameters.description: `no` to trace only the call IDs you sent. Defaults to `yes`.

parameters.name: margin
parameters.description: Seconds added before `start_time` and after `end_time`. A whole number. Defaults to `10`.

parameters.name: ds
parameters.description: Event sources, comma-separated: `diag` or `ncs`. Defaults to `diag`.

parameters.name: show_attendees
parameters.description: `yes` to follow a conference bridge and include every attendee's legs.

200.description: The export. The stored type is the default, `image/svg+xml`; `export_format=csv` answers `text/csv` and `export_format=base64` answers `text/plain`, as the description lists.

400.description: `Invalid export_format`, a missing `start_time`, `end_time`, or `callids`, or `Invalid "start_time" or "end_time"`. Fix the request and retry.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired, or invalid. Get a new token and retry. A share key (`k`) needs no token.

403.description: Your scope does not hold the call-trace privilege. Call with an Office Manager, Reseller, Super User, or Super User Read Only token.

404.description: No call in your scope matches the call IDs and window, or the share key is unknown, expired, revoked, or for a call outside your scope. Check the call IDs and widen the window.

post.description:
Exports a call's trace as a file: the ladder diagram as SVG, or the event rows as CSV. Name the call by its SIP call IDs and a time window, as in `GET /sipflow`, or send a share key `k` for a stored trace. `GET /sipflow/export` takes the same fields as query parameters.

Super User and Super User Read Only see every trace. A Reseller sees calls that have a party domain (originating, terminating, or `by`) in its territory. Office Manager and the other domain-tier scopes see calls that have their own domain as a party domain. User-tier scopes see only calls where their own user is the originating or terminating party. A call outside your scope answers the same `404` as a call that does not exist. A scope without the call-trace privilege gets `403`; by default Office Manager, Reseller, Super User, and Super User Read Only hold it. Every call ID you send must match a CDR in your scope inside the window; the rest are ignored, and if none remain the answer is `404`. A share key needs no token and exports read-only; with a token, the stored call must be in your scope.

The answer is a file in the media type `export_format` picks:

- `image` (the default): the SVG ladder diagram, `image/svg+xml`, sent inline
- `csv`: the event rows with a header row, `text/csv`, as an attachment
- `base64`: base64 of the PHP-serialized raw rows, `text/plain`. The cluster's servers use this format with each other; integrations should use `csv`. Times in CSV and base64 rows, and in the `call_trace_text` block headers, are `YYYY-MM-DD_HH:MM:SS` in UTC (an underscore, no offset); the millisecond Unix time is the `UnixTsm` column.

For JSON renderings, use `GET /sipflow`.

1.description: The event rows of one call, as CSV.

2.description: The ladder diagram, as an SVG file.

3.description: A stored trace, by its share key, with no token.

200.description: The export. The stored type is the default, `image/svg+xml`; `export_format=csv` answers `text/csv` and `export_format=base64` answers `text/plain`, as the description lists.

400.description: `Invalid export_format`, a missing `start_time`, `end_time`, or `callids`, or `Invalid "start_time" or "end_time"`. Fix the request and retry.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired, or invalid. Get a new token and retry. A share key (`k`) needs no token.

403.description: Your scope does not hold the call-trace privilege. Call with an Office Manager, Reseller, Super User, or Super User Read Only token.

404.description: No call in your scope matches the call IDs and window, or the share key is unknown, expired, revoked, or for a call outside your scope. Check the call IDs and widen the window.

delete.description:
Revokes a call trace share, so its key stops working at once, before it would expire. Use it when a share link went somewhere it should not.

Requires the `delete` privilege on call traces: by default Office Manager, Reseller, and Super User. Super User Read Only and scopes without the privilege get `403`. A share key never authorizes a revoke; you always need a token. The shared call must be in your scope: Super User any call, a Reseller calls with a party domain in its territory, a domain-tier scope calls with its own domain as a party domain, and a user-tier scope calls where its user is a party. A key that does not exist, has expired, or is for a call outside your scope answers the same `404`.

The share is removed at once from the server you call: call the server named in the share's `store-location`. `200` means the share is gone. Only `DELETE` is served on this path; any other method gets `405`.

`DELETE /domains/{domain}/sipflow/share/{k}` is the same call, confined to one domain.

parameters.name: k
parameters.description: Share key to revoke, the `key` a share answer gave: 8 digits, then 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters.

200.description: The share is revoked. The body is `{"code": 200, "message": "Success"}`.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired, or invalid. Get a new token and retry. A share key is not a credential here.

403.description: Your scope does not hold the `delete` privilege on call traces. Call with an Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User token.

404.description: No share with this key is stored on the server you called, it has expired, or its call is outside your scope. Check the key, and call the server named in `store-location`.

405.description: `Method Not Allowed. Use DELETE.`: the path serves `DELETE` only.

post.description:
Stores a copy of one call's trace and returns a key that opens it without a token. The call is taken from its CDR ID. The path names no domain, so the call only has to be in your scope.

Requires the `create` privilege on call traces: by default Office Manager, Reseller, and Super User. Super User Read Only and scopes without the privilege get `403`. You can share only a call in your scope: Super User any call, a Reseller calls with a party domain in its territory, a domain-tier scope calls with its own domain as a party domain, and a user-tier scope calls where its user is the originating or terminating party. A call outside your scope answers the same `404` as one that does not exist.

Every share expires: after `ttl` seconds, capped at `NsTraceShareMaxTtl` (30 days by default), or after `NsTraceShareTempTtl` (15 minutes by default) when you send no `ttl`. The answer gives the moment it stops working twice: `expires` as a Unix time and `expires-datetime` as RFC 3339. Revoke a share early with `DELETE /sipflow/share/{k}`. Until then, anyone with the key can read the whole trace, read-only, including other parties' numbers and the raw SIP messages. Open it with `GET /sipflow?k=<key>` in any rendering, or `GET /sipflow/download/<key>.txt` for plain text.

The copy is stored on the server you call, named in `store-location`, before the answer is sent: `200` means the link works now. Only `POST` is served on this path; any other method gets `405`. Prefer `POST /domains/{domain}/cdrs/{id}/sipflow/store`, which names the domain.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID of the call's CDR, as `id` in `GET /domains/{domain}/cdrs`. Letters and digits only.

1.description: A share that expires in an hour.

2.description: No `ttl`: the share lives for `NsTraceShareTempTtl`, 15 minutes by default.

200.description: The share. `key` opens it until `expires-datetime`.

400.description: `date` is not `YYYYMM` or a date. Fix it and retry.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired, or invalid. Get a new token and retry.

403.description: Your scope does not hold the `create` privilege on call traces. Call with an Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User token.

404.description: No CDR has this ID in the months searched, the CDR does not name the domain in the path, the call is outside your scope, the CDR has no call IDs, or no server logged the call. Send `date` for an older call, or check the ID.

405.description: The path serves `POST` only. Use `POST`.

500.description: `Unable to save call trace`: the copy could not be stored. Retry; if it fails again, contact support.

get.description:
Returns the transcript, sentiment, topics, and AI summary of one call recording. Requires Office Manager, Site Manager, Reseller, Super User, or Super User Read Only scope. A Site Manager reads only calls whose leg in the domain belongs to its own site.

Name the transcription with `id`, the `call-intelligence-job-id` from the CDR, and the month of the call with `date`. A transcription finished in the month after the call is found as well. Also send a call ID that belongs to the domain, and to the call the transcription is for: `orig_callid`, `term_callid`, or `by_callid` when you know which side it is, or `callid` to check both originating and terminating sides.

Processing is asynchronous. Until `call-intelligence-processing-status` is `finished`, some fields are empty.

For the whole call as one document, with every leg, recording, and transcript, use `GET /domains/{domain}/vcon/{cdr_id}`.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The transcription job ID: `call-intelligence-job-id` on the CDR. `call-intelligence-job-id` is also accepted as the parameter name. A number.

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: The month of the call, as 6 digits `YYYYMM`, such as `202609`. Anything else returns `400`.

parameters.name: callid
parameters.description: A call ID of the call, checked against both the originating and terminating sides. Send at least one of `callid`, `orig_callid`, `term_callid`, and `by_callid`; one of them must belong to a call of the domain in that month.

parameters.name: orig_callid
parameters.description: The originating call ID of the call. Send at least one of `callid`, `orig_callid`, `term_callid`, and `by_callid`; one of them must belong to a call of the domain in that month.

parameters.name: term_callid
parameters.description: The terminating call ID of the call. Send at least one of `callid`, `orig_callid`, `term_callid`, and `by_callid`; one of them must belong to a call of the domain in that month.

parameters.name: by_callid
parameters.description: The call ID of the leg the call was transferred or forwarded by. Send at least one of `callid`, `orig_callid`, `term_callid`, and `by_callid`; one of them must belong to a call of the domain in that month.

200.description: The transcription, with its segments and analysis.

example.call-intelligence-summary: The caller asks about a replacement part that has not arrived. The agent finds the order and confirms it ships later in the week.

call-intelligence-segments.speaker: sip:1001@example.com
call-intelligence-segments.comment: Hello, and thanks for calling. How can I help you today?

call-intelligence-segments.speaker: sip:+15555550100@203.0.113.30
call-intelligence-segments.comment: Hi. I am calling about a part I ordered that has not arrived.

400.description: `id` or `date` is missing, `date` is not a month as `YYYYMM`, or `id` is not a number. The message names the problem. Correct it and retry.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired, or invalid. Get a new token and retry.

403.description: Your token cannot read transcriptions for this domain, or no call ID you sent belongs to a call of the domain in that month (for a Site Manager, to a call of its own site). The message is `Bad request. Invalid domain or callids.` for the call ID case. Check the call ID and `date`, and use a token with rights to the domain.

404.description: No transcription with this `id` exists in the month of `date` or the month after, or it is for a call other than the call IDs you sent. Check the job ID on the CDR.

500.description: The transcription could not be read. Retry later, and contact support if it persists.

get.description:
Returns how many calls were in progress over a recent window, for your territory or the whole platform, as a series of buckets ending now.

Requires Reseller, Super User, or Super User Read Only scope. A Reseller always gets its own territory, and `reseller` and `domain` are ignored. A Super User gets the whole platform, or one reseller with `reseller`, or one domain with `domain`.

The platform-wide series counts all calls and ignores `type`. Only `GET` is accepted.

parameters.name: range
parameters.description: Window to cover, ending now. Defaults to `24h`.

parameters.name: period
parameters.description: Bucket size. Defaults to `minute` for `1h` and `3h`, `hour` up to `7d`, and `day` for `28d`. Minute buckets are kept for about 3.5 hours and hourly buckets for 15 days: a size that does not cover `range` returns `400`.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Which calls to count: calls between users on the platform (`onnet`), calls to or from outside it (`offnet`), or both. Defaults to `all`. Ignored for the platform-wide series.

parameters.name: reseller

post.description:
Adds a contact to a user's personal address book.

Basic User, Advanced User, Simple User, Call Center Agent, and Call Center Supervisor can create their own contacts only. Site Manager can create its own contacts and those of users at its own site. Office Manager can create the contacts of any user in its domain, Reseller those of users in domains of its territory, and Super User any user's. A request for any other address book returns `403`.

`name-first-name` and `name-last-name` are required. The server assigns `unique-id` unless you send one. An ID you send must be 1 to 32 letters, digits, `-`, or `_`, not `groups`, `list`, or `count` in any case, and unused in every address book; an ID in use returns `409` and no contact is overwritten. `na`, `undefined`, or an empty value also gets a generated ID. `is-favorite` marks the contact as a favorite and `groups` files it in contact groups. `avatar` is ignored; set the picture with `POST /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/contacts/{contact_id}/avatar`. A contact that repeats an existing one in the same address book, with the same names and the same phone numbers, email, and fax that you send, returns `409`.

The contact is written asynchronously. The call waits up to 2 seconds for the write to apply and then returns the stored contact. If it has not applied by then, the response holds the fields you sent and the new `unique-id`, in the same shape; read the contact again shortly after.

When the user has video meetings, the contact is also added to their video contact list.

parameters.name: user

Fix the request and retry.

Deletes every contact in a user's personal address book that matches a first and last name, and optionally a tag. To delete one contact, use `DELETE /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/contacts/{contact_id}` instead.

Basic User, Advanced User, Simple User, Call Center Agent, and Call Center Supervisor can delete from their own address book only. Site Manager can delete from its own and from those of users at its own site, Office Manager from any user's in its domain, Reseller from those of users in domains of its territory, and Super User from any. Any other address book returns `403`.

`name-first-name` and `name-last-name` are required and match exactly; `tags` narrows the match to contacts whose stored tags contain its text. Send them in the query string or the JSON body. Every contact that matches is deleted, so check the matches with the list first. When none match, nothing is deleted and the call still returns `202`. Only this address book is searched; the domain's shared contacts are never deleted this way. Unlike the delete by ID, this call leaves the contacts' avatars and video contact copies in place.

`202` means the deletes were accepted and are applied shortly after.

Needs domain tier or above: Office Manager can create its own domain's shared contacts, Reseller those of domains in its territory, and Super User any domain's. Scopes that can only read them, including Site Manager and Call Center Supervisor, get `403`.

post.description:
Sends a chat, SMS, or MMS message without a session ID, and answers with the stored message. Every scope reaches its own user. Office Manager reaches every user in its domain, Reseller the domains in its territory, and Super User every domain. You send as the user in the path.

The session is found from who takes part: the same sender and recipients always land in the same session, so calling this again continues the conversation. Read `messagesession-id` in the answer and use it with `POST /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/messagesessions/{messagesession}/messages` for later messages.

`type` is one of these values:

- `chat`: a text message to users in the same domain. The default.
- `chat-media`: a chat message with a file attached.
- `sms`: a text message to phone numbers, sent from one of your SMS numbers.
- `mms`: an SMS with a file attached.
- `chat-video-invite`, `chat-video-decline`: video call invitations sent in a chat.

The API itself writes `chat-name-change`, `chat-participant-add`, `chat-participant-remove`, `chat-participant-remove-notification`, and `chat-participant-leave` messages when a session changes. Do not send them.

### Chat

Send `message` and `destination`, the extension of a user in the same domain. `type` can be left out.

### Group chat

Send `destination` as a list of extensions, or as one comma-separated string.

### Media chat

Set `type` to `chat-media` and attach the file as base64 in `data`, with `mime-type` and `size`. Or send `upload_id` for a file you already uploaded. `message` is still required.

### SMS

Set `type` to `sms`, `destination` to the phone number, and `from-number` to your SMS number. `from-number` must be assigned in this domain to the sending user, or to a call queue.

### Group SMS

Send `destination` as a list of numbers. The message goes out as a group MMS.

### MMS

Set `type` to `mms`, add `from-number`, and attach the file as for a media chat.

A number that texted STOP to `from-number` does not get the message. When every recipient has opted out, the request answers `409`. For the opt-out list, see `GET /domains/{domain}/smsblocks`.

Send `session-name`. Every participant's copy is renamed, and every participant gets a `chat-name-change` message.

### Set the participants

Send `messagesession-participants` with the complete list of user IDs, including your own, for example `1001@example.com,1002@example.com,1003@example.com`. post.description:
Sends a chat, SMS, or MMS message in an existing session. Every scope reaches its own user. Office Manager reaches every user in its domain, Reseller the domains in its territory, and Super User every domain. You send as the user in the path.

Leave `type` out, or send `chat`, in an SMS or MMS session, and the message goes out as that session's type, to its number, from the number used last. To start a conversation without a session ID, use `POST /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/messages`.

`type` is one of these values:

- `chat`: a text message to users in the same domain. The default.
- `chat-media`: a chat message with a file attached.
- `sms`: a text message to phone numbers, sent from one of your SMS numbers.
- `mms`: an SMS with a file attached.
- `chat-video-invite`, `chat-video-decline`: video call invitations sent in a chat.

The API itself writes `chat-name-change`, `chat-participant-add`, `chat-participant-remove`, `chat-participant-remove-notification`, and `chat-participant-leave` messages when a session changes. Do not send them.

### Chat

Send `message` and `destination`, the extension of a user in the same domain. `type` can be left out.

### Group chat

Send `destination` as a list of extensions, or as one comma-separated string.

### Media chat

Set `type` to `chat-media` and attach the file as base64 in `data`, with `mime-type` and `size`. Or send `upload_id` for a file you already uploaded. `message` is still required.

### SMS

Set `type` to `sms`, `destination` to the phone number, and `from-number` to your SMS number. `from-number` must be assigned in this domain to the sending user, or to a call queue.

### Group SMS

Send `destination` as a list of numbers. The message goes out as a group MMS.

### MMS

Set `type` to `mms`, add `from-number`, and attach the file as for a media chat.

A number that texted STOP to `from-number` does not get the message. When every recipient has opted out, the request answers `409`. For the opt-out list, see `GET /domains/{domain}/smsblocks`.

Below Office Manager, your token's user must be a participant of the session: posting into anyone else's session answers `403`. A session ID that no session has yet is allowed, and starts that session. A video meeting chat is the exception: your token's user must attend the meeting, even to post its first message, and only a host or presenter can post into the meeting's hosts chat.

A `202` means the change is accepted and applied shortly after, so a read made right away can still show the old values.

With no filters, every number in the domain is returned. Filter with `dest`, `number`, `number_LIKE`, or `site`, and page with `start` and `limit`. `mms-capable` and `group-mms-capable` appear only on numbers whose carrier supports them.

To count the same numbers, use `GET /domains/{domain}/smsnumbers/count`. To read one number, use `GET /domains/{domain}/smsnumbers/{smsnumber}`. To list one user's numbers, use `GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/smsnumbers`.

Requires Reseller or Super User scope. To take a number out of service without deleting it, set `application` to `available` with `PUT /domains/{domain}/smsnumbers/{smsnumber}`.

get.description:
Returns every recording of a call in the domain, each with a signed `file-access-url` that plays it, whether or not you were a party to the call. Scopes: Office Manager and Site Manager on their domain, Reseller on their territory, and Super User. A Basic User reads their own calls with `GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/recordings/{callid}`.

A call can have several recordings, one per case it matched, such as the user's own rule and a domain-wide rule. Only recordings whose case belongs to the domain, or to a SIP trunk in it, are returned. Narrow them with `call-recording-match-pattern`.

A Super User Read Only token is refused unless it is a party to the call.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

parameters.name: callid
parameters.description: The SIP call ID of either leg of the call, as `orig-callid` or `term-callid` on its CDR. Letters, digits, `@`, `*`, `.`, `-`, `_`, and `'`.

parameters.name: call-recording-match-pattern
parameters.description: Return only the recording made for this case, exact match: `user@domain`, or `*@domain` for a domain-wide rule. Also accepted as `case_id`.

200.description: The recordings of the call. An empty array when none belongs to the domain.

400.description: The path ends with `/`, or a query option is malformed. Correct the request and retry.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired, or invalid. Get a new token and retry.

404.description: No playable recording exists for this call ID, or none of its recordings belong to the path. Recordings still converting, or that failed conversion or archiving, are not returned. Check the call ID against the CDR and retry later if the call just ended.

get.description:
Returns the recording of a call that the user in the path was part of, with a signed `file-access-url` that plays it. Scopes: Basic User and Call Center Agent on their own user; Office Manager and Site Manager on their domain; Reseller on their territory; Super User.

The response is one recording, not an array. When a call has several recordings, the first one made for this user, one of the user's devices, or a domain-wide rule (`*@domain`) is returned. Narrow it with `call-recording-match-pattern`.

A Super User Read Only token is refused unless it is a party to the call.

To list every recording of a call in a domain, use `GET /domains/{domain}/recordings/{callid}`. To play the audio, open `file-access-url`.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

parameters.name: user
parameters.description: User's extension, such as `1001`. `~` means the user your token belongs to.

parameters.name: callid
parameters.description: The SIP call ID of either leg of the call, as `orig-callid` or `term-callid` on its CDR. Letters, digits, `@`, `*`, `.`, `-`, `_`, and `'`.

parameters.name: call-recording-match-pattern
parameters.description: Return only the recording made for this case, exact match: `user@domain`, or `*@domain` for a domain-wide rule. Also accepted as `case_id`.

200.description: The recording.

400.description: The path ends with `/`, or a query option is malformed. Correct the request and retry.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired, or invalid. Get a new token and retry.

403.description: Your token cannot read this recording. Only a party to the call, an Office Manager of a party's domain, a Site Manager of a party's site, a Call Center Supervisor of the queue, a Reseller, or a Super User can. The message is `You do not have permission to access this recording.`

404.description: No playable recording exists for this call ID, or none of its recordings belong to the path. Recordings still converting, or that failed conversion or archiving, are not returned. Check the call ID against the CDR and retry later if the call just ended.

get.description:
Streams the audio of a call recording. Open the `file-access-url` that a recording read returns; do not build the link yourself. The response is binary audio, `audio/wav` by default, or `audio/aac` or `audio/ogg` with `convert`. There is no example body.

No access token is needed. The link is its own credential: anyone who has it can play the recording until it expires, 180 minutes after it was created by default. Every link expires. Read the recording again for a new link.

Byte ranges are honored with `206 Partial Content`, so a media player can seek, unless `download` is set. Each play is recorded in the access log once, on the request for the start of the file.

A link whose signature does not match, that has expired, whose `time` is more than 5 minutes in the future, or whose `uid` names no active login, returns `403` with no body. A recording whose file is no longer on the Recording server or in remote storage returns `404` with no body.

parameters.name: accel
parameters.description: The Recording server element that holds the file. Copy it from `file-access-url`.

parameters.name: casid
parameters.description: The case the recording was made for, such as `1001@example.com`. Copy it from `file-access-url`.

parameters.name: cccid
parameters.description: The ID of the recording. Copy it from `file-access-url`.

parameters.name: calid
parameters.description: The SIP call ID of the recorded leg, URL-encoded. Copy it from `file-access-url`.

parameters.name: uid
parameters.description: The hostname of the server that created the link. Copy it from `file-access-url`. It does not name the person who reads the recording.

parameters.name: time
parameters.description: When the link was created, in UTC, as `YYYYMMDDHHMMSS`. Copy it from `file-access-url`. The link expires 180 minutes later by default. A time more than 5 minutes in the future fails with `403`.

parameters.name: auth
parameters.description: The signature over the other link parameters, as 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters. Copy it from `file-access-url`. Changing any signed parameter makes it fail with `403`.

parameters.name: convert
parameters.description: Transcodes the audio before sending it. `aac` answers `audio/aac` and `ogg` answers `audio/ogg`. `wav16`, `signed`, `signed_ffmpeg`, and `gsm` answer a converted WAV file as `audio/wav`. Any other value, `mp3` included, returns the original WAV file. If a conversion fails, the original file is sent.

parameters.name: stereo
parameters.description: `true` builds a two-channel file, one channel per side of the call, when the stored file is mono. `force` rebuilds it even when the stored file is already stereo. Works only while the raw call audio is still on the Recording server. A rebuilt file is sent whole, with no byte ranges.

parameters.name: download
parameters.description: Present with any value, even blank, the whole file is sent in one `200` response with no byte ranges. A value other than `false` also records the request as a download rather than a play. The file is always sent as an attachment.

parameters.name: Range
parameters.description: A single byte range, such as `bytes=0-` or `bytes=1000-1999`. Honored with `206` unless `download` is set. A suffix range (`bytes=-500`) or several ranges are not supported and return the whole file.

200.description: The whole recording, as `audio/wav`, `audio/aac`, or `audio/ogg`, with `Content-Disposition: attachment`.

206.description: The requested byte range, with `Content-Range` and `Accept-Ranges: bytes`.

400.description: A required link parameter is missing or blank. The message names it, such as `Please provide a "auth" value`. Use the complete `file-access-url`.

403.description: The signature does not match the other parameters, the link has expired, its `time` is not a valid creation time, or its `uid` names no active login. The body is empty. Read the recording again for a new link.

404.description: The recording file is not on the Recording server or in remote storage. The body is empty.

post.description:
Sends a templated email to a user, at the address stored on their account. `template` picks the email:

- **Call center report.** A call center statistics report for a time window, `call_center_*.php`.
- **Account email.** Welcome, password reset, or forgotten login name.
- **Custom template.** A `custom_*` template uploaded for the domain.
- **Lost authenticator.** A recovery link for a user who lost their authenticator app.
- **Email verification.** A verification link for one of the user's addresses.

A Basic User can send to themselves. Office Manager can send to users in their domain, Reseller to users in their territory, and Super User to anyone. Below Office Manager, every `cclist` address must also be one of the user's own addresses, or the answer is `403`.

The response is `200` when the request was understood, with `sent` saying whether the email went out: `sent: false` means it could not be built, for example because the user has no email address. A body that matches no email is a `400`.

parameters.name: user

Connects to an SMTP server, logs in, optionally sends a test message, and reports each step. Nothing is stored, so you can check settings before you save them on a reseller or domain. Requires Reseller or Super User scope.

The response is `200` whenever the test ran, with `success` saying whether it worked and `details.stage` saying where it stopped. A login failure is never retried without encryption. A request that cannot be tested is a `400`. Each connection attempt has 10 seconds by default.

Returns the number of connections. Requires the scope `GET /connections` requires, and a Reseller is confined to its territory the same way.

Without `routechain`, route profiles are left out of the count. `GET /domains/{domain}/connections/count` counts one domain.

parameters.description: Exact `connection-term-match-pattern`. Returns at most one row. Below the Super User tier, the lookup stays inside your territory or domain, and a token with neither gets `403`.

get.description:
Returns connections across domains. Requires Super User, Super User Read Only, or Reseller scope. A Reseller sees its own territory's domains; Super User and Super User Read Only see every domain. Office Manager, Route Manager, Call Center Supervisor, and Office Manager Read-Only can call it with `domain` set to their own domain, or use `GET /domains/{domain}/connections`.

Narrow the list with `domain`, `reseller`, `connection-usage-role`, or `connection-connectivity-type`. `connection-orig-match-pattern` and `connection-term-match-pattern` are exact lookups that return at most one row, and a Reseller's lookup stays inside its territory. Without `routechain`, route profiles are left out; read them with `GET /routeprofiles`. Page with `start` and `limit`, 100 rows by default. Use `GET /connections/count` for a total, and `GET /connections/list` for the identity fields only.

A `domain` or `reseller` outside your scope returns `403`.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Only this domain's connections. Omit it, or send `*`, for every domain you can see.

parameters.name: routechain
parameters.description: `yes` returns only route profiles, whose address is a route name in angle brackets. `no` leaves them out.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Number of records to skip before the first one returned. Defaults to `0`. Use it with `limit` to page.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of records to return. Defaults to `100`. Use it with `start` to page.

parameters.name: reseller
parameters.description: Only the connections of this territory's domains. A Reseller's own territory applies by default, and another territory returns `403`.

parameters.name: connection-orig-match-pattern
parameters.description: Exact `connection-orig-match-pattern`. Returns at most one row.

parameters.name: connection-term-match-pattern
parameters.description: Exact `connection-term-match-pattern`. Returns at most one row. Below the Super User tier, the lookup stays inside your territory or domain, and a token with neither gets `403`.

parameters.name: connection-usage-role
parameters.description: Only connections with this role, such as `vendor`.

parameters.name: connection-connectivity-type
parameters.description: Only connections of this connectivity type.

200.description: The matching connections. None returns `[]`.

400.description: The request is malformed. The message says what to correct.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired, or invalid. Get a new token and retry.

403.description: Your scope does not cover the `domain` or `reseller` you named, or cannot list connections across domains. Add `domain` for your own domain, or use `GET /domains/{domain}/connections`.

post.description:
Creates a connection in the domain that the body's `domain` names. Requires Office Manager, Route Manager, or Call Center Supervisor scope in that domain, Reseller scope in its territory, or Super User scope. The API publishes the connection on the service bus (SBUS) `connection_events` channel, and each server writes it when the event arrives, so `202` means published, not applied.

`connection-orig-match-pattern` and `domain` are required. `connection-orig-match-pattern` is the connection's key and must be unique across the platform, not only the domain: a value any connection already uses returns `409`. `connection-term-match-pattern` defaults to it, and `connection-translation-request-host` and `connection-translation-destination-host` default to `connection-address`, as the API formats it for the connectivity type. `connection-source-ip-checking-enabled` and `connection-include-server-header-enabled` default to `no`. `connection-connectivity-type` defaults to `header_ip_match` and sets `connection-sip-authenticate-as-client-enabled`: `yes` for `outbound_registration`, `no` for every other type. A value you send that contradicts the type is overridden, and the response carries a `Warning` header and a `warnings` list. `connection-sip-registration-password` defaults to a random 8-character value.

Create route profiles with `POST /domains/{domain}/routeprofiles`. Sending `call-routing` here returns `404`.

Send `synchronous=yes`, in the body or the query string, to wait up to 2 seconds for the connection to be written. You then get `200` with the connection. If it is not written in time, you get the usual `202`.

If a connection with the same `connection-orig-match-pattern` was deleted in the last 15 minutes, and the platform is set to block re-created connections, some servers can refuse the new one after the `202`. Read it back, and repeat the create if it is missing.

`POST /domains/{domain}/connections` does the same with the domain in the path.

2.description: An IP peer, identified by its address, with no registration.

3.description: A carrier the platform registers to with SIP credentials.

4.description: A system that registers to the platform. The address is its SIP address.

5.description: `synchronous=yes` waits up to 2 seconds and answers `200` with the connection.

200.description: Returned for `synchronous=yes` once the connection is written: the connection.

202.description: The connection was published on the SBUS. It is written after this response.

warnings: connection-sip-authenticate-as-client-enabled: 'no' stored as 'yes'. connection-connectivity-type 'outbound_registration' determines it, and the two values sent contradict each other.

400.description: `connection-orig-match-pattern` is missing, a value is invalid (`connection-connectivity-type`, `connection-require-encrypted-audio-enabled`, or `connection-sip-session-timer-enabled`), or the SBUS publish failed. The message says which. Correct the request and retry.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired, or invalid. Get a new token and retry.

403.description: Your scope cannot create connections in the body's `domain`. Use a token for that domain or its territory.

404.description: `call-routing` was sent. Create route profiles with `POST /domains/{domain}/routeprofiles`.

409.description: A connection with this `connection-orig-match-pattern` already exists on the platform, in this or another domain. Choose another value, or update the existing connection.

get.description:
Returns one connection by `connection-id`, without naming its domain. Requires Office Manager, Route Manager, Call Center Supervisor, or Office Manager Read-Only scope in the connection's domain, Reseller scope in its territory, or Super User or Super User Read Only scope.

An id that names no connection returns `404`, and so does a route profile's id; read those with `GET /routeprofiles/{connection-id}`. One in a domain your scope does not cover returns `403`.

parameters.name: connection-id
parameters.description: The connection's `connection-id`, as a list returns it: base64url, without padding, of `connection-orig-match-pattern`. The raw `connection-orig-match-pattern` is also accepted.

200.description: The connection.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired, or invalid. Get a new token and retry.

403.description: Your scope does not cover the connection's domain. Use a token for that domain or its territory.

404.description: No connection has this `connection-id`. List the connections to find the id.

put.description:
Changes a connection by `connection-id`, without naming its domain. Requires Super User or Reseller scope. A Reseller can change only a connection in its own territory; other scopes use `PUT /domains/{domain}/connections/{connection-id}`. The API publishes the change on the service bus (SBUS) `connection_events` channel, and each server applies it when the event arrives, so `202` means published, not applied.

The path identifies the connection. A `domain` or `connection-orig-match-pattern` in the body is ignored, so the key cannot be renamed. An id that names no connection, or one outside your territory, returns `404`. A route profile's id keeps its route-name address and its `route_profile` type: a different `connection-connectivity-type` returns `400`, and a different `connection-address` is ignored with a `Warning` header. Send only what changes. Omitted fields keep their stored values, the call-processing fields such as `connection-sip-transport-protocol` included. Changing `connection-connectivity-type` also sets `connection-sip-authenticate-as-client-enabled` and reformats `connection-address` to suit the type. An invalid `connection-connectivity-type`, `connection-require-encrypted-audio-enabled`, or `connection-sip-session-timer-enabled` returns `400`. Sending `call-routing` returns `404`: change a route profile's route through the route-profile endpoints. `synchronous` is ignored.

parameters.name: connection-id
parameters.description: The connection's `connection-id`, as a list returns it: base64url, without padding, of `connection-orig-match-pattern`. The raw `connection-orig-match-pattern` is also accepted.

1.description: Only the fields sent change.

2.description: Call-processing fields you leave out keep their stored values.

3.description: Cap simultaneous calls on the connection.

202.description: The change was published on the SBUS. It is applied after this response.

400.description: A value is invalid (`connection-connectivity-type`, `connection-require-encrypted-audio-enabled`, or `connection-sip-session-timer-enabled`), the id names a route profile and the body asks for another `connection-connectivity-type`, or the SBUS publish failed. The message says which. Correct the request and retry.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired, or invalid. Get a new token and retry.

403.description: Your scope cannot update connections without a domain. Use `PUT /domains/{domain}/connections/{connection-id}`.

404.description: No connection has this `connection-id` within your territory, or `call-routing` was sent. List the connections to find the id.

delete.description:
Deletes a connection by `connection-id`, without naming its domain. Requires Office Manager, Route Manager, or Call Center Supervisor scope in the connection's domain, Reseller scope in its territory, or Super User scope. The API publishes the delete on the service bus (SBUS) `connection_events` channel, and each server removes the row when the event arrives, so `202` means published, not deleted.

An id that names no connection returns `404`. One in a domain your scope does not cover returns `403`. A route profile's id deletes the profile with its route and route connections.

Read the connection back to confirm it is gone. A connection that another platform service keeps registering, most often an `outbound_registration` one, can be written back about 30 to 60 seconds after the delete. If it keeps coming back, contact support.

400.description: The SBUS publish failed. Retry the request.

403.description: Your scope does not cover the connection's domain. Use a token for that domain or its territory.

404.description: No connection has this `connection-id`. List the connections to find the id.

Without a filter it counts every route connection on the platform. To count one route's connections, use `/routes/{route-id}/routecon/count`. `GET /routecon` lists the same rows. Without a filter it lists every route connection on the platform, including those of route-profile routes. Page with `start` and `limit`, 100 rows by default. `GET /routecon/count` counts the same rows. To read one route's connections, use `GET /routes/{route-id}/routecon`.

The path is read-only, so any other method returns `405`. Write a route connection through `/routes/{route-id}/routecon`.

Returns the platform's call routes from `route_config`, each with the `route-id` you use to read, update, or delete it and to manage its route connections. Routes apply to the whole platform, not to one domain or territory. Requires Super User, Reseller, or Super User Read Only scope.

Without `route-destination-match-pattern`, the list holds only routes whose destination pattern starts with `sip` and contains `@`, such as `sip:1800*@*`. That leaves out the routes behind route profiles, which you read with `GET /domains/{domain}/routeprofiles`. Every filter is an exact match, and filters combine. Rows are sorted by `route-destination-match-pattern` and paged with `start` and `limit`, 100 rows by default.

`GET /routes/count` takes the same filters and counts the same rows. `GET /routes/{route-id}` returns one route.

post.description:
Creates a route profile in the domain, with its route and route connections. Requires Office Manager, Route Manager, or Call Center Supervisor scope in the domain, Reseller scope in its territory, or Super User scope. The API publishes the route on the service bus (SBUS) `NmsRoute` channel and then the profile on `connection_events`, and each is applied when its event arrives, so `202` means published, not applied.

`connection-orig-match-pattern` is required and is the profile's key. It must be unique across the platform, not only the domain: a value any connection already uses returns `409`. The API sets the address itself: the domain in capitals, `_`, and the part of `connection-orig-match-pattern` after any `@`, in angle brackets, such as `<EXAMPLE.COM_tollfree>`. The name inside the brackets is the route's `route-destination-match-pattern`. `connection-connectivity-type` is always `route_profile`.

Put the route in `call-routing`. `route-method` defaults to `percentage`, `route-is-enabled` to `yes`, and `description` to the profile's `description`. Each entry in `routecon` needs `route-connection-translation-destination-host`. `route-connection-ordinal-index` is optional: an entry without one takes the next free index. The whole of `call-routing` is checked before anything is published, so a missing host, or an index that is repeated or not a positive whole number, returns `400` with nothing created. Without `call-routing`, no route is created.

A failed create leaves nothing behind, so it is always safe to retry. Send `synchronous=yes`, in the body or the query string, to wait up to 2 seconds for the change to be applied. You then get `200` with the profile. If it is not applied in time, you get the usual `202` and the write still completes.

Requires a token for the user in the path, or Office Manager scope or higher for the domain. A Basic User creates meetings only for itself.

The meeting is owned by the user in the path. Creating it also sets up its audio bridge and invites everyone in `attendees` by email. Omitted settings take their defaults: the start is now, the length is 60 minutes, and the participant limit comes from the domain's configuration. The response is the new meeting as a one-item array. When the create has not been applied yet, the item holds the fields that were accepted.

To choose the ID yourself, reserve one with `POST /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/meetings/getId`, then create the meeting with `POST /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/meetings/{meeting}`.

get.description:
Returns one meeting with its attendees, as seen by the user in the path.

Access is checked against the meeting's owner: any user in the owner's domain can read it, and Office Manager, Reseller, and Super User can read it in the domains they manage. When you are the user in the path and you are on the meeting, you are checked as yourself, so an attendee from another domain reads the meeting through its own path. `meeting-passcode` is shown only to the meeting's owner, its hosts, and Office Manager or higher for its domain. Everyone else gets it masked with asterisks; `include-secret=yes` does not change that.

The meeting is returned when the user in the path owns it or is on it, or when it is open to anyone with its ID (`meeting-join-require-invite-enabled` is `0`) and not locked. When you read as yourself with a token that can write, the read also joins you: it adds you as an attendee of an open meeting you are not on, adds you as a host of your own meeting when you are missing from its attendees, and with `isInit=1` starts an instance. Reading on behalf of another user never changes the meeting. `attendees` is a JSON-encoded string.

parameters.name: user

The meeting is owned by the user in the path. Creating it also sets up its audio bridge and invites everyone in `attendees` by email. Omitted settings take their defaults: the start is now, the length is 60 minutes, and the participant limit comes from the domain's configuration. The response is the new meeting. When the create has not been applied yet, it holds the fields that were accepted.

put.description:
Changes a meeting's settings, schedule, or attendees. Send only the fields to change.

Only the meeting's owner, its hosts, Office Manager for the meeting's domain, Reseller for its territory, and Super User can change it. Anyone else gets `403`. A host who is not the owner puts its own user in the path.

Some fields act at once: `meeting-lock-enabled` locks or unlocks the meeting for the attendees connected now, `meeting-recording-enabled` starts or stops recording, `meeting-status` `ended` ends the current instance, and `attendees` replaces the attendee list and emails the new attendees. Each change raises `meeting-ordinal-sequence` so calendar invitations update in place. Sending back the masked `meeting-passcode` a read returned leaves the passcode unchanged. A change never moves the meeting to another owner or domain.

`202` means the change is accepted and applied shortly after.

delete.description:
Cancels a meeting, cancels one occurrence of it, removes it for good, or removes some of its attendees. The `type` field in the body chooses which.

Only the meeting's owner, its hosts, Office Manager for the meeting's domain, Reseller for its territory, and Super User can change it. Anyone else gets `403`. A host who is not the owner puts its own user in the path.

- `meeting` marks the meeting cancelled, removes its audio bridge, and emails a cancellation to the attendees. It returns `412` while anyone is connected.
- `instance` cancels one occurrence of a recurring meeting, named by `meeting-instance-schedule-start-datetime`.
- `record` removes the meeting, its attendees, and its audio bridge.
- `attendee` removes the attendees listed in `attendeeids`.

`202` means the delete is accepted and applied shortly after.

Requires Super User scope. Super User Read Only and every other scope get `403`. This path accepts only `POST`; any other method returns `405`.

Counts configuration rows that match the filters. Configurations are the named settings the portal and the API look up at run time, such as `PORTAL_SHOW_SHARED_CONTACTS`. Each row sets one value for one combination of key parts: `reseller`, `domain`, `user`, `user-scope`, `admin-ui-account-type`, and `core-server`. A key part of `*` matches everything, so the row with every key part `*` is the system value.

The count is confined like `GET /configurations`: Super User and Super User Read Only count every row, Reseller its territory's rows, its domains' rows, and system rows, Office Manager its own domain's rows and system rows, and other scopes the rows for their own domain, user, and scope.

Unlike the list, a key part you leave out matches every value, and rows are not collapsed to one per name. With no filters this counts every row you can read, at every tier. `config-name` takes one name, a pattern with `*`, or a comma-separated list, and defaults to `*`. A `reseller` or `domain` that does not exist returns `403`.

parameters.name: reseller
parameters.description: Counts rows for this territory, such as `example-reseller`. A territory that does not exist returns `403`.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Counts rows for this domain, such as `example.com`. A domain that does not exist returns `403`.

parameters.name: user
parameters.description: Counts rows for this user (extension), such as `1001`.

parameters.name: include_wildcards
parameters.description: `true` also counts rows with `*` in each key part you sent. Defaults to `true` for one exact `config-name` and `false` otherwise.

parameters.name: config-name
parameters.description: Name to count, such as `PORTAL_SHOW_SHARED_CONTACTS`. `*` matches any run of characters, and a comma-separated list counts each name. Defaults to `*`.

parameters.name: user-scope
parameters.description: Counts rows for this user scope, such as `Office Manager`. Scopes below Office Manager may send only their own.

parameters.name: admin-ui-account-type
parameters.description: Counts rows for this login type, such as `Domain` or `Subscriber`.

parameters.name: core-server
parameters.description: Counts rows for this core server, such as `core1.example.com`.

200.description: The number of matching rows.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired, or invalid. Get a new token and retry.

403.description: `Reseller not found or access denied` or `Domain not found or access denied`: the `reseller` or `domain` you named does not exist. Check the name. `Invalid Scope`: you sent a `user-scope` other than your own. Your scope may also lack access to configurations.

get.description:
Lists configuration rows. Configurations are the named settings the portal and the API look up at run time, such as `PORTAL_SHOW_SHARED_CONTACTS`. Each row sets one value for one combination of key parts: `reseller`, `domain`, `user`, `user-scope`, `admin-ui-account-type`, and `core-server`. A key part of `*` matches everything, so the row with every key part `*` is the system value.

Every scope reads its own tiers and the system rows, never another tenant's:

- Super User and Super User Read Only read every row.
- Reseller reads its territory's rows, rows of domains in its territory, and system rows.
- Office Manager reads its own domain's rows and system rows.
- Other scopes read the rows for their own domain, user, and scope, and system rows. Sending a `user-scope` other than your own returns `403`.

Values of secret-named settings are masked, as `/nmsconfig` masks them: a name containing a secret keyword (`password`, `key`, `token`, `secret`, and others), less the names in the `NsConfigurationMaskExempt` setting, has its value masked unless the value is shorter than `NsConfigurationMaskMinLength` (default `4`) or a plain switch (`yes`, `no`, `true`, `false`, `on`, `off`, `enabled`, `disabled`). A Super User can send `include-secrets=yes` to get them in clear; any other scope that sends it gets `403`.

How the filters work:

- `config-name` takes one name, a pattern with `*`, or a comma-separated list. It defaults to `*`.
- Each key part you send matches that value. Each key part you leave out matches only `*`, so with no filters the list holds the system rows.
- For one exact `config-name`, rows with `*` in a key part you sent match too, and the most specific row comes first. That row is the value that applies in that context. `include_wildcards` turns this on or off.
- The result has one row per config name.

Rows are paged with `start` and `limit`, which defaults to `100`. No match returns an empty array. `GET /configurations/count` counts differently: a key part it is not sent matches every value. To see what each setting means, call `GET /config-definitions`.

parameters.name: config-name
parameters.description: Name to return, such as `PORTAL_SHOW_SHARED_CONTACTS`. `*` matches any run of characters (`PORTAL_CONTACTS_*`), and a comma-separated list returns each name. Defaults to `*`.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Returns rows for this domain, such as `example.com`. Left out, only rows whose `domain` is `*` match.

parameters.name: reseller
parameters.description: Returns rows for this territory, such as `example-reseller`. Left out, only rows whose `reseller` is `*` match.

parameters.name: user
parameters.description: Returns rows for this user (extension), such as `1001`. Left out, only rows whose `user` is `*` match.

parameters.name: user-scope
parameters.description: Returns rows for this user scope, such as `Office Manager`. Scopes below Office Manager may send only their own. Left out, only rows whose `user-scope` is `*` match.

parameters.name: admin-ui-account-type
parameters.description: Returns rows for this login type, such as `Domain` or `Subscriber`. Left out, only rows whose `admin-ui-account-type` is `*` match.

parameters.name: core-server
parameters.description: Returns rows for this core server, such as `core1.example.com`. Left out, only rows whose `core-server` is `*` match.

parameters.name: include_wildcards
parameters.description: `true` also matches rows with `*` in each key part you sent. Defaults to `true` for one exact `config-name` and `false` for a pattern or list.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: Returns rows where the name, value, `reseller`, `domain`, `user-scope`, `user`, or `admin-ui-account-type` contains this text. With a `*` or list `config-name`, replaces the name filter.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Number of records to skip before the first one returned. Defaults to `0`. Use it with `limit` to page.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Most rows to return. Defaults to `100`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort order: comma-separated column names, each optionally followed by `asc` or `desc`. Columns: `config_name`, `config_value`, `description`, `reseller`, `domain`, `user`, `role`, `login_type`, and `hostname`. Anything else returns `400`. With no `sort`, the most specific rows come first.

parameters.name: include-secrets
parameters.description: `yes` returns secret-named values in clear. Super User only; any other scope that sends `yes` gets `403`. Defaults to `no`.

200.description: The matching rows, one per config name. No match returns an empty array.

example.description: Show shared contacts to every user

400.description: `Bad request. sort must be a comma-separated list of "<column> [asc|desc]", column one of: ...`: use a listed column. `Bad request. Invalid field name requested: <field>`: `fields` named something other than a column.

403.description: Your scope cannot read configurations. `Invalid Scope`: you sent a `user-scope` other than your own; leave it out. `Forbidden. include-secrets=yes requires the 'Super User' scope.`: leave `include-secrets` out.

post.description:
Creates a configuration row: one value for one combination of key parts. Each key part you leave out is `*`, except that below Reseller your own domain and user fill in. Configurations are the named settings the portal and the API look up at run time, such as `PORTAL_SHOW_SHARED_CONTACTS`. Each row sets one value for one combination of key parts: `reseller`, `domain`, `user`, `user-scope`, `admin-ui-account-type`, and `core-server`. A key part of `*` matches everything, so the row with every key part `*` is the system value.

Who can write:

- Super User writes any row, including system rows, for any name.
- Reseller writes rows for its own territory or a domain in it. With neither `reseller` nor `domain`, the row is stored for your territory.
- Office Manager and Route Manager write their own domain's rows. `domain` left out means your domain.
- Other scopes with write rights write only their own user's rows in their own domain. `user` and `domain` left out mean yours.
- Super User Read Only, Route Manager Reseller, Call Center Supervisor, Site Manager, and Office Manager Read-Only are read-only and get `403`.

Below Super User, the setting must have a definition whose `config-def-allow-reseller-access` is `yes`. A key outside your tier returns `403`.

`config-name` takes letters, digits, and `@ . - _ '`; `*` returns `400`. `config-value` is stored as a string and is not checked against the definition's `data-type`. A row with the same key returns `409`; change it with `PUT /configurations/{config-name}`. A masked value for a secret-named setting returns `400`: send the real value.

The row is checked, then published over the service bus (SBUS) and applied on every server shortly after, so `202` means accepted, not yet stored. Send `domain`, `reseller`, and `user` in the body: in the query string they're ignored.

value.description: Hide shared contacts in this domain

2.description: A Reseller: one domain in its territory gets a different value.

202.description: The change passed every check and was published over the service bus (SBUS); it is applied on every server shortly after: `{"code": 202, "message": "Accepted"}`. Read the row back to confirm it.

400.description: The row was refused before anything was published. `Bad request. Missing parameter 'config-name'.`: send it. `Bad request. config-name may contain only letters, digits and @ . - _ '`: rename it. `Cannot save a masked value for new sensitive configuration '<name>'; provide the real value.` `Bad request. Domain does not belong to reseller`: a Reseller named a domain outside its territory. `Bad request. Config definition does not exist` or `Bad request. Config definition does not allow reseller access`: below Super User, only settings a definition opens to resellers can be set. `Service bus communication error`: the change could not be published; retry.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired, or invalid. Get a new token and retry.

403.description: The write was refused before anything was published. `Forbidden. This scope may not change configurations.`: your scope is read-only here. `Forbidden. Reseller does not match the token.`, `Forbidden. Domain does not match the token.`, or `Forbidden. User does not match the token.`: the key names a tier outside yours; send your own or leave it out.

409.description: `Config params already exists`: a row with this name and key parts exists. Change it with `PUT /configurations/{config-name}`.
