get.description:
Lists the settings in the API and portal config files. Config file settings are the entries in each server's API and portal config files: `/etc/netsapiens/api_config.php` (`config-type` `api`) and `/etc/netsapiens/portal_config.php` (`portal`). They override the defaults the software ships, per server, and take effect on the next request that server handles.

Requires Super User or Super User Read Only scope. A request from the server itself (localhost) may read without a token. Every other scope gets `403`.

Send `include-api=true`, `include-portals=true`, or both: with neither, the list is empty. By default only the answering server's files are read. `local-only=false` also asks every other server, with your token, and adds their settings; each row names its server in `config-server`. A server that cannot be read is left out and named in a `Warning` response header.

Values of settings whose names contain a secret keyword (`password`, `secret`, `key`, `token`, `smtp`, and others) are masked for every scope, Super User included. Settings with a string, number, boolean, or array value are listed; one set by an expression is not.

parameters.name: local-only
parameters.description: `false` also reads every other server's files. Defaults to `true`.

parameters.name: include-api
parameters.description: `true` reads `/etc/netsapiens/api_config.php`. Defaults to `false`.

parameters.name: include-portals
parameters.description: `true` reads the portal config file. Defaults to `false`.

200.description: The settings, from every file and server read. Empty when neither `include-api` nor `include-portals` is sent. A server that could not be read is named in a `Warning: 299` header.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired, or invalid. Get a new token and retry.

403.description: `Forbidden. Super User scope required.`: only Super User and Super User Read Only can read config files.

post.description:
Sets a setting in a server's API or portal config file, adding it when the file does not have it. Config file settings are the entries in each server's API and portal config files: `/etc/netsapiens/api_config.php` (`config-type` `api`) and `/etc/netsapiens/portal_config.php` (`portal`). They override the defaults the software ships, per server, and take effect on the next request that server handles.

Requires Super User scope, with a token. Every other scope gets `403`.

`config-name`, `config-value`, and `config-type` are required. POST and PUT do the same thing (see `PUT /nsconfigs`). `config-comment` left out keeps the existing comment.

`config-server` picks where the change goes: left out or this server's hostname changes this server, another cluster server's hostname changes only that server, and `geo` changes this server and then every other server. Any other value returns `404`. Other servers are reached from this one with your token.

The file is edited under a lock, checked, and replaced in one step. Nothing is written when the setting shares its line with other code, when the edit would drop the opening `<?php` tag or change any other setting (`409`), or when the result would not parse (`500`).

`202` means this server's file was written, where this server is a target. A server that could not be reached or refused the change is listed in `warnings`, and the answer is still `202`: check `warnings`, or read back with `GET /nsconfigs?local-only=false`.

`config-value-type` decides how the value is written: `string` (the default), `boolean`, `integer`, `float`, or `array`. Send `boolean` for an on/off setting, since the string `false` counts as true. A masked value from `GET /nsconfigs`, sent back unchanged, keeps the stored value; a mask sent for a new secret-named setting returns `400`.

202.description: The change was applied to this server's file where it was a target: `{"code": 202, "message": "Accepted"}`. Servers that failed are listed in `warnings`.

warnings: Not applied on unreachable or refusing server(s): core2.example.com (unreachable: Connection timed out after 3001 milliseconds)

400.description: Nothing was written. `config_name is required`, `config_name must be 128 characters or fewer`, or `config_name must be a PHP identifier or dot-delimited path ...`: fix the name. `config_type must be "api" or "portal"`. `config-value-type must be one of: ...`, `config_value is required`, or a `config_value ...` message: send a value that matches `config-value-type`. `config_comment must ...`: shorten the comment, and remove line breaks, control characters, `?>`, and `<?`. `Cannot save a masked value for new sensitive config '<name>'; provide the real value.` `Config file not found`: the file is missing on this server.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired, or invalid. Get a new token and retry.

403.description: `Forbidden. Super User scope required.`: only a Super User can change config files.

404.description: `Unknown server: config-server must be 'geo' or a server in this cluster`: send `geo`, this server's hostname, or a hostname from `GET /nsconfigs?servers-only=yes`. Nothing was written.

409.description: `Config file not changed: <path>. ...`: nothing was written. The setting shares its line with other code (`... shares its line with other code; move it to its own line by hand before editing it here`), or the edit would have removed the file's opening `<?php` tag or changed another setting. Fix the file by hand, then retry.

500.description: Nothing was written. `Config file is not writable: <path>`: the file's permissions are wrong; the package sets it to `netsapiens:www-data`, mode 664. `Config file write failed: <path>. ...`: the file could not be locked, read, or replaced, or the result would not parse (`Refusing to write ...: the result would not parse`). Fix the file, then retry.

- `yes`: every expected server answered and all hold the key with the same value. Compare `config-servers-reporting` with `config-servers-expected`. A cluster whose inventory holds exactly one server gives `yes` when that server answers.
- `no`: the values differ, or some servers hold the key and others do not, and the difference is visible in this response. A deliberate `config-server` override looks the same as drift.
- `unknown`: agreement cannot be shown. A server did not answer, `local-only=yes` was sent, an inventory entry is not a valid hostname, the values are masked, one server masked the value and another did not, the values differ only as text (`1.10` and `1.1`), or a key is missing from a server whose page was full or started past `start=0`.

`include-secrets=yes` compares the stored values instead of masks, so masked keys get a definite answer.

**Values whose key looks like a credential are masked.** The key name is the only signal, so any key containing `password`, `secret`, `key`, `token`, `auth`, `smtp`, `license`, `cert`, or a similar keyword is masked and carries `config-value-redacted: yes`. Each server masks its own rows with its own settings.

`config-value` is returned exactly as stored, so a leading or trailing zero survives.

To see which servers answered and how many keys each disagrees on, call `GET /nmsconfig/servers`.

The check reads the server that takes the request, so it is a safeguard, not a lock.

`config-name` and `config-value` are both required. A mask-shaped `config-value` (`****` or `Ex****01`) on a credential-shaped key returns `400` for a new key, since there is no stored value to keep; over an existing key with `overwrite=yes` it is dropped, and the answer is `202` with nothing changed.

Requires Super User or Super User Read Only. `include-secrets=yes` requires Super User.

post.description:
Creates a configuration definition. A configuration definition describes one setting: what it controls, its `default` value, its `data-type`, the release it first applies to, and whether a Reseller may set it. Configuration rows (`/configurations`) then set values for it at each tier.

Requires Super User scope. Every other scope gets `403`.

`config-name`, `description`, `default`, `code-version`, and `data-type` are required. `config-name` takes letters, digits, and `@ . - _ '`. `config-def-allow-reseller-access` and `config-def-allow-hostname` take `yes` or `no` and default to `yes`; the scope-specific defaults default to empty. A name that already has a definition returns `409`. A masked default value for a secret-named setting returns `400`.

Definitions the platform ships are reloaded from its master list on every upgrade, which resets their fields; a definition you create keeps its values. The definition is published over the service bus (SBUS) and applied on every server shortly after, so `202` means accepted, not yet stored.

example.description: Show shared contacts to every user

202.description: The change passed every check and was published over the service bus (SBUS); it is applied on every server shortly after: `{"code": 202, "message": "Accepted"}`. Read the row back to confirm it.

400.description: Nothing was published. `Bad request. Missing parameter '<field>'.`: send `config-name`, `description`, `code-version`, `data-type`, and `default`. `Bad request. config-name must be 1-128 characters: letters, digits and @ . - _ '`. `Bad request. <flag> must be yes or no`. `Bad request. <field> must be <n> characters or fewer` or `... must be a string`. `Cannot save a masked <column> for new sensitive definition '<name>'; provide the real value.` `Service bus communication error`: retry.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired, or invalid. Get a new token and retry.

403.description: `Forbidden. Super User scope required.`: only a Super User can change configuration definitions.

409.description: `Config definition already exists`: the name has a definition. Change it with `PUT /config-definitions/{config-name}`.

A definition the platform ships comes back on the next upgrade; its configuration rows do not. The deletes are published over the service bus (SBUS) and applied on every server shortly after, so `202` means accepted.

An image that applies to every reseller and every domain (`reseller` and `domain` both `*`) is platform-wide, and only a Super User can create, change, or delete it. Other scopes get `403`.

If an image already exists under this name for the same reseller, domain, and server, the request returns `400`; replace it with `PUT /images/{filename}`.

delete.description:
Deletes one stored template.

Requires Super User or Reseller scope. A Reseller can manage templates stored for its own reseller or for a domain in it. A template that applies to every reseller and every domain (`reseller` and `domain` both `*`) is platform-wide, and only a Super User can create, change, or delete it. Other scopes get `403`.

A template is stored per reseller, domain, and server, and each defaults to `*`, meaning all. The values are matched exactly here: a template stored for every domain is not found when you name one domain. Name the reseller and domain in the request body; query-string values for them are ignored. With no body, the request targets the platform-wide template, which only a Super User can delete. An image stored under the same name is not deleted here.

When a reseller or domain copy is deleted, emails fall back to the next most specific copy, usually the platform-wide one. The request returns `202`: the template is removed shortly after.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: Name the template is stored under, such as `welcome_email.php`. Letters, digits, `-`, `.`, and `_` only. The name is matched exactly. Email templates use the fixed names the platform looks up, such as `welcome_email.php`, `password_reset_email.php`, or `email_vmail_link.php`; the fax cover letter is `fax_cover_letter.docx`. A language copy adds `_` and the user's language code before `.php`.

202.description: Accepted. The template is removed shortly after.

400.description: The file stored under this name is an image, not a template (`Incorrect file type for template operation.`), the JSON body is malformed, or the change could not be accepted right now (retry).

401.description: The access token is missing, expired, or invalid. Get a new token and retry.

403.description: Your scope cannot manage templates, the reseller or domain is outside your reseller, or the template is platform-wide and you are not a Super User.

example.message: Forbidden. Only a Super User can change a platform-wide file.

404.description: No template is stored under this name for exactly this reseller, domain, and server (`File does not exist.`). Check the body values; omitted values mean `*`.

Use `/domains/{domain}/users/{user}/timeframes/count` for one user's time frames, or `GET /domains/{domain}/timeframes?users=all` for a per-user count.

Requires the `list` privilege on time frames, which Basic User, Site Manager, and Office Manager hold in their domain, and Reseller and Super User more widely. The owner must be one you can reach, or the call returns `403`.

Returns the name and state of each shared time frame of the domain: whether an answer rule uses it (`selected`) and whether every range in it is in the past (`expired`). Requires the `list` privilege on time frames, which Basic User, Site Manager, and Office Manager hold in their domain, and Reseller and Super User more widely. get.description:
Returns the domain's shared time frames with their entries. Answer rules of every user in the domain can use them.

Any Basic User, Site Manager, or Office Manager in the domain can read its shared time frames. A Reseller can read the domains in its territory, and a Super User any domain.

Each time frame carries its date ranges, days of week entry, or holidays, with the next dates it applies (`timeframe-next-observance-datetime`) and `end_on`. Page with `limit` and `start`; `limit` defaults to `100`. Time frames created before IDs existed are converted on the fly and added after the page. A domain with no time frames returns `[]`.

`GET /domains/{domain}/timeframes/list` returns only names and state, and `GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/timeframes` returns a user's own time frames.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Most time frames to return, a whole number. Defaults to `100`. Anything but digits returns `400`. Legacy time frames that have no ID yet are added after the page, whatever the limit.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Time frames to skip before the first one returned, a whole number. Defaults to `0`. Anything but digits returns `400`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Order of the result. `name asc|desc` orders by `timeframe-name`. `ends_on asc|desc` orders by `end_on`, time frames that never end last in ascending order, and also orders each time frame's entries by recurrence end date. The `user`, `user_name`, and `owner` values order the per-user rows of `users=all`. Any other value returns `400`.

parameters.name: order
parameters.description: Storage order of the time frames before paging: comma-separated `id`, `domain`, `user`, `name`, or `type`, each optionally followed by `asc` or `desc`. Any other value returns `400`. Use `sort` to order the result.

parameters.name: users
parameters.description: `all` returns, instead of the time frames, one row per user of the domain with how many time frames it owns (`time_frame` `all`, `domain`, `user`, `count`, `user_name`), the domain's shared row first. Requires Office Manager, Call Center Supervisor, Site Manager (its own site's users only), Reseller, or Super User; others get `403`. Sort those rows with `sort=user asc|desc` or `user_name asc|desc`.

post.description:
Creates a time frame owned by the domain, shared by every user in it, of the type `timeframe-type` names. Answer rules use it by `timeframe-name`.

Requires Site Manager, Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User. A Basic User can read shared time frames but gets `403` on a write.

The write is published over the service bus (SBUS) and applied a moment later, so the call answers `202` by default. Send `synchronous=yes` to wait up to 10 seconds and get `200` with the time frame instead. The time frame ID is generated from the name and owner, so you do not send one; it is `timeframe-id` in the response.

**Always.** Matches at every moment and has no entries. The call waits about 2 seconds and always answers `200` with the time frame.

**Days of week.** One weekly schedule in `timeframe-days-of-week-array`, with up to 2 periods per day as `hhmm` times. The array is required and holds at most 1 entry. `timeframe-recurrence-type` is `weekly`, or `custom` with the custom interval fields.

**Specific dates.** Date ranges in `timeframe-specific-dates-array`, each with begin and end dates as `YYYYMMDD` and times as `hhmm`. With more than 1 range, all must share one recurrence type, `annual-month-day` or `doesNotRecur`.

**Holiday.** Holidays in `timeframe-holiday-array`, copied from `GET /holidays/{country}/{year}` or `GET /holidays/{country}/{region}/{year}`. Every holiday needs `timeframe-holiday-begin-date` and a `timeframe-recurrence-type`, `never` or `yearlyOnHoliday`, and all must share it. A holiday may appear once. A holiday whose date has already passed answers `422` and nothing is created.

**Custom.** Any mix of the three arrays, without the single-entry and shared-recurrence rules.

Every entry is checked before anything is published, so a `400` or `422` creates nothing. A name the owner already uses returns `400`, and a user that does not exist returns `400` with `Invalid user/domain.` Add entries later with `POST` on the time frame, and change or convert it with `PUT`.

parameters.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

1.description: A time frame that always matches. The call waits about 2 seconds and returns it.

2.description: Weekdays 8:00 to 17:00, waiting for the result.

3.description: December 24 to 26 every year, waiting for the result.

4.description: Thanksgiving Day every year, waiting for the result.

5.description: A date range, a weekly schedule, and a holiday in one time frame, waiting for the result.

6.description: The same days of week create without `synchronous`. The call answers `202` as soon as the change is published.

202.description: The time frame was published and is being applied. Read it with `GET` on the collection, or send `synchronous=yes` next time.

Returns one shared time frame of the domain, by ID or by name.

Any Basic User, Site Manager, or Office Manager in the domain can read its shared time frames. A Reseller can read the domains in its territory, and a Super User any domain.

By ID you get the time frame with its entries. By name you get the legacy view: the time ranges generated for it, the shape answer rules were first built on. Prefer the ID. An unknown ID or name returns `404`.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description:

- a time frame ID, 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters, such as `94d4b86a0e8bedd0bb61feaa0aa0a4db`. Take it from `timeframe-id`
- a time frame name, such as `Business Hours`. Anything that is not 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters is read as a name

An ID returns the time frame with its entries (`RecurringTimeframe`). A name returns the legacy view of the same time frame: its generated time ranges, in the `Timeframe` shape. A time frame whose name is itself 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters can be reached only by ID.

200.description: The time frame. `RecurringTimeframe` by ID, `Timeframe` by name.

400.description: A query option is invalid: `order`, `sort`, `limit`, or `start` outside its allowed values, or a `uid` that does not match the path (message `'uid' does not match the path.`). The message says what to correct.

post.summary: Add entries to domain time frame
post.description:
Adds entries to an existing time frame: date ranges, holidays, or, for a custom time frame, any of the three. Requires Site Manager, Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User. A Basic User can read shared time frames but gets `403` on a write.

The write is published over the service bus (SBUS) and applied a moment later, so the call answers `202` by default. Send `synchronous=yes` to wait up to 10 seconds and get `200` with the time frame instead. Entry IDs are generated; do not send `timeframe-id`.

**Specific dates.** New ranges must use the recurrence type the time frame already uses, `annual-month-day` or `doesNotRecur`.

**Holiday.** New holidays must use the time frame's recurrence type and must not repeat one already there. A holiday whose date has passed answers `422` and nothing is added.

**Days of week.** A days of week time frame holds 1 entry; once it has one, this returns `400`. Change it with `PUT`.

**Custom.** Any of the three arrays.

Every entry is checked before anything is published. An ID that does not exist, or that belongs to another owner than the path, returns `404` with `Provided 'id' does not exist.`

422.description: A holiday has a date that has already passed. Nothing was added. Send a future occurrence of the holiday.

put.description:
Changes a time frame: converts its type, updates some entries, or replaces them all. Requires Site Manager, Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User. A Basic User can read shared time frames but gets `403` on a write.

The call waits up to 10 seconds for the change and answers `200` with the time frame, except a type conversion, which answers `202` as soon as it is published.

**Convert type.** Send `timeframe-type` with a type other than the current one. Converting to `custom` keeps every entry; converting an `always` time frame to `custom` removes its all-day range, so it starts empty. Converting to any other type deletes every entry; send the new type's array in the same request to fill it. A `custom` time frame cannot be converted, and the request is treated as an update.

**Update entries.** Send `update-only=yes` with the entries to change, each with its `timeframe-id`. An entry without an ID is created. Nothing is deleted. For a holiday, only its hours, observance options, workweek, and recurrence change; delete it and add the new one to change the holiday itself.

**Replace entries.** Without `update-only`, every entry you do not list by `timeframe-id` is deleted, including every entry of a kind whose array you leave out. Listed entries are updated, and entries without an ID are created.

**Days of week.** A days of week time frame holds 1 entry: send exactly 1. More than 1 returns `400`.

The name cannot be changed. An always time frame has nothing to update; sending `timeframe-type=always` to one does nothing and answers `202`.

Every entry is checked before anything is published, so a `400` changes nothing. An ID that does not exist, or that belongs to another owner than the path, returns `404`. A holiday date that has already passed returns `400`.

- a time frame name, such as `Business Hours`. Anything that is not 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters is read as a name

4.description: Shortens the hours of one holiday and leaves the others.

5.description: Keeps the date range and weekly schedule of a custom time frame, by `timeframe-id`, and deletes its holiday.

Adds entries to an existing time frame: date ranges, holidays, or, for a custom time frame, any of the three. Requires Basic User for your own time frames, or Site Manager, Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User for the users you administer. An Office Manager can change any user in its domain, and a Site Manager any user in its own site. A user outside your reach returns `403` with `Issue with timeframe access`.

The write is published over the service bus (SBUS) and applied a moment later, so the call answers `202` by default. Send `synchronous=yes` to wait up to 10 seconds and get `200` with the time frame instead. Entry IDs are generated; do not send `timeframe-id`.

**Holiday.** New holidays must use the time frame's recurrence type and must not repeat one already there. A holiday whose date has passed answers `422` and nothing is added.

**Days of week.** A days of week time frame holds 1 entry; once it has one, this returns `400`. Change it with `PUT`.

**Custom.** Any of the three arrays.

Every entry is checked before anything is published. An ID that does not exist, or that belongs to another owner than the path, returns `404` with `Provided 'id' does not exist.`

put.description:
Changes a time frame: converts its type, updates some entries, or replaces them all. Requires Basic User for your own time frames, or Site Manager, Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User for the users you administer. An Office Manager can change any user in its domain, and a Site Manager any user in its own site. A user outside your reach returns `403` with `Issue with timeframe access`.

The call waits up to 10 seconds for the change and answers `200` with the time frame, except a type conversion, which answers `202` as soon as it is published.

**Convert type.** Send `timeframe-type` with a type other than the current one. Converting to `custom` keeps every entry; converting an `always` time frame to `custom` removes its all-day range, so it starts empty. Converting to any other type deletes every entry; send the new type's array in the same request to fill it. A `custom` time frame cannot be converted, and the request is treated as an update.

**Update entries.** Send `update-only=yes` with the entries to change, each with its `timeframe-id`. An entry without an ID is created. Nothing is deleted. For a holiday, only its hours, observance options, workweek, and recurrence change; delete it and add the new one to change the holiday itself.

**Replace entries.** Without `update-only`, every entry you do not list by `timeframe-id` is deleted, including every entry of a kind whose array you leave out. Listed entries are updated, and entries without an ID are created.

**Days of week.** A days of week time frame holds 1 entry: send exactly 1. More than 1 returns `400`.

The name cannot be changed. An always time frame has nothing to update; sending `timeframe-type=always` to one does nothing and answers `202`.

Every entry is checked before anything is published, so a `400` changes nothing. An ID that does not exist, or that belongs to another owner than the path, returns `404`. A holiday date that has already passed returns `400`.

Requires Basic User for your own time frames, or Site Manager, Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User for the users you administer. An Office Manager can delete for any user in its domain, and a Site Manager for any user in its own site. A user outside your reach returns `403` with `Issue with timeframe access`.

A file that already exists is refused with `409`; replace it with `PUT /firebase/{filename}`.

post.description:
Requests a Let's Encrypt certificate for a hostname. The certificate manager places the order, proves control of each name with the chosen challenge, installs the certificate, and renews it before it expires.

Requires Super User or Reseller scope. A Reseller creates certificates for its own territory only: `reseller` is set to the token's territory, and `default-ssl-cert` can't be `yes`. A Super User who leaves out `reseller` creates a system-level certificate, owned by `*`.

get.description:
Checks whether each hostname can take a new certificate and points at this cluster. Run it before `POST /certificates`: a certificate whose hostname points elsewhere is accepted, then fails its challenge minutes later. Nothing is written.

Requires Super User, Super User Read Only, or Reseller scope.

Each hostname gets these checks, in order:

1. **Availability.** The name is not already a certificate's common name and, for a Reseller, is not covered by another owner's certificate. These are the two `409` cases of `POST /certificates`.
2. **Endpoints server check.** With `replicate=ndp` only, the host must answer as an Endpoints server.
3. **DNS.** A CNAME is reported for information. The address checked is the first A record, or the first AAAA record when there is no A record.
4. **Cluster membership.** The certificate manager confirms that the address is on its allowlist of this cluster's servers.

Every verdict is a `200`, with one row per hostname, so one bad alternative name does not cost you the verdicts on the others. `in-cluster` is `unknown` when the certificate manager could not be reached: the check went unanswered, so there is no DNS record to fix.

Wildcard names are not resolved, so `resolves` is `not-applicable`. A wildcard certificate is proven by a `dns-01` challenge against the parent zone. The availability check still runs.

delete.description:
Removes a NetSapiens apt repository version from one server, then runs `apt update`. Installed packages stay installed.

Requires Super User scope.

The response streams plain text: a `Repo <version> removed successfully` line, then the `apt update` output. A failed apt run still answers `200`: read the last line. If the removal fails after the stream has started, the text ends with `Failed to remove repository` instead.

When it names a server other than the one you called, the request is forwarded there with your token.

parameters.name: ticket
parameters.description: Ticket number to record with this change in the audit log. get.description:
Returns a time series for one iNSight metric, such as active calls or registered devices, for a window that ends now. Requires Super User, Super User Read Only, or Reseller scope.

A Super User reads the whole platform. A Reseller always reads its own territory, and only the labels with a reseller form: `core_activecalls`, `core_domains`, `core_subscribers`, and `core_registered`. Any other label returns `403` for a Reseller, except the `nodeping_` health-check labels. A Super User Read Only token must name a `reseller`.

Set the window with `range`, or with `start` and `end` as Unix timestamps. `step` sets the interval between points. Times in the response are Unix timestamps in seconds, not RFC 3339. A window with no data returns `404`.

The alert labels `active_alerts`, `alert_groups`, `alert_silences`, `ruler_alerts`, and `ruler_rules` need Super User or Super User Read Only scope, ignore the window parameters, and answer an alert envelope instead of a series. See `GET /insight/active_alerts`. `ruler_rules` also takes `type`, `rule_name`, `rule_group`, and `file`.

parameters.name: label
parameters.description: The metric to read. One of `core_activecalls`, `core_domains`, `core_subscribers`, `core_registered`, `node_load5`, `node_load5_max`, `alerts`, `nsnode_sockets`, `system_packet_dispatched_total`, `sip_invite_received_total`, `sbus_system_queued`, `netsapiens_email_smtp_requests`, and the `nsmatrix_` labels `nsmatrix_primaries`, `nsmatrix_tuwunel_up`, `nsmatrix_primary_row_consistent`, `nsmatrix_inbound_events`, `nsmatrix_rooms_created`, `nsmatrix_homeserver_errors`, and `nsmatrix_detached_job_failures`. Any name that starts with `nodeping_` reads that health-check series. `custom` runs your own query, sent in `query`. The alert labels `active_alerts`, `alert_groups`, `alert_silences`, `ruler_alerts`, and `ruler_rules` return the alert envelope described on `GET /insight/active_alerts` instead of a series. Any other name returns `400`. A `nodeping_` label must be `nodeping_` followed by letters, digits, `_`, and `:` only.

parameters.name: range
parameters.description: How far back to read, ending now. A named range (`last_hour`, `last_6_hours`, `last_12_hours`, `last_24_hours`, `last_2_days`, `last_7_days`, or `last_28_days`) or a number followed by `m`, `h`, or `d`, such as `90m`, `24h`, or `3d`. A number with no unit is hours. Defaults to `last_24_hours`. The range also sets the default `step`: `1m` up to 1 day, `10m` up to 3 days, `1h` up to 14 days, and `1d` beyond. `last_7_days` uses `1h` and `last_28_days` uses `1d`.

parameters.name: aggregated
parameters.description: `aggregated`, the default, returns one series for the whole platform. `server` returns one series per server, each row naming its `server`. Not every label has a per-server form; one without it returns `400`. Ignored when the request is answered for a reseller.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: The start of the window, as a Unix timestamp in seconds. Overrides the start that `range` sets. Not an RFC 3339 date-time.

parameters.name: end
parameters.description: The end of the window, as a Unix timestamp in seconds. Overrides the end that `range` sets, which is now, rounded down to the step.

parameters.name: step
parameters.description: The interval between points: a number and one unit, `ms`, `s`, `m`, `h`, `d`, or `w`, such as `30s`, `10m`, `1h`, or `1d`. Overrides the step that `range` sets. Any other value returns `400`.

parameters.name: reseller
parameters.description: The reseller (territory) to read. A Reseller token always reads its own territory, and naming another one returns `403`; you can leave it out. A Super User or Super User Read Only token that names a reseller gets that reseller's series. Only `core_activecalls`, `core_domains`, `core_subscribers`, and `core_registered` have a reseller form; any other label returns `403`. A quote, backslash, brace, or line break in it returns `400`.

parameters.name: transport
parameters.description: For `nodeping_` labels only: return only the checks over this transport. One of `udp`, `tcp`, `tls`, `ws`, `wss`, `http`, and `https`, in any letter case. Any other value returns `400`.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: For `custom` only, and required there: the query to run, in the metrics service's query language. Double quotes are changed to single quotes before it is sent. Needs a platform with iNSight Pro; otherwise `403`.

200.description: The series, as an array of points. Only the first point carries `debug-parameters`.

400.description: The label, `range`, `aggregated`, `step`, `transport`, or `reseller` is not valid, or `custom` was sent without `query`. The message names which: `Invalid Label.`, `Invalid Range.`, `Invalid Aggregated setting.`, `Invalid step. Use a duration such as 30s, 5m or 1h.`, `Invalid transport. Use one of: udp, tcp, tls, ws, wss, http, https.`, `Invalid reseller.`, or `Custom query is required.` Correct the request and retry.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired, or invalid. Get a new token and retry.

403.description: Your token cannot read this label. Only Super User, Super User Read Only, and Reseller tokens can call this endpoint (`Access Denied` otherwise). A Super User Read Only token must name a `reseller`, and the label must have a reseller form. `custom` needs iNSight Pro on the platform. The message says which.

example.message: Please provide reseller and ensure the label supports reseller scope.

404.description: The query ran but returned no data for the window. The body also carries the `query` that ran. Widen the window or check the label.

example.message: No data found for the specified query.

500.description: The metrics service could not be reached or refused the query, or iNSight is not set up on this platform. The message starts with `Failed to query Prometheus:` or `Prometheus query failed:`. Retry later, or contact support if it persists.

get.description:
Returns the alerts currently firing on the platform, as the iNSight alerting service reports them. Requires Super User or Super User Read Only scope; alerts are platform-wide and are not filtered by reseller.

The service's answer is passed through unchanged in `data`, wrapped with `status`, `source`, `endpoint`, and `count`. Filter with `filter`, `active`, `silenced`, `inhibited`, and `receiver`; any other parameter is ignored. Nothing firing returns `200` with an empty `data`.

This is `GET /insight/{label}` with the label `active_alerts`. The same envelope answers the other alert labels: `alert_groups` (alerts grouped by route), `alert_silences` (silences), `ruler_alerts` and `ruler_rules` (alert rules, with `source` `prometheus` and no `count`). For the number of firing alerts over time, read the `alerts` label as a series.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: Return only alerts that match this label matcher, such as `severity="critical"`. To send several, repeat it as `filter[]`; an alert must match all of them.

parameters.name: active
parameters.description: `true` to include active alerts, `false` to leave them out. Defaults to `true`.

parameters.name: silenced
parameters.description: `true` to include silenced alerts, `false` to leave them out. Defaults to `true`.

parameters.name: inhibited
parameters.description: `true` to include inhibited alerts, `false` to leave them out. Defaults to `true`.

parameters.name: receiver
parameters.description: Return only alerts sent to receivers whose name matches this regular expression.

200.description: The firing alerts, in the alert envelope.

post.description:
Creates a conference bridge in a domain, with the SIP device and dial rule that route calls to it.

Requires Office Manager scope for your own domain, or Reseller or Super User scope. A Basic User, Simple User, Call Center Agent, or Route Manager can create only an owned conference for their own extension.

There are two kinds of conference:

- **owned**, the default: a personal bridge for an existing user. `conference-direct-dial-number` is required, and a dial rule sends that number to the bridge. The conference's key becomes `conference-owner-user`
- **dedicated**: a bridge with its own extension, `conference`. When the extension has no user yet, a system user with an answering rule and a dial rule is created for it

Setting `conference-leader-pin` also requires `conference-participants-pin`, and `conference-require-leader-to-start` requires a leader PIN. Send PINs and the SIP password themselves: a masked value returns `400`.

A `202` means the conference was accepted and is applied shortly after. A conference that already exists, an extension already taken by a user, or a direct-dial number already in use returns `409`. A `conference-sip-uri` or `conference-owner-user-id` in another domain returns `403`.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

202.description: The request was accepted. The change is applied shortly after.

400.description: A required field is missing or a value is invalid: `conference`, `conference-name`, or `conference-owner-user` is empty, a PIN is not up to 6 digits, a PIN or the SIP password is masked, `conference-direct-dial-number` is missing for an owned conference or longer than 6 characters, or `limits-max-participants` is not a number, `-`, or `unlimited`. The message names the problem. A `400` can also mean the conference could not be created; retry the request.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired, or invalid. Get a new token and retry.

403.description: Your scope cannot create this conference. A Basic User, Simple User, Call Center Agent, or Route Manager can create only an owned conference for their own extension in their own domain. A `conference-sip-uri` or `conference-owner-user-id` in another domain is also refused.

404.description: The domain does not exist. Check the domain name, or use `~` for your own domain.

409.description: The conference already exists, the user already has an owned conference, a user already has the dedicated conference's extension, or the direct-dial number is already in use. Choose another extension or number.

get.description:
Lists configuration changes made on the platform, newest first: who made each change, from where, and to which domain, user, and object. With no dates it covers the last 7 days, and it returns up to 100 entries unless you set `limit`.

Requires Reseller, Super User, or Super User Read Only scope. A Reseller sees only entries for domains in its own territory, in the change log and the access log alike, and naming any other domain in `target-domain` returns `403`.

Every filter is an exact match. Dates in the request are converted to UTC from any offset; dates in the response are in UTC. Credentials in `auditlog-details` are shown as `********`.

`event-category` chooses other kinds of entries: `session` returns sign-ins and sign-outs instead of changes, `change,session` returns both, and `access`, `disclosure`, or `all` return entries from the access log, described under `GET /accesslog`.

Send only the filters listed here. A query-builder key such as `OR` or `joins`, or a filter name that is not a plain field name, returns `400`.

parameters.name: datetime-start
parameters.description: Start of the time window, in RFC 3339, such as `2026-09-01T00:00:00+00:00`. An offset or a `[Zone]` suffix is converted to UTC, and `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` is read as UTC. Defaults to 7 days ago.

parameters.name: datetime-end
parameters.description: End of the time window, in the same forms as `datetime-start`. Defaults to now.

parameters.name: by-ip
parameters.description: Only changes made from this IP address.

parameters.name: action-type
parameters.description: Only entries of this kind, such as `create`, `update`, or `delete`, or `login` or `logout` with `event-category=session`.

parameters.name: target-domain
parameters.description: Only entries for this domain. To match any of several domains, repeat it with brackets: `target-domain[]=example.com&target-domain[]=example.net`. A Reseller may name only domains in its own territory.

parameters.name: target-object
parameters.description: Only changes to this kind of object, by the name the entries show, such as `Subscriber` or `Call Queue`.

parameters.name: target-host
parameters.description: Only changes recorded by this server.

parameters.name: target-user
parameters.description: Only changes to this user, by extension, such as `1002`.

parameters.name: by-client
parameters.description: Only changes made through this client, such as `api` or `api-` followed by an OAuth client ID.

parameters.name: by-domain
parameters.description: Only changes made by users of this domain.

parameters.name: by-user
parameters.description: Only changes made by this user, by extension, such as `1001`.

parameters.name: auditlog-details
parameters.description: Only changes whose recorded details contain this text. Applies only when `datetime-start` is also set.

parameters.name: event-category
parameters.description: Kinds of entries to return, as a comma-separated list of `change`, `session`, `access`, and `disclosure`, or `all`. Leave it out for configuration changes alone. `session` alone returns sign-ins and sign-outs. An unrecognized value is ignored.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of records to return. Defaults to `100`. Use it with `start` to page.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Number of records to skip before the first one returned. Defaults to `0`. Use it with `limit` to page.

200.description: The matching entries, newest first. An empty array when none match.

400.description: A date carries a time zone that cannot be converted (`Issue with timezone conversion`), or a filter is not a plain field name. Use an RFC 3339 offset or a valid IANA zone name.

example.message: Bad Request: 'OR' is not accepted as a request filter.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired, or invalid. Get a new token and retry.

403.description: Your scope cannot read the audit log, or `target-domain` names a domain outside your territory (`Domain not found or access denied`). Use a Reseller token for that territory, or a Super User token.

example.message: Domain not found or access denied

get.description:
Returns the compliance log: who signed in, who changed configuration, who read personal data or a credential, and what data left the platform, newest first. Requires Reseller, Super User, or Super User Read Only scope. A Reseller sees only entries about data in the domains of its territory.

**Choose the entries with `event-category`.** Without it you get sign-ins and sign-outs (`session`) from the last 7 days. Send `access`, `disclosure`, or `all` for data reads and disclosures. Sign-in and change entries carry fewer fields: the filters marked "access and disclosure entries only" do not apply to them.

**Two common questions.** "What did this account read" is `by-user` with a date range. "Who read this record" is `record-id` with `target-object`. Add `credential=yes` to see every read that returned a secret.

**Data subjects are listed, not filterable.** Each entry names the people whose data it disclosed in `data-subjects`. To find who accessed data about one person, contact support.

**What counts as a disclosure depends on the regime.** `actor-tier` records where the reader sat relative to the data, and `exclude` removes categories. A HIPAA accounting of disclosures is `exclude=own-organisation`. GDPR excludes nothing.

Access entries are read from at most the 6 most recent months of the date range. Every page you read is itself recorded in the log. `GET /accesslog/count` returns the number of matching entries as `{"total": N}`.

parameters.name: datetime-start
parameters.description: Entries at or after this time, as an RFC 3339 date-time such as `2026-09-01T00:00:00+00:00`. A trailing time zone name in brackets, such as `[America/New_York]`, and `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` in UTC are also accepted. Without it, sign-in and change entries start 7 days ago, and access entries start at the beginning of the month of `datetime-end`.

parameters.name: datetime-end
parameters.description: Entries at or before this time, in the same formats as `datetime-start`. Defaults to now. Access entries are read from at most the 6 most recent months of the range.

parameters.name: by-ip
parameters.description: Entries from this IP address. Exact match.

parameters.name: action-type
parameters.description: Entries with this action, such as `read`, `list`, `search`, `play`, `download`, `export`, `login`, or `logout`. Exact match. `download` and `export` are the disclosure actions.

parameters.name: target-domain
parameters.description: Entries about data in this domain. Repeat the parameter to name several. Every domain named must be inside your scope, or the request returns `403`. A blank value or `*` means no filter.

parameters.name: target-object
parameters.description: Entries about this kind of object. Takes the object name or the display label, so `user` and `Subscriber` match the same entries. Credential reads use the object name, such as `device`, `phoneconfiguration`, or `connection`.

parameters.name: target-host
parameters.description: Entries recorded by this server. Exact match.

parameters.name: target-user
parameters.description: Entries about this person, as a bare extension. Qualify it with `target-domain`.

parameters.name: by-client
parameters.description: Entries from this application. Exact match.

parameters.name: by-domain
parameters.description: Entries where the reader belongs to this domain. It does not widen your scope: entries are still limited to data in domains you manage.

parameters.name: event-category
parameters.description: The kinds of entry to return, separated by commas: `session` (sign-ins and sign-outs), `change` (configuration changes), `access` (reads of personal data or a credential), `disclosure` (data that left the platform on its own, such as a served export file), or `all`. Defaults to `session`. An unrecognized value falls back to the default. Asking for `access` alone leaves out disclosures, and the other way around.

parameters.name: exclude
parameters.description: Leave out entries by the reader's relationship to the data, separated by commas: `own-user` (the reader is the person the data is about), `own-domain` (the reader is in the same domain), `own-organisation` (the same organization; `own-organization` also works), `reseller` (an intermediary), or `platform` (platform staff). Nothing is excluded by default, and an unrecognized value is ignored. Access and disclosure entries only; ignored for sign-in and change entries.

parameters.name: record-id
parameters.description: Entries about this one record, such as a CDR ID or a phone MAC address. Access and disclosure entries only; ignored for sign-in and change entries.

parameters.name: actor-tier
parameters.description: Entries where the reader was in this tier. To leave a tier out instead, use `exclude`. Access and disclosure entries only; ignored for sign-in and change entries.

parameters.name: by-scope
parameters.description: Entries where the reader held this scope, such as `Office Manager`. Access and disclosure entries only; ignored for sign-in and change entries.

parameters.name: schema-version
parameters.description: Entries written under this set of fields, such as `1.1`. Access and disclosure entries only; ignored for sign-in and change entries.

parameters.name: part2-covered
parameters.description: `yes` returns entries where the data was subject to 42 CFR Part 2 when read; `no` returns the rest. `part2` is also accepted as the name. `true`, `1`, and `on` also mean yes; any other value means no. Access and disclosure entries only; ignored for sign-in and change entries.

parameters.name: hipaa-covered
parameters.description: `yes` returns entries where the data was subject to HIPAA when read; `no` returns the rest. `hipaa` is also accepted as the name. `true`, `1`, and `on` also mean yes; any other value means no. Access and disclosure entries only; ignored for sign-in and change entries.

parameters.name: gdpr-covered
parameters.description: `yes` returns entries where the data was subject to GDPR when read; `no` returns the rest. `gdpr` is also accepted as the name. `true`, `1`, and `on` also mean yes; any other value means no. Access and disclosure entries only; ignored for sign-in and change entries.

parameters.name: credential
parameters.description: `yes` returns only entries whose response carried a secret, such as a SIP registration password, a provisioning password, a client secret, or a PIN. `no` returns the rest. `true`, `1`, and `on` also mean yes. Access and disclosure entries only; ignored for sign-in and change entries.

parameters.name: recipient
parameters.description: Entries where the data went to this destination rather than to the reader, such as a scheduled export's host. Access and disclosure entries only; ignored for sign-in and change entries.

parameters.name: by-user
parameters.description: Entries recorded against this reader, as a bare extension. Exact match.

parameters.name: mask-chain
parameters.description: Entries where this account started a masquerade. Access and disclosure entries only; ignored for sign-in and change entries.

parameters.name: ticket-reference
parameters.description: Entries recorded under this support ticket. Access and disclosure entries only; ignored for sign-in and change entries.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most entries to return. Defaults to 100. There is no upper limit. `0` or a negative number returns 1 entry.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Number of records to skip before the first one returned. Defaults to `0`. Use it with `limit` to page.

parameters.name: auditlog-details
parameters.description: Sign-in and change entries only: entries whose details contain this text. Applied only when `datetime-start` is also sent.

200.description: The matching entries, newest first. An empty array when none match. Sign-in and change entries have no `event-category`, `id`, or access fields.

400.description: A query parameter is malformed, such as a `sort` or `fields` value the API cannot parse. The message names the problem. Correct the request and retry.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired, or invalid. Get a new token and retry.

403.description: Your token cannot read the log, or `target-domain` names a domain outside your scope. The message is `Domain not found or access denied` for a domain outside your territory. Use a Reseller, Super User, or Super User Read Only token, and name only domains you manage.

Adds an OIDC provider offered only to this domain. Requires Super User scope. The path sets `domain`. An OIDC provider lets users log in through an external identity provider, such as a company's single sign-on service. A provider with `domain` set to `*` is offered to every domain; one with a domain name only to that domain.

Send `provider-name`, `client-id`, and `client-secret`, and either a `discovery-url` or the endpoints themselves. Check the settings first with `POST /oidc-providers/verify`. A `provider-id` you omit is generated.

The response is `202`: the provider is accepted and applied shortly after. The response has no body; read the new provider's `id` from `GET /oidc-providers`. To add a logo, use `POST /oidc-providers/{provider-id}/logo`.

get.description:
Returns the OIDC providers, in login-page order. An OIDC provider lets users log in through an external identity provider, such as a company's single sign-on service. A provider with `domain` set to `*` is offered to every domain; one with a domain name only to that domain.

Without `domain`, every provider is returned. With it, that domain's providers and the ones offered to every domain. Disabled providers are left out unless you send `include_disabled=yes`.

`client-secret` is never returned. `client-secret-set` says whether one is stored. For what a login page sees, use `GET /oidc-providers/public`.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Return the providers for this domain and the ones offered to every domain. Omit it for every provider.

parameters.name: include_disabled
parameters.description: `yes` includes disabled providers. Only the exact value `yes` works, spelled with an underscore.

200.description: The providers. An empty array when none match.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired, or invalid. Get a new token and retry.

403.description: Your token cannot manage OIDC providers.

post.description:
Adds an OIDC provider. Requires Super User scope. An OIDC provider lets users log in through an external identity provider, such as a company's single sign-on service. A provider with `domain` set to `*` is offered to every domain; one with a domain name only to that domain.

Send `provider-name`, `client-id`, and `client-secret`, and either a `discovery-url` or the endpoints themselves. Check the settings first with `POST /oidc-providers/verify`. A `provider-id` you omit is generated.

The response is `202`: the provider is accepted and applied shortly after. The response has no body; read the new provider's `id` from `GET /oidc-providers`. To add a logo, use `POST /oidc-providers/{provider-id}/logo`.

202.description: The provider is accepted and applied shortly after.

400.description: A required field is missing, or an `allowed-cidrs` entry is not a valid address or range. The message names it. Correct it and retry.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired, or invalid. Get a new token and retry.

403.description: Your token is not Super User. Only Super User can add, change, or delete OIDC providers.

409.description: A provider with this `provider-id` already exists. Choose another, or omit it to have one generated.

500.description: The change could not be published. Retry later.

get.description:
Returns one OIDC provider, disabled or not. An OIDC provider lets users log in through an external identity provider, such as a company's single sign-on service. A provider with `domain` set to `*` is offered to every domain; one with a domain name only to that domain.

`client-secret` is never returned. `client-secret-set` says whether one is stored.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The provider's `id`.

200.description: The provider.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired, or invalid. Get a new token and retry.

403.description: Your token cannot manage OIDC providers.

404.description: No OIDC provider has this `id`. List the providers with `GET /oidc-providers`.

put.description:
Changes an OIDC provider. Requires Super User scope. Send only the fields to change; the stored client secret is kept unless you send a new `client-secret`. Send `allowed-cidrs` as an empty string to show the provider to everyone.

The response is `202`: the change is accepted and applied shortly after.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The provider's `id`.

202.description: The change is accepted and applied shortly after.

400.description: An `allowed-cidrs` entry is not a valid address or range. Correct it and retry.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired, or invalid. Get a new token and retry.

403.description: Your token is not Super User. Only Super User can add, change, or delete OIDC providers.

404.description: No OIDC provider has this `id`. List the providers with `GET /oidc-providers`.

500.description: The change could not be published. Retry later.

delete.description:
Deletes an OIDC provider. Requires Super User scope. Users linked to it for sign-in are unlinked, and its logo goes with it. To stop logins through it without deleting it, set `enabled` to `no` instead.

The response is `202`: the delete is accepted and applied shortly after.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The provider's `id`.

202.description: The delete is accepted and applied shortly after.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired, or invalid. Get a new token and retry.

403.description: Your token is not Super User. Only Super User can add, change, or delete OIDC providers.

404.description: No OIDC provider has this `id`. List the providers with `GET /oidc-providers`.

500.description: The change could not be published. Retry later.

get.summary: List OIDC providers for login page
get.description:
Returns the enabled OIDC providers a login page shows, with only what a button needs. No token is needed.

Send `domain` to get that domain's providers and the ones offered to every domain; without it, every enabled provider. A provider with `allowed-cidrs` is returned only to callers from those addresses. Changes can take up to a minute to appear. Show a logo from `logo-url`.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Return the providers for this domain and the ones offered to every domain. Omit it for every provider.

200.description: The providers, in login-page order. An empty array when none apply.

post.description:
Checks OIDC provider settings without saving them, and returns the endpoints the discovery document names so you can fill them in. Requires Super User scope. The checks, in order:

- the discovery document can be fetched and is JSON
- it names an issuer, an authorization endpoint, a token endpoint, and a key set
- the key set can be fetched and holds keys
- the identity provider accepts the client ID and secret, tested with a code it must refuse

The credential check runs only with a client ID, a secret, and a token endpoint. To check a saved provider without its secret, send `existing-provider-id`. When the stored secret is used, it is sent only to that provider's stored token endpoint, or, with none stored, to the one its unchanged discovery document names; a `token-endpoint` in the request is not used for it.

The discovery document, the key set, and the token endpoint must be `https` URLs on public addresses. Any other URL fails its check, and the credential check is then not run. A failed check is still a `200`, with `valid: false`. You can call this 15 times a minute.

200.description: The check results.

checks.name: DISCOVERY_HAS_REQUIRED_FIELDS
checks.detail: issuer, authorization_endpoint, token_endpoint, jwks_uri all present.

checks.name: CLIENT_CREDENTIALS_VALID
checks.detail: IdP returned invalid_grant. The client_id and client_secret are recognized.

checks.name: DISCOVERY_HAS_REQUIRED_FIELDS
checks.detail: issuer, authorization_endpoint, token_endpoint, jwks_uri all present.

checks.name: CLIENT_CREDENTIALS_VALID
checks.detail: IdP returned invalid_client. The client_id or client_secret is wrong.

400.description: `discovery-url` is missing. Send it and retry.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired, or invalid. Get a new token and retry.

403.description: Your token is not Super User. Only Super User can check OIDC provider settings.

429.description: You sent more than 15 checks in a minute. Wait a minute and retry.

get.description: Returns a provider's uploaded logo as an image, so a login page can show it. No token is needed. The body is the image itself, PNG, JPEG, WebP, SVG, or GIF, with a matching `Content-Type`. Browsers may cache it for an hour.

parameters.name: provider-id
parameters.description: The provider's `provider-id`.

200.description: The logo image. The `Content-Type` is the stored image type.

404.description: The provider has no uploaded logo, or no provider has this `provider-id`.

post.description: Stores a logo for a provider and points its `logo-url` at it. Requires Super User scope. Send the image as `multipart/form-data` in a field named `logo`: PNG, JPEG, WebP, SVG, or GIF, up to 5 MB. The type is read from the file content, not from the file name. A new upload replaces the old logo.

parameters.name: provider-id
parameters.description: The provider's `provider-id`.

logo.description: The image file, up to 5 MB.

200.description: The logo is stored.

400.description: The `logo` field is missing or empty, or the upload failed. Send the file in a field named `logo`.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired, or invalid. Get a new token and retry.

403.description: Your token is not Super User. Only Super User can change a provider's logo.

404.description: No provider has this `provider-id`.

413.description: The logo is over 5 MB. Send a smaller file.

415.description: The file is not PNG, JPEG, WebP, SVG, or GIF. Convert it and retry.

get.description: Serves an avatar image of at most 48 by 48 pixels: a user's, a contact's, or a generic one. `path`, `path-small`, and `path-large` in the avatar reads point here. No authentication is needed, so an `` tag can load it directly. Anyone who has the filename can load the image. Images are stored as WebP. Ask for the same name with `.jpg` or `.png` and you get a JPEG or PNG copy, converted on first request and kept on disk; a JPEG has a white background in place of transparency. The answer carries `Cache-Control: public, max-age=2592000` (30 days), `Expires`, `Last-Modified`, and a strong `ETag`. Send `If-None-Match` or `If-Modified-Since` to get a bodyless `304` while your copy is current. A filename never changes content, so a new avatar has a new filename; a deleted avatar returns `404` here, but copies already cached by browsers or proxies can outlive it by up to 30 days. For the image of at most 256 by 256 pixels, call `GET /avatar/256/{filename}`.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: Avatar filename: the stored name, 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters plus `.webp`, as `filename` in the avatar reads. Send the same name with `.jpg` or `.png` instead for a JPEG or PNG copy. Any other form is not an image request: without a token it returns `401`.

200.description: The image: `image/webp`, or `image/jpeg` or `image/png` for a `.jpg` or `.png` name.

304.description: Your cached copy is current: `If-None-Match` matched the `ETag`, or `If-Modified-Since` is at or after the image's `Last-Modified`. No body.

401.description: The filename is not 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters plus `.webp`, `.jpg`, or `.png`, so the request is not an image request and needs a token. Take the filename from the avatar reads.

404.description: `Avatar not found`: no avatar has this filename, or it was deleted. `Avatar image data not found`: the stored row has no image in this size. Take the filename from the avatar reads.

message.description: Error detail.

500.description: `Avatar conversion failed`: the JPEG or PNG copy could not be made. Ask for the `.webp` name, or retry later.

delete.description:
Removes one image from the generic avatar library that `GET /avatar` lists.

Requires Super User. Any other scope gets `403`.

Only generic avatars can be removed here: a user's or a contact's avatar filename returns `404`. `202` means the delete was published over the service bus (SBUS), not yet applied; it is applied shortly after. After that the image paths return `404`, but copies already cached by browsers or proxies can outlive it by up to 30 days. `DELETE /avatar` without a filename returns `400`. Only `DELETE` removes an image here: `POST` and `PUT` on this path return `405`.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: Filename of the generic avatar, as `filename` in `GET /avatar`: 32 random hexadecimal characters plus `.webp`.

202.description: The delete was published over SBUS and is applied shortly after: `{"code": 202, "message": "Accepted"}`.

400.description: `filename is required to delete a generic avatar`: the request named no filename (`DELETE /avatar`), or `Path contains missing parameters`. Add the filename from `GET /avatar`.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired, or invalid. Get a new token and retry.

403.description: Only Super User can remove generic avatars: any other scope gets `Access Denied`. Call with a Super User token.

404.description: `Avatar not found`: no generic avatar has this filename. Take the filename from `GET /avatar`.

503.description: `Service bus communication error`: the change could not be published over the service bus (SBUS). Nothing changed. Retry later.

No authentication is needed, so an `` tag can load it directly. Anyone who has the filename can load the image. Images are stored as WebP. Ask for the same name with `.jpg` or `.png` and you get a JPEG or PNG copy, converted on first request and kept on disk; a JPEG has a white background in place of transparency. parameters.name: size
parameters.description: Size to serve: `48` for the image of at most 48 by 48 pixels, `256` for the image of at most 256 by 256 pixels. Any other value returns `404`.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: Avatar filename: the stored name, 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters plus `.webp`, as `filename` in the avatar reads. Send the same name with `.jpg` or `.png` instead for a JPEG or PNG copy. Any other form returns `404`.

get.description:
Returns the metadata of the avatar of one of the domain's shared contacts: filename, file sizes, the image paths, and when it was stored. The answer is a list, normally of one row.

Access follows the contact's own: every scope in the domain can read the avatars of its shared contacts. Reseller can read those of domains in its territory, and Super User and Super User Read Only those of any domain. A scope from another domain gets `403`.

The contact must be a shared contact of the domain, or the call returns `404`, as does a contact with no avatar. The image itself is served without authentication at `path` (at most 48 by 48 pixels), `path-small` (the same image), and `path-large` (at most 256 by 256 pixels), so anyone who has the filename can load it.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

parameters.name: contact_id
parameters.description: The contact's `unique-id`, as returned when it was created or listed: up to 32 characters.

200.description: The contact's avatar.

filename.description: Stored filename: 32 random hexadecimal characters plus the `.webp` extension. It is opaque and carries no user information. Filenames created before API-3198 have the same shape.

filetype.description: MIME type of the stored image. Always `image/webp`.

path.description: Default public path. It serves the 48x48 variant and needs no authentication.

created-datetime.description: When the avatar was stored (RFC3339).

400.description: `Path contains missing parameters`: a path segment is empty. Fill it in and retry.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired, or invalid. Get a new token and retry.

403.description: The domain is outside your scope (`Access Denied: scope '<scope>' may only use address books in its own domain` or `... in its own territory`), or your scope lacks the privilege on `contact`. Call with a token for this domain.

404.description: `Contact not found`: no shared contact with this ID is in the domain. `No avatars found for user`: the contact has no avatar. Check the ID.

post.description:
Uploads an image and makes it the avatar of one of the domain's shared contacts, replacing the current one. Every user in the domain sees it.

Needs domain tier or above, as for the shared contact itself: Office Manager can change the avatars of its own domain's shared contacts, Reseller those of domains in its territory, and Super User any domain's. Scopes that can only read shared contacts, including Site Manager and Call Center Supervisor, get `403`.

The contact must be a shared contact of the domain, or the call returns `404`.

Send the image as `multipart/form-data` in a part named `file`. JPEG, PNG, GIF, and WebP are accepted, recognized from the file's content rather than its name or content type; a GIF keeps its first frame only. The image must be square, at most 20 MB, and at most 8,000 pixels on a side; the size is checked before the image is decoded. It is re-encoded as WebP, which drops embedded metadata, in two sizes: at most 256 by 256 pixels and 100 KB, and at most 48 by 48 pixels and 20 KB. A smaller image is not enlarged. `file-modified-for-limits: yes` means the image had to be scaled down or compressed further to fit. The request body is the image itself, so this page shows no request example.

`202` means the change was published over the service bus (SBUS), not yet applied. The image is stored, and the contact points at it, shortly after, so `path` can return `404` for a moment. The previous avatar is deleted the same way. If the change can't be published, the call returns `503` and nothing changes. `POST` and `PUT` on this path do the same thing.

The image itself is served without authentication at `path` (at most 48 by 48 pixels), `path-small` (the same image), and `path-large` (at most 256 by 256 pixels), so anyone who has the filename can load it.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

parameters.name: contact_id
parameters.description: The contact's `unique-id`, as returned when it was created or listed: up to 32 characters.

file.description: The image: JPEG, PNG, GIF, or WebP, square, at most 20 MB. The part may also be named `File`.

202.description: The upload was published over SBUS and is applied shortly after; see the description.

400.description: The image was refused. The message says why: `No file uploaded` (no part named `file`), `File size exceeds maximum upload size of 20MB`, `File is not a valid image`, `Only JPG, PNG, WebP, and GIF formats are supported`, `Image dimensions <w>x<h> are outside the supported range (1 to 8000 pixels per side)`, or `Avatar image must be square (1:1). Received <w>x<h>. Crop the image before uploading.` Fix the image and retry. An empty path segment returns `Path contains missing parameters`.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired, or invalid. Get a new token and retry.

403.description: Your scope can read the domain's shared contacts but not change them (`Access Denied: scope '<scope>' may read the domain's shared contacts but not change them`), the domain is outside your scope, or your scope lacks the privilege on `contact`. Call with an Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User token.

404.description: `Contact not found`: no shared contact with this ID is in the domain, or the domain does not exist. Check the ID.

500.description: The image could not be stored: `Failed to process image. Unable to reduce image to required size constraints.`, `Failed to process image. Temporary file was not available.`, or `Failed to link avatar to contact`. Nothing changed. Retry; if it fails again, contact support.

503.description: The change could not be published over the service bus (SBUS). Nothing changed. Retry later.

get.summary: Read shared contact avatar by filename
get.description:
Returns the metadata of one stored avatar of a shared contact of the domain, addressed by its filename.

Access follows the contact's own: every scope in the domain can read the avatars of its shared contacts. Reseller can read those of domains in its territory, and Super User and Super User Read Only those of any domain. A scope from another domain gets `403`.

The contact must be in the address book the path names, and the avatar must belong to it; otherwise the call returns `404`. The image itself is served without authentication at `path` (at most 48 by 48 pixels), `path-small` (the same image), and `path-large` (at most 256 by 256 pixels), so anyone who has the filename can load it. To read the contact's current avatar without knowing its filename, call `GET /domains/{domain}/contacts/{contact_id}/avatar`. Only `GET` and `DELETE` are served on this path; `POST` and `PUT` return `405 Method Not Allowed. Upload to the avatar collection path, not to a filename`.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

parameters.name: contact_id
parameters.description: The contact's `unique-id`, as returned when it was created or listed: up to 32 characters.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: Avatar filename, as `avatar` on the contact or `filename` in `GET .../contacts/{contact_id}/avatar`: 32 random hexadecimal characters plus `.webp`.

200.description: The avatar's metadata.

400.description: `Path contains missing parameters`: a path segment is empty. Fill it in and retry.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired, or invalid. Get a new token and retry.

403.description: The address book is outside your scope. The message says why, as for the contact itself: `Access Denied: scope '<scope>' may only use its own address book`, `... may only use the address books of users in site '<site>'`, `... may only use address books in its own domain` or `... in its own territory`, or a missing privilege on `contact`. Call with a token that administers this address book.

404.description: `Contact not found`: no contact with this ID is in the address book the path names. `Avatar not found`: the contact has no avatar with this filename. Either way the domain may also not exist. Call `GET /domains/{domain}/contacts/{contact_id}/avatar` for the contact's avatars.

delete.summary: Delete shared contact avatar by filename
delete.description:
Deletes one stored avatar of a shared contact of the domain, addressed by its filename, and clears the contact's avatar.

Needs domain tier or above, as for the shared contact itself: Office Manager can delete the avatars of its own domain's shared contacts, Reseller those of domains in its territory, and Super User any domain's. Scopes that can only read shared contacts, including Site Manager and Call Center Supervisor, get `403`.

The contact must be in the address book the path names, and the avatar must belong to it, or the call returns `404`. `202` means the delete was published over the service bus (SBUS), not yet applied; it is applied shortly after. To delete the contact's current avatar without knowing its filename, call `DELETE /domains/{domain}/contacts/{contact_id}/avatar`. Only `GET` and `DELETE` are served on this path; `POST` and `PUT` return `405 Method Not Allowed. Upload to the avatar collection path, not to a filename`.

After the delete is applied, the image paths return `404`.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

parameters.name: contact_id
parameters.description: The contact's `unique-id`, as returned when it was created or listed: up to 32 characters.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: Avatar filename, as `avatar` on the contact or `filename` in `GET .../contacts/{contact_id}/avatar`: 32 random hexadecimal characters plus `.webp`.

202.description: The delete was published over SBUS and is applied shortly after: `{"code": 202, "message": "Accepted"}`.

400.description: `Path contains missing parameters`: a path segment is empty. Fill it in and retry.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired, or invalid. Get a new token and retry.

get.summary: Read user contact avatar by filename
get.description:
Returns the metadata of one stored avatar of a contact in a user's personal address book, addressed by its filename.

Access follows the contact's own: Basic User, Advanced User, Simple User, Call Center Agent, and Call Center Supervisor can read the avatars of their own contacts only. Site Manager can read those of its own contacts and of users at its own site, Office Manager and Office Manager Read-Only those of any user in their domain, Reseller those of users in domains of its territory, and Super User and Super User Read Only any user's. Any other address book returns `403`.

The contact must be in the address book the path names, and the avatar must belong to it; otherwise the call returns `404`. The image itself is served without authentication at `path` (at most 48 by 48 pixels), `path-small` (the same image), and `path-large` (at most 256 by 256 pixels), so anyone who has the filename can load it. To read the contact's current avatar without knowing its filename, call `GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/contacts/{contact_id}/avatar`. Only `GET` and `DELETE` are served on this path; `POST` and `PUT` return `405 Method Not Allowed. Upload to the avatar collection path, not to a filename`. A shared contact's avatar is under `/domains/{domain}/contacts/{contact_id}/avatar/{filename}`.

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: Avatar filename, as `avatar` on the contact or `filename` in `GET .../contacts/{contact_id}/avatar`: 32 random hexadecimal characters plus `.webp`.
