Call with a token that administers this address book.

404.description: `Contact not found`: no contact with this ID is in the address book the path names. `Avatar not found`: the contact has no avatar with this filename. Either way the domain may also not exist. Call `GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/contacts/{contact_id}/avatar` for the contact's avatars.

delete.summary: Delete user contact avatar by filename
delete.description:
Deletes one stored avatar of a contact in a user's personal address book, addressed by its filename, and clears the contact's avatar.

Access follows the contact's own: Basic User, Advanced User, Simple User, Call Center Agent, and Call Center Supervisor can delete the avatars of their own contacts only. Site Manager can delete those of its own contacts and of users at its own site, Office Manager those of any user in its domain, Reseller those of users in domains of its territory, and Super User any user's. Any other address book returns `403`.

The contact must be in the address book the path names, and the avatar must belong to it, or the call returns `404`. `202` means the delete was published over the service bus (SBUS), not yet applied; it is applied shortly after. To delete the contact's current avatar without knowing its filename, call `DELETE /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/contacts/{contact_id}/avatar`. Only `GET` and `DELETE` are served on this path; `POST` and `PUT` return `405 Method Not Allowed. Upload to the avatar collection path, not to a filename`.

After the delete is applied, the image paths return `404`. A shared contact's avatar is under `/domains/{domain}/contacts/{contact_id}/avatar/{filename}`.

get.description:
Lists the generic avatar library: the images any user can pick instead of uploading their own.

No authentication is needed. Each row gives the image's `filename` and `path`, the image of at most 256 by 256 pixels; the 48 by 48 image is at `/ns-api/v2/avatar/{filename}`. An empty library returns `404`, not an empty array. Super User adds images with `POST /avatar`.

post.description:
Adds an image to the generic avatar library that `GET /avatar` lists. Every call adds a new image; none is replaced.

Requires Super User. Any other scope gets `403`.

Send the image as `multipart/form-data` in a part named `file`. JPEG, PNG, GIF, and WebP are accepted, recognized from the file's content rather than its name or content type; a GIF keeps its first frame only. The image must be square, at most 20 MB, and at most 8,000 pixels on a side; the size is checked before the image is decoded. It is re-encoded as WebP, which drops embedded metadata, in two sizes: at most 256 by 256 pixels and 100 KB, and at most 48 by 48 pixels and 20 KB. A smaller image is not enlarged. `file-modified-for-limits: yes` means the image had to be scaled down or compressed further to fit. The request body is the image itself, so this page shows no request example.

The answer comes back as soon as the image is published over the service bus (SBUS), and the image is stored shortly after. The answer shows `user` and `domain` as `*`. To remove one, call `DELETE /avatar/{filename}`.

The message says why: `No file uploaded` (no part named `file`), `File size exceeds maximum upload size of 20MB`, `File is not a valid image`, `Only JPG, PNG, WebP, and GIF formats are supported`, `Image dimensions <w>x<h> are outside the supported range (1 to 8000 pixels per side)`, or `Avatar image must be square (1:1). Received <w>x<h>. Crop the image before uploading.` Fix the image and retry. An empty path segment returns `Path contains missing parameters`.

post.description:
Creates one translation, or several when the body has a `translations` array. Requires Super User scope.

A key created in any namespace other than `common` is also created in `common`, with the same locale, value, and description, unless `common` already has that key. The response reports this in `common_entry_created`. An `id` is generated when you omit it.

A new translation is marked as customized (`source` is `api`), so a filesystem sync never overwrites it. Send `source=filesystem` to let the next sync replace it.

The change is accepted and applied shortly after this response, so a read made immediately after can still show the old value.

A single create of a `locale`, `namespace`, and `key` that already exists returns `409`; change it with `PUT /translations`. Send a `translations` array to act on several translations in one request. A bulk request always returns `200`: each item that failed is listed in `errors` with its position in the array and the reason, and `summary` counts the results.

errors.error: Translation already exists for this locale, namespace, and key combination

403.description: Your token is not Super User. Only Super User can change translations.

put.description:
Changes the value, the description, or both, of one translation, or of several when the body has a `translations` array. Requires Super User scope.

Identify each translation by `id`, or by `locale`, `namespace`, and `key`. When `id` is sent it wins. The locale, namespace, and key themselves cannot be changed: delete the translation and create it again.

You can send `description` alone. Every change marks the translation as customized, even a description-only one, so a filesystem sync no longer overwrites its value.

The change is accepted and applied shortly after this response, so a read made immediately after can still show the old value. Send a `translations` array to act on several translations in one request. A bulk request always returns `200`: each item that failed is listed in `errors` with its position in the array and the reason, and `summary` counts the results.

Deletes one translation, or several when the body has a `translations` array. Requires Super User scope.

Identify a translation by `id`, or by `locale`, `namespace`, and `key`, in the body or as query parameters. A query parameter overrides the same field in the body. When you use query parameters, the body can be empty.

The copy in `common` that a create may have added is not deleted. Delete it separately if you no longer want it.

The change is accepted and applied shortly after this response, so a read made immediately after can still show the old value. Send a `translations` array to act on several translations in one request. A bulk request always returns `200`: each item that failed is listed in `errors` with its position in the array and the reason, and `summary` counts the results.

get.description:
Returns every translation for a locale, grouped by namespace, as `{namespace: {key: value}}`. No token is required. A token that you send and that is not valid returns `401`.

Every key comes from the `en-US` translations. Where the requested locale has its own value for a key, that value is returned; otherwise the `en-US` value is. A key or a namespace that exists only in the requested locale, and not in `en-US`, is not returned. There is no other fallback: `fr-CA` does not fall back to `fr`, and the result does not depend on any domain setting. A locale with no translations at all returns the `en-US` values.

The response may be cached for up to 1 hour (`Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600`), so a browser that already loaded it can show an older value after an edit.

To fetch one namespace, use `/translations/{locale}/{namespace}`.

parameters.name: locale
parameters.description: The locale code: 2 letters, optionally followed by a hyphen and 2 letters, such as `en-US`, `fr-CA`, or `fr`. Matched without regard to case. Any other form, such as `zh-Hans`, returns `404`.

200.description: The translations, grouped by namespace. An empty result is returned as `[]`.

401.description: The access token you sent is expired or invalid. This endpoint needs no token: send a valid token or none, and retry.

404.description: `locale` is not 2 letters, optionally followed by a hyphen and 2 letters, so no route matches. Use a code such as `en-US` or `fr`.

get.summary: Get translation descriptions for a locale
get.description:
Returns the translator descriptions for a locale, grouped by namespace and key. A description explains where a string appears, to help translators. Requires Reseller, Super User, or Super User Read Only scope.

Only keys with a non-empty description are returned, and there is no fallback to `en-US`. A locale that has translations but no descriptions returns an empty result, as `[]`. A locale with no translations returns `404`.

The response may be cached for up to 30 seconds. To set a description, use `PUT /translations`.

parameters.description: The locale code, such as `en-US`. Use a value from `GET /translations/locales`. A code that is not 2 letters, optionally followed by a hyphen and 2 letters, returns `404`.

Use a value from this list as `{namespace}` in `/translations/{locale}/{namespace}`. Takes no parameters. The response may be cached for up to 30 seconds.

get.description:
Returns every translation record with its metadata, most recently updated first, for managing translations. Requires Reseller, Super User, or Super User Read Only scope.

Takes no parameters. Filtering, paging, and sorting are not supported: any query parameter, such as `locale` or `limit`, is ignored and the whole table is returned. Filter the result yourself.

Each record's `availability` lists the locales that have the same `namespace` and `key`, next to every locale in use, so you can find keys that are missing a translation. The response is never cached, so it shows a change as soon as the change is applied.

To read translations as an app uses them, with the `en-US` fallback applied, use `/translations/{locale}`.

post.description:
Loads translations from the locale files installed on the server that answers the request. Requires Super User scope.

Send `project` to load one set of files: `horizon` for the web app, or `auth` for the login pages. Omit it, or send `all`, to load both. For each key in a file:

- **Not in the database:** created, along with its copy in `common` when `common` lacks the key.
- **Customized through this API:** left alone.
- **Already present, `auth` files:** left alone, so the web app's text wins on shared keys.
- **Value changed in the file:** updated.

Keys that are no longer in the files are not deleted. For `horizon`, translator descriptions are also loaded, for keys that already exist. Only files named like `en.json` or `en-US.json` are read.

The response lists every change per project and locale, with totals. A project with no locale files on this server is reported with `success: false` inside `projects`, with `200`. The change is accepted and applied shortly after this response, so a read made immediately after can still show the old value.

An unknown `project` returns `400` with the list of valid names.

200.description: The changes made, per project and locale, with totals.

400.description: `project` is not a known project. The message lists the valid names. Send `horizon`, `auth`, or `all`, or omit it.

403.description: Your token is not Super User. Only Super User can change translations.

get.description:
Returns the translations for one namespace in a locale, as a flat `{key: value}` object. No token is required. A token that you send and that is not valid returns `401`.

Every key comes from the `en-US` translations. Where the requested locale has its own value for a key, that value is returned; otherwise the `en-US` value is. A key or a namespace that exists only in the requested locale, and not in `en-US`, is not returned. There is no other fallback: `fr-CA` does not fall back to `fr`, and the result does not depend on any domain setting. A locale with no translations at all returns the `en-US` values. An unknown namespace, or one that has no `en-US` translations, returns an empty result.

The response may be cached for up to 1 hour (`Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600`), so a browser that already loaded it can show an older value after an edit.

To fetch every namespace at once, use `/translations/{locale}`.

get.description:
Lists the license records of every core server in the cluster as one list, with each license's product, expiry, authorized endpoints and sessions, and authorization keys.

Requires Super User or Super User Read Only scope. The authorization keys are masked unless a Super User sends `include-secret=yes`.

Each server answers for its own records. A server that does not answer within 3 seconds is left out of the list, without an error. Filters, `sort`, `limit`, and `start` apply on each server, so one page can hold up to `limit` records from every server. To page through one server, use `GET /license/{hostname}`.

Send only the filters listed here. A query-builder key such as `OR` or `joins`, or a filter name that is not a plain field name, returns `400`.

parameters.description: Only the records with this element ID. Exact match.

parameters.name: license-mac-address
parameters.description: Only the records for this MAC address, in the form the server stores it. Exact match.

parameters.name: license-product
parameters.description: Only the records for this product, such as `NMS`. Exact match.

parameters.name: license-status
parameters.description: Only the records with this license status, such as `active`. Exact match.

parameters.name: license-update-status
parameters.description: Only the records with this update status, such as `idle`. Exact match.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum records to return from each server. Defaults to `100`.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Number of records to skip on each server before returning results. Defaults to `0`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Field to sort on, such as `license-expiration-date`, optionally followed by `asc` or `desc`. Ascending by default. The column form, such as `expiration_date`, works too. Any other value returns `400`.

parameters.name: include-secret
parameters.description: `yes` returns the authorization keys in clear. Super User only: any other scope gets `403`. `include-secrets` is accepted too. Leave it out for masked keys.

200.description: License records from every server that answered. An empty array when none match.

400.description: `sort` names something other than a license field (`Invalid sort. ...`), or a filter is not a plain field name.

get.description:
Lists the license records of one server in the cluster.

Requires Super User or Super User Read Only scope. The authorization keys are masked unless a Super User sends `include-secret=yes`.

`hostname` must be the server answering the request or a core server in the cluster; any other name returns `400`. For another server the request is passed on over HTTPS, which must answer within 6 seconds, or 15 seconds when `limit` is over 2,000. A server that cannot be reached, or does not answer in time, returns an empty array rather than an error, so an empty array does not prove the server has no licenses.

get.description:
Returns the SIP requests that core servers rejected, newest first, one row per source address, method, and address of record. The reject log is platform-wide. It is not filtered by domain or territory, and it holds source addresses and addresses of record from every domain. Requires Super User or Super User Read Only scope.

Each core server keeps its own reject log. Without `reject-hostname`, you get the rows of the core server that answers the request. The other core servers are asked too, but their rows are not included in the response today. To read every server, call `GET /rejectlog/{hostname}` for each core server. `reject-hostname` must name a core server of the platform; any other name returns `404` and no server is asked.

Filter with `reject-received-from`, `reject-method`, `reject-address-of-record`, `reject-user-agent`, `reject-result`, and `reject-cause`. Each is an exact match on the whole value.

`GET /rejectlog/count` returns `{"total": N}` for the same filters, counted on the answering core server only.

parameters.description: Return only requests from this source address. Exact match. Also accepted as `rcv_from`.

parameters.name: reject-hostname
parameters.description: Read only this core server, the same as `GET /rejectlog/{hostname}`. This is not a filter on the rows: it selects the server to ask. Also accepted as `hostname`. A name that is not a core server of the platform returns `404`. A core server that does not answer returns an empty array.

parameters.name: reject-method
parameters.description: Return only requests with this SIP method, such as `REGISTER`. Exact match. Also accepted as `method`.

parameters.name: reject-address-of-record
parameters.description: Return only requests for this address of record. Exact match. Also accepted as `aor`.

parameters.name: reject-user-agent
parameters.description: Return only requests with this `User-Agent`. Exact match. Also accepted as `user_agent`.

parameters.name: reject-result
parameters.description: Return only requests with this result. Exact match. Also accepted as `result`.

parameters.name: reject-action
parameters.description: Not applied today: every action is returned whatever you send. Filter the response on `reject-action` instead.

parameters.name: reject-cause
parameters.description: Return only requests with this cause. Exact match. Also accepted as `cause`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: The most rows to return. Defaults to 100. There is no upper limit.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Number of records to skip before the first one returned. Defaults to `0`. Use it with `limit` to page.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: The sort order: one or more of `rcv_from`, `hostname`, `method`, `aor`, `rcv_time`, `user_agent`, `contact`, `result`, `action`, `cause`, `count`, and `rate`, each optionally followed by a space and `asc` or `desc`, separated by commas. Who can call it:

- Reseller reads domains in its territory.
- Super User and Super User Read Only read any domain.
- Scopes below Reseller read only their own registrations, and must add `user` with their own user (or `~`). Without it they get `403`.

post.description:
Registers a device's push token so the device gets call and message notifications in one domain. A mobile or web app calls it after it gets a token from its push service, and again whenever that token changes.

Who can call it:

- Reseller manages registrations in domains of its territory.
- Super User manages any domain.
- Scopes below Reseller, except the read-only ones, manage only their own registrations in their own domain. Add `user` with your own user (or `~`).

Super User Read Only and Office Manager Read-Only get `403`.

What happens:

- `push-device` must be an existing device within your reach. Any other answers `404` with `Device not found.`, whether the device is missing or someone else's.
- The registration belongs to the device's owner, taken from the device. `push-device` must be a device in the path's domain, and your own below Reseller.
- Push delivery is switched on for the device if it is not already.
- The token replaces any other token on the same device and `push-network`, so a device holds one token per push service.
- `push-network` defaults to `firebase`. A `pwa` token is URL-decoded before it is checked and stored.

Answers `202` with `{"response": "ok", "device": ...}`. The change is accepted and applied shortly after, so a read made straight after it can still show the previous state.

An `apns` registration returns `400` when the platform is not set up for Apple push. Contact support. To remove the registration, see the matching `DELETE`.

parameters.description: Domain name. Use `~` for your own domain. The device must belong to this domain.

- `Bad request. Missing parameter ...`: a required field is missing
- `push-network` or `push-test` is not one of the listed values
- `push-device-token` is empty, longer than 1,024 characters, contains characters other than printable ASCII, or is a masked value
- `Missing 'APNS' config property`: the platform is not set up for Apple push, so contact support

`Device not found.`: `push-device` is not an existing device, or it is outside your reach. Both answer the same way. Use the device's full AOR, for example `sip:1001a@example.com`, as `GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/devices` returns it.

Who can call it:

- Reseller updates registrations in domains of its territory.
- Super User updates any domain.
- Scopes below Reseller, except the read-only ones, update only their own registrations in their own domain. Add `user` with your own user (or `~`).

Super User Read Only and Office Manager Read-Only get `403`.

The token must be registered in the path's domain, and be your own below Reseller. A token that is not registered, or whose registration is outside your reach, returns `404`. The registration keeps its owner: `domain` and `user` in the body never move it. A new `push-device` must be another device of the same user.

Answers `202`. The change is accepted and applied shortly after, so a read made straight after it can still show the previous state.

delete.description:
Unregisters a device from push notifications in one domain. A mobile or web app calls it when the user logs out.

Who can call it:

- Reseller unregisters registrations in domains of its territory.
- Super User unregisters any domain.
- Scopes below Reseller, except the read-only ones, unregister only their own registrations in their own domain. Add `user` with your own user (or `~`).

Super User Read Only and Office Manager Read-Only get `403`.

What happens:

- `push-device` is required and must be an existing device within your reach. Any other answers `404` with `Device not found.` It must be a device in the path's domain, and your own below Reseller.
- With `push-device-token`, that registration is removed. The token must be registered on that device, or the request returns `404`. A token that is not registered at all is treated as already removed.
- Without `push-device-token`, the registrations stay and only the device's push delivery is switched off.
- Push delivery is switched off for the device, except for an `apns_chat` token, which covers chat only and leaves call notifications on.
- With `push-network` `pwa`, every web push registration of `user` is removed instead, and `push-device` is not needed. Send `user`; without it the request returns `400`. The answer is `{"response": "ok"}` with no `device`.

Returns one vCon document for a call in a domain, addressed under its CDR. It is the same read as `GET /domains/{domain}/vcon/{cdr_id}`. Requires Office Manager, Site Manager, Reseller, Super User, or Super User Read Only scope: the same rights as reading the domain's CDRs. A Site Manager reads a call only when a user of its own site is a party on a leg in the path domain; any other call returns `404`, as a CDR that does not exist does.

The document follows the IETF vCon core format. It joins every CDR leg of the call, including transfers and queue hops linked by call ID, with the recordings, transcript segments, sentiment, AI summary, and the internal parties' user profiles. Times are RFC 3339 in UTC with a `Z` suffix. Below Super User and Super User Read Only, a party from another domain carries only what your own CDR names: its SIP URI, extension, and user ID, with no user profile.

CDRs are stored by month. Send `yyyymm` when you know the month of the call. Without it, the API searches back from the current month, 12 months by default, and uses the first month that holds the CDR.

Each recording entry in `dialog` carries a signed `url` you can play without a token, through `GET /recordings/play`.

get.description:
Returns one vCon document for a call in a domain, built from its CDRs. Requires Office Manager, Site Manager, Reseller, Super User, or Super User Read Only scope: the same rights as reading the domain's CDRs. A Site Manager reads a call only when a user of its own site is a party on a leg in the path domain; any other call returns `404`, as a CDR that does not exist does.

delete.description:
Deletes a shared or main-number inbox. Its conversations are kept, the inbox is marked deactivated, and the extension is freed for reuse. A new inbox on the same extension starts empty. The API has no restore.

Deleted inboxes appear in `GET /domains/{domain}/inboxes` with `include_deactivated`. A user's extension returns `404`: a personal inbox cannot be deleted. A `202` means the delete is accepted and already applied.

Requires Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User scope. A Site Manager reaches only the inboxes whose owner is a user in its own site. An inbox with no owner, or whose owner cannot be read, is out of its reach. A Site Manager gets `403` for an inbox out of its reach. Other callers get `403`.

get.description:
Returns the members of an inbox and their roles. `{extension}` can be a shared inbox, or a user's own extension to address that user's personal inbox.

A member's `role` is one of these values:

- `owner`: the inbox owner. Set when the inbox is created, and never changed.
- `can-reply`: reads and replies to conversations.
- `view`: reads conversations only.

`include_deactivated` lists the members of a deleted inbox. It accepts `1`, `true`, or `yes`, and only Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User scope can use it.

You can read the members of an inbox you are a member of, or, for a personal inbox, the one you own. Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User scope can read any inbox's members. Other callers get `403`.

Adding a user who is already a member succeeds and changes nothing. Change a member's role with `PUT /domains/{domain}/inboxes/{extension}/members/{user}`.

`user` must be a user of the same domain, not another inbox. A `202` means the change is accepted and already applied.

For a shared or main-number inbox, requires Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User scope. For a personal inbox, its owner can also add members. Other callers get `403`.

Assigns one of the domain's unassigned SMS numbers to a shared or main-number inbox. The inbox can then text from it, and texts sent to it arrive in the inbox. An inbox can have any number of SMS numbers, or none.

Only a number whose SMS application is `available` can be assigned. A number already held by a user, a call queue or another inbox answers `409`; unassign it on the phone numbers page first. Assigning a number the inbox already has succeeds and changes nothing. The inbox's numbers are listed in `sms_numbers` on `GET /domains/{domain}/inboxes`.

A `202` means the assignment is accepted; it is applied within a few seconds.

Requires Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User scope. Other callers get `403`.

Removing the inbox's last number is allowed: the inbox stays active for internal notes, calls and fax, and can't send texts until a number is assigned again.

A `202` means the removal is accepted; it is applied within a few seconds.

Requires Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User scope. Other callers get `403`.

get.description:
Returns every inbox a user is a member of: shared and main-number inboxes, the user's own personal inbox, and personal inboxes other users have shared with them. Use it to build an inbox list for that user.

`inbox_kind` is one of these values:

- `shared`: an inbox you create, with its own extension, one owner, and the members you add.
- `main_number`: an inbox you create, with its own extension and no owner.
- `personal`: the inbox every user already has, holding their SMS conversations across all their phone numbers (DIDs). It is addressed by the user's own extension and is never created or deleted here.

A personal inbox returns one row per phone number: `did` is the number, and `user` and `owner` are the owner. `space_id` identifies each inbox's conversations, and stays unique when an extension is reused. `include_deactivated` adds deleted inboxes, with `deactivated: true`. It accepts `1`, `true`, or `yes`, and only Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User scope can use it: for other scopes it is ignored. A user with no inboxes returns an empty array.

Any user can list their own inboxes. Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User scope can list any user's in the domain. Site Manager and Call Center Supervisor scopes can list the inboxes of users in their own site. Other callers get `403`.

parameters.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

parameters.name: user
parameters.description: User's extension, such as `1001`. `~` means the user your token belongs to.

parameters.name: include_deactivated
parameters.description: Set to `1`, `true`, or `yes` to include deleted inboxes. Only Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User scope can use it; for other scopes it is ignored.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired, or invalid. Get a new token and retry.

403.description: Your token cannot list this user's inboxes.

404.description: The domain does not exist. Check the spelling and retry.

502.description: The messaging service did not answer or refused the request. Retry later.

get.description:
Lists stored default values: the rows that fill fields a create leaves out. Each row names an object, a v2 field, a value, and the tier it applies at: the whole system (`reseller` and `domain` both `*`), one territory (`reseller` set), or one domain (`domain` set).

Each scope reads its own tier and the tiers above it, never another tenant's rows:

- Super User and Super User Read Only read every row.
- Reseller and Route Manager Reseller read their territory's rows, the rows of domains in their territory, and, with `full=true`, the system rows.
- Office Manager, Office Manager Read-Only, Call Center Supervisor, Route Manager, and Site Manager read their own domain's rows and, with `full=true`, the territory and system rows that apply to it.
- Basic User, Advanced User, Simple User, and Call Center Agent get `403`.

Each filter matches exactly, and `*` or an empty value means no filter. `full=true` adds the rows your tier inherits. Rows are paged with `start` and `limit`, which defaults to `100`. For keys without values, append `/list`.

How defaults apply: when a domain, user, or device is created, each field the request leaves out takes the value of the most specific matching row. A domain row wins over a territory row, which wins over a system row. Within one tier, a row for the object wins over one whose `default-object` is `*`. User and device creates read the domain's rows, its territory's rows, and the system rows; a domain create reads territory and system rows, since the domain can't hold rows yet. Fields no row covers fall back to the legacy default values.

To see what can carry a default, call `GET /defaults/objects` and `GET /defaults/objects/{object}/fields`.

parameters.name: default-object
parameters.description: Returns only rows for this object: `domain`, `user`, or `device`. `*` or empty means any. With `full=true`, rows with `default-object` `*` are included too.

parameters.name: default-field
parameters.description: Returns only rows for this field, as a v2 field name such as `time-zone`. `*` or empty means any. Always an exact match.

parameters.name: reseller
parameters.description: Returns only rows for this territory, such as `example-reseller`. `*` or empty means any. Super User and Super User Read Only can name any territory; a Reseller or Route Manager Reseller naming another territory gets `403`.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Returns only rows for this domain, such as `example.com`. Office Manager, Office Manager Read-Only, Call Center Supervisor, Route Manager, and Site Manager must send their own domain (another returns `403`, none returns `400`); a Reseller may name a domain in its territory. `*` does not count as a domain.

parameters.name: full
parameters.description: `true` also returns the rows the tier inherits. For a domain: the rows of its territory and the system rows (never another territory's). For a Reseller without `domain`: the system rows. `yes` and `1` also work. Defaults to `false`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Most rows to return, 1 to 1000. Defaults to `100`. Anything else returns `400`.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: Number of rows to skip before the first one returned. Defaults to `0`. A negative or non-integer value returns `400`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Sort order: one or more comma-separated terms, each a field name optionally followed by `asc` or `desc` (`asc` when left out; any case). Field names are the seven v2 names `default-object`, `default-field`, `reseller`, `domain`, `default-value`, `created-datetime`, and `updated-datetime`, or the legacy column names `default_object`, `default_field`, `default_value`, `created_at`, and `updated_at`. Anything else returns `400`. With no `sort`, rows come in key order.

200.description: The matching rows. No match returns an empty array.

400.description: `Invalid limit: must be an integer from 1 to 1000`, `Invalid start: must be a non-negative integer`, or `Invalid sort: use one of ...`: fix the parameter. `A specific domain is required`: Office Manager, Office Manager Read-Only, Call Center Supervisor, Route Manager, and Site Manager must send their own domain in `domain`.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired, or invalid. Get a new token and retry.

403.description: Your scope cannot read these rows. `Access Denied: scope '<scope>' may not read defaults`: user scopes. `... may only read its own domain's defaults`: a domain scope named another domain. `... may only read its own territory's defaults` or `... may only read defaults of a domain in its territory`: a Reseller named another tenant. `... has no '<tier>_<action>' privilege on object 'default'`: the scope has no defaults rights at all. Name your own domain or territory.

post.description:
Creates a default value, or replaces the value of the row with the same key. The key is `default-object`, `default-field`, `reseller`, and `domain`; each one you leave out is `*`. Send `reseller` for a territory row, `domain` for a domain row, and neither for a system row.

Who can write:

- Super User writes every tier. Only Super User writes system rows (`reseller` and `domain` both `*`).
- Reseller writes its territory's rows (`reseller` set to your territory) and rows of domains in its territory.
- Office Manager and Route Manager write their own domain's rows.
- Route Manager Reseller, Call Center Supervisor, Office Manager Read-Only, Site Manager, Super User Read Only, and user scopes get `403`.

`default-object` is `domain`, `user`, `device`, or `*`, and is stored lowercase. `default-field` must be a field `GET /defaults/objects/{object}/fields` lists for that object (for `*`, a field of any of the three); credentials, `scope`, and key fields (`domain`, `user`, `device`, `reseller`, `territory`) can't carry a default. Keys and value are held to their lengths. Anything else returns `400` before the change is published. `default-value` is up to 255 characters; a number is stored as its string form.

The change is checked, then published over the service bus (SBUS) and applied on every server shortly after, so `202` means accepted, not yet stored. Read the row back to confirm it. Send `domain` and `reseller` in the body: in the query string they're ignored.

1.description: A Reseller: every new domain in the territory gets this time zone.

2.description: Super User only: every new user on the platform gets voicemail.

202.description: The default passed every check and was published over the service bus (SBUS); it is applied shortly after: `{"code": 202, "message": "Accepted"}`.

400.description: The row was refused before anything was published. `Bad request. Missing parameter '<field>'.`: send `default-field` (and `default-value` on a create). `Invalid <field>: longer than <n> characters` or `Invalid <field>: must be a string`: shorten it or send a string. `Invalid default-object: must be one of *, domain, user, device`. `Invalid default-field: <field> may not carry a default` (a credential, `scope`, or key field) or `Invalid default-field: <field> is not a field of <object>`: pick one from `GET /defaults/objects/{object}/fields`. `Service bus communication error`: the change could not be published; retry.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired, or invalid. Get a new token and retry.

403.description: Your scope cannot write this row. `Access Denied: scope '<scope>' may read defaults but not change them`: a read-only scope. `Access Denied: system defaults are Super User only`: `reseller` and `domain` are both `*`. `... may only change its own territory's defaults`, `... may only change defaults of a domain in its territory`, or `... may only change its own domain's defaults`: the key names another tenant. Send a key in your own tier.

put.description:
Changes the value of an existing default. Name the row by its key: `default-object`, `default-field`, `reseller`, and `domain`, as the list returns them; each one you leave out is `*`. A key that matches no row returns `404`; to create or replace in one call, use `POST /defaults`. `created-datetime` never changes.

Who can write:

- Super User writes every tier. Only Super User writes system rows (`reseller` and `domain` both `*`).
- Reseller writes its territory's rows (`reseller` set to your territory) and rows of domains in its territory.
- Office Manager and Route Manager write their own domain's rows.
- Route Manager Reseller, Call Center Supervisor, Office Manager Read-Only, Site Manager, Super User Read Only, and user scopes get `403`.

`default-object` is `domain`, `user`, `device`, or `*`, and is stored lowercase. `default-field` must be a field `GET /defaults/objects/{object}/fields` lists for that object (for `*`, a field of any of the three); credentials, `scope`, and key fields (`domain`, `user`, `device`, `reseller`, `territory`) can't carry a default. Keys and value are held to their lengths. Anything else returns `400` before the change is published.

The change is checked, then published over the service bus (SBUS) and applied on every server shortly after, so `202` means accepted, not yet stored. Read the row back to confirm it.

202.description: The change passed every check and was published over the service bus (SBUS); it is applied shortly after: `{"code": 202, "message": "Accepted"}`.

400.description: The row was refused before anything was published. `Bad request. Missing parameter '<field>'.`: send `default-field` (and `default-value` on a create). `Invalid <field>: longer than <n> characters` or `Invalid <field>: must be a string`: shorten it or send a string. `Invalid default-object: must be one of *, domain, user, device`. `Invalid default-field: <field> may not carry a default` (a credential, `scope`, or key field) or `Invalid default-field: <field> is not a field of <object>`: pick one from `GET /defaults/objects/{object}/fields`. `Service bus communication error`: the change could not be published; retry.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired, or invalid. Get a new token and retry.

403.description: Your scope cannot write this row. `Access Denied: scope '<scope>' may read defaults but not change them`: a read-only scope. `Access Denied: system defaults are Super User only`: `reseller` and `domain` are both `*`. `... may only change its own territory's defaults`, `... may only change defaults of a domain in its territory`, or `... may only change its own domain's defaults`: the key names another tenant. Send a key in your own tier.

404.description: `Default not found`: no row has this key. List the defaults to find the key, or create the row with POST.

delete.description:
Deletes one default. Name the row in the body by its key: `default-object`, `default-field`, `reseller`, and `domain`; each one you leave out is `*`, so the call removes exactly one row. `default-value` is ignored. The key is not checked against the catalog, so a row stored before the catalog rules can still be removed; `default-object` is matched as sent.

Who can delete:

- Super User writes every tier. Only Super User writes system rows (`reseller` and `domain` both `*`).
- Reseller writes its territory's rows (`reseller` set to your territory) and rows of domains in its territory.
- Office Manager and Route Manager write their own domain's rows.
- Route Manager Reseller, Call Center Supervisor, Office Manager Read-Only, Site Manager, Super User Read Only, and user scopes get `403`.

The change is checked, then published over the service bus (SBUS) and applied on every server shortly after, so `202` means accepted, not yet stored. Read the row back to confirm it. A key that matches no row deletes nothing and still answers `202`.

202.description: The delete passed every check and was published over the service bus (SBUS); it is applied shortly after: `{"code": 202, "message": "Accepted"}`.

400.description: `Bad request. Missing parameter 'default-field'.`: send `default-field`. `Invalid <field>: longer than <n> characters` or `... must be a string`: fix the key. `Service bus communication error`: the delete could not be published; retry.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired, or invalid. Get a new token and retry.

403.description: Your scope cannot write this row. `Access Denied: scope '<scope>' may read defaults but not change them`: a read-only scope. `Access Denied: system defaults are Super User only`: `reseller` and `domain` are both `*`. `... may only change its own territory's defaults`, `... may only change defaults of a domain in its territory`, or `... may only change its own domain's defaults`: the key names another tenant. Send a key in your own tier.

get.description:
Lists the objects whose create applies defaults: `domain`, `user`, and `device`, each with its display label.

Office Manager, Office Manager Read-Only, Call Center Supervisor, Route Manager, Reseller, Route Manager Reseller, Super User, and Super User Read Only can call it. Site Manager and user scopes get `403`. Only `GET` is allowed.

For an object's fields, call `GET /defaults/objects/{object}/fields`.

200.description: The three objects, in the order `domain`, `user`, `device`.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired, or invalid. Get a new token and retry.

403.description: `Access Denied: scope '<scope>' has no '<tier>_read' privilege on object 'default'`: Site Manager and user scopes cannot read the catalog.

405.description: `Method Not Allowed`: only `GET` is allowed on this path.

get.description:
Lists the fields of one object that a default can set: the writable properties of the object's create request body, less credentials, `scope`, key fields (`domain`, `user`, `device`, `reseller`, `territory`), `synchronous`, and audit timestamps. These are exactly the fields a create or update of a default accepts for `domain`, `user`, and `device`. Each entry carries the field's type and description and, where the API reference states them, `nullable`, `enum`, `pattern`, `format`, `default`, `min-length`, `max-length`, `minimum`, `maximum`, `example`, and for an array `items`.

Scopes are as for `GET /defaults/objects`: Site Manager and user scopes get `403`. Only `GET` is allowed.

`{object}` is case-insensitive and may be plural: `users` is `user`. `all` returns every field of `domain`, `user`, and `device`, one entry per field name. An unknown object returns an empty array, not `404`.

parameters.name: object
parameters.description: Object whose fields to list: `domain`, `user`, or `device`, or `all` for the three together. Letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`, and spaces.

200.description: The fields, sorted by `field`. An unknown object returns an empty array.

example.description: Dial permission applied to users in the domain

400.description: `Missing object name`: the object is only spaces. Send an object from `GET /defaults/objects`.

401.description: The access token is missing, expired, or invalid. Get a new token and retry.

403.description: `Access Denied: scope '<scope>' has no '<tier>_read' privilege on object 'default'`: Site Manager and user scopes cannot read the catalog.

405.description: `Method Not Allowed`: only `GET` is allowed on this path.

get.description:
Lists a domain's defaults reduced to their keys: `default-object`, `default-field`, `domain`, and `reseller`. The values are on `GET /domains/{domain}/defaults`.

Needs the `list` privilege on defaults rather than `read`; `/list` and `/count` share it. The same scopes can call it as `GET /domains/{domain}/defaults`, with the same tenant rules.

Takes the same filters as the full read, including `full=true`. `limit` defaults to `1000` here.

parameters.name: domain
parameters.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

parameters.name: default-object
parameters.description: Returns only rows for this object: `domain`, `user`, or `device`. `*` or empty means any. With `full=true`, rows with `default-object` `*` are included too.

parameters.name: default-field
parameters.description: Returns only rows for this field, as a v2 field name such as `time-zone`. `*` or empty means any. Always an exact match.

parameters.name: full
parameters.description: `true` also returns the rows the tier inherits. For a domain: the rows of its territory and the system rows (never another territory's). For a Reseller without `domain`: the system rows. `yes` and `1` also work. Defaults to `false`.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Most rows to return, 1 to 1000. Defaults to `1000`. Anything else returns `400`.

parameters.name: start

get.description:
Returns one core server's status counters over a time window, grouped into time buckets for graphing. Requires Super User or Super User Read Only scope.

The response has one shared `timestamps` array, and for each metric a `values` array aligned to it, plus summary figures: `current`, `first`, `min`, `max`, `avg`, `change-percent`, `samples`, and, for a counter, `total`.

**`hostname` is required.** Each core server keeps only its own status rows, so name the server to read. Use a `hostname` from `GET /nmsstatus/servers`. A request for another core server is passed to that server, and you get its answer.

**Gauges and counters.** A gauge, such as active sessions or a queue depth, is averaged per bucket unless you set `gauge-aggregate`, and its `current` is the latest raw sample. A counter, such as packets or SIP responses, only increases, so it is reported as a rate per second between consecutive buckets. A counter reset, such as a process restart, shows as `null` for that bucket, never as a negative rate. `GET /nmsstatus/metrics` says which metric is which.

**Window and buckets.** Use `range` for a window ending now, or `datetime-start` and `datetime-end` together for a fixed window. The explicit pair wins over `range`. Buckets are `1m`, `10m`, or `1h`; raw samples are never returned. Without `interval`, the bucket follows the range: `1m` up to `24h`, `10m` for `2d` and `7d`, and `1h` for `28d`. A series is limited to 2,000 buckets by default. An `interval` that would exceed it returns `400`, naming a coarser interval to use. A bucket with no samples is `null`, not `0`.

Times in the response use the offset of the `datetime-start` and `datetime-end` you send, or `+00:00`. Check `start-datetime` and `end-datetime` in the response: today a pair that cannot be read, or whose start is not before its end, is not always refused and can be replaced by a default window of about 61 days.

A series that ends now is cached for up to 60 seconds.

parameters.name: hostname
parameters.description: The core server to read, as listed by `GET /nmsstatus/servers`. Exact match: hostnames are lowercase in that list.

parameters.name: range
parameters.description: The window, ending now. Defaults to `24h`. Ignored when `datetime-start` and `datetime-end` are sent.

parameters.name: datetime-start
parameters.description: The start of a fixed window, in RFC 3339, such as `2026-09-01T14:20:00+00:00`. `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` in UTC, and `YYYY-MM-DD` for midnight, are also accepted. Send it with `datetime-end`; one without the other returns `400`.

parameters.name: datetime-end
parameters.description: The end of a fixed window, in RFC 3339. `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` in UTC is also accepted, and `YYYY-MM-DD` means the end of that day. It must be after `datetime-start`.

parameters.name: interval
parameters.description: The bucket width. Defaults by window: `1m` up to `24h`, `10m` for `2d` and `7d`, and `1h` for `28d`. A value that would return more than 2,000 buckets returns `400` naming a coarser interval.

parameters.description: The metrics to return, as metric IDs from `GET /nmsstatus/metrics` separated by commas. The column names are also accepted. Omit it, or send `*` or `all`, for every metric. An unknown ID returns `400` naming it.

parameters.name: gauge-aggregate
parameters.description: How the samples of a gauge inside one bucket are combined. Defaults to `avg`. Counters ignore it.

200.description: The series for the requested window and metrics.

400.description: A parameter is not valid: `hostname` is missing, only one of `datetime-start` and `datetime-end` was sent, or `range`, `interval`, `metrics`, or `gauge-aggregate` has a value the API does not accept. An `interval` that would exceed 2,000 buckets is also refused, and the message names a coarser one. Correct the request and retry.

get.description:
Returns the custom scopes, sorted by name. Requires Super User or Super User Read Only scope.

A custom scope takes a built-in parent scope and removes rights from it, so it can never do more than its parent. Users and API keys are assigned it by name. Its rights come from these settings:

- **`modifications`.** Per-object limits, keyed by API object name: `none` removes the object, `ro` allows reads only, `update-only` allows reads and updates, and `no-delete` allows everything but deletes.
- **`read-only`.** `yes` refuses every write, on every object.

Requires Office Manager scope for your own domain, Reseller for domains in your territory, or Super User. Call Center Supervisor can read storage services but not change them, and gets `403`.

get.description:
Lists every unit in the service catalog with its live state on one server, read from systemd in a single call.

Requires Super User scope.

A catalog unit that is not installed on the server is still listed, with `installed: false` and empty state fields, so every server answers the same set of units. A unit installed under an alias, such as `mysql` for `mariadb`, is reported under the catalog name with `resolved-unit` naming what systemd loaded.

An `active` unit is not proof of health: every platform daemon restarts itself after a crash, so check `restart-count` too.

Runs `systemctl daemon-reload` on one server, so systemd reads every changed unit file again. It restarts nothing.

Requires Super User scope.

You rarely need it: a start, stop or restart reloads first when its own unit file has changed. Use it to clear `need-daemon-reload` on every unit at once, typically after an upgrade that replaced several unit files.

post.description:
Starts, stops or restarts one systemd unit on one server and waits for systemctl to finish, up to 90 seconds.

Requires Super User scope.

A `200` means systemctl ran. Check `success` and `exit-code`: a unit that fails to start is a `200` with `success: false`. Every platform daemon is a `simple` unit, so systemd answers as soon as the process is spawned, before it is ready. The response flags that with `ready-unknown: true`; poll `GET /services/{hostname}/{unit}` to confirm the unit stayed up.

When the unit file changed on disk since systemd read it, the server reloads it first and reports `daemon-reloaded: true`, so the action uses the current file.

An `apache2` restart is scheduled a few seconds later and answered `202`, because the API itself is served through `apache2`. `apache2` cannot be stopped: that is a `403`, because it could then only be started again from the server console.

The action is refused with `409` while an apt operation is running on the server, while another action on the same unit is running, or when the unit is masked. Retry once the apt operation or action finishes, or unmask the unit.

> **Warning:** a stop or restart of `netsapiens_nms`, `netsapiens_ncs` or `netsapiens_licf` drops the calls on that server immediately. This route does not check for active calls, unlike the package upgrade scripts.

Sends a document as a fax from one of the user's fax numbers, optionally with a cover page. The fax is accepted at once and sent in the background: the response is the stored fax with `status` `pending` (or `error` when the vendor refused it). user-authentication.description:
Defines the login authentication method for users within the domain.

There are four possible settings for this parameter.
- ‎`login_name_and_password` allows for username/password login, SSO (Single Sign-On) or TOTP (multi-factor authentication using an authenticator app).
- ‎`authenticator_totp` forces all users in the domain to log in using TOTP (multi-factor authentication using an authenticator app).
- `single_sign_on`forces all users in the domain to log in using SSO (Single Sign-On).
- `authenticator_totp_sso` allows users to log in using TOTP or SSO.

devices.description: The lifelines, keyed by lifeline key.

CallTraceShare.title: Call trace share

callids.description: Every call ID the stored trace covers.

key.description: The share key: the call's date as `YYYYMMDD`, then 32 hexadecimal characters. Anyone who has it can read this trace without a token, read-only, until the share expires or is revoked with `DELETE /sipflow/share/{k}`. Open it with `GET /sipflow?k=<key>` or `GET /sipflow/download/<key>.txt`.

expires.description: When the share stops working, as a Unix timestamp in seconds. The same instant as `expires-datetime`.

expires-datetime.description: When the share stops working, RFC 3339 in UTC. The same instant as `expires`; null exactly when `expires` is null.

hostname.description: Hostname to build share links on.

store-location.description: Hostname of the server that holds the stored copy. Send it base64-encoded as `location` when you open the share on another server of the cluster.

CallTraceShare.description: A stored copy of a call trace, and the key that opens it without a token.

CallTraceShareEnvelope.title: Call trace share envelope
CallTraceShareEnvelope.description: The envelope a share answer comes in.

CallTraceShareRequest.title: Call trace share options

ttl.description: Lifetime of the share, in seconds. Without it, the share lives for `NsTraceShareTempTtl`, 900 seconds (15 minutes) by default. A value above `NsTraceShareMaxTtl`, 30 days by default, is lowered to it. A value that is not a positive number is ignored.

temp.description: Accepted for older clients. `true` means the same as sending no `ttl`.

date.description: Month the call was made in, as `YYYYMM`, to pick which monthly CDR table to search first.

CallTraceShareRequest.description: How long a call trace share lives.

CallTraceExportRequest.title: Call trace export

start_time.description: Start of the window to search, RFC 3339. A legacy `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` value is also accepted. Required unless `k` is sent.

end_time.description: End of the window. Same forms as `start_time`. Required unless `k` is sent.

callids.description: Comma-separated SIP call IDs to trace. Each must match a CDR in your scope inside the window; the rest are ignored. Related calls are added automatically. Required unless `k` is sent.

export_format.description: `image` for the SVG diagram (`image/svg+xml`, the default), `csv` for a CSV file of the event rows (`text/csv`), or `base64` for the raw rows in the form the cluster's servers exchange (`text/plain`).

k.description: Share key. Exports the stored trace it opens, with no token needed, read-only; the search fields are then ignored.

search_callids.description: `no` to trace only the call IDs you sent, without following related calls. `false` and `0` also turn it off.

margin.description: Seconds added before `start_time` and after `end_time` when reading events.

ds.description: Event sources, comma-separated: `diag` for the SIP servers, `ncs` for the conferencing servers.

show_attendees.description: `yes` to follow a conference bridge and include every attendee's legs.

servers.description: Comma-separated hostnames of cluster servers to read, used with `search_callids=no`.

CallTraceExportRequest.description: What to export, and in which form.

CallTraceEventInject.title: Trace event

orig_callid.description: SIP call ID of the call the event belongs to. No control characters.

event_type.description: Label for the event, such as `app`, `ivr`, `media`, or `push`. `push` rows are drawn on a push-notification lifeline. No control characters.

event_text.description: Body of the event, rendered as written with line breaks kept. At most 60,000 bytes. A longer value is refused, never shortened.

servedCallId.description: Second call ID to file the event under. Defaults to `orig_callid`. The trace finds the event under either one.

hostname.description: Hostname stamped on the event. Defaults to the hostname of the server you call. It also picks the `<hostname>_event_YYYYMMDD` table when there is no plain `event_YYYYMMDD` table. It never sends the event to another server.

event_time.description: When the event happened. Send RFC 3339 with an offset, which is converted to UTC, or `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`, read as UTC. Defaults to now. Include milliseconds so the event sorts into place. An impossible date, such as `2026-02-30`, returns `400`. It also picks the day's event table.

event_ts.description: Sort key, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch. Defaults to `event_time`. Send `event_time` instead: a backdated `event_ts` with the default `event_time` can fall outside the trace window, and then the event does not show.

CallTraceEventInject.description: One event row to place in a call's trace.

event-index.description: Index the row was written with.

orig-callid.description: Call ID the event belongs to.

served-callid.description: Second call ID the event is filed under, or `orig-callid` when you sent none.

event-time.description: When the event happened, RFC 3339 in UTC (`+00:00`), to the second. The millisecond value is in `event-ts`.

event-ts.description: Sort key, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.

hostname.description: Hostname stamped on the event.

table.description: Event table the row was written to, on the server you called.

CallQueueCreate.title: CallQueueCreate

callqueue.description: Extension of the new queue. Letters, digits, `.`, `-`, and `_` only, so the queue can be addressed by path. `all`, `list`, and `count` are reserved

description.description: Name of the queue. Also names the queue's system user: the first word is its first name, the rest its last name (`Call Queue` when there is one word)

callqueue-dispatch-type.description: How calls are offered to agents. See `CallQueue`. Left out on create, the queue is a call park with no dispatch settings

callqueue-agent-dispatch-timeout-seconds.description: Seconds an agent is rung before the queue moves on

callqueue-max-wait-timeout-minutes.description: Minutes a caller can wait before the no-answer forward. `0` is unlimited

callqueue-max-current-wait-to-accept-new.description: Expected wait above which new callers follow the busy forward. `0` is unlimited

callqueue-max-current-callers-to-accept-.description: Callers allowed to wait before new callers follow the busy forward. `0` is unlimited

callqueue-require-available-agents-to-ac.description: `yes` sends new callers to the busy forward when no agent is logged in. Defaults to `no`

callqueue-max-callback-queueing-hours.description: Hours a caller-requested callback stays queued. `0` turns callbacks off

callqueue-debug.description: `yes` turns on debug logging for the queue

callqueue-local-only.description: `yes` dispatches only to agents registered on the same core server as the call

callqueue-force-full-intro-playback.description: `yes` plays the whole intro message before a caller is offered to an agent

callqueue-source-match.description: Caller ID sent to the agent on the dispatched leg, such as `<Queue>`. `""` uses the default

callqueue-agent-auto-logout-after-missed.description: `yes` logs out an agent who misses a dispatched call. Defaults to `no`

callqueue-sim-ring-1st-round.description: Agents rung together in the first round

callqueue-sim-ring-increment.description: Agents added to each later round

callqueue-sms-enable.description: `yes` lets the queue take SMS conversations

callqueue-sms-phrase-initiate-chat.description: Keyword that starts a conversation. `STOP`, `END`, `QUIT`, `CANCEL`, `UNSUBSCRIBE`, `START`, `UNSTOP`, `HELP`, and `INFO` are refused, in any case

callqueue-sms-phrase-initiate-success.description: Reply sent when a conversation starts
callqueue-sms-phrase-initiate-success.example: Thanks for texting Sales. An agent will reply shortly.

callqueue-sms-phrase-initiation-fail.description: Reply sent when a text arrives without the start keyword
callqueue-sms-phrase-initiation-fail.example: Text SALES to reach the sales team.

callqueue-sms-phrase-no-agents-available.description: Reply sent when no agent can take a conversation
callqueue-sms-phrase-no-agents-available.example: No agents are available. Please try again later.

callqueue-sms-phrase-terminate-chat.description: Keyword that ends a conversation. The reserved words listed for the start keyword are refused

callqueue-sms-phrase-terminate-success.description: Reply sent when a conversation ends by keyword

department.description: Department of the queue's system user. `""` clears it

site.description: Site of the queue's system user. For a Site Manager, left out means its own site and any other site returns `403`

phone-number.description: Phone number to route to the queue. It must be in the domain's number inventory; anything but digits and `+` is stripped. Clearing it is not supported here

callqueue-hold-audio-type.description: `ringback` plays ringing while callers wait; `moh`, the default, plays the queue's music on hold

forward-on-busy.description: Where new callers go when the queue is full, or needs an agent and has none: an extension, `vmail_<extension>` for voicemail, or a number. `""` turns it off

forward-when-unregistered.description: Where callers go when no agent device is registered. `""` turns it off

forward-no-answer.description: Where callers go when the wait limit runs out, such as `vmail_4000`. `""` turns it off

callqueue-ring-timeout-seconds.description: Seconds the queue rings agents before the no-answer forward

AgentStatus.title: AgentStatus
AgentStatus.description: An agent's current call center status. Three fields name the status, because the agent log, the action paths, and the portal each spell it differently.

domain.description: Domain of the user the status belongs to

user.description: The user the status belongs to. A device agent is resolved to the user who owns the device

callqueue-agent-id.description: The agent as its queue entries hold it. The path value when the agent is on no queue

callqueue-agent-status.description: The status the agent log stores: `Auto` (Online), `Manual-avail` (Single Call), `Manual` (Offline), `Logout` (End shift), `Manual-unavail` (Unavailable), `Break`, `Lunch`, `Meeting`, `Web`, `Other`, or `cust1` to `cust8`. Older data can also hold `cust9` and `cust10`. `null` when the agent has never logged a status: treat it as unknown

callqueue-agent-status-action.description: The last path segment to `PATCH` to return to this status: `login`, `onecall`, `manual`, `logout`, or the reason itself (`Break`, `cust1`, `Manual-unavail`) on `PATCH /domains/{domain}/callqueues/all/agents/{callqueue-agent-id}/{status}`. Match a status control on this field

callqueue-agent-status-label.description: What the portal shows: `Online`, `Single Call`, `Offline`, `End shift`, `Unavailable`, the reason itself, or for `cust1` to `cust8` the domain's own label, falling back to the slot name

callqueue-agent-logged-in.description: `no` after `Logout` and for an agent who has never logged a status. Every other status counts as logged in: an offline reason means on shift but not taking calls

callqueue-agent-availability-type.description: The availability setting on the agent's queues. `mixed` when the queues disagree, which a per-queue action leaves behind. `null` when the agent is on no queue

domain.description: Domain of the queue

time_queued.description: When the call entered the queue, as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` in UTC

queued_second.description: Seconds the call has waited, as the core last reported it

prioritized.description: `yes` when the call was moved to the front of the queue

dial-rule-translation-source-name.description: Caller ID name of the caller

dial-rule-translation-source-user.description: Caller ID number of the caller

dial-rule-translation-source-host.description: Host part of the caller's address

dial-rule-translation-source-scheme.description: Scheme of the caller's address, such as `sip`

dial-rule-translation-destination-user.description: Number or extension the caller dialed

dial-rule-translation-destination-host.description: Host part of the dialed address

callqueue-agent-availability-for-dispatc.description: State of the waiting call in the queue, as the core reports it. The name is shared with an agent field and does not describe an agent here

by_sub.description: User the call was queued by, when a user transferred it in

by_uri.description: Address the call was queued by

hostSesKey.description: Session key of the call on its core server

session_key.description: Key of the waiting call, from `GET /domains/{domain}/queuedcall/{callqueue}`

prioritized.description: `yes` moves the call to the front of the queue; `no` puts it back in order

destination.description: Who to call back: an extension or phone number, dialed in the queue's domain, or a full SIP address with `@`. `PLUS` is read as `+`

filename.description: File name on the server: `greeting-` and the index with no padding, or `name.wav` for index `0`, the recorded name.

ordinal-order.description: Index of the greeting. Use it as `{index}` in the path. `0` is the recorded name (`name.wav`).

file-duration-seconds.description: Length in seconds, worked out from the file size at 8,000 bytes a second.

file-size-kilobytes.description: File size as a formatted string with its unit, `B`, `KB`, `MB`, or `GB`, despite the name.

created-datetime.description: When the file was last written.

file-access-url.description: Signed link that plays this file with no token: `GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/greetings/{index}/play` with `expires` and `signature` added. Put it straight in an `<audio>` element. It works for that one file only and expires after 24 hours by default; read the file again for a fresh link. Anyone holding it can play the file, so do not log or share it. Left out only when the server cannot sign links.

file-script-text.description: The words spoken for a text-to-speech greeting, or the description sent with an upload. Empty when none was sent. Stored on one line: line breaks become spaces and double quotes become single quotes.
file-script-text.example: Hi, you have reached extension 1001. Please leave a message after the tone.

file-source.description: How the file was made, as the client that created it said. Empty unless one was sent.

text-to-speech-voice-id.description: Voice used for a text-to-speech file. Empty for an upload.

text-to-speech-language.description: Language of the voice for a text-to-speech file. Empty for an upload.

GreetingFileList.description: Greetings in index order. The recorded name (`name.wav`) is not listed; read it as index `0`.

filename.description: File name on the server, `msg-` and the two-digit index. Stored beside the owner's music on hold (MoH) files.

ordinal-order.description: Index of the hold message. Messages are in index order. Use it as `{index}` in the path.

file-duration-seconds.description: Length in seconds, worked out from the file size at 8,000 bytes a second.

file-size-kilobytes.description: File size as a formatted string with its unit, `B`, `KB`, `MB`, or `GB`, despite the name.

created-datetime.description: When the file was last written.

file-access-url.description: Signed link that plays this file with no token: `GET /domains/{domain}/msg/{index}/play (or the user path for a user's message)` with `expires` and `signature` added. NsConfigEntry.title: NsConfigEntry
NsConfigEntry.description: One setting read from a server's API or portal config file.

config-name.description: Name of the setting

config-value.description: Value as the file sets it. For every scope, a setting whose name contains a secret keyword (`password`, `secret`, `key`, `token`, `smtp`, and others) is masked: 8 characters or fewer become at least 4 asterisks, longer values keep their first 2 and last 2 characters. Each string in an array is masked the same way

config-type.description: Type of the value in the file. Not the file: that is `source`

config-comment.description: Comment after the setting on the same line, without the `//`. Empty when there is none

config-server.description: Hostname of the server the file is on

source.description: File the setting came from: `api` or `portal`

NsConfigWrite.title: NsConfigWrite
NsConfigWrite.description: Body of a config file write.

config-name.description: Name of the setting: a PHP identifier, optionally dot-delimited, such as `NsSlowQueryThresholdMs` or `NsAllowedRedirectUris.100`. Anything else returns `400`

config-value.description: New value. Must match `config-value-type`. A string is up to 4,096 characters with no line breaks or control characters (tab is allowed). A `boolean` takes `true`, `false`, `yes`, `no`, `1`, or `0`. An `array` is a JSON array or object of strings, numbers, booleans, or null, nested up to 5 deep and up to 4,096 characters as JSON; it is written on one line. For a secret-named setting, the masked value read back and sent unchanged keeps the stored value

config-value-type.description: How the value is written into the file. Defaults to `string`. Send `boolean` for an on/off setting: the string `false` is true in PHP

config-comment.description: Comment written after the setting. Left out keeps the existing comment. A comment with a line break, a control character, `?>`, or `<?` returns `400`

config-server.description: Where to apply it: `geo` for this server and every other server in the cluster, this server's own hostname, or another cluster server's hostname (only that server is changed). Left out means this server. Any other value returns `404`

NsConfigKey.title: NsConfigKey
NsConfigKey.description: Body of a config file delete: the setting to remove.

config-name.description: Name of the setting: a PHP identifier, optionally dot-delimited, such as `NsSlowQueryThresholdMs` or `NsAllowedRedirectUris.100`. Anything else returns `400`

config-server.description: Where to apply it: `geo` for this server and every other server in the cluster, this server's own hostname, or another cluster server's hostname (only that server is changed). Left out means this server. Any other value returns `404`

enabled.description: Whether the feature is on

AnswerruleToggle.description: An answer rule feature that is only switched on or off.

time-frame.description: Time frame the rule applies to, such as `Business Hours`. `*` or `Default` creates the default rule. The time frame must already exist for the user or the domain. A time frame that already has a rule for this user returns `409`.

enabled.description: Whether the rule is used at all. A disabled rule is skipped when calls are matched. Defaults to `yes`.

simultaneous-ring.description: Rings every destination in `parameters` at the same time as the user's own devices. Each entry is an extension, a device such as `1001wp`, or a phone number.

do-not-disturb.description: Stops the user's devices from ringing. Calls go to `forward-on-dnd` when that is enabled, otherwise to voicemail.

forward-always.description: Forwards every call to the first destination in `parameters`, without ringing the user.

forward-on-active.description: Forwards a call to the destination in `parameters` when the user is already on a call.

forward-on-busy.description: Forwards a call to the destination in `parameters` when the user's devices answer busy.

forward-no-answer.description: Forwards a call to the destination in `parameters` when the user does not answer.

forward-when-unregistered.description: Forwards a call to the destination in `parameters` when none of the user's devices is registered.

forward-on-dnd.description: Forwards a call to the destination in `parameters` while `do-not-disturb` is enabled.

forward-on-spam-call.description: Forwards a call flagged as spam to the destination in `parameters`.

prompt-no-answer.description: A no-answer feature kept alongside `forward-no-answer`, which is set up and switched together with it. Takes its destination in `parameters`.

call-screening.description: Asks the caller to record their name, then plays it to the user before the call connects.

phone-numbers-to-allow.description: Caller numbers that bypass `do-not-disturb` and `call-screening` and always ring the user.

phone-numbers-to-reject.description: Caller numbers that are refused. `anonymous` matches a caller who withheld caller ID.

synchronous.description: `yes` waits up to 5 seconds for the rule to be applied and answers `200` with the new rule. If it is not applied in time, the answer is `202`. `no`, the default, answers `202` as soon as the change is accepted.

AnswerruleCreate.description: Body of a request that creates an answer rule. Send `time-frame` and at least one feature.

enabled.description: Whether the rule is used at all. A disabled rule is skipped when calls are matched.

simultaneous-ring.description: Rings every destination in `parameters` at the same time as the user's own devices. Each entry is an extension, a device such as `1001wp`, or a phone number.

do-not-disturb.description: Stops the user's devices from ringing. Calls go to `forward-on-dnd` when that is enabled, otherwise to voicemail.

forward-always.description: Forwards every call to the first destination in `parameters`, without ringing the user.

forward-on-active.description: Forwards a call to the destination in `parameters` when the user is already on a call.

forward-on-busy.description: Forwards a call to the destination in `parameters` when the user's devices answer busy.

forward-no-answer.description: Forwards a call to the destination in `parameters` when the user does not answer.

forward-when-unregistered.description: Forwards a call to the destination in `parameters` when none of the user's devices is registered.

forward-on-dnd.description: Forwards a call to the destination in `parameters` while `do-not-disturb` is enabled.

forward-on-spam-call.description: Forwards a call flagged as spam to the destination in `parameters`.

prompt-no-answer.description: A no-answer feature kept alongside `forward-no-answer`, which is set up and switched together with it. Takes its destination in `parameters`.

call-screening.description: Asks the caller to record their name, then plays it to the user before the call connects.

phone-numbers-to-allow.description: Caller numbers that bypass `do-not-disturb` and `call-screening` and always ring the user. Send `remove: yes` with `parameters` to drop those numbers. Send only `enabled` to turn every number already on the list on or off.

phone-numbers-to-reject.description: Caller numbers that are refused. `anonymous` matches a caller who withheld caller ID. Send `remove: yes` with `parameters` to drop those numbers. Send only `enabled` to turn every number already on the list on or off.

new-position.description: Moves the rule to the top (checked first) or the bottom (checked last) of the user's rules.

AnswerruleUpdate.description: Body of a request that changes an answer rule. Send only the fields to change. A feature you leave out keeps its settings.

time-frame.description: Time frame of one of the user's answer rules. `*` is the default rule.

AnswerruleReorder.description: The user's answer rules in their new order, first checked first. List every current rule exactly once.

device-provisioning-mac-address.description: MAC address of the phone: 12 hex digits with no separators.

domain.description: Domain the phone belongs to. Required unless you are a Super User. Not needed on `/domains/{domain}/phones`, where the path names it.

id.description: Device to take off the phone, such as `1002a`. Send it with `user` to free only that device's line. If the device is on line 1, the whole phone is removed.

user.description: User that owns the device in `id`, such as `1002`. Needed only when freeing one line.

PhoneDeleteRequest.description: Body of a request that removes a phone, or frees one of its lines.

description.description: New label for the park. Also renames the park's system user. An empty value sets it back to the extension. Left out, the label is not changed.

site.description: Site to file the park under. An empty value clears it. A Site Manager can only keep its own site, and any other site returns `403`.

department.description: Department to file the park under. An empty value clears it.

ParkUpdate.description: Body of a request that changes a call park. Send only the fields to change.

code.description: `201` when new audio was recorded, `200` when the recording was already current. The HTTP status is `200` either way.

message.description: Matches `code`.

content-hash.description: Fingerprint of the recording now stored.

source-type.description: `tts` when new audio was recorded. Absent when it was already current.

file.description: The audio file. Its `Content-Type` picks the decoder: `audio/mpeg` or `audio/mp3` for MP3, `audio/ogg` or `audio/webm` for Ogg or WebM, and WAV otherwise.

language.description: Language of the speech word, such as `en_us` or `fr_ca`. Defaults to `en_us`.

script.description: New text for the speech word, describing what the audio says. The stored text is kept when you leave it out.

SpeechWordUploadMultipart.description: Multipart body of an audio upload.

batch.description: Always `true`. Marks a batch answer; a request that sent one value never gets it.

count.description: Number of items in the request.

results.description: One result per item, in request order.

items.description: A succeeded item also carries the fields the single-value answer has, such as `status`.

index.description: Position of the item in the request, from `0`.

input.description: The item as sent. `null` when it was not a string.

error.description: Failed items only. Why the item failed.

code.description: Failed items only. The status the same request with this item alone would have returned.
