IpawareBatchResult.description: Answer to a request that sent an array of addresses. Each item is applied in order and reported on its own. The status is `200` when every item succeeded and `207` when at least one failed.

code.description: HTTP status code, repeated in the body.

message.description: Why the request failed. Read it for troubleshooting; it is not a stable value to match on.

detail.description: Only on `503` for a server that could not be reached. The transport error behind `message`.

retry-after.description: Only on `503` while calls to this server are paused. Seconds until the next call is sent to it. The `Retry-After` header carries the same value.

method.description: Only alongside `detail`. Method of the request that failed.

IpawareProxyOrServiceError.description: Error body in one of two forms. The API answers with `code` and `message` for failures it decides itself: your scope, an unknown server, or a server it cannot reach. The IP rules service answers with `error` for failures it decides, and that body is passed through unchanged.

IpawareAllowedIpAnswer.description: Answer to an allow-list change: the single-entry result when you sent one value, or the batch result when you sent an array.

IpawareFirewallOpAnswer.description: Answer to a block or unblock: the single-address result when you sent one value, or the batch result when you sent an array.

IpawareConfigUpdate.description: Configuration keys to set, as an object of key names and values, such as `{"firewall_block_ttl": 86400}`. You can also wrap them in `updates`. Integer keys take an integer. Yes-or-no keys take `yes` or `no`, and `true` or `false` are converted. Text values must be one line with no `#`. `listen_addr` and `listen_port` cannot be changed here.

updates.description: Optional wrapper. When present, only the keys inside it are applied.

value.description: New value. Integer keys take an integer. Yes-or-no keys take `yes` or `no`, and `true` or `false` are converted. Text values must be one line with no `#`.

IpawareConfigValue.description: New value for one configuration key.

push-device.description: AOR of the device that gets the notifications, as `sip:<device>@<domain>`. Must be an existing device within your reach.

push-device-token.description: Push token the app got from its push service. Printable ASCII, at most 1,024 characters. A `pwa` token is URL-decoded first. A masked value is refused.

push-network.description: Push service the token belongs to: `firebase` (Firebase Cloud Messaging, Android), `apns` (Apple Push Notification service, iOS), `apns_chat` (an Apple token used for chat and messages only), or `pwa` (a web push subscription for a progressive web app). Defaults to `firebase`.

push-test.description: `yes` sends Apple notifications through Apple's development (sandbox) service, for a development build of the app. Applies to `apns` only. Defaults to `no`.

domain.description: Your own domain, to identify you on `/push` below Reseller. It never changes the registration's owner. Ignored on the domain and user paths, which take it from the path.

user.description: Your own user (extension), or `~`, to identify you below Reseller on `/push` and `/domains/{domain}/push`. It never changes the registration's owner. Ignored on the user path.

PushCreate.description: Body of a push registration create.

push-device-token.description: Token of the registration to change. Finds the registration; it is not itself changed.

push-device.description: Moves the registration to another device of the same user, as `sip:<device>@<domain>`.

push-network.description: Push service the token belongs to: `firebase` (Firebase Cloud Messaging, Android), `apns` (Apple Push Notification service, iOS), `apns_chat` (an Apple token used for chat and messages only), or `pwa` (a web push subscription for a progressive web app). Defaults to `firebase`.

push-test.description: `yes` sends Apple notifications through Apple's development (sandbox) service, for a development build of the app. Applies to `apns` only.

domain.description: Your own domain, to identify you on `/push` below Reseller. It never changes the registration's owner. Ignored on the domain and user paths, which take it from the path.

user.description: Your own user (extension), or `~`, to identify you below Reseller on `/push` and `/domains/{domain}/push`. It never changes the registration's owner. Ignored on the user path.

PushUpdate.description: Body of a push registration update. The token finds the registration.

push-device.description: AOR of the device to unregister, as `sip:<device>@<domain>`. Required unless `push-network` is `pwa`.

push-device-token.description: Token to remove. It must be registered on `push-device`. Without it the registrations stay, and only the device's push delivery is switched off.

push-network.description: Push service the token belongs to: `firebase` (Firebase Cloud Messaging, Android), `apns` (Apple Push Notification service, iOS), `apns_chat` (an Apple token used for chat and messages only), or `pwa` (a web push subscription for a progressive web app). `pwa` removes the user's web push registrations. `apns_chat` leaves call notifications on.

domain.description: Your own domain, to identify you on `/push` below Reseller. On a `pwa` delete on `/push` it names the user's domain. Ignored on the domain and user paths.

user.description: Your own user (extension), or `~`, to identify you below Reseller on `/push` and `/domains/{domain}/push`. On a `pwa` delete it names whose web push registrations go. Ignored on the user path.

PushDelete.description: Body of a push unregister. `push-device` is required unless `push-network` is `pwa`.

response.description: Always `ok`: the change is accepted and applied shortly after.

device.description: AOR of the device the change applies to. Absent when a `pwa` delete removes web push registrations.

PushWriteResult.description: Answer to a push register or unregister.

time-frame.description: Read only. Time frame of the answering rule the list belongs to. Always `*`, the default rule.

domain.description: Domain the list belongs to.

user.description: User the list belongs to. `domain` for the domain-wide list.

enabled.description: Whether the default answering rule is in use.

is-active.description: Read only. Whether the rule is handling calls now. Always `true` here, because only the default rule is returned.

phone-numbers-to-reject.description: Blocked-number list. `null` when the list is empty.

enabled.description: Whether blocking is on. When `no`, calls from these numbers are not rejected.

parameters.description: Blocked numbers, as strings of 8 to 14 digits.

NumberFilter.description: Blocked-number list of a user or a domain, as it is read.

phone-numbers-to-reject.description: Numbers to block, and whether blocking is on.

enabled.description: Whether blocking is on for the numbers sent. With an empty `parameters` list, applies to every number already on the list. Defaults to `yes`.

anyOf.description: Number as a string. Use this form for a number with a leading zero.

parameters.description: Numbers to add, each 8 to 14 digits with no `+`, spaces, or other characters. Send a number with a leading zero as a string. A single number in place of the list is taken as a one-item list. Leave empty to pause or resume the whole list.

NumberFilterWrite.description: Body of a request that adds blocked numbers, or pauses or resumes the whole list.

anyOf.description: Number as a string, as a read returns it.

parameters.description: Numbers to remove, as a read returns them. Any non-empty value is accepted, so a number stored in another format can still be removed. A single number in place of the list is taken as a one-item list.

NumberFilterRemove.description: Body of a request that removes blocked numbers.

type.description: Kind of backup. Send it as `type` when you restore.

day.description: Index of the restore point. Nightly backups use the day of the week, `0` (Sunday) to `6`. Manual backups use the `backup-index` the backup returned. Send it as `index` when you restore.

lastModified.description: When the newest file in the restore point was stored, in UTC with milliseconds, such as `2026-09-01T07:00:12.000Z`.

date_updated.description: When the restore point was last updated, in the same form as `lastModified`.

sql-file-count.description: Number of database files in the restore point.

sql-file-size-bytes.description: Total size of the database files, in bytes.

confirmation-value.description: Value to send as `confirmation-value` when you restore this point. It changes when the restore point changes.

files.description: Stored files behind the restore point. Returned only with `show-file-details=yes`.

LastModified.description: When the file was stored, in UTC.

Size.description: Size of the file, in bytes.

RestorePoint.description: One backup a domain can be restored from.

additionalProperties.description: Restore points on this server, newest first.

RestorePointsByServer.description: Restore points keyed by the hostname of the server that holds them, each list newest first. With no restore points, the API returns an empty array, `[]`, instead of an object.

core-server.description: Server the restored backup came from.

domain.description: Domain that was restored.

type.description: Kind of backup that was restored.

ordinal-order.description: Index of the restore point that was restored.

resultsArr.description: Import result for each database file, keyed by file name. `false` means the file could not be imported at all.

oneOf.title: Imported
oneOf.description: Statement counts for the imported file.

oneOf.title: Not imported
oneOf.description: The target database was not reachable or does not exist.

syncResults.description: Result of restoring the domain's stored files, as reported by the backup service.

logs.description: Link to the backup log dashboard for this server and domain, covering the last 2 hours. Absent when the platform has no backup log dashboard.

RestoreResult.description: Result of a domain restore. With `geo` set to `yes`, only `logs` is returned.

status.description: Confirms the backup started.

backup-log-link.description: Link to the backup log dashboard for this server, covering the last 2 hours. Absent when the platform has no backup log dashboard.

FullBackupStartResponse.description: Result of a request that starts the full system backup.

hostname.description: Server that holds the backup, as keyed in the restore-point list.

type.description: Kind of backup, from the restore point's `type`.

index.description: Restore point to restore, from its `day`. Nightly backups use `0` to `6`. Manual backups use the `backup-index` the backup returned.

confirmation-value.description: The restore point's `confirmation-value`, from the restore-point list. It proves you picked the point that exists now.

geo.description: `yes` queues the restore and answers at once, without waiting for it to finish.

DomainRestoreRequest.description: Restore point to restore the domain in the path from.

common-name.description: Hostname the certificate is issued for, and the key that addresses it. Use a fully qualified domain name whose CNAME or A record points at this cluster. Up to 63 characters: letters, digits, dots, hyphens, and underscores. Can't contain `*` (put a wildcard in `subject-alternative-name`) and can't be `validate`, `count`, or `list`, in any case. Can't be changed later.

subject-alternative-name.description: Comma-separated list of extra hostnames the certificate covers. Each entry is a hostname that points at this cluster, or a wildcard with a single leading `*.` label such as `*.example.com`. A wildcard requires `challenge-type` `dns-01`. Spaces around entries and empty entries are removed, and the result can be up to 512 characters.

reseller.description: Super User only. Territory that owns the certificate, or `*` for a system-level certificate. A Super User who leaves it out on create gets `*`. For a Reseller token, the token's own territory is always used, and `*` returns `400`.

account-email-address.description: Email address registered with Let's Encrypt for this certificate. Expiry notices go here. Up to 63 characters.

challenge-type.description: How Let's Encrypt confirms you control the hostnames. `http-01` fetches a file from each hostname over HTTP and suits most certificates. `dns-01` checks a DNS TXT record and is required when `subject-alternative-name` has a wildcard. Defaults to `http-01`.

default-ssl-cert.description: Super User only. `yes` makes this the web server's default certificate, served for any hostname that has no certificate of its own. A Reseller that sends `yes` gets `400`.

replicate-ssl-cert.description: Where the certificate is installed. `yes` installs it on every server in the cluster. `ndp` installs it on the Endpoints server, for phone provisioning: the request is then sent to that server directly, and fails with `400` when none is configured or `502` when it does not accept the request. `no` keeps it on the server that issued it. Defaults to `yes`.

SslCertificateCreate.description: Body of a request that creates an SSL certificate.

subject-alternative-name.description: Comma-separated list of extra hostnames the certificate covers. Replaces the current list. Each entry is a hostname, or a wildcard with a single leading `*.` label such as `*.example.com`. A wildcard requires `challenge-type` `dns-01`. Spaces around entries and empty entries are removed, and the result can be up to 512 characters. Send `na` to remove every alternative name.

reseller.description: Super User only. Territory that owns the certificate, or `*` for a system-level certificate. For a Reseller token, the token's own territory is always used, and `*` returns `400`.

account-email-address.description: Email address registered with Let's Encrypt for this certificate. Expiry notices go here. Up to 63 characters.

expiration-datetime.description: Send `0` to renew the certificate on the certificate manager's next check. Don't echo the value from a read: any other value is overwritten when the certificate is next issued. Also accepts a Unix timestamp or a `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` date, read as UTC.

challenge-type.description: How Let's Encrypt confirms you control the hostnames. `http-01` fetches a file from each hostname over HTTP. `dns-01` checks a DNS TXT record and is required when `subject-alternative-name` has a wildcard. A field you leave out keeps its stored value, so a certificate that already has a wildcard keeps needing `dns-01`.

default-ssl-cert.description: Super User only. `yes` makes this the web server's default certificate, served for any hostname that has no certificate of its own. A Reseller that sends `yes` gets `400`.

SslCertificateUpdate.description: Body of a request that changes an SSL certificate. Send only the fields to change. A field you leave out keeps its stored value.

number.description: SMS number: digits with the country code and no `+`, such as `15555550100`. A number belongs to one domain only. Use digits only, or the number cannot be changed or deleted by its path later.

application.description: What the number delivers to: `user` for a user's extension, `callqueue` for a call queue, or `available` for the domain's pool of unassigned numbers.

dest.description: Extension or call queue that receives messages to this number. Required in practice for `user` and `callqueue`. Cleared when `application` is `available`.

carrier.description: SMS carrier that sends and receives messages for this number, such as `bandwidth`. It must be a carrier configured on the platform, listed by `GET /smscarriers`. Matched without regard to case and stored as the configured name.

notes.description: Free-text note, for example why the number was released.

SmsNumberCreate.description: Body of a request that adds an SMS number to a domain.

application.description: What the number delivers to: `user` for a user's extension, `callqueue` for a call queue, or `available` for the domain's pool of unassigned numbers. Required on every update.

dest.description: New extension or call queue for the number. Omit it to keep the current one. Cleared when `application` is `available`.

carrier.description: SMS carrier that sends and receives messages for this number, such as `bandwidth`. It must be a carrier configured on the platform, listed by `GET /smscarriers`. Matched without regard to case and stored as the configured name.

notes.description: Free-text note, for example why the number was released.

SmsNumberUpdate.description: Body of a request that changes an SMS number. The number itself comes from the path.

conference-sip-uri.description: Read only. SIP address of the bridge, `sip:<conference>.<domain>@conference-bridge`. It is the conference's key.

conference-owner-domain.description: Read only. Domain the conference belongs to.

conference-owner-user.description: Extension that owns the conference. It is also the conference's `{conference}` key. Returned as a number when it is numeric.

conference-leader-pin.description: PIN a caller enters to join as leader. Masked unless you send `include-secret=yes` and may see it. Empty when none is set.

conference-participants-pin.description: PIN a caller enters to join as a participant. Masked unless you send `include-secret=yes` and may see it. Empty when none is set.

conference-speaker-pin.description: PIN a caller enters to join as speaker. Masked unless you send `include-secret=yes` and may see it. Empty when none is set.

conference-participants-count-current.description: Read only. Number of participants on the bridge now.

limits-max-participants.description: Maximum participants, 1 to 99. `-` means no limit.

conference-time-begin.description: Deprecated. Use `conference-time-begin-datetime`. Start of a scheduled conference, as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`, or `0000-00-00 00:00:00` when the conference is not scheduled.

conference-time-end.description: Deprecated. Use `conference-time-end-datetime`. End of a scheduled conference, as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`, or `0000-00-00 00:00:00` when the conference is not scheduled.

conference-time-begin-datetime.description: Read only. Start of a scheduled conference. `null` when the conference is not scheduled.

conference-time-end-datetime.description: Read only. End of a scheduled conference. `null` when the conference is not scheduled.

conference-announcement-join.description: Audio file played when a participant joins. `null.wav` when join and leave announcements are off.

conference-announcement-depart.description: Audio file played when a participant leaves. `null.wav` when join and leave announcements are off.

dial-plan.description: Dial plan the bridge uses for its actions.

conference-save-participants-enabled.description: Whether participants are kept on the bridge after they leave, so they can be called back.

conference-request-name-enabled.description: Whether callers are asked to record their name when they join.

conference-lock-participants-enabled.description: Whether the bridge is locked to new participants.

conference-announce-participants-enabled.description: Whether joins and departures are announced.

conference-trigger-by.description: Bridge setting kept with the conference. Leave it unchanged.

conference-require-leader-to-start.description: `to-start` when the conference starts only once a leader joins, `no` otherwise.

conference-quorum-minimum-participants.description: Participants needed before the conference starts. `0` means no minimum.

conference-sip-proxy.description: SIP proxy of the bridge's device. Empty for the default.

conference-sip-auth-user.description: SIP authentication user of the bridge's device. Defaults to the owner extension. Returned as a number when it is numeric.

conference-sip-auth-key.description: SIP password of the bridge's device. Masked unless you send `include-secret=yes` and may see it.

conference-registration-required-enabled.description: Whether the bridge's device must register and authenticate.

utc-offset.description: UTC offset of the conference schedule, in hours.

conference-audio-directory.description: Bridge setting kept with the conference. Leave it unchanged.

conference-prompt-audio-id.description: Bridge setting kept with the conference. Leave it unchanged.

conference-options.description: Bridge setting kept with the conference. Leave it unchanged.

earliest.description: Read only. Present only with `filter_bridges=num_participants`: when the first active participant joined, as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` in UTC.

duration.description: Read only. Present only with `filter_bridges=num_participants`: seconds since the first active participant joined.

ConferenceRecord.description: A conference bridge as it is read.

conference.description: Extension of a dedicated conference. For an owned conference it is replaced by `conference-owner-user`.

conference-type.description: `owned` gives an existing user a personal bridge, reached through `conference-direct-dial-number`. `dedicated` creates a bridge with its own extension, and creates the system user for that extension when it does not exist.

conference-name.description: Display name of the conference. Keep it to 40 characters, the most an update accepts.

conference-owner-user.description: Extension that owns the conference. For a dedicated conference, send the same value as `conference`.

conference-direct-dial-number.description: Required for an owned conference. Number that dials straight into the bridge. It must not be an existing user's extension.

conference-leader-pin.description: PIN a caller enters to join as leader, up to 6 digits. Requires `conference-participants-pin`. Send it as a string to keep a leading zero.

conference-participants-pin.description: PIN a caller enters to join as a participant, up to 6 digits. Send it as a string to keep a leading zero.

conference-speaker-pin.description: PIN a caller enters to join as speaker. Send it as a string to keep a leading zero.

conference-sip-auth-key.description: SIP password of the bridge's device. Omit it to have a random one generated.

limits-max-participants.description: Maximum participants. A number below 1 is stored as 1 and above 99 as 99. `-` or `unlimited` means no limit.

conference-quorum-minimum-participants.description: Participants needed before the conference starts. `0` means no minimum. Any other value is stored as `2`.

conference-require-leader-to-start.description: `yes` or `to-start` starts the conference only once a leader joins, and then `conference-leader-pin` is required. Stored as `to-start` or `no`.

conference-announce-participants-enabled.description: Whether joins and departures are announced.

conference-request-name-enabled.description: Whether callers are asked to record their name when they join.

conference-save-participants-enabled.description: Whether participants are kept on the bridge after they leave.

conference-direct-dial-number.description: New number that dials straight into the bridge. The old direct-dial rule is replaced. It must not be an existing user's extension.

conference-leader-pin.description: PIN a caller enters to join as leader, up to 6 digits. Requires `conference-participants-pin`, sent or already set. An empty string clears it. A masked value leaves it unchanged.

conference-participants-pin.description: PIN a caller enters to join as a participant, up to 6 digits. An empty string clears it. A masked value leaves it unchanged.

conference-speaker-pin.description: PIN a caller enters to join as speaker. A masked value leaves it unchanged.

conference-sip-auth-key.description: New SIP password of the bridge's device. A masked value leaves it unchanged.

limits-max-participants.description: Maximum participants. A number below 1 is stored as 1 and above 99 as 99. `-` or `unlimited` means no limit.

conference-quorum-minimum-participants.description: Participants needed before the conference starts. `0` means no minimum. Any other value is stored as `2`.

conference-require-leader-to-start.description: `yes` or `to-start` starts the conference only once a leader joins, and then `conference-leader-pin` must be in the same request. A masked leader PIN counts. Stored as `to-start` or `no`.

conference-announce-participants-enabled.description: Whether joins and departures are announced.

conference-request-name-enabled.description: Whether callers are asked to record their name when they join.

conference-save-participants-enabled.description: Whether participants are kept on the bridge after they leave.

ConferenceUpdate.description: Changes to a conference bridge. Send only the fields to change. A masked PIN or SIP password, as a read returns it, leaves the stored value unchanged.

participant_match.description: Read only. SIP address of the participant on the bridge.

conference-sip-uri.description: Read only. SIP address of the conference.

name.description: Display name of the participant.

aor_user.description: Read only. User part of the participant's address.

aor_host.description: Read only. Host part of the participant's address.

contact.description: Read only. SIP contact of the participant's call leg.

received_from.description: Read only. Address the participant's call came from.

user_agent.description: Read only. User agent of the participant's device.

core-server.description: Read only. Server handling the participant's call.

pin.description: Read only. PIN the participant joined with. Masked unless you send `include-secret=yes` and may see it. Empty when none was entered.

call-start-datetime.description: Read only. When the participant joined.

auto-answer-enabled.description: Whether the participant's device is asked to answer automatically when the bridge calls it.

conference-participant-persistent-enable.description: Whether the participant stays on the bridge's list after hanging up.

conference-participant-mode.description: Read only. Call state of the participant. `active` while the participant is connected.

conference-participant-rate.description: Read only. Audio sample rate of the participant's call, in hertz.

gain_tx.description: Read only. Transmit gain applied to the participant.

gain_rx.description: Read only. Receive gain applied to the participant.

audioId.description: Read only. Audio stream the participant is on. Filter on it with the `audioId` query parameter.

media.description: Read only. Audio codec of the participant's call.

created-datetime.description: Read only. When the participant entry was last written.

ConferenceParticipantRecord.description: A participant on a conference bridge, as it is read.

conference-participant-sip-uri.description: Number or SIP address of the participant, such as `15555550100` or `sip:1001@example.com`. It is stored as `sip:<user>@conference-bridge`. The user part can be at most 11 characters unless the domain allows longer.

name.description: Display name of the participant.

call.description: `yes`, the default, has the bridge call the participant now. `no` only adds the participant to the bridge's list.

auto-answer-enabled.description: Whether the participant's device is asked to answer automatically when the bridge calls it.

conference-participant-persistent-enable.description: Whether the participant stays on the bridge's list after hanging up.

ConferenceParticipantCreate.description: A participant to add to a conference bridge.

name.description: Display name of the participant.

auto-answer-enabled.description: Whether the participant's device is asked to answer automatically when the bridge calls it.

conference-participant-persistent-enable.description: Whether the participant stays on the bridge's list after hanging up.

ConferenceParticipantUpdate.description: Changes to a participant on a conference bridge. Send only the fields to change; the rest keep their values.

domain.description: Read only. Domain of the conference.

conf_name.description: Read only. Name of the conference at the time of the session.

conference-sip-uri.description: Read only. SIP address of the conference.

conference-session-id.description: Read only. Identifier of the session.

conference-session-start-datetime.description: Read only. When the session started.

conference-session-end-datetime.description: Read only. When the session ended.

conference-session-duration-seconds.description: Read only. Length of the session in seconds.

conference-session-participants-count.description: Read only. Number of participant sessions in the session.

conference-session-participants.description: Read only. Present only with `include-participants=yes`: each participant's part in the session, earliest join first.

domain.description: Domain of the conference.

user.description: User part of the participant's address.

conference-participant-host.description: Host part of the participant's address.

conference-participant-contact.description: SIP contact of the participant's call leg.

call-id.description: SIP Call-ID of the participant's call leg.

conference-participant-received-from.description: Address the participant's call came from.

conference-participant-role.description: Role of the participant in the session.

conference-participant-direction.description: Direction of the participant's call leg.

conference-participant-duration-seconds.description: How long the participant was in the session, in seconds.

conference-session-report-url.description: Read only. Reserved for a link to the session report. Always empty.

ConferenceSessionSummary.description: Summary of one past session of a conference bridge.

CallDialRequest.title: Dial a number
CallDialRequest.description: Start a call: ring the first party, then dial the destination once that party answers.

call-id.description: Call ID for the new call. Generate a random value and keep it: it is the `{callid}` you use to read, transfer, hold, or end the call.

dial-rule-application.description: Dial-rule application that routes the call. Omit it for an ordinary call, `call`. Sending it empty returns `400`.

call-term-user.description: Destination dialed once the first party answers: an extension, a phone number, or a SIP URI. A value without `@` is dialed in the domain in the path. `PLUS` in the value is sent as `+`.

call-orig-user.description: First party to ring, as a user (`1001@example.com`), a device (`sip:1001wp@example.com`), or a number. Defaults to the user in the path. A user must be in the same domain as the path. Basic User, Advanced User, Simple User, and Call Center Agent tokens can name only their own user or one of their own devices, or an outside number or SIP address.

auto-answer-enabled.description: Whether the first party's device is asked to answer automatically. Defaults to `no`.

caller-id-number.description: Caller ID shown to the destination. Defaults to the caller ID of the user in the path.

callback-caller-id-number.description: Caller ID shown to the first party when it is rung. Defaults to the caller ID of the user in the path.

call-term-added-sip-header.description: Extra SIP header for the destination leg. Only a `P-Served-Parameters` header is accepted; any other value is ignored.

CallRecordRequest.title: Record an audio file
CallRecordRequest.description: Ring a phone so its user can record a greeting, music on hold, or a message by voice.

call-id.description: Call ID for the new call. Generate a random value and keep it to follow or end the call.

call-term-user.description: Phone to ring for the recording: an extension, a number, or a SIP URI. `PLUS` in the value is sent as `+`.

call-record-type.description: Kind of file to record. `greeting` is a voicemail greeting, `moh` a music on hold file, and `mesg` a message file.

call-record-index.description: Index of the file to record. Greeting `0` is the recorded name.

auto-answer-enabled.description: Whether the phone is asked to answer automatically. Defaults to `no`.

caller-id-number.description: Caller ID shown on the phone that is rung.

CallCreateRequest.description: Body of a request that starts a call. `dial-rule-application` selects the shape: omit it or send `call` to dial a number, or send `record` to ring a phone for a voice recording.

CallActionRequest.description: Body of a call control action. Which fields apply depends on the action.

call-term-user.description: For `answer`, the device that answers, such as `sip:1001wp@example.com`. For `transfer`, `xfer`, and `transferPeer`, the transfer destination. Required for `answer`.

hostname.description: For an attended `transfer`, the core server that holds the call to merge in, from its `core-server`. Send it with `call-destination-session-id`.

call-destination-session-id.description: For an attended `transfer`, the `call-session-id` of the call to merge in. Send it with `hostname`.

state.description: For `recording`, the recording state to set. Required for `recording`.

valid.description: For `park` and `transferPeer`, a comma-separated list of call park names to choose from. The first free one is used.

prefix.description: For `park` and `transferPeer` with `valid`, text put before the chosen park name to form the destination.

ActiveCallHistory.description: Count of concurrent calls over time, one point per bucket, oldest first.

domain.description: Domain the series covers. Present for a domain series.

reseller.description: Reseller the series covers. Present for a reseller series.

scope.description: `system` for the platform-wide series. Present only then.

range.description: Window the series covers, ending now.

type.description: Which calls are counted. The platform-wide series always counts all calls, whatever this says.

start.description: Start of the first bucket, as a Unix timestamp in seconds.

end.description: Start of the last bucket, as a Unix timestamp in seconds.

start-datetime.description: Start of the first bucket in RFC 3339 form, in the server's time zone. Same instant as `start`.

end-datetime.description: Start of the last bucket in RFC 3339 form, in the server's time zone. Same instant as `end`.

data-points.description: One point per bucket from `start` to `end`. A bucket with no data counts `0`.

timestamp.description: Start of the bucket, as a Unix timestamp in seconds.

datetime.description: Start of the bucket in RFC 3339 form, in the server's time zone.

active-calls.description: Most calls in progress at once during the bucket.

CallActivityReportRequest.description: Body of a concurrent-call report request.

start_date.description: Start of the report window, such as `2026-09-01 00:00:00`. Any date and time PHP can parse is accepted. Must be before `end_date`.

end_date.description: End of the report window, in the same form as `start_date`.

group_by.description: What to break the report down by. `huntgroup` and `callswaiting` report the call queues of `domain` and need it. `hostname` breaks it down by core server and is for Super User scopes only. Any other value returns `400`.

report_by.description: Bucket size: one minute, ten minutes, one hour, or one day. Minute data is kept for about 3.5 hours and hourly data for 15 days. Any other value returns `400`.

type.description: Which calls to count: calls between users on the platform, calls to or from outside it, or both. Any other value returns `400`.

domain.description: Domain to report on. Required with `group_by` `huntgroup` or `callswaiting`. A domain that does not exist, or for a Reseller one outside its territory, returns `403`.

value_offset.description: For `huntgroup` and `callswaiting`, hours to subtract from each bucket time, such as `5 HOUR`. Ignored with `report_by=day`.

reseller.description: Reseller the image applies to. `*` means every reseller.

domain.description: Domain the image applies to. `*` means every domain in the reseller.

server.description: Hostname of the server the image applies to. `*` means every server.

description.description: What the image is used for, as stored. Empty when none was given.

file-mime-type.description: Media type of the image, such as `image/png`. It is detected from the file's contents when the image is uploaded.

file-size-bytes.description: Size of the image file in bytes.

file-access-url.description: Link that downloads the image file itself. Query values in it are percent-encoded, so `*` appears as `%2A`.

ImageDetails.description: An image's details. The image file itself is not included; download it from `file-access-url`.

ImageUpload.title: Upload a file
ImageUpload.description: The image as a multipart file part named `file`, with the other values as form fields.

file.description: The image file. The part's `Content-Type` must be `image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `image/gif`, `image/webp`, or `image/x-icon`, and the file's contents must match one of those types; anything else, including SVG, returns `400`. The part may also be named `File`. An empty file returns `400`.

reseller.description: Reseller the image applies to. `*`, the default, means every reseller. A Reseller token can name only its own reseller.

domain.description: Domain the image applies to, such as `example.com`. `*`, the default, means every domain in the reseller. A Reseller token can name only a domain in its own reseller.

server.description: Hostname of the server the image applies to, such as `core1.example.com`. `*`, the default, means every server.

description.description: What the image is used for. Optional; stored as sent.

ImageBase64.title: Base64 file
ImageBase64.description: The image as base64 in `file-base64`, with its media type in `file-mime-type`. The legacy names `base64_file` and `filetype` are also accepted.

file-base64.description: The image file as standard base64, without a `data:` prefix. A value that is not valid base64 returns `400`, and so does one that decodes to an empty file.

file-mime-type.description: Media type of the image: `image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `image/gif`, `image/webp`, or `image/x-icon`. The decoded file's contents must also be one of those types. Any other value, or none, returns `400`. The type detected from the contents is the one stored.

reseller.description: Reseller the image applies to. `*`, the default, means every reseller. A Reseller token can name only its own reseller.

domain.description: Domain the image applies to, such as `example.com`. `*`, the default, means every domain in the reseller. A Reseller token can name only a domain in its own reseller.

server.description: Hostname of the server the image applies to, such as `core1.example.com`. `*`, the default, means every server.

description.description: What the image is used for. Optional; stored as sent.

reseller.description: Reseller the image applies to. `*`, the default, means every reseller. A Reseller token can name only its own reseller.

domain.description: Domain the image applies to, such as `example.com`. `*`, the default, means every domain in the reseller. A Reseller token can name only a domain in its own reseller.

server.description: Hostname of the server the image applies to, such as `core1.example.com`. `*`, the default, means every server.

ImageLocation.description: Which stored copy of an image to act on. Omitted fields default to `*`.

voicemail-reminder-phonecall-enabled.description: Whether reminders are sent as phone calls to the numbers in `voicemail-reminder-phonecall-phonenumber-array`.

voicemail-reminder-phonecall-phonenumber.description: Phone numbers to call, 3 to 15 digits with an optional leading `+`, such as `15555550100`. At most 10. The list replaces the stored one. Send `[]` to clear it.

voicemail-reminder-sms-enabled.description: Whether reminders are sent as SMS messages to the numbers in `voicemail-reminder-sms-phonenumber-array`.

voicemail-reminder-sms-phonenumber-array.description: Numbers to text, 3 to 15 digits with an optional leading `+`, such as `15555550100`. At most 10. The list replaces the stored one. Send `[]` to clear it.

voicemail-reminder-email-enabled.description: Whether reminders are sent by email to the addresses in `voicemail-reminder-email-address-array`.

voicemail-reminder-email-address-array.description: Email addresses to notify, each a valid address of up to 254 characters. At most 10. The list replaces the stored one. Send `[]` to clear it.

voicemail-reminder-interval-minutes.description: Minutes between reminders while the user has unheard voicemail. A whole number, at least 5.

VmailnagWrite.description: Body of a request that creates or changes a user's voicemail reminder settings. Every field is optional. The user is the one in the path. When reminders were last sent and which server sends them are set by the platform and cannot be written.

reseller.description: Reseller the template applies to. `*` means every reseller.

domain.description: Domain the template applies to. `*` means every domain in the reseller.

server.description: Hostname of the server the template applies to. `*` means every server.

description.description: What the template is used for, as stored. Empty when none was given.

file-mime-type.description: Media type of the template, detected from the file's contents when it was uploaded: `text/html`, `text/plain`, `text/x-php` for one whose contents read as PHP, such as a file that begins with `<?php`, or `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.word` for a Word `.docx`. Templates stored earlier can carry the type they were uploaded with, such as `text/php`.

file-size-bytes.description: Size of the template file in bytes. At most 1,048,576 for a template uploaded through this API.

file-access-url.description: Link that downloads the template file itself. Query values in it are percent-encoded, so `*` appears as `%2A`.

TemplateDetails.description: A template's details. The template file itself is not included; download it from `file-access-url`.

TemplateUpload.title: Upload a file
TemplateUpload.description: The template as a multipart file part named `file`, with the other values as form fields. Send it with `Content-Type: multipart/form-data`.

file.description: The template file: HTML, plain text, or a Word `.docx`, at most 1 MB. The file's contents are checked and the type detected from them is stored. The part's `Content-Type` is optional (`application/octet-stream` counts as none); when it names a type, it must be `text/html`, `text/plain`, a PHP text type such as `text/php`, or a Word or zip type for a `.docx`, and match the contents. Anything else returns `400`, and so does an empty file. The part may also be named `File`.

reseller.description: Reseller the template applies to. `*`, the default, means every reseller. A Reseller token can name only its own reseller.

domain.description: Domain the template applies to, such as `example.com`. `*`, the default, means every domain in the reseller. A Reseller token can name only a domain in its own reseller.

server.description: Hostname of the server the template applies to, such as `core1.example.com`. `*`, the default, means every server.

description.description: What the template is used for. Optional; stored as sent.

TemplateBase64.title: Base64 file
TemplateBase64.description: The template as base64 in `file-base64`, with its media type in `file-mime-type`. The legacy names `base64_file` and `filetype` are also accepted. Send the body with `Content-Type: application/json`.

file-base64.description: The template file as standard base64, without a `data:` prefix. The decoded file must be HTML, plain text, or a Word `.docx`, and at most 1 MB (1,048,576 bytes). A value that is not valid base64, that decodes to an empty file, or that decodes to any other kind of file returns `400`; a larger file returns `413`.

file-mime-type.description: Media type of the template. Optional: omit it, or send `application/octet-stream`, and the type is taken from the file's contents. When sent, it must be `text/html`, `text/plain`, a PHP text type such as `text/php`, or, for a `.docx`, `application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document` or `application/zip`, and it must name the same kind as the contents; otherwise the request returns `400`. The type detected from the contents is the one stored.

reseller.description: Reseller the template applies to. `*`, the default, means every reseller. A Reseller token can name only its own reseller.

domain.description: Domain the template applies to, such as `example.com`. `*`, the default, means every domain in the reseller. A Reseller token can name only a domain in its own reseller.

server.description: Hostname of the server the template applies to, such as `core1.example.com`. `*`, the default, means every server.

description.description: What the template is used for. Optional; stored as sent.

reseller.description: Reseller the template applies to. `*`, the default, means every reseller. A Reseller token can name only its own reseller.

domain.description: Domain the template applies to, such as `example.com`. `*`, the default, means every domain in the reseller. A Reseller token can name only a domain in its own reseller.

server.description: Hostname of the server the template applies to, such as `core1.example.com`. `*`, the default, means every server.

TemplateLocation.description: Which stored copy of a template to act on. Omitted fields default to `*`.

AutoAttendantScript.title: AutoAttendantScript
AutoAttendantScript.description: A greeting to make by text to speech.

file-script-text.description: Words to speak. They are read aloud in the default voice and saved as the tier's greeting, replacing any greeting it had.
file-script-text.example: Thank you for calling. For sales, press 1.

AutoAttendantIntroInput.title: AutoAttendantIntroInput
AutoAttendantIntroInput.description: An intro greeting to add before the menu.

time-frame.description: Time frame whose calls hear the intro greeting first, then the menu. The user's answering rule for it is set to the intro. A time frame that already sends calls to an attendant returns `409`.

AutoAttendantOptionInput.title: AutoAttendantOptionInput
AutoAttendantOptionInput.description: What one key does, as sent to create or update an auto attendant. Send `destination-application` with `destination-user`, `auto-attendant` for a submenu, or `remove`. The shape **Read auto attendant** returns for a key is accepted.

destination-application.description: Where the key sends the call. `repeat-tier` plays this tier again, and `play-message` plays `audio` and returns to the menu. Any other value routes the call to `destination-user` with that application. Leave it out when the key opens a submenu.

destination-user.description: Destination of the call, such as extension `1001` or call queue `2000`. Used with every `destination-application` except `repeat-tier` and `play-message`.

caller-name-translation.description: Caller name the destination sees. `[*]`, the default, keeps the caller's name; any other text replaces it.

description.description: Label for the key, such as `Sales`. **Read auto attendant** returns it as sent, so a label you read back can be sent again unchanged.

auto-attendant.description: Submenu the key opens. It takes the same fields as the request's `auto-attendant`. A key that already opens a submenu keeps its tier number.

audio.description: With `play-message`, the message to play. With `auto-attendant`, the submenu's greeting, as **Read auto attendant** shows it. A greeting inside the submenu's own `auto-attendant` wins when both are sent.

remove.description: `yes` takes the key out of the menu. The key's other fields are ignored.

AutoAttendantTierInput.title: AutoAttendantTierInput
AutoAttendantTierInput.description: One tier of an auto attendant menu, as sent to create or update it. Only the fields you send are changed.

audio.description: Greeting of this tier, made by text to speech. It can also be sent beside the tier, where **Read auto attendant** shows it; this one wins when both are sent.

intro-greetings.description: Intro greetings played before the menu, one per time frame. Usually sent on the starting tier only. The recording for each is not set here: upload it with the greetings endpoints, using the number **Read auto attendant** shows for it.

2-digit-dial-by-extension.description: `yes` lets callers dial a 2-digit extension from this tier, and `no` turns that off. Leave it out to keep the current setting. Not shown by **Read auto attendant**.

3-digit-dial-by-extension.description: `yes` lets callers dial a 3-digit extension from this tier, and `no` turns that off. Leave it out to keep the current setting.

4-digit-dial-by-extension.description: `yes` lets callers dial a 4-digit extension from this tier, and `no` turns that off. Leave it out to keep the current setting.

5-digit-dial-by-extension.description: `yes` lets callers dial a 5-digit extension from this tier, and `no` turns that off. Leave it out to keep the current setting.

6-digit-dial-by-extension.description: `yes` lets callers dial a 6-digit extension from this tier, and `no` turns that off. Leave it out to keep the current setting. Not shown by **Read auto attendant**.

no-key-press.description: What happens when the caller presses nothing: `repeat` plays the tier again, `hangup` ends the call, and `option-<key>` does what that key does. An `option-<key>` applies only when that key is in the same request.

unassigned-key-press.description: What happens when the caller presses a key with no destination. Takes the same values as `no-key-press`.

option-1.description: What key `1` does. Keys you leave out keep their current destination.

option-2.description: What key `2` does. Keys you leave out keep their current destination.

option-3.description: What key `3` does. Keys you leave out keep their current destination.

option-4.description: What key `4` does. Keys you leave out keep their current destination.

option-5.description: What key `5` does. Keys you leave out keep their current destination.

option-6.description: What key `6` does. Keys you leave out keep their current destination.

option-7.description: What key `7` does. Keys you leave out keep their current destination.

option-8.description: What key `8` does. Keys you leave out keep their current destination.

option-9.description: What key `9` does. Keys you leave out keep their current destination.

option-0.description: What key `0` does. Keys you leave out keep their current destination.

option-*.description: What key `*` does. Keys you leave out keep their current destination.

option-#.description: What key `#` does. Keys you leave out keep their current destination.

attendant-name.description: Name of the auto attendant, shown in lists. Without it the attendant has an empty name until **Update auto attendant** sets one.

user.description: Extension that answers as the auto attendant, such as `8000`. An extension that does not exist is created as an attendant user with its own dial plan. An existing user keeps its dial plan, and the menu is added to it. It becomes `{user}` in the attendant's path.

time-frame.description: Time frame whose calls go to the attendant. The user's answering rule for it is set to send calls to the menu. Leave it out, or send `Default` or `*`, for the user's default answering rule.

audio.description: Greeting of the starting tier, sent beside it as **Read auto attendant** shows it. `auto-attendant.audio` wins when both are sent.

auto-attendant.description: Starting tier of the menu, `Prompt_100`. Submenus and greetings take the next free numbers.

synchronous.description: `yes` waits up to about five seconds for the attendant to be applied and answers `200` with it, or `202` if it is not applied by then. `no`, the default, answers `202` as soon as the request is accepted.

AutoAttendantUpdate.title: AutoAttendantUpdate
AutoAttendantUpdate.description: Changes to one tier of an auto attendant. Only the fields you send are changed. The time frame is not changed by an update.

attendant-name.description: New name of the auto attendant. Only on the attendant's starting tier: on a submenu tier it returns `400`.

audio.description: Greeting of the tier, sent beside it as **Read auto attendant** shows it. `auto-attendant.audio` wins when both are sent.

auto-attendant.description: The tier named by `{prompt}`. Only the keys and settings you send are changed.

meeting-instance-id.description: Instance of the meeting the event belongs to.

file-source.description: What wrote the event, such as `api`, or `apiv2` for events written with `POST .../log`.

source_id.description: User who wrote the event, when known.

target.description: Who or what the event is about, such as the user who joined.

details.description: Extra detail as stored, usually a JSON string. For `part_join` it describes the attendee who joined.

timestamp.description: When the event was logged, as stored.

MeetingEvent.description: One entry in a meeting's event log.

meeting-name.description: Name of the meeting, shown in invitations and in the app. Required on a create.

description.description: Longer text about the meeting, shown in invitations.

meeting-type.description: `conference` is a meeting where everyone can take part. `presentation` is a webinar: guests register themselves with the meeting's `meeting-registration-id`.

meeting-schedule-start-datetime.description: When the meeting starts, in RFC 3339 form. Unix seconds are also accepted. Omit it on a create to start the meeting now.

timezone.description: Time zone the meeting was scheduled in, such as `US/Eastern`. Used for the calendar invitation.

meeting-schedule-duration-minutes.description: Planned length in minutes. Defaults to `60` on a create.

meeting-schedule-recurrence-rule.description: Repeat rule for a recurring meeting, as an RFC 5545 `RRULE` (with any `EXDATE`), such as `FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=TU;UNTIL=20261215T150000Z`. An `UNTIL` without a trailing `Z` is read as UTC. Empty for a one-time meeting.

limits-max-participants.description: Most participants the meeting allows. Omit it on a create to use the domain's configured maximum for the meeting type.

meeting-chat-enabled.description: `1` turns on chat in the meeting.

meeting-chat-history-enabled.description: `1` keeps the chat history after the meeting.

meeting-recording-enabled.description: `1` records the meeting. On a change, turning it on starts recording now unless `meeting-require-host-to-begin-enabled` is sent as `1`, and turning it off stops recording.

meeting-join-require-invite-enabled.description: `1` admits only invited attendees. `0` lets anyone with the meeting ID join while the meeting is not locked.

meeting-join-require-passcode-enabled.description: `1` requires `meeting-passcode` to join. Sending `0` clears the passcode.

meeting-passcode.description: Passcode attendees enter to join. Kept only when `meeting-join-require-passcode-enabled` is `1`. A masked value (asterisks, as a read returns it to someone who may not see the passcode) is refused on a create and leaves the passcode unchanged on a change.

meeting-require-host-to-begin-enabled.description: `1` keeps attendees waiting until a host joins.

meeting-allow-changes-from-hosts-enabled.description: `1` lets hosts other than the owner change the meeting in the app. The API does not check it: every host can change the meeting through the API.

meeting-hide-attendee-list-enabled.description: `1` hides the attendee list from attendees who are not hosts or presenters.

meeting-lock-enabled.description: `1` locks the meeting: only attendees already connected can stay or rejoin. Takes effect on a change.

meeting-room-enabled.description: `1` makes this a permanent room rather than a scheduled meeting. List rooms with `type=room`.

meeting-status.description: Set on a change only. `started` starts recording when recording is on. `ended` ends the current instance and resets the meeting.

meeting-video-layout.description: Default video layout for the meeting.

meeting-presenter-attendee-id.description: Attendee ID of the attendee presenting now. Empty when nobody is.

meeting-dial-in-number-blob.description: Phone numbers audio-only attendees dial to join. Filled from the domain's configuration when a meeting is created without an ID.

meeting-registration-id.description: Registration ID guests use to register for a `presentation` meeting: 8 letters or digits. Generated when omitted or not in that form. Ignored for other meeting types.

attendees.description: People to invite. On a change, the list replaces the stored one: attendees left out are removed, and new ones are invited by email.

name.description: Display name.

email.description: Email address the invitation goes to.

role.description: Role in the meeting. Defaults to `attendee`.

uid.description: Platform user, as `user@domain`, when the attendee is a user on the platform.

phonenumber.description: Phone number of an attendee who joins by phone.

contact_id.description: ID of the contact the attendee came from, when any.

MeetingWrite.description: Fields a client can set when it creates or changes a meeting. Every field is optional on a change; `meeting-name` is required on a create. The meeting ID comes from the path or is generated, and the owner is the user in the path.

type.description: What to delete: `meeting` cancels the meeting, `instance` cancels one occurrence of a recurring meeting, `record` removes the meeting and its attendees for good, and `attendee` removes the attendees in `attendeeids`.

meeting-instance-schedule-start-datetime.description: Required with `type` `instance`. Scheduled start of the occurrence to cancel, in Unix seconds.

attendeeids.description: Required with `type` `attendee`. Attendee IDs to remove, 6 letters or digits each. A comma-separated string is also accepted.

MeetingDelete.description: Body of a meeting delete. `type` chooses what is deleted.

event.description: What happened, such as `part_join` or `meeting_locked`. Not checked against a list.

target.description: Who or what the event is about, such as the user who joined.

details.description: Extra detail, stored with the event. An object is stored as a JSON string.

MeetingEventWrite.description: Body of a meeting event to log. The meeting, the instance, and the writer come from the path.

id.description: Reserved meeting ID. Create the meeting with it using `POST /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/meetings/{meeting}` and the same user in the path. `999999999` means no free ID was found; ask again.

meeting-registration-id.description: Suggested registration ID for a `presentation` meeting: 8 letters or digits. Send it as `meeting-registration-id` on the create.

phonenumbers.description: Dial-in numbers configured for the user's domain. Present only when one is configured.

MeetingIdReservation.description: A meeting ID reserved for a new meeting.

name.description: Name of the guest registering, 1 to 128 characters.

email.description: Email address the meeting details are sent to. A guest already on the meeting with this address is not added again.

name.description: Display name.

screenshare_restricted.description: `1` stops the attendee sharing its screen.

access_restricted.description: `1` removes the attendee's access to the meeting.

MeetingAttendeeWrite.description: Fields of one attendee a host can change. Send only the fields to change. The meeting and the attendee come from the path; the attendee's meeting, ID, domain, and user cannot be changed.

access_token.description: Token the client presents to the video service. Treat it as a secret.

MeetingVideoToken.description: Credentials from the video service for a meeting. `access_token` is always present; the other fields are passed through as the video service sends them.

meeting.description: The meeting, as one item, with the attendee's own fields added.

MeetingAttendeeView.description: A meeting read through an attendee path. The meeting is wrapped in a one-item `meeting` array, and five fields keep their legacy names: `name` (`meeting-name`), `type` (`meeting-type`), `capacity` (`limits-max-participants`), `status` (`meeting-status`), and `duration` (`meeting-schedule-duration-minutes`).

name.description: Display name of the account at the video service, usually the organization's name.

subdomain.description: Subdomain the domain's meetings open on at the video service, such as `example`. The domain's video hostname, returned as `iotum_domain` by **Read domain video account**, is this value followed by the territory's video hostname suffix, when the territory has one.

VideoAccountCreate.description: Body of a request that creates a video account for a domain.

company-name.description: New display name of the account at the video service.

VideoAccountUpdate.description: Body of a request that changes a domain's video account.

switch-plan.description: Whether the new plan replaces the account's current plan. `yes` replaces it. `no` adds the new plan alongside the current plans. Left out, the video service's default applies. `true`, `false`, `1`, and `0` are also accepted, and any other value returns `400`.

host-limit.description: Number of hosts the subscription covers. Passed to the video service as sent.

VideoSubscriptionCreate.description: Options for a new video subscription. Every field is optional.

plans.description: Every plan the account keeps, as slugs from **List available video products**. Current subscriptions that are not listed are cancelled. `no-plan` alone cancels every subscription. A comma-separated string is also accepted.

default-plan.description: Slug of the domain's default video plan. Must be in `plans`. Required when `plans` leaves out the domain's current default plan.

VideoPlansUpdate.description: The complete set of plans for a domain's video account, and its default plan.

iotum_domain.description: The domain's video hostname, where its meetings open. Added by the API. Left out when the domain has none.

VideoAccount.description: A domain's account at the video service, as the video service returns it, plus the domain's video hostname. Apart from `iotum_domain`, the fields are set by the video service and passed through.

id.description: ID of the new account at the video service. The domain is linked to it.

VideoAccountCreateResult.description: The video service's answer to an account create, passed through. Apart from `id`, the fields are set by the video service.

id.description: ID of the subscription at the video service.

slug.description: Slug of the product, as **List available video products** lists it.

plan.description: `1` when the product is a plan, which `switch-plan` can replace.

VideoSubscription.description: One subscription of a domain's video account, as the video service returns it. Only `id`, `product.slug`, and `product.plan` are relied on by the API; the other fields are set by the video service and passed through.

slug.description: Slug that names the product in subscription requests.

VideoProduct.description: One product in the video service's catalogue, as the video service returns it. Only `slug` is relied on by the API; the other fields are set by the video service and passed through.

VideoAccountHost.description: One host of a domain's video account, as the video service returns it. The fields are set by the video service and passed through.

VideoResellerList.description: The reseller accounts under the platform's own account at the video service. The shape is set by the video service and passed through unchanged.

plan-slug.description: Read-only. Product slug of the plan the host has, or `null` for none.

iotum_domain.description: Read-only. Hostname of the domain's video portal.

IotumVideoHost.description: A user's video host as the video service reports it. Fields other than `iotum_domain` come from the video service and keep its names, except `plan_slug` and `add_on_slugs`, which are returned as `plan-slug` and `add-on-slugs`.

IotumVideoContact.description: One contact in a user's video address book, as the video service reports it. The fields come from the video service and keep its names, except `contact_id`, `first_name`, and `time_zone`, which are returned as `unique-id`, `name-first-name`, and `time-zone`.

iotum_domain.description: Read-only. Hostname of the domain's video portal. Present on a single conference only, not on list entries.

IotumVideoConference.description: One video conference as the video service reports it. The fields come from the video service and keep its names, except `start` and `time_zone`, which are returned as `meeting-schedule-start-datetime` and `time-zone`. A single conference, such as the answer to a create, also carries `iotum_domain`.

iotum_domain.description: Read-only. Hostname of the domain's video portal.

IotumVideoResult.description: The video service's answer to a change, passed through. When the answer is an object, it also carries `iotum_domain`. `plan_slug` and `add_on_slugs` are returned as `plan-slug` and `add-on-slugs`.

name.description: Name shown for the host.

email.description: Email address of the host.

password.description: Write-only. New password for signing in to the video portal directly.

role.description: Role of the host in the domain's video account, as the video service defines it. Office Manager scope or higher only.

auto_record.description: Whether the host's conferences are recorded automatically.

plan_slug.description: Plan to give the host, by its product slug. `no-plan` removes the plan. Leave it out to keep the current plan. Office Manager scope or higher only. List the domain's plans with `GET /domains/{domain}/video/products`.

diff_user.description: Public user name of the host in the video portal. A new host gets the extension.

locale.description: Language of the host's video portal. Any other value is ignored.

language.description: Same as `locale`. Used only when `locale` is not sent.

iotum_time_format.description: How the video portal shows dates and times for this host. Sent to the video service as it is.

IotumHostUpdate.description: Body of a request that changes a user's video host. Every field is optional, and only the fields you send change. Each value goes to the video service, which validates it.

participants.description: Who to invite. Each entry is an email address, or an extension in the host's domain that has a video host. An extension is invited through its video host, and an email address by email. No participant is a moderator.

start.description: When the conference starts, sent to the video service as it is. Defaults to now.

secure.description: Sent to the video service as its `secure_url` setting.

IotumConferenceCreate.description: Body of a request that starts an ad hoc video conference. Every field is optional.

domain.description: Domain to back up, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. On `POST /backup`, backs up only this domain instead of every domain on the server, with the same access as `POST /domains/{domain}/backup`. On `POST /domains/{domain}/backup`, it must name the domain in the path, or the request returns `400`.

BackupRequest.description: Optional body of a backup request. Every field is optional.

id.description: Read-only. ID of the dashboard. Use it as `dashboard_id` on the charts endpoints.

name.description: Name of the dashboard.

description.description: Description of the dashboard. No practical length limit.
description.example: Live view of the support queues.

owner_type.description: Kind of owner. `1` is a user, the only owner type that grants owner access. `null` when the dashboard has no owner.

owner_id.description: Extension of the user who owns the dashboard, such as `1001`.

public_id.description: ID of the dashboard's public link. Anyone holding it can open the dashboard. `null` when it has none.

properties.description: Display settings, as a JSON string the app defines. No practical length limit.

layouts.description: Chart positions, as a JSON string the app defines. No practical length limit.

share_type.description: Who else sees the dashboard: `select` for the rules in `share_details`, `domain` for every user in the domain, `stock` for users whose scope matches a `scope` rule in `share_details`.

share_details.description: Sharing rules, as a JSON string holding an array of `{"type": ..., "value": ...}` objects. `type` is `scope` (a scope name), `subscriber` (a user as `user@domain`), or `department` (a department name).

status.description: Status value the app defines.

domain.description: Domain the dashboard belongs to. `*` for a stock dashboard offered across the platform.

created.description: Read-only. When the dashboard was created.

last-modified-datetime.description: Read-only. When the dashboard was last changed. `null` when it never was.

favorite.description: Read-only. Whether you marked the dashboard a favorite.

hide.description: Read-only. Whether you hid the dashboard. Hidden dashboards are left out of the list and count.

DashboardDetail.description: A dashboard with its layout and sharing settings.

id.description: ID of the dashboard. On create, leave it out to have one assigned; an ID already in use returns `409`. On update, the dashboard to change.

name.description: Name of the dashboard.

description.description: Description of the dashboard. No practical length limit.
description.example: Live view of the support queues.

owner_type.description: Kind of owner. Send `1`, a user: without it the dashboard has no owner, and only an Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User can change it. Any other value needs Office Manager scope or higher for the domain.

owner_id.description: Extension of the user who owns the dashboard, such as `1001`. On create, defaults to the user in the path. Naming another user needs the right to change that user's dashboards.

public_id.description: ID of the dashboard's public link. Anyone holding it can open the dashboard.

properties.description: Display settings, as a JSON string the app defines. No practical length limit.

layouts.description: Chart positions, as a JSON string the app defines. No practical length limit.

share_type.description: Who else sees the dashboard: `select` for the rules in `share_details`, `domain` for every user in the domain, `stock` for users whose scope matches a `scope` rule in `share_details`.

share_details.description: Sharing rules, as a JSON string holding an array of `{"type": ..., "value": ...}` objects. `type` is `scope` (a scope name), `subscriber` (a user as `user@domain`), or `department` (a department name).

status.description: Status value the app defines.

DashboardRequest.description: Fields for creating or changing a dashboard. `name` is required on create; `id` is required on update.

id.description: Read-only. ID of the chart.

name.description: Name of the chart.

type.description: How the chart is drawn, such as `ResponsiveLine`, `ResponsiveStat`, or `ResponsiveTable`.

description.description: Description of the chart.

properties.description: Display settings, as a JSON string the app defines. No practical length limit.

data_sources.description: What data the chart shows, as a JSON string the app defines. No practical length limit.

status.description: Status value the app defines.

dashboard_id.description: Read-only. ID of the dashboard the chart is on.

created.description: Read-only. When the chart was created.

last-modified-datetime.description: Read-only. When the chart was last changed. `null` when it never was.

data_token.description: Read-only. Access token for loading the chart's data, issued to you with `Call Center Data` scope. It has no refresh token.

access_token.description: Bearer token with `Call Center Data` scope, issued to you.

expires_in.description: Seconds until `access_token` expires. A day, `86400`, by default.

token_type.description: How to send the token: in an `Authorization: Bearer` header.

ChartDetail.description: A chart with its properties, data sources, and data token.

id.description: ID of the chart. On create, leave it out to have one assigned; an ID already in use returns `409`. On update, the chart to change, which must be on the dashboard in the path.

name.description: Name of the chart.

type.description: How the chart is drawn, such as `ResponsiveLine`, `ResponsiveStat`, or `ResponsiveTable`.

description.description: Description of the chart.

properties.description: Display settings, as a JSON string the app defines. No practical length limit.

data_sources.description: What data the chart shows, as a JSON string the app defines. No practical length limit.

status.description: Status value the app defines.

ChartRequest.description: Fields for creating or changing a chart. `name` and `type` are required on create; `id` is required on update.

reseller.description: The reseller (territory) the domain belongs to. Required on create. Send `~` for your own territory. Changing it moves the domain and its devices to the new territory.

description.description: A display name for the domain, up to 127 characters. Defaults to the domain name.

domain-type.description:
The feature set of the domain:

- `Standard` is for a business, with a company directory and configurable PBX features
- `Residential` has no company directory and no PBX features, like an analog line
- `Hospitality` is for hotels, with limited voicemail and no company directory. Errors forward to the operator

Any other value is stored as `Standard`.

dial-plan.description: The dial plan new users in the domain get. On create, a dial plan with this name is created; it defaults to the domain name. On update, it changes the plan for users created afterward.

dial-policy.description: The dial permission new users in the domain get. Name an existing dial permission.

time-zone.description: The time zone new users in the domain get. Answering rules run in it. `timezone` is accepted as another name for this field.

language-token.description: The language new users in the domain see in the portal.

area-code.description: The area code added to a 7-digit number dialed by users in the domain.

caller-id-name.description: The caller ID name used on outbound calls when no user or site caller ID applies.

caller-id-number.description: The caller ID number used on outbound calls when no user or site caller ID applies.

caller-id-number-emergency.description: The caller ID number used on emergency calls when no user or site emergency caller ID applies.

emergency-address-id.description: The emergency address used for users that have no user or site address. Use the `address-id` of an address in the domain.

music-on-hold-enabled.description: `no` turns off music on hold for the domain: callers on hold hear silence and MoH cannot be configured.

music-on-ring-enabled.description: `yes` plays music instead of the spoken announcement while a call is forwarded or transferred.

music-on-hold-randomized-enabled.description: `yes` plays the domain's MoH files in random order instead of in sequence.

voicemail-user-control-enabled.description: Whether voicemail is enabled for new users in the domain.

voicemail-transcription-enabled.description: The vendor that transcribes voicemail for new users in the domain. `no` turns transcription off.

recording-configuration.description: Records every call in the domain: `yes`, `yes-with-transcription`, or `yes-with-transcription-and-sentiment`. `no` removes the domain-wide recording. Requires Reseller scope or above to set: Office Manager scope gets `403`. To record one user or device, set `recording-configuration` on that user or device instead.

is-domain-locked.description: `yes` blocks every call from the domain except emergency calls.

is-stir-enabled.description: `yes` marks likely spam calls to the domain using STIR/SHAKEN, where the platform has it configured.

is-ivr-forward-change-blocked.description: `yes` skips the prompt to change call forwarding in the voicemail menu for users in the domain.

single-sign-on-enabled.description: Legacy single sign-on (SSO) switch. Use `user-authentication` instead. When you send `user-authentication` without this field, it is set for you: `no` for `authenticator_totp`, `yes` otherwise.

allow_user_primary_email_edit.description: `1` lets Office Manager and lower scopes edit primary email addresses. Which addresses a user can change still depends on scope.

account_recovery_user_primary_email.description: `1` lets users recover their account from the login page with a verified email. `0` means an Office Manager or above must reset the password.

require_unique_primary_user_email.description: `1` requires each user's primary email to be unique in the domain.

allow_sso_with_additional_emails.description: `1` lets one user log in with SSO from more than one email address.

email-send-from-address.description: The sender address for email the platform sends for the domain. Use an address your mail server and SPF record allow, or email can be marked as spam. An address that is not valid is replaced by the platform default when email is sent.

email-send-smtp-hostname.description: SMTP server for the domain's email. Empty uses the reseller or platform server.

email-send-smtp-port.description: SMTP port, 1 to 65535, sent as a string. Empty uses the reseller or platform server.

email-send-smtp-username.description: SMTP user name. Empty uses the reseller or platform server.

email-send-smtp-password.description: SMTP password. Empty uses the reseller or platform server. Send the masked value a read returned to keep the stored password. Any other masked value returns `400`.

limits-max-subscriber-resources-total.description: Maximum number of users in the domain, counting the system users that call queues, auto attendants, and other features create. To limit regular users only, use `limits-max-users`.

limits-max-users.description: Maximum number of regular users in the domain.

limits-max-active-calls-total.description: Maximum number of simultaneous calls in the domain, on-net and off-net.

limits-max-active-calls-offnet.description: Maximum number of simultaneous calls to or from off-net destinations.

limits-max-call-queues.description: Maximum number of call queues in the domain.

limits-max-auto-attendants.description: Maximum number of auto attendants in the domain.

limits-max-conferences.description: Maximum number of conference bridges in the domain.

limits-max-departments.description: Maximum number of departments in the domain.

limits-max-sites.description: Maximum number of sites in the domain.

limits-max-fax-accounts.description: Maximum number of fax accounts in the domain.

maxCallMinute.description: Maximum length of any call in the domain. On a call between two domains, the lower non-zero limit applies.

hipaa-covered.description: `1` when the domain handles protected health information. Reads of personal data in the domain are then recorded in the access log.

gdpr-covered.description: `1` when the domain is in GDPR scope. Reads of personal data in the domain are then recorded in the access log.

part2-covered.description: `1` when the domain is a 42 CFR Part 2 covered facility.

account-id.description: Your own account reference for the domain, up to 64 characters.

provider-notes.description: Free-form notes about the domain. No practical length limit.

user-authentication.description:
