Defines the login authentication method for users within the domain.

There are four possible settings for this parameter.
- ‎`login_name_and_password` allows for username/password login, SSO (Single Sign-On) or TOTP (multi-factor authentication using an authenticator app).
- ‎`authenticator_totp` forces all users in the domain to log in using TOTP (multi-factor authentication using an authenticator app).
- `single_sign_on`forces all users in the domain to log in using SSO (Single Sign-On).
- `authenticator_totp_sso` allows users to log in using TOTP or SSO.

UserRead.description: A user as a read returns it: every `User` field plus the read-only fields in `UserReadAdditions`.

passwordLength.description: Generates a random numeric voicemail PIN of this many digits. Ignored when `voicemail-login-pin` is sent.

UserCreate.description: The body of a user create. `user`, `name-first-name`, and `name-last-name` are required.

current_password.description: Your current password. Required when you change your own `password-hash` or `email` and a password is already set. Without it those two fields are not changed. A wrong value is a `403`.

reset_mfa.description: `yes` removes the user's multi-factor enrollment, so the user sets it up again at the next login.

phonenumber.description: The phone number, digits with the country code, for example `15555550123`. 7 to 249 characters, and 16 at most when the number has an SMS assignment. The API stores it exactly as sent and does not convert it to E.164, so use the same form everywhere.

enabled.description: Whether the number routes calls. A disabled number is skipped when a call is matched. Defaults to `yes` on create.

dial-rule-application.description: The application that handles a call to the number. `available-number` keeps the number in the domain without routing it. Left out, no application is set.

dial-rule-parameter.description: An extra setting for the application, such as the SIP header an `*-add-header` application adds. Send `<NULL>` to clear it. It reads back as an empty string.

dial-rule-translation-destination-user.description: Where the call goes, read together with `dial-rule-application`: a user's extension, a call queue's extension, or an off-net number. `[*]` keeps the dialed number.

dial-rule-translation-destination-host.description: The host part of the destination, usually your domain. `[*]` keeps the dialed host. Left out, it is empty.

dial-rule-translation-source-name.description: The caller ID name sent with the call. `[*]` keeps the caller's name, and text around it is added to that name, for example `Sales_[*]`. Defaults to `[*]` on create.

dial-rule-description.description: A note on the number for your own tracking, up to 63 characters. Send an empty string to clear it.

sms-enabled.description: Whether the number has an SMS assignment. On a write, `true` creates or keeps the assignment and `false` removes it. Sending `sms-application`, `sms-carrier`, or `sms-dest` alone means `true`. Leave all four out to keep the assignment as it is.

sms-application.description: What receives the number's messages. `available` unassigns the number and clears `sms-dest`. Left out on a write, it is `user` when `sms-dest` is sent and `available` otherwise.

sms-carrier.description: The carrier the number sends and receives messages through, one of the platform's configured SMS carriers such as `bandwidth`. Not case-sensitive. Left out on an update, the current carrier is kept.

sms-dest.description: The extension of the user or call queue that receives the number's messages. Left out on an update, the current destination is kept.

CallQueueStatistics.title: Call queue statistics

calls-total-count.description: `VOL`. Calls that entered the queue in the window, whatever the outcome.

calls-presented-count.description: `CO`. Calls offered to agents, abandoned calls included. Calls that ended in an error are not counted.

calls-presented-adjusted-count.description: `ACO`. Calls offered to agents, leaving out calls abandoned within 10 seconds.

calls-abandoned-count.description: `AC`. Calls that left the queue before an agent answered.

calls-abandoned-adjusted-count.description: `AAC`. Abandoned calls that waited 10 seconds or more.

calls-abandoned-rate.description: `AR`. Abandoned calls as a percentage of calls offered (`AC` / `CO` x 100), 0 to 100.

calls-abandoned-adjusted-rate.description: `AAR`. Abandoned calls that waited 10 seconds or more, as a percentage of adjusted calls offered (`AAC` / `ACO` x 100), 0 to 100.

calls-service-level-percent.description: `SL`. Calls answered within the `sla` wait (60 seconds unless you set `sla`), as a percentage of calls offered, 0 to 100.

calls-presented-percent.description: `DT`. Calls offered to agents as a percentage of all calls (`calls-total-count`), 0 to 100.

calls-forwarded-count.description: `FWD`. Calls forwarded out of the queue because no agent answered or was registered.

calls-assisted-count.description: `AST`. Calls an agent answered and passed to another agent.

calls-callback-requests-count.description: `CB`. Callers who asked for a callback instead of waiting.

calls-talking-avg-duration-minutes.description: `ATT`. Average talk time per answered call, hold time excluded. In minutes, rounded to 2 decimals.

calls-talking-duration-minutes.description: `TT`. Total talk time on answered calls. In minutes.

calls-handling-avg-duration-minutes.description: `AHT`. Average handling time per answered call: talk, hold, and disposition time. In minutes, rounded to 2 decimals.

calls-holding-avg-duration-seconds.description: `AH`. Average hold time per answered call, in seconds. Calls with no hold count as 0.

calls-queueing-avg-duration-seconds.description: `AWT`. Average wait in the queue before an agent answered, in seconds. Abandoned calls are left out. `AAS` is the same statistic.

calls-after-call-work-avg-duration-secon.description: `ACW`. Average disposition (wrap-up) time after a call, for agents in Single Call Mode. In **minutes** without `interval`, despite the name, and in seconds with `interval`.

name.description: The call queue's description. Only on the per-queue list, where each row is one queue.

sms-handling-avg-duration-seconds.description: `SMS_AHT`. Average time from an agent accepting an SMS conversation to its end, in seconds.

CallQueueStatistics.description: The statistics for one call queue, or for every queue together. Only the fields named in `fields` are present.

AgentStatistics.title: Agent statistics

name.description: `NAME`. The agent's first and last name.

calls-abandoned-count.description: `AC`. Queue calls offered to the agent that were abandoned before anyone answered.

calls-abandoned-adjusted-count.description: `AAC`. As `AC`, counting only calls that waited 10 seconds or more.

calls-callback-requests-count.description: `CB`. Queue calls offered to the agent that ended in a callback request.

calls-assisted-count.description: `AST`. Queue calls the agent answered and passed to another agent.

calls-unanswered-count.description: `MC`. Queue calls offered to the agent that the agent did not answer, each offer counted.

calls-talking-avg-duration-minutes.description: `ATT`. Average talk time per answered queue call, in minutes, rounded to 2 decimals.

calls-talking-duration-minutes.description: `TT`. Total talk time on answered queue calls, in minutes.

calls-handling-avg-duration-minutes.description: `AHT`. Average handling time per answered queue call (talk, hold, and disposition), in minutes.

calls-holding-avg-duration-seconds.description: `AH`. Average hold time per answered queue call, in seconds.

calls-queueing-avg-duration-seconds.description: `AWT`. Average wait in the queue before the agent answered. In **minutes** on this endpoint, despite the name.

calls-after-call-work-avg-duration-secon.description: `ACW`. Average disposition (wrap-up) time, for agents in Single Call Mode. In **minutes** on this endpoint, despite the name.

sms-conversations-count.description: `SMS_VOL`. Queue SMS conversations the agent completed.

sms-handling-avg-duration-seconds.description: `SMS_AHT`. Average time the agent spent on a queue SMS conversation, in seconds.

outbound-calls-attempted-count.description: `OATT`. Off-net outbound calls the agent placed, conference calls excluded.

outbound-calls-answered-count.description: `OANS`. Off-net outbound calls that connected, voicemail pickups included.

outbound-calls-duration-minutes.description: `OM`. Total time on off-net outbound calls. In **seconds**, despite the name.

outbound-calls-avg-duration-minutes.description: `OAVG` (send `OAVG`). Average off-net outbound call length. In **seconds**, despite the name.

inbound-calls-presented-count.description: `IA`. Off-net inbound calls offered to the agent, queue calls included.

inbound-calls-answered-count.description: `IANS`. Off-net inbound calls the agent answered, queue calls included.

inbound-calls-duration-minutes.description: `IM`. Total time on off-net inbound calls. In **seconds**, despite the name.

inbound-calls-avg-duration-minutes.description: `IAVG`. Average off-net inbound call length. In **seconds**, despite the name.

AgentStatistics.description: The statistics for one agent. Only the fields named in `fields` are present.

DnisStatistics.title: Dialed number statistics

calls-total-count.description: `VOL`. Calls that entered the dialed number in the window, whatever the outcome.

calls-presented-count.description: `CO`. Calls offered to agents, abandoned calls included. Calls that ended in an error are not counted.

calls-presented-adjusted-count.description: `ACO`. Calls offered to agents, leaving out calls abandoned within 10 seconds.

calls-abandoned-count.description: `AC`. Calls that left the queue before an agent answered.

calls-abandoned-adjusted-count.description: `AAC`. Abandoned calls that waited 10 seconds or more.

calls-abandoned-rate.description: `AR`. Abandoned calls as a percentage of calls offered (`AC` / `CO` x 100), 0 to 100.

calls-abandoned-adjusted-rate.description: `AAR`. Abandoned calls that waited 10 seconds or more, as a percentage of adjusted calls offered (`AAC` / `ACO` x 100), 0 to 100.

calls-service-level-percent.description: `SL`. Calls answered within the `sla` wait (60 seconds unless you set `sla`), as a percentage of calls offered, 0 to 100.

calls-presented-percent.description: `DT`. Calls offered to agents as a percentage of all calls (`calls-total-count`), 0 to 100.

calls-forwarded-count.description: `FWD`. Calls forwarded out of the queue because no agent answered or was registered.

calls-assisted-count.description: `AST`. Calls an agent answered and passed to another agent.

calls-callback-requests-count.description: `CB`. Callers who asked for a callback instead of waiting.

calls-talking-avg-duration-minutes.description: `ATT`. Average talk time per answered call, hold time excluded. In **seconds** on this endpoint, despite the name.

calls-talking-duration-minutes.description: `TT`. Total talk time on answered calls. In **seconds** on this endpoint, despite the name.

calls-handling-avg-duration-minutes.description: `AHT`. Average handling time per answered call: talk, hold, and disposition time. In **seconds** on this endpoint, despite the name.

calls-holding-avg-duration-seconds.description: `AH`. Average hold time per answered call, in seconds. Calls with no hold count as 0.

calls-queueing-avg-duration-seconds.description: `AWT`. Average wait in the queue before an agent answered, in seconds. Abandoned calls are left out. `AAS` is the same statistic.

calls-after-call-work-avg-duration-secon.description: `ACW`. Average disposition (wrap-up) time after a call, for agents in Single Call Mode. In seconds.

DnisStatistics.description: The statistics for one dialed number. Only the fields named in `fields` are present. Every duration is in seconds.

AgentStatusTime.title: Agent status time

status-login-duration-minutes.description: `LI`. Minutes the agent was logged in, no more than the window length.

status-available-duration-minutes.description: `AM`. Minutes the agent was available for calls, logged-in time included, no more than the window length.

status-unavailable-duration-minutes.description: `UM`. Minutes the agent was in any unavailable status: offline, break, lunch, meeting, and the others, no more than the window length.

status-lunch-duration-minutes.description: `L`. Minutes the agent was in the `lunch` status, no more than the window length.

status-break-duration-minutes.description: `B`. Minutes the agent was in the `break` status, no more than the window length.

status-meeting-duration-minutes.description: `M`. Minutes the agent was in the `meeting` status, no more than the window length.

status-other-duration-minutes.description: `O`. Minutes the agent was in a status other than available, break, lunch, meeting, or web, no more than the window length.

status-web-duration-minutes.description: `W`. Minutes the agent was in the `web` status, no more than the window length.

status-custom1-duration-minutes.description: `CUST1`. Minutes the agent was in your custom status 1, no more than the window length.

status-custom2-duration-minutes.description: `CUST2`. Minutes the agent was in your custom status 2, no more than the window length.

status-custom3-duration-minutes.description: `CUST3`. Minutes the agent was in your custom status 3, no more than the window length.

status-custom4-duration-minutes.description: `CUST4`. Minutes the agent was in your custom status 4, no more than the window length.

status-custom5-duration-minutes.description: `CUST5`. Minutes the agent was in your custom status 5, no more than the window length.

status-custom6-duration-minutes.description: `CUST6`. Minutes the agent was in your custom status 6, no more than the window length.

status-custom7-duration-minutes.description: `CUST7`. Minutes the agent was in your custom status 7, no more than the window length.

status-custom8-duration-minutes.description: `CUST8`. Minutes the agent was in your custom status 8, no more than the window length.

AgentStatusTime.description: Minutes one agent spent in each status. Only the fields named in `fields` are present.

emergency-address-id.description: The address ID. IDs the API generates are `a-` followed by 13 hexadecimal characters. Paths accept only letters, digits, spaces, and `* . - _ '`. Optional: without it the API generates one. An ID used in any domain returns `409`.

address-name.description: A label for the address, shown when users pick one.

caller-name.description: The caller name stored with the address.

address-line-1.description: The house number and street. The house number is the text up to the first space.

address-state-province-abbreviation.description: The state or province code, such as `CA`.

address-postal-code.description: The postal code. Send it as a string to keep leading zeros.

address-country-abbreviation.description: The country code, such as `US` or `CA`.

address-location-description.description: Where in the building, such as a room or desk.

ip-address-public.description: A public IP address stored with the address, as sent. The API does not detect it.

address-formatted-pidflo.description: The standardized address from `POST /domains/{domain}/addresses/validate`, as an object. Send it back unchanged with `carrier`. Its keys depend on the carrier: `bandwidth` and `inteliquent` use `HouseNumber`, `StreetName`, `StreetSuffix`, `City`, `StateCode`, `Zip`, `PlusFour`, and `Country`; `brightlink` uses `houseNumber`, `streetName`, `streetSuffix`, `city`, `stateCode`, `zip`, `plusfour`, and `country`.

carrier.description: The emergency calling carrier, as returned by validate. `address-formatted-pidflo` is used only with one of these values.

user.description: `POST /domains/{domain}/addresses` only: leave it out for a domain-level address, or send a site name for a site address. On a user path, the path decides.

locale.description: The locale code: 2 letters, optionally followed by a hyphen and 2 letters, such as `en-US` or `fr-CA`. Use this form so the translation can be read back by `/translations/{locale}`.

namespace.description: The namespace, such as `common`. Letters, digits, `.`, `_`, and `-` only, so the namespace can be read back by `/translations/{locale}/{namespace}`.

key.description: The translation key, such as `SEARCH_TRANSLATIONS`. Unique within a locale and namespace.

value.description: The translated text. No practical length limit.

description.description: Context for translators, such as where the text appears. No practical length limit. Also copied to the `common` copy when one is created.
description.example: Placeholder text in the translation search box

source.description: Where the value comes from. `api`, the default, marks it as customized, so a filesystem sync never overwrites it. `filesystem` lets the next sync overwrite it with the value from the locale files.

id.description: The translation ID, a UUID. Generated when you omit it.

TranslationCreateItem.description: One translation to create. `locale`, `namespace`, `key`, and `value` are required and must not be blank.

translations.description: The translations to create. Each one is checked and created on its own.

TranslationCreateRequest.description: The body of a translation create: one translation, or a `translations` array of them.

id.description: The ID of the translation to change. When sent, `locale`, `namespace`, and `key` are not needed and are ignored.

locale.description: The locale of the translation to change. Required with `namespace` and `key` when `id` is not sent. Cannot be changed.

namespace.description: The namespace of the translation to change. Required with `locale` and `key` when `id` is not sent. Cannot be changed.

key.description: The key of the translation to change. Required with `locale` and `namespace` when `id` is not sent. Cannot be changed.

value.description: The new translated text. Send `value`, `description`, or both. An empty string counts as not sent, so a value cannot be set to empty.

description.description: The new context for translators. Send `value`, `description`, or both.
description.example: Placeholder text in the translation search box

value.description: The new translated text. Present only when sent.

additionalProperties.description: One namespace: each property is a translation key and its text.

project.description: The set of locale files to load. `horizon` is the web app's files, including its translator descriptions. `auth` is the login pages' files. `all`, the default, loads both. The names are case-sensitive, except `all`.

TranslationSyncRequest.description: The body of a filesystem sync. Every field is optional.

added.description: Keys that were not in the database and were created.

updated.description: Keys whose value changed in the file and was updated.

skipped_user_customized.description: Keys left alone because they were customized through this API.

skipped_secondary.description: Keys left alone because they already exist and this project does not overwrite them.

TranslationSyncSummary.description: Counts for one locale file, or totals across all of them.

success.description: Always `true`. Check each project and locale for its own `success`.

projects.description: One entry per project synced, keyed by project name.

success.description: `false` when the project has no valid locale files on this server.

error.description: Why the project failed. Present only when `success` is `false`.

translations_path.description: The directory the locale files were read from.

descriptions_path.description: The directory the description files were read from. `null` for `auth`.

locales.description: One entry per locale file, keyed by locale code.

success.description: `false` when the file is missing or not valid JSON.

error.description: Why the file failed. Present only when `success` is `false`.

changes.description: Every key added or updated from this file.

action.description: What was done to the key.

value.description: The value created. Present when `action` is `added`.

old_value.description: The value before. Present when `action` is `updated`.

new_value.description: The value after. Present when `action` is `updated`.

descriptions.description: The result of loading translator descriptions for this locale. `horizon` only.

success.description: `true` also when there is no description file.

error.description: A note or an error, such as a missing description file.

total_keys.description: Keys read from the description file.

updated.description: Descriptions that changed and were updated.

not_found.description: Keys with no translation to attach the description to.

skipped.description: Entries that were neither text nor an object with `description`.

TranslationSyncResponse.description: The result of a filesystem sync, per project and per locale file, with totals.

name.description: Display name of the extension.

webpack_module.description: Module Federation container name, in camelCase. It must be unique across the platform and cannot be changed later. The extension `id` is derived from it.

remote_entry_url.description: URL of the Module Federation `remoteEntry.js` bundle. It must be a valid URL. No length limit. The bundle is not fetched until you deploy it with `POST /ui-extensions/registry/{id}/deploy`.

version.description: Initial display version, in `major.minor.patch` form. Defaults to `1.0.0` when omitted or blank. After registration only a deploy changes it.

reseller.description: Owning reseller. `*` makes the extension platform-wide. A super user may set any value and defaults to `*`. A Reseller may omit it or send its own reseller; any other value returns `403`.

enabled.description: Master switch. `no` turns the extension off for everyone. Any other value, such as `restricted` echoed from a read, is ignored and the stored value is kept.

description.description: What the extension does. No length limit.
description.example: Adds a notes panel to the inbound call view.

allowed_hostnames.description: Origins that the remote authentication callbacks may use. Send an array, a comma-separated string, or a JSON array as a string. No member may contain a comma. Stored and returned as a comma-separated string.

remote_auth_enabled.description: `yes` turns on remote authentication with the vendor. `no` turns it off.

remote_callback_url.description: Vendor endpoints that receive the remote authentication webhook, in failover order: the first is tried first. Send an array or a comma-separated string. Blank entries and repeats are dropped. Stored and returned as a comma-separated string. This is the only place the webhook destination is set.

remote_callback_secret.description: Shared secret used to sign the remote authentication webhook with HMAC-SHA256. Reads return it masked: the first 2 and last 2 characters, with asterisks between; 8 characters or fewer is all asterisks, at least 4. On update, sending back the masked value keeps the secret unchanged. Any other mask-shaped value returns `400`, on create as well.

remote_timeout_seconds.description: How long, in seconds, to wait for the vendor during remote authentication.

FlowSdkExtensionUpdate.description: Body for updating an extension. Send only the fields you change. `id`, `webpack_module`, `version`, `integrity_hash`, `active_version`, and the verification fields are ignored, so a response from a read can be sent back as it is.

hostname.description: Portal hostname the rule applies to. `*` matches every hostname.

reseller.description: Reseller the rule applies to. `*` matches every reseller. A Reseller must send its own reseller here: `*` and other resellers return `403`.

domain.description: Domain the rule applies to. `*` matches every domain.

role.description: User scope the rule applies to, by scope name, such as `Basic User` or `Office Manager`. `*` matches every scope.

enabled.description: `yes` shows the extension to callers that match the rule. `no` hides it.

FlowSdkAccessRuleWrite.description: Body for creating or updating an access rule. On create, an omitted scope field is `*`. On update, an omitted or blank field keeps its stored value.

rule_id.description: Handle of the new rule, for `PUT` and `DELETE`. It is derived from the rule's scope, so recreating the same rule returns the same value.

FlowSdkAccessRuleCreated.description: Result of creating an access rule.

FlowSdkRulePolicyOverride.description: Override for one rule. Send any of `mode`, `severity`, and `buckets`. An empty object `{}` removes the override and restores the shipped default.

mode.description: `enforce` counts toward the verdict. `monitor` reports only. `off` does not run the rule.

severity.description: Verdict the rule produces when it fires.

buckets.description: Severity for hits in dependency code or in code the build tool added.

vendored.description: Severity for a hit in a dependency.

build-injected.description: Severity for a hit in code the build tool added.

disabled-zones.description: Zones no extension may mount into. Replaces the stored list. `[]` clears it.

disabled-capabilities.description: Capabilities withheld from every extension. Replaces the stored list.

api-read-deny-resources.description: API resources extensions may not read. Replaces the stored list.

api-write-deny-resources.description: API resources extensions may not change. Replaces the stored list.

approved-cdn-origins.description: Hosts an extension bundle may be served from: bare hostnames or `*.example.com` wildcards, with no scheme or port. Replaces the stored list. `[]` approves no host, which blocks every deploy and reanalysis.

analysis-settings.description: Bundle-analysis limits. Send only the keys you change; the rest keep their values. An unknown key, a numeric string, or a value out of range returns `400`.

analysis-denylist.description: Denied packages and suppressed findings. Each key you send replaces that list; the built-in suppressions always apply. An unknown key returns `400`.

analysis-rule-policy.description: Per-rule overrides, keyed by rule id. Send only the rules you change. An unknown rule id returns `400`. `missing-source-map` must stay in `enforce` mode.

FlowSdkSettingsUpdate.description: Body for updating the Flow SDK settings. Send only the fields you change. Each key is also accepted in snake_case, such as `disabled_zones`; the kebab-case key wins when both are sent.

limit.description: Most versions to analyze in this call.

dry_run.description: Analyze and report without saving anything; `remaining` does not go down. JSON `true`, a non-zero number, or the strings `yes`, `true`, `1`, and `on` in any case turn it on. Any other value, or none, is a real run.

extension_id.description: Analyze only this extension's versions. Omit it to cover every extension.

FlowSdkReanalyzeRequest.description: Options for a reanalysis run. Every field is optional.

remote_entry_url.description: URL of the `remoteEntry.js` to deploy. Its host must be in `approved-cdn-origins`, and it must use HTTPS. Otherwise the deploy is rejected.

source_map_url.description: URL of the source map for the entry. Optional when the bundle links its maps itself. Without a usable source map the deploy is rejected.

version.description: Version to deploy as. Omit it to use the next free patch version. When sent, it must be greater than the current version. The first deploy may reuse the version you registered.

synchronous.description: `yes` waits up to 2 seconds for the new version to take effect, and adds `landed` to the response. Also accepted in the query string.

FlowSdkDeployRequest.description: Body for deploying an extension version.

findings.description: What the analysis found. Empty when nothing fired.

rule.description: Rule that fired, such as `fetch-failed` or `eval`.

severity.description: `reject` fails the bundle, `flag` records a finding, `info` is informational.

message.description: Readable explanation of the finding.

FlowSdkVerificationReport.description: The analysis report for a bundle.

version_id.description: Handle of the new version. Absent when `unchanged` is `true`.

version.description: Version this deploy carries, or the live version when `unchanged` is `true`.

status.description: `approved` passed and is live. `flagged` has findings and is live. `rejected` did not pass and changes nothing live. `dev` is a local development build served without analysis, on development servers only. `unchanged` means the bytes match the live version and nothing was written.

has_chunk_sri.description: `yes` when the bundle's chunks carry integrity hashes. Absent when `unchanged` is `true`.

promoted.description: `true` when the version was accepted as the live version. It takes effect shortly after.

unchanged.description: `true` when the bytes match the live version.

landed.description: Present only with `synchronous=yes` on a promoted version. `true` means the new version is live on this server. `false` means not yet; read the extension again shortly.

FlowSdkDeployResult.description: Result of a deploy. When the bytes match the live version, only `version`, `status`, `promoted`, and `unchanged` are returned.

versions.description: Every deployed version, newest first. An empty array before the first deploy.

InboxCreate.description: The body of an inbox create. `inbox_name` and `extension` are required. `owner` applies to `shared` inboxes only.

inbox_name.description: The inbox name, unique in the domain. It is split at the first space: each part holds up to 64 characters. A one-word name has ` Inbox` appended.

extension.description: The extension the inbox answers on: letters and digits only. It must not be in use in the domain.

inbox_kind.description: The kind of inbox: `shared` (the default) has an owner and members you add; `main_number` has no owner.

owner.description: The owner of a `shared` inbox: a user's extension in the domain, or `<extension>@<domain>` naming this domain. Defaults to you. Required when your token is not in this domain. Not allowed for `main_number`. For a Site Manager, the owner, named or defaulted, must be a user in its own site.

InboxUpdate.description: The body of an inbox rename. `inbox_name` is the only field taken.

inbox_name.description: The inbox name, unique in the domain. It is split at the first space: each part holds up to 64 characters. A one-word name has ` Inbox` appended.

InboxMemberAdd.description: The body of an inbox member add.

user.description: The extension of a user in the same domain. It cannot be another inbox.

InboxMemberRole.description: The body of an inbox member role change.

role.description: The new role: `can-reply` (reads and replies) or `view` (reads only). `owner` cannot be assigned.

UserInbox.description: An inbox a user is a member of: shared, main-number, or personal. A personal inbox has one row per phone number.

name.description: The inbox name. For a personal inbox, the owner's display name.

user.description: The inbox, as `<extension>@<domain>`. For a personal inbox, the owner.

owner.description: The owner, as `<extension>@<domain>`. `null` for a `main_number` inbox.

inbox_kind.description: The kind of inbox: one of `shared`, `main_number`, or `personal`. `null` when it could not be read.

space_id.description: Identifies the inbox's conversations, for opening the right one in a client. Unique per inbox, even when an extension is reused.

did.description: For a personal inbox, the phone number this row covers, as digits. `null` for other kinds.

deactivated.description: `true` for a deleted inbox. Listed only with `include_deactivated`.

message.description: The message text. Required, even with a file.

MessageSendRequest.description: The body of a message send. Pick the shape for your case. There is no discriminator: `type` does not tell the shapes apart on its own, because a chat and a group chat both use `chat`, and an SMS and a group SMS both use `sms`. The shape of `destination` does.

oneOf.title: Rename the session
oneOf.description: Names a group session for every participant. Each participant gets a `chat-name-change` message. `messagesession-name` is accepted as the same field.

session-name.description: The new name. Send an empty string to clear it.

oneOf.title: Set the participants
oneOf.description: Replaces the participants of a group chat with the list you send, including yourself. A user added gets the session, and a user left out loses it. Every participant gets a `chat-participant-add` or `chat-participant-remove` message.

messagesession-participants.description: The complete list of participants, as comma-separated user IDs with no spaces. Include your own.

oneOf.title: Mark read or mute
oneOf.description: Changes only your own copy of the session.

messagesession-last-status.description: Set to `read` once the user has seen the last message.

messagesession-muted.description: `yes` mutes notifications for the session. `no` turns them back on.

MessagesessionUpdate.description: The body of a session change. Pick the shape for your case. No field selects the shape, so there is no discriminator.

messagesession-queue-termination.description: The call queue the conversation is waiting in, as its user ID. Read it from the session's `messagesession-queue-termination`.

messagesession-last-status.description: Optionally marks the conversation `read` or `unread` for you.

MessagesessionAccept.description: The body of a call queue conversation accept.

requesting-number.description: The off-net number that asked to stop receiving messages. Spaces and punctuation are removed, and a 10-digit number gets `+1`.

blocked-number.description: Your number that may no longer message `requesting-number`. Normalized the same way.

SmsBlockCreate.description: The body of an SMS block create. The domain comes from the path, and the block is always created `active`.

status.description: `active` blocks messages again. `inactive` stops blocking but keeps the record.

SmsBlockUpdate.description: The body of an SMS block change. Only `status` can change.

name.description: The scope name, assigned to users and API keys and carried by their tokens. 1 to 32 characters: letters, digits, spaces, `.`, `_`, and `-`, starting with a letter or digit. It cannot be the name of a built-in scope.

parent-scope.description: The built-in scope this one takes its rights from. A custom scope cannot be a parent.

enabled.description: `no` refuses the scope's tokens until it is enabled. Defaults to `yes`; any value other than `yes`, `true`, or `1` means `no`.

hidden.description: `yes` leaves the scope out of `GET /scopes`. `true` and `1` also mean `yes`. Defaults to `no`.

UserEmailCallCenterReport.title: Call center report
UserEmailCallCenterReport.description: Emails a call center statistics report for a time window to the user's email address, with any `cclist` addresses copied. The subject is the report's own title.

start_date.description: The start of the report window. RFC 3339, such as `2026-09-01T00:00:00+00:00`. `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` and `YYYY-MM-DD` also work. The offset is dropped and the clock time kept; use `range_interval` to shift the window.

end_date.description: The end of the report window. RFC 3339, such as `2026-09-01T00:00:00+00:00`. `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` and `YYYY-MM-DD` also work. The offset is dropped and the clock time kept; use `range_interval` to shift the window. A date alone means the end of that day.

range_interval.description: Shifts the window by a relative time, such as `-7 hours` or `4 hour`. Use it to report in local time.

report.description: The report period label. Defaults to `custom`.

queue_fields.description: The columns of the queues table, separated by commas. Defaults to `NAME,VOL,SL,AWT`.

agent_fields.description: The columns of the agents table, separated by commas. Defaults to `NAME,CH,AHT`.

dnis_fields.description: The columns of the DNIS table, separated by commas. Defaults to `NAME,VOL,SL,AWT`.

include_csv.description: `true` or `1` attaches the raw data as CSV. Defaults to `false`.

cclist.description: More addresses to copy, separated by semicolons. Below Office Manager, each must be one of the user's own addresses.

UserEmailAccount.title: Account email
UserEmailAccount.description: Emails the user an account message from the domain's template: a welcome with a link to set up the account, a password reset link, or their login name.

subject.description: The subject line. Send `<UseHtmlTitle>` to use the template's own title.

sent.description: `true` when the email was handed to the mail server. `false` when it could not be built: the user was not found, has no email address, the address is not theirs, or the domain does not allow it.

success.description: `true` when the connection, login, and any test message all worked.

authentication_successful.description: `true` when a username was sent and the login worked.

verified.description: `true` when the address is verified. `false` when it is not, or when the user or address is unknown.

EmailVerifiedStatus.description: Whether an email address is verified.

filename.description: The file name the account is stored under.

valid-json.description: `yes` when the file is JSON with `type`, `project_id`, `client_email`, and `client_id`; `no` otherwise. See `valid` for whether the key itself loads.

type.description: The account type from the file, normally `service_account`.

project_id.description: The Firebase project the account belongs to.

private-key-id.description: The key's ID from the file, masked: only its first and last two characters are shown.

key-fingerprint.description: SHA-256 of the public key, in hex. Tells two keys apart without showing either. Empty when the key does not load.

valid.description: `yes` when the file is a service account whose private key loads as an RSA key.

user-agent-match.description: The file name without `.json`. A device uses this account when its SIP User-Agent, lowercased with dashes removed and its first one to three words joined by `-`, is a prefix of this value.

modified-datetime.description: When the file was last written.

FirebaseServiceAccount.description: A Firebase service account file on the server, as a read returns it. The private key is never returned.

filename.description: The file name to store the account under. Lowercase letters, digits, `.`, `-` and `_`, ending in `.json`. Start it with the app's SIP User-Agent first word, lowercased with dashes removed (for example `acmephone-android.json`), because that is how devices are matched to accounts. Required on `POST /firebase`; ignored on `PUT /firebase/{filename}`.

service-account.description: The whole key file, as an object or as a JSON string, instead of its fields at the top level.

type.description: From the key file: must be `service_account`.

project_id.description: From the key file: the Firebase project.

private_key_id.description: From the key file: the key's ID.

private_key.description: From the key file: the PEM private key, with its line breaks (sent as real line breaks or as `\n`). It must be a readable RSA key; a masked value is refused. Never returned by a read.

client_email.description: From the key file: the service account's email address.

client_id.description: From the key file: the service account's client ID.

FirebaseServiceAccountCreate.description: The body of a Firebase service account add or replace. Send the fields of the service account JSON key file from the Firebase console, each as its own top-level field, or send the whole file under `service-account`. Either way the key file must carry `type`, `project_id`, `private_key_id`, `private_key`, `client_email` and `client_id`. `filename` is required on `POST /firebase` and ignored on `PUT /firebase/{filename}`. Fields not listed here are not stored.

ResellerPath.description: Reseller (territory) name, such as `example-reseller`. `~` means your own territory.

IpawareHostnamePath.description: Hostname of the server whose IP rules service you are managing, such as `core1.example.com`. It must be one of the platform's servers, matched without regard to case. Any other name returns `404`, and nothing is sent.

Synchronous.description: `yes` waits until the change is applied before answering.

SynchronousTimeout.description: How long `synchronous=yes` waits, in milliseconds, 0 to 5000. Defaults to `2000`. A larger value returns `400`.

IncludeSecrets.description: `yes` returns secret values in full instead of masked.

DatetimeStart.description:
This is the start of the time window for a given query. The format is based on RFC3339 but also will support additonal params for use in providing a timezone which will allow the API to give the correct range for a given set of data and will be formated in respone using the same format. 

Supported formats include. 
* 2023-11-27 13:00:00
* 2023-11-27T13:00:00Z
* 2023-11-27T13:00:00-08:00
* 2023-11-27T13:00:00-08:00[US/Pacific]
* 2023-11-27T13:00:00Z[America/Phoenix]

DatetimeEnd.description: This is the end of the time window for a given query. The format is based on RFC3339 but also will support additonal params for use in providing a timezone which will allow the API to give the correct range for a given set of data and will be formated in respone using the same format. Allowed values same as datetime-start.

status-login-duration-minutes.description: This is the total time the call center agent's status was set to "online". Starting in v43.2, an agent has to manually change their status from offline to online when they begin their shift; logging into the portal no longer affects the LI stat.

status-available-duration-minutes.description: This is the total time the call center agent was available for calls. This includes time logged in / online. It excludes statuses of unavailable such as break, lunch, meeting, web, and other.

status-unavailable-duration-minutes.description: This is the total time the call center agent was not available for calls. Includes time agent has the offline statuses, such as offline, break, lunch, meeting, web, and other. Excludes online / available.

status-lunch-duration-minutes.description: This is the total time the call center agent's status was set to "lunch".

status-break-duration-minutes.description: This is the total time the call center agent's status was set to "break".

status-meeting-duration-minutes.description: This is the total time the call center agent's status was set to "meeting".

status-other-duration-minutes.description: This is the total time the call center agent's status is not set to available, break, lunch, meeting, or web. Excludes unavailable status.

status-web-duration-minutes.description: This is the total time the call center agent's status was set to "web".

status-custom1-duration-minutes.description: This is the total time the call center agent's status was set to "CUST1".

status-custom2-duration-minutes.description: This is the total time the call center agent's status was set to "CUST2".

status-custom3-duration-minutes.description: This is the total time the call center agent's status was set to "CUST3".

status-custom8-duration-minutes.description: This is the total time the call center agent's status was set to "CUST8".

calls-total-count.description: Number of calls originating through a Call Queue. Includes answered calls, abandoned calls, forwards, and voicemail.

calls-answered-count.description: Number of calls answered by agent originating through a Call Queue. The call must also terminate with the agent to be counted as a call handled.

calls-presented-count.description: Number of calls that reached the queue to be dispatched to agents. Includes abandoned calls. Excludes forwards and voicemail.

calls-presented-adjusted-count.description: Adjusted number of calls that reached the queue. Excludes calls abandoned in less than 10 seconds.

calls-voicemailed-count.description: Number of calls handled by the automated voicemail system.

calls-forwarded-count.description: Number of calls forwarded to another queue or off-net phone number for handling. Includes forwarded calls to voicemail.

calls-talking-avg-duration-minutes.description: Average number of minutes spent by agent talking per call, on calls originating through a Call Queue. Excludes hold time.

calls-assisted-count.description: Number of calls answered and then transferred to another agent.

calls-after-call-work-avg-duration-secon.description:
Average time an agent spends between the end of a call and submitting call disposition.

This metric is only applied to agents using Single Call Mode.

calls-callback-requests-count.description: Number of calls that requested a callback rather than waiting in the queue.

calls-holding-avg-duration-seconds.description: Average time a caller spends on hold with an agent. Excludes waiting time in the Call Queue.

calls-service-level-percent.description: The ratio of calls meeting the configurable service level agreement.

calls-presented-percent.description: Percentage of calls that landed in the queue and were offered to an agent.

calls-abandoned-count.description: Number of calls that abandoned the queue before being answered by an agent.

calls-abandoned-adjusted-count.description: Adjusted number of calls that abandoned the queue. Excludes calls abandoned in less than 10 seconds.

calls-abandoned-rate.description: Percentage of calls offered that were abandoned before being offered to an agent.

calls-abandoned-adjusted-rate.description: Percentage of calls offered that were abandoned in under 10 seconds.

calls-handling-avg-duration-minutes.description: Average time an agent spent on a call. Includes Talk Time (TT), Hold Time (AH), and Disposition Time (ACW).

calls-queueing-avg-duration-seconds.description: Average number of seconds a caller spent in the selected queue before being dispatched to an agent. If none selected, total for all queues will be displayed.

outbound-calls-attempted-count.description: Number of outbound call attempts by an agent. Excludes on-net calls and conference calls.

outbound-calls-answered-count.description: Number of outbound calls by agent answered by a remote party. Includes calls answered by voicemail. Excludes on-net calls and conference calls.

outbound-calls-duration-minutes.description: Number of minutes spent by an agent on outbound calls. Includes talk and hold time. Excludes call center calls, on-net calls, and conference calls.

outbound-calls-avg-duration-minutes.description: Average length of time spent by an agent on outbound calls. Excludes call center calls, on-net calls, and conference calls.

inbound-calls-presented-count.description: Number of attempted calls inbound to agent. Includes call center calls. Excludes on-net calls and conference calls.

inbound-calls-answered-count.description: Number of inbound answered calls to an agent. Includes call center calls. Excludes on-net calls and conference calls.

inbound-calls-duration-minutes.description: Number of minutes spent by an agent on inbound calls. Includes call center calls. Includes talk and hold time. Excludes on-net calls and conference calls.

inbound-calls-avg-duration-minutes.description: Average length of time spent by an agent on inbound calls. Includes call center calls. Excludes on-net calls and conference calls.

sms-conversations-count.description: Number of SMS sessions handled through a Call Queue.

sms-handling-avg-duration-seconds.description: Average time an agent spent handling an SMS session from the queue, starting from the moment they accept the message until it is terminated.

calls-unanswered-count.description: Number of calls originating through a call queue offered to an agent but not answered. This includes multiple attempts if a call loops through all agents, but excludes unanswered simultaneous ring calls.
