domain.description: The domain name. Letters, digits, and `. - _`, up to 63 characters. It cannot be changed after the domain is created.

reseller.description: The reseller (territory) the domain belongs to. Required on create. Send `~` for your own territory. Changing it moves the domain and its devices to the new territory.

description.description: A display name for the domain, up to 127 characters. Defaults to the domain name.

synchronous.description: Create only. `yes` waits for the domain to be created and answers `200` with it, or `202` if it is not ready within about 10 seconds. `no`, the default, answers `202` at once.

domain-type.description:
The feature set of the domain:

- `Standard` is for a business, with a company directory and configurable PBX features
- `Residential` has no company directory and no PBX features, like an analog line
- `Hospitality` is for hotels, with limited voicemail and no company directory. Errors forward to the operator

Any other value is stored as `Standard`.

dial-plan.description: The dial plan new users in the domain get. On create, a dial plan with this name is created; it defaults to the domain name. On update, it changes the plan for users created afterward.

dial-policy.description: The dial permission new users in the domain get. Name an existing dial permission.

time-zone.description: The time zone new users in the domain get. Answering rules run in it. `timezone` is accepted as another name for this field.

language-token.description: The language new users in the domain see in the portal.

area-code.description: The area code added to a 7-digit number dialed by users in the domain.

caller-id-name.description: The caller ID name used on outbound calls when no user or site caller ID applies.

caller-id-number.description: The caller ID number used on outbound calls when no user or site caller ID applies.

caller-id-number-emergency.description: The caller ID number used on emergency calls when no user or site emergency caller ID applies.

emergency-address-id.description: The emergency address used for users that have no user or site address. Use the `address-id` of an address in the domain.

music-on-hold-enabled.description: `no` turns off music on hold for the domain: callers on hold hear silence and MoH cannot be configured.

music-on-ring-enabled.description: `yes` plays music instead of the spoken announcement while a call is forwarded or transferred.

music-on-hold-randomized-enabled.description: `yes` plays the domain's MoH files in random order instead of in sequence.

voicemail-user-control-enabled.description: Whether voicemail is enabled for new users in the domain.

voicemail-transcription-enabled.description: The vendor that transcribes voicemail for new users in the domain. `no` turns transcription off.

recording-configuration.description: Records every call in the domain: `yes`, `yes-with-transcription`, or `yes-with-transcription-and-sentiment`. `no` removes the domain-wide recording. Requires Reseller scope or above to set: Office Manager scope gets `403`. To record one user or device, set `recording-configuration` on that user or device instead.

is-domain-locked.description: `yes` blocks every call from the domain except emergency calls.

is-stir-enabled.description: `yes` marks likely spam calls to the domain using STIR/SHAKEN, where the platform has it configured.

is-ivr-forward-change-blocked.description: `yes` skips the prompt to change call forwarding in the voicemail menu for users in the domain.

single-sign-on-enabled.description: Legacy single sign-on (SSO) switch. Use `user-authentication` instead. When you send `user-authentication` without this field, it is set for you: `no` for `authenticator_totp`, `yes` otherwise.

allow_user_primary_email_edit.description: `1` lets Office Manager and lower scopes edit primary email addresses. Which addresses a user can change still depends on scope.

account_recovery_user_primary_email.description: `1` lets users recover their account from the login page with a verified email. `0` means an Office Manager or above must reset the password.

require_unique_primary_user_email.description: `1` requires each user's primary email to be unique in the domain.

allow_sso_with_additional_emails.description: `1` lets one user log in with SSO from more than one email address.

email-send-from-address.description: The sender address for email the platform sends for the domain. Use an address your mail server and SPF record allow, or email can be marked as spam. An address that is not valid is replaced by the platform default when email is sent.

email-send-smtp-hostname.description: SMTP server for the domain's email. Empty uses the reseller or platform server.

email-send-smtp-port.description: SMTP port, 1 to 65535, sent as a string. Empty uses the reseller or platform server.

email-send-smtp-username.description: SMTP user name. Empty uses the reseller or platform server.

email-send-smtp-password.description: SMTP password. Empty uses the reseller or platform server. Office Manager, Reseller, and Super User scopes get it masked, such as `co*****************ry`. Other scopes do not get the field. A Super User can send `include-secrets=yes` to get it in full. On update, sending the masked value back keeps the stored password, and any other masked value returns `400`.

limits-max-subscriber-resources-total.description: Maximum number of users in the domain, counting the system users that call queues, auto attendants, and other features create. To limit regular users only, use `limits-max-users`.

limits-max-users.description: Maximum number of regular users in the domain.

limits-max-active-calls-total.description: Maximum number of simultaneous calls in the domain, on-net and off-net.

limits-max-active-calls-offnet.description: Maximum number of simultaneous calls to or from off-net destinations.

limits-max-call-queues.description: Maximum number of call queues in the domain.

limits-max-auto-attendants.description: Maximum number of auto attendants in the domain.

limits-max-conferences.description: Maximum number of conference bridges in the domain.

limits-max-departments.description: Maximum number of departments in the domain.

limits-max-sites.description: Maximum number of sites in the domain.

limits-max-fax-accounts.description: Maximum number of fax accounts in the domain.

maxCallMinute.description: Maximum length of any call in the domain. On a call between two domains, the lower non-zero limit applies.

active-calls-total-current.description: Calls in progress in the domain, including calls across geographic servers and guest video sessions.

active-calls-against-license-count.description: Calls in progress that count against the platform license. Excludes legs on other geographic servers and guest video sessions.

active-calls-offnet-current.description: Calls in progress to or from off-net destinations.

count-users-configured.description: Number of users in the domain, not counting departments and the system users that features create. In a list, it is counted only when `limit` is 100 or less.

hipaa-covered.description: `1` when the domain handles protected health information. Reads of personal data in the domain are then recorded in the access log.

gdpr-covered.description: `1` when the domain is in GDPR scope. Reads of personal data in the domain are then recorded in the access log.

part2-covered.description: `1` when the domain is a 42 CFR Part 2 covered facility.

account-id.description: Your own account reference for the domain, up to 64 characters.

provider-notes.description: Free-form notes about the domain. No practical length limit.

iotum-default-plan.description: The premium video plan new users in the domain get. `null` when premium video is not set up.

iotum-video-status.description: Premium video status for the domain, as a JSON-encoded string such as `{"status":"active"}`. `null` when premium video is not set up.

iotum_company_id.description: The premium video account ID of the domain. `null` when premium video is not set up.

iotum_domain.description: The premium video host name of the domain, such as `example.video.example.com`. `null` when premium video is not set up.

iotum-default-add-ons.description: Legacy. Premium video add-ons are no longer used.

last-modified-datetime.description: When the domain record last changed, in RFC 3339 format.

user-authentication.description:
Defines the login authentication method for users within the domain.

There are four possible settings for this parameter.
- ‎`login_name_and_password` allows for username/password login, SSO (Single Sign-On) or TOTP (multi-factor authentication using an authenticator app).
- ‎`authenticator_totp` forces all users in the domain to log in using TOTP (multi-factor authentication using an authenticator app).
- `single_sign_on`forces all users in the domain to log in using SSO (Single Sign-On).
- `authenticator_totp_sso` allows users to log in using TOTP or SSO.

Domain.description: A domain: one customer organization on the platform, with its defaults for new users, limits, and email settings.

domain.description: The user's domain. Set by the path.

user.description: The user's extension. Unique in the domain. Letters, digits, spaces, and `. - _`. Set it on create; the path names it afterwards.

name-last-name.description: The user's last name. The dial-by-name digits are computed from it on create.

login-username.description: The name the user logs in with. Unique on the platform. Defaults to the extension and domain, such as `1001@example.com`.

email.description: The user's email address, used for notifications. Send several addresses separated by semicolons. The first is the primary address.

user-scope.description: The user's scope, which sets what the user can do. A custom scope name is also accepted. Defaults to the domain's default scope.

department.description: The user's department. Departments group users for call pickup, shared caller ID, and filtering call history and contacts.

site.description: The user's site. A site name that does not exist creates the site. A new user takes its defaults, such as dial plan and caller ID, from its site.

time-zone.description: The user's time zone, as an IANA name.

voicemail-login-pin.description: The voicemail PIN. Masked on a read unless `include-secret=yes` is sent: 8 characters or fewer are all asterisks, and a longer PIN shows its first 2 and last 2 characters. Sending the masked value back leaves the PIN unchanged.

password-hash.description: The user's password, in plain text. The API stores only a hash and never returns it. An empty value resets the account and signs the user out.

privacy.description: Whether the user's caller ID is shown as anonymous on calls that leave the platform.

dial-plan.description: The name of the dial plan the user's calls use.

dial-policy.description: The name of the dial permission that limits where the user can call.

status-message.description: The user's status message, shown to other users in the domain. Send `<null>` to clear it.

user-presence-status.description: The user's presence, such as `inactive` or `open`.

directory-name-number-dtmf-mapping.description: The digits a caller dials to find the user in the auto attendant directory, up to 3. Computed on create from the last name, or from the first name when the domain is set to use it. Duplicates are allowed.

voicemail-user-control-enabled.description: Whether the user has a voicemail box.

phone-numbers-to-allow-enabled.description: Whether the answering rules' list of numbers to allow is applied.

phone-numbers-to-reject-enabled.description: Whether the answering rules' list of numbers to reject is applied.

call-screening-enabled.description: Whether call screening can run. With `no`, screening in an answering rule is skipped.

ring-no-answer-timeout-seconds.description: Seconds an incoming call rings before it goes to voicemail or to the answering rule's no-answer destination. Defaults to `25`.

language-token.description: The user's language for prompts and the portal, such as `en_US`.

limits-max-data-storage-kilobytes.description: The storage limit for voicemail, greetings, and faxes, in kilobytes. `0` means no limit.

limits-max-active-calls-total.description: The most calls the user can have at once.

directory-announce-in-dial-by-name-enabl.description: Whether the user is in the auto attendant's dial-by-name directory. `1` is read as `yes`, and any other value as `no`.

directory-name-visible-in-list-enabled.description: Whether the user is listed in the domain's contact directory. `1` is read as `yes`, and any other value as `no`.

voicemail-greeting-index.description: The index of the voicemail greeting that plays. `0` plays the generic "not available" message.

voicemail-receive-broadcast-enabled.description: Whether the user receives broadcast voicemail messages.

reject-anonymous-calls-enabled.description: Whether calls from anonymous or unknown callers are rejected.

voicemail-playback-announce-date-time-re.description: Whether voicemail playback announces when each message was received.

voicemail-playback-announce-caller-id.description: Whether voicemail playback announces the caller ID of each message.

voicemail-playback-sort-newest-to-oldest.description: Whether voicemail plays the newest message first.

email-send-alert-new-voicemail-cc-list-c.description: Extensions in the domain that get a copy of every voicemail left for this user, separated by spaces. Commas are accepted and changed to spaces. Send an empty value to clear the list.

email-send-alert-new-voicemail-behavior.description: What the new-voicemail email contains, and what happens to the message after it is sent. `no` sends no email. `yes` sends a link. Values starting `att` attach the audio, and values starting `brief` send a short email (`briefatt` attaches the audio too). The ending says where the message goes after the email: `new` leaves it new, `save` moves it to saved, and `trash` moves it to trash.

email-send-alert-new-voicemail-enabled.description: Whether an email is sent for each new voicemail.

email-send-alert-new-missed-call-enabled.description: Whether an email is sent for each missed call.

email-send-alert-data-storage-limit-reac.description: Whether an email is sent when the user reaches the storage limit.

caller-id-number.description: The caller ID number on calls that leave the platform.

caller-id-name.description: The caller ID name on calls that leave the platform.

caller-id-number-emergency.description: The caller ID number on emergency calls.

area-code.description: The area code added to a 7-digit number the user dials.

service-code.description: A code that marks what the user is for. Empty for a person. System users start with `system-`, such as `system-queue`, `system-aa` (auto attendant), and `system-conf` (conference bridge). A code starting with `service-` hides the user in the portal by default.

voicemail-transcription-enabled.description: The transcription service for the user's voicemail, or `no` for none.

emergency-address-id.description: The ID of the emergency address sent on emergency calls. When it is empty, a single-user read shows the site's or domain's address and sets `emergency-address-source`.

call-recordings-hide-from-others-enabled.description: Whether the user's call recordings are hidden from others in the domain's call history. Reseller and Super User tokens still see them.

music-on-hold-randomized-enabled.description: Whether music on hold plays in random order.

music-on-hold-comfort-message-repeat-int.description: Seconds between hold messages that interrupt music on hold.

active-calls-total-current.description: The number of calls the user is on now.

account-status.description: Whether the account is set up. `standard` has a password. `pwd reset` has a voicemail PIN but no password. `new` has a name and email but no password or PIN. `reset` has none of these. Returned only when the response includes all fields.

created-datetime.description: When the user was created.

last-modified-datetime.description: When the user was last changed.

recording-configuration.description: Whether the user's calls are recorded, and whether recordings are transcribed and analyzed for sentiment. A domain-wide recording setting applies regardless.

User.description: A user (an extension) in a domain. The same fields are read and written: read-only fields are ignored on a write, and `password-hash` is never returned. A read narrowed with `fields` returns only the fields named.

device-provisioning-core-server.description: Core server name, as configured in the provisioning server profile. The canonical spelling; the collection also returns it as the deprecated `name`.

device-provisioning-core-server-backup-a.description: Whether this server may be used as a backup provisioning target. `yes` or `no`.

device-provisioning-core-server-status.description: Provisioning status of the server, e.g. `valid tokens`.

device-provisioning-core-server-location.description: Free-text site or datacenter label for the server, e.g. `US West (Phoenix)`. Also returned under the deprecated `address-location-description`, which is a postal-address name and misleading here.

device-provisioning-redundancy-group.description: Geographic redundancy group the server belongs to. Raw column `geo_group`.

device-provisioning-core-server-tcp-port.description: SIP TCP port the server advertises for provisioned devices. Raw column `port_tcp`.

device-provisioning-core-server-tls-port.description: SIP TLS port the server advertises for provisioned devices. Raw column `port_tls`.

device-provisioning-core-server-postfix-.description: FQDN appended to provisioned device configuration. Raw column `postfix`.

device-provisioning-core-server-api-fqdn.description: FQDN devices use to reach the NetSapiens API. Raw column `ns_api_hostname`.

address-location-description.description: DEPRECATED - use `device-provisioning-core-server-location`. Produced by a global field mapping shared with postal addresses; for a core server the value is a site label, not an address. Removed on the next major.

backup_ok.description: DEPRECATED - use `device-provisioning-core-server-backup-allowed`. A raw database column name that reached the v2 response; retained so existing clients keep working. Removed on the next major.

status.description: DEPRECATED - use `device-provisioning-core-server-status`. A raw database column name that reached the v2 response; retained so existing clients keep working. Removed on the next major.

DomainNamePath.description: Domain name, such as `example.com`. `~` means your own domain. A domain that does not exist returns `404`.

UserNamePath.description: User's extension, such as `1001`. `~` means the user your token belongs to.

device.description: Device name, such as `1001a`: the user part of `device-sip-registration-uri`. On create, send it bare, or as a full SIP URI in the path domain; it is qualified with the path domain.

user.description: User who owns the device, such as `1001`. `domain` for a device no user owns.

domain.description: Domain the device belongs to.

device-sip-registration-uri.description: SIP address the device registers as: `sip:<device>@<domain>`. Read-only.

device-sip-registration-state.description: `registered` while the device's last registration has not expired, allowing about 2 minutes of grace. Otherwise `unregistered`. Read-only.

device-sip-registration-password.description: SIP password the device registers with. Returned on single-device reads, not on lists. In plain text only when your token is the device's own user; every other caller gets it masked: the first 2 and last 2 characters around asterisks, or all asterisks for 8 characters or fewer. A Super User gets it in plain text with `include-secrets=yes`, and that read is audit-logged. On create, a random 16-character password of letters and digits is generated when you send none. On update, sending back the masked value you read keeps the stored password; any other mask-shaped value returns `400`.

caller-id-number-emergency.description: Caller ID number sent on emergency calls from this device. `[*]`, stored when you send nothing, uses the user's emergency caller ID.

core-server.description: Core server that holds the device's registration.

device-force-notify-new-voicemails-enabl.description: `yes` sends a message-waiting notification on every registration, for devices that do not subscribe to it. Defaults to `no`.

device-level-call-recording-enabled.description:
The device's recording settings. Note that if domain-wide call recording is set, the device will adopt that setting regardless of this parameter.
If unset, the device will inherit the user setting.

device-push-enabled.description: `yes` lets the device be reached through mobile push notifications. Defaults come from the domain's and territory's device defaults. A push-enabled device counts as registered in the `registered_endpoint` filter.

device-sip-registration-contact.description: Contact header from the device's last registration. Read-only. `null` when it has never registered.

device-sip-registration-datetime.description: When the device last registered, RFC 3339 in UTC. Read-only. `null` when it has never registered. It can lag slightly, because registrations are replicated in batches.

device-sip-registration-expires-datetime.description: When the device's registration expires, RFC 3339 in UTC. Read-only. `null` when it has never registered.

device-sip-registration-expiry-seconds.description: Re-registration period the device is given, in seconds. Defaults to `60`, `30` for a push-enabled app, and `180` for a video bridge.

device-sip-registration-ignore-for-prese.description: `yes` lets the device register without changing the user's presence. Calls on it still show the user as busy. Meant for devices such as video bridges.

device-sip-registration-ignore-report-en.description: `yes` ignores the `rport` parameter in the device's registration and leaves it out of the `Via` header the core sends back.

device-sip-registration-ip-address.description: IP address and port of the device's last registration. Read-only. `null` when it has never registered.

device-sip-registration-user-agent.description: User agent of the device's last registration. Read-only. `null` when it has never registered.

device-sip-no-to-tag-in-cancel.description: `yes` leaves the To tag out of a SIP CANCEL. `no` copies it from an earlier provisional response when there is one.

device-transcode-opus.description: `yes` lets the device negotiate the Opus codec.

device-srtp-enabled.description: Encrypted media (SRTP): `yes` requires it, `opportunistic` uses it when the other side supports it, and `no` turns it off.

auto-answer-enabled.description: `yes` answers calls to this device automatically. Defaults to `no`.

device-sip-allowed-user-agent.description: User agent the device is allowed to register with. Where the core enforces a user agent allowlist, this is filled in automatically when the device's user agent matches the core's `UaAcceptPatterns` setting.

device-sip-nat-traversal-enabled.description: Whether the core relays the device's media (RTP): `automatic` relays unless the other side is `never`; `none` leaves it to the other side, with no relay when both are `none`; `never` never relays; `fixed` is like `automatic` without mid-call port changes; `Sdp` relays at once between the addresses in each side's SDP. Defaults to `automatic`.

device-sip-latency-seconds-current.description: Latency of the last registration, in seconds: the time from the core's authentication challenge to the device's authenticated answer. Read-only.

device-sip-latency-seconds-average.description: Average registration latency over recent registrations, in seconds. Read-only.

emergency-address-id.description: Emergency address used for calls from this device. When the device has none, the user's, site's, or domain's address is returned and `emergency-address-source` says which.

error-reading-from-endpoint-module.description: `yes` when the provisioning lookup on the Endpoints server failed, so the provisioning fields are missing. Otherwise `no`. Read-only.

login-username.description: Login of the device's owner, such as `1001@example.com`. Read-only.

name-full-name.description: Full name of the device's owner. `Unassigned` for a device no user owns. Read-only.

device-models-model.description: Phone brand and model the device is linked to, such as `Yealink T54W`. Send it with `device-provisioning-mac-address` to link a phone. `Manual or Softphone` links nothing.

device-provisioning-mac-address.description: MAC address of the phone the device is linked to, such as `00005e005301`. Send it with `device-models-model` to link a phone.

device-provisioning-registration-core-se.description: Core server the phone is told to register to, by its server name on the platform. Defaults to the platform's configured core server.

device-provisioning-sip-transport-protoc.description: SIP transport the phone is configured to use.

device-provisioning-username.description: User name the phone presents to fetch its configuration file.

device-provisioning-password.description: Password the phone presents to fetch its configuration file. In plain text only when your token is the device's own user; every other caller gets it masked the same way as `device-sip-registration-password`. A Super User gets it in plain text with `include-secrets=yes`, and that read is audit-logged. On update, sending back the masked value you read keeps the stored password; any other mask-shaped value returns `400`.

device-provisioning-line.description: Line on the phone that carries this device. Set it on create, with `device-provisioning-mac-address` and `device-models-model`. Defaults to `1`.

device-provisioning-overrides.description: Provisioning overrides set on this phone only, as `name="value"` pairs joined by `&`. Brand, domain, and site defaults are not included. No length limit.

recording-configuration.description: Deprecated. Use `device-level-call-recording-enabled`. Returned on single-device reads.

geo-country.description: Country of the device's registration IP address, from geolocation. Read-only. `null` when unknown.

geo-region.description: Region or state of the device's registration IP address, from geolocation. Read-only. `null` when unknown.

geo-city.description: City of the device's registration IP address, from geolocation. Read-only. `null` when unknown.

geo-latitude.description: Latitude of the device's registration IP address, from geolocation. Read-only. `null` when unknown.

geo-longitude.description: Longitude of the device's registration IP address, from geolocation. Read-only. `null` when unknown.

device-models-brand-and-model.description: Model name the phone's provisioning row stores, such as `Yealink T54W`. Read-only; send `device-models-model` to change it.

device-sip-registration-transport.description: SIP transport of the device's last registration, as the core recorded it. Read-only. Not the same field as `device-provisioning-sip-transport-protocol`.

emergency-address-source.description: Where `emergency-address-id` came from when the device has no address of its own: `user_level`, or the level the user inherited it from. Read-only.

emergency-address-pretty-printed.description: Emergency address as one line of text. Read-only.

emergency-address-source-ip-address.description: IP address recorded with the emergency address. Read-only.

emergency-address-provisioned-as-endpoin.description: `true` when `caller-id-number-emergency` is provisioned as an endpoint caller ID with the emergency service. Read-only.

Device.description: A SIP device: a registration identity a user's phone, soft phone, or app signs in with. Reads join the device's registration row with its owner and, when the device is linked to a phone, the phone's provisioning row on the Endpoints server. Datetimes are RFC 3339 in UTC (`+00:00`).

domain.description: Domain the row is filed under

reseller.description: Territory of `domain`

call-direction.description: Kind of call, from this row's point of view: `0` outbound, `1` inbound and answered, `2` inbound and missed, `3` on-net (extension to extension)

call-parent-cdr-id.description: Id of the call record. It is on every row, and it is the id the keyed paths and `/quality` take.

call-orig-user.description: Originating user or extension, such as `1001`

call-orig-from-uri.description: SIP From URI of the originating leg

call-orig-from-name.description: Display name in the originating leg's From header

call-orig-to-user.description: User part of the originating leg's To header: the number dialed

call-orig-request-uri.description: SIP Request-URI of the originating leg

call-orig-request-user.description: User part of the originating leg's Request-URI

call-through-user.description: User the call was routed through, such as a forwarding user or a call queue

call-term-to-uri.description: SIP To URI of the terminating leg

call-answer-datetime.description: When the call was answered. Left out for an unanswered call.

call-total-duration-seconds.description: Length of the call, in seconds

hide-from-results.description: `1` hides the row from reads unless they send `showhidden`

privacy.description: `true` when the caller asked for privacy. Name and number fields then read `Anonymous` for scopes below Reseller. Returned under this v1 name.

call-orig-match-uri.description: Connection or route the originating leg matched

call-intelligence-job-id.description: Id of the call's transcription job

call-intelligence-percent-positive.description: Share of the transcript with positive sentiment, as a percent

call-intelligence-percent-neutral.description: Share of the transcript with neutral sentiment, as a percent

call-intelligence-percent-negative.description: Share of the transcript with negative sentiment, as a percent

ending_sentiment.description: Sentiment at the end of the call. Returned under this v1 name.

call-intelligence-topics-top.description: Main topics found in the transcript

call-disposition.description: Disposition set on the call, such as a wrap-up code

call-disposition-notes.description: Notes recorded with the disposition. Stored as text with no practical length limit.

call-account-code.description: Account code entered for the call

call-disconnect-reason-text.description: Why the call ended, as text

call-recording-status.description: Recording state of the call, as a number. `0` is the default.

call-audio-quality-orig-mos.description: Summary MOS of the originating leg, on the 1 to 5 scale: the worse of its two audio directions. Left out until quality scanning has seen the call. `GET /cdrs/{id}/quality` has each direction.

call-audio-quality-term-mos.description: Summary MOS of the terminating leg, on the 1 to 5 scale: the worse of its two audio directions. Left out until quality scanning has seen the call. `GET /cdrs/{id}/quality` has each direction.

call-intelligence-summary.description: Summary of the call written by call intelligence. Stored as text with no practical length limit.

call-last-updated-datetime.description: When the row last changed, in UTC

call-term-to-name.description: Display name in the terminating leg's To header

id.description: Id of the full call record, the same value as `call-parent-cdr-id`. Expanded shape only.

core-server.description: Core server that handled the call

call-server-mac-address.description: MAC address of the core server

call-leg-ordinal-index.description: Position of this leg in the call

call-orig-call-id.description: SIP Call-ID of the originating leg

call-orig-ip-address.description: IP address the originating leg came from

call-orig-from-user.description: User part of the originating leg's From header

call-orig-from-host.description: Host part of the originating leg's From header

call-orig-request-host.description: Host part of the originating leg's Request-URI

call-orig-to-uri.description: SIP To URI of the originating leg

call-orig-to-host.description: Host part of the originating leg's To header

call-through-action.description: How the call reached `call-through-user`, such as `ForwardAlways`, `ForwardNoAns`, `QueueDispatch`, `XferBlind`, or `XferSup`

call-through-call-id.description: SIP Call-ID of the leg through `call-through-user`

call-term-call-id.description: SIP Call-ID of the terminating leg

call-term-ip-address.description: IP address the terminating leg was sent to

call-term-match-uri.description: Connection or route the terminating leg matched

call-ringing-datetime.description: When the terminating party started ringing

call-on-hold-duration-seconds.description: Seconds the call spent on hold

call-record-creation-datetime.description: When the call record was written

call-disposition-submitted-datetime.description: When the disposition was submitted. Left out when there is none.

call-batch-sequence-marker.description: Release code of the leg, such as `end`

call-audio-relay-side-a-local-port.description: Local port of the audio relay, side A

call-audio-relay-side-a-remote-ip.description: Remote address and port of the audio relay, side A, as `address:port`

call-audio-relay-side-b-remote-ip.description: Remote address and port of the audio relay, side B, as `address:port`

call-audio-relay-side-a-packet-count.description: Audio packets relayed on side A

call-audio-relay-side-b-packet-count.description: Audio packets relayed on side B

call-fax-codec.description: Codec the fax media used, as the switch recorded it (for example `T.38`). Absent when the call carried no fax.

call-fax-relay-side-a-local-port.description: Local port of the fax relay, side A

call-fax-relay-side-a-remote-ip.description: Remote address and port of the fax relay, side A, as `address:port`

call-fax-relay-side-b-remote-ip.description: Remote address and port of the fax relay, side B, as `address:port`

call-fax-relay-side-a-packet-count.description: Fax packets relayed on side A

call-fax-relay-side-b-packet-count.description: Fax packets relayed on side B

call-video-codec.description: Codec the video media used, as the switch recorded it. Absent on an audio-only call.

call-video-relay-side-a-local-port.description: Local port of the video relay, side A

CdrU.description: A user's call detail record (CDR), expanded shape: the base fields plus the full call record. Returned when `limit` is 100 or less, when `raw` is sent, and on every read by id. Empty fields are left out.

id.description: The entry's ID. Access and disclosure entries only.

event-category.description: The kind of entry. Present on access and disclosure entries, and on every entry when `event-category` names more than one log.

by-user.description: Who did this, as a bare extension.

by-domain.description: The reader's domain. Not necessarily the domain of the data.

by-client.description: The application that made the request.

by-scope.description: The reader's scope, such as `Office Manager`. Three values name a request that carried no token: `signed-url` (a file fetched through a signed link), `share-link` (a public SIP trace share link), and `matrix-token` (a chat attachment). Access entries only.

mask-chain.description: Who the reader really is, when masquerading. Empty otherwise.

action-type.description: `read`, `list`, `search`, `play`, `download`, `export`, `login`, `logout`, or a configuration action. `download` and `export` are the disclosure actions.

target-object.description: The kind of thing the entry is about. Access entries use the object name in lower case, such as `cdr`, `recording`, `voicemail`, `user`, or `device`. Change entries use display labels, such as `Subscriber` and `Call Queue`.

target-domain.description: The domain the data belongs to.

target-user.description: The person whose data was read, as a bare extension in `target-domain`. Empty for a search covering many people.

target-host.description: The server that recorded the entry.

auditlog-details.description: What changed, with secrets replaced by `********`. Change entries only, and omitted when empty.

record-id.description: The record that was read, such as a CDR ID, a recording ID, a device address, or a phone MAC address. Empty for a search or list. Access entries only.

query-parameters.description: What was searched for. Personal attributes are replaced with `<REMOVED>`. Access entries only.

result-count.description: How many records came back: the real count, not the requested limit. Access entries only.

data-subjects.description: The people whose data this disclosed, as phone numbers and extensions. Always the complete list. Access entries only.

data-subjects-count.description: How many distinct people are in `data-subjects`. Access entries only.

actor-tier.description: Where the reader sat relative to the data: `self` (the same organization), `reseller` (an intermediary), or `platform` (platform staff). Access entries only.

part2-covered.description: Whether the data was subject to 42 CFR Part 2 when read. Access entries only.

hipaa-covered.description: Whether the data was subject to HIPAA when read. Access entries only.

gdpr-covered.description: Whether the data was subject to GDPR when read. Access entries only.

credential.description: Whether the response carried a secret, such as a SIP registration password or a PIN. Logged whatever the reader's relationship to the data. Blank on entries written before `schema-version` `1.1`. Access entries only.

recipient.description: Where the data went, when that was not the reader, such as a scheduled export's destination host. Empty for an interactive read. Access and disclosure entries only.

ticket-reference.description: The support ticket the session was opened under. Empty when none.

schema-version.description: The set of fields that existed when the entry was written, such as `1.1`. A field added later is blank on older entries.

Accesslog.description: One compliance log entry. Sign-in and change entries carry the reader and target fields only; access and disclosure entries carry every field.

token.description: The JWT access token. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. If its `user_scope` claim is `mfa_required`, it only completes MFA login and expires in 5 minutes.

refresh.description: A JWT that can only be exchanged for a new token pair through `POST /jwt` with `refresh`. It is not accepted by other endpoints.

JwtRequestSuccess.description: A JWT access token and the refresh token that renews it.

exp.description: Expiry time, as a Unix timestamp in seconds

iat.description: Issue time, as a Unix timestamp in seconds

iss.description: Issuer: the server that issued the token

jti.description: JWT ID, 40 lowercase hexadecimal characters. Pass it to `DELETE /jwt/{jti}` to revoke the token

domain.description: The owner's domain

user.description: The owner's user (extension)

user_email.description: The owner's email address, or `null` if none is set

user_scope.description: The owner's user scope, such as `Basic User` or `Office Manager`. `mfa_required` marks a token that only completes MFA login

displayName.description: The owner's first and last name

apiversion.description: The API version of the server that answered, or `development`

req_host.description: The hostname the token was requested from

token_type.description: Whether this is an access or refresh token

mask_chain.description: For a masquerade token, the users who masqueraded, starting with the real user. For an API-key token, the key ID

login.description: The owner's login name, if set

parent_scope.description: For a custom scope, the built-in scope it derives from

scope_mods.description: For a custom scope, the permissions it removes from its parent

scope_read_only.description: For a custom scope, whether it is read-only

mfa_vendor.description: Only on an `mfa_required` token: the MFA vendor, such as `google`

mfa_type.description: Only on an `mfa_required` token: the MFA type, such as `authenticator`

application.description: Only on a token from `POST /jwt/application-token`: the application it was issued for

JwtResponse.description: The claims of a JWT, plus the `apiversion` of the server that decoded it. Claims that do not apply to a token may be `null` or absent.

application.description: The target application, such as `websocket`. Letters, digits, hyphens and underscores only. Copied into the token's `application` claim

ApplicationTokenRequest.description: Names the application a short-lived token is for.

token.description: A JWT that expires 30 seconds after issue. It carries every claim of the caller's token plus `application`
JWT access token. It is valid for 1 hour and is also set as the `ns_access_token` cookie. While MFA is pending, it only allows the MFA step.

refresh.description: JWT refresh token. It is valid for 30 days and is also set as the `ns_refresh_token` cookie. Absent while MFA is pending.

auth_requirement.description: Login policy of the user's domain, for example `login_name_and_password` (the default), `single_sign_on` or `authenticator_totp`

allow_user_primary_email_edit.description: `true` if the domain lets users change their own primary email address

account_recovery_user_primary_email.description: `true` if the domain uses the user's primary email address for account recovery

email.description: The user's primary email address, or an empty string

domain.description: The user's domain

mfa.description: MFA state. `mfa_required_setup` means the domain requires MFA and the user hasn't enrolled yet. Absent when MFA doesn't apply.

email_verification_data.description: Email verification status for the user, when available

scope.description: `mfa_required` when MFA is pending. Absent otherwise.

mfa_vendor.description: Vendor of the user's MFA enrollment, such as `google`. Present only while MFA is pending.

mfa_type.description: Type of the user's MFA enrollment, such as `authenticator`. Present only while MFA is pending.

user_email.description: The user's email address. Present only while MFA is pending.

NetsapiensJsResponse.description: Successful login from `/netsapiensjs`. The tokens are also set as `ns_access_token` and `ns_refresh_token` cookies. If `scope` is `mfa_required`, the body instead holds a limited `token` and the MFA fields.

authenticated.description: Always `true`. An unauthenticated request gets `401` instead.

uid.description: User ID in `user@domain` form

user.description: User part of `uid`, for example `1001` in `1001@example.com`

domain.description: The user's domain

expires_at.description: When the token expires, as a Unix timestamp in seconds

expires_in.description: Seconds until the token expires. Never negative.

email.description: The user's email address from the subscriber record

scope.description: The user's scope, for example `Basic User` or `Office Manager`

territory.description: Territory that the user's domain belongs to

department.description: The user's department, from the subscriber record

avatar.description: Path of the user's avatar image, `/ns-api/v2/avatar/{filename}`. Absent when the user has no avatar.

avatar_filename.description: File name of the user's avatar. Absent when the user has no avatar.

parent_scope.description: Built-in scope that a custom scope is derived from. Present only for custom scopes.

scope_mods.description: Restrictions that the custom scope applies to its parent scope. Present only for custom scopes.

scope_read_only.description: `true` if the custom scope is read-only. Present only for custom scopes.

masquerading.description: `true` during a masquerade session. The other fields then describe the masqueraded user.

real_user.description: The admin behind a masquerade session, with `uid`, `user`, `domain`, `scope` and `territory`

mask_chain.description: Chain of identities in a masquerade session, starting with the admin

depth.description: Number of masquerade levels in the session

masquerade_expired.description: `true` if an expired masquerade session was just cleared

previous_masquerade_uid.description: User that the expired masquerade session was for

active_masquerade_sessions.description: Masquerade sessions this user has open on any device. Empty if there are none.

MeResponse.description: Identity of the access token holder, from `/oauth/me`. Fields not marked required appear only when the token or subscriber record has them.

message.description: A readable summary, such as `Masquerade ended successfully` or `Ended 2 masquerade session(s)`

real_user.description: You: the logged-in user now in effect

uid.description: Unique identifier for the real user in the format user@domain.

scope.description: Your user scope

domain.description: The domain the real user belongs to.

previous_effective_user.description: The user you were acting as. Present only when a masquerade session was resolved.

uid.description: Unique identifier for the previous effective user in the format user@domain.

scope.description: That user's user scope

session_id.description: Always `null`: you are no longer in a session

ended_session_ids.description: The IDs of the sessions that ended

end_mode.description: `session_scoped` means one named session ended, and `end_all` means every session you own ended

success.description: Indicates whether the pop operation completed successfully.

message.description: A readable summary, such as `Popped back to 1001@example.com`

masquerading.description: `true`: you are still acting as another user

effective_user.description: The user identity that is now active after popping back one level.

scope.description: The effective user's user scope

domain.description: The domain the effective user belongs to.

popped_to_real_user.description: `true`: the session ended and you are acting as yourself

scope.description: user scope of the real user.

territory.description: The territory or region assigned to the real user.
