tag.description: Account label shown in the authenticator app, usually the user's `user@domain`. Must not be empty or `0`.

title.description: Issuer name shown next to the code in the authenticator app, usually your app or company name. Optional.

MfaVerifyRequest.title: MfaVerifyRequest
MfaVerifyRequest.description: Request body for `/oauth/mfaVerify`. No authentication is required, and nothing is saved.

mfa_key.title: TOTP secret
mfa_key.description: Base32 TOTP secret from `/oauth/genAuthenticator`: 16 uppercase characters from `A-Z2-7`

mfa_passcode.title: Authenticator app code
mfa_passcode.description: The 6-digit code currently shown in the authenticator app. Codes up to 60 seconds early or late are accepted.

mfa_vendor.title: MFA vendor
mfa_vendor.description: Must be `google`, in lowercase. Any other value returns `valid: false` with `Unsupported MFA vendor/type combination`.

mfa_type.title: MFA mechanism
mfa_type.description: Must be `authenticator`, in lowercase. Any other value returns `valid: false` with `Unsupported MFA vendor/type combination`.

MfaVerifyResponse.title: MfaVerifyResponse
MfaVerifyResponse.description: Response from `/oauth/mfaVerify`. Always sent with HTTP `200`.

status.title: Outcome
status.description: `success` if the passcode matched, `error` for any failure

valid.title: Verification result
valid.description: `true` if the passcode matched. Branch on this field.

message.title: Outcome message
message.description: Reason for the result: `MFA passcode verified successfully`, `Invalid MFA passcode`, `Missing required parameters for MFA verification` or `Unsupported MFA vendor/type combination`
enum: Missing required parameters for MFA verification

apiversion.title: Server build version
apiversion.description: Build version of the API that answered, or `development` on a development server

MfaEnrollRequest.title: MfaEnrollRequest
MfaEnrollRequest.description: Request body for `/oauth/mfaEnroll`. The user's `username` and `password` stand in for an access token.

ns_id.title: Subject identifier
ns_id.description: The subscriber to enroll, in `user@domain` form

ns_id_type.title: Subject type
ns_id_type.description: Kind of identity in `ns_id`. Use `subscriber` for users.

mfa_key.title: TOTP secret
mfa_key.description: Base32 TOTP secret from `/oauth/genAuthenticator`: 16 uppercase characters from `A-Z2-7`

mfa_vendor.title: MFA vendor
mfa_vendor.description: Must be `google`, in lowercase. The value is saved as sent, and later logins only recognize `google`.

mfa_type.title: MFA mechanism
mfa_type.description: Must be `authenticator`, in lowercase. The value is saved as sent.

mfa_passcode.title: Authenticator app code
mfa_passcode.description: The 6-digit code currently shown in the authenticator app. It is checked against `mfa_key` before anything is saved, and codes up to 60 seconds early or late are accepted.

password.title: Portal password
password.description: The user's password. Wrong credentials return `409`.

MfaEnrollWithTokenRequest.title: MfaEnrollWithTokenRequest
MfaEnrollWithTokenRequest.description: Request body for `/oauth/mfaEnrollWithToken`. The subscriber comes from the access token, and `ns_id_type` is always `subscriber`.

mfa_key.title: TOTP secret
mfa_key.description: Base32 TOTP secret from `/oauth/genAuthenticator`: 16 uppercase characters from `A-Z2-7`

mfa_vendor.title: MFA vendor
mfa_vendor.description: Must be `google`, in lowercase. The value is saved as sent, and later logins only recognize `google`.

mfa_type.title: MFA mechanism
mfa_type.description: Must be `authenticator`, in lowercase. The value is saved as sent.

mfa_passcode.title: Authenticator app code
mfa_passcode.description: The 6-digit code currently shown in the authenticator app. It is checked against `mfa_key` before anything is saved, and codes up to 60 seconds early or late are accepted.

MfaDeleteRequest.title: MfaDeleteRequest
MfaDeleteRequest.description: Request body for `/oauth/mfaDelete`. Leave out `ns_id` to remove your own enrollment.

mfa_vendor.title: MFA vendor
mfa_vendor.description: Vendor of the enrollment to remove, `google`. A value that doesn't match removes nothing.

mfa_type.title: MFA mechanism
mfa_type.description: Type of the enrollment to remove, `authenticator`. A value that doesn't match removes nothing.

ns_id.title: Target subscriber (admin only)
ns_id.description: Subscriber whose enrollment to remove, in `user@domain` form. Defaults to the token holder. Naming another user requires Super User, Reseller, Office Manager or Site Manager scope.

ns_id_type.title: Target subject type
ns_id_type.description: Kind of identity in `ns_id`. Defaults to `subscriber`, and is used only with `ns_id`.

grant_type.description: OAuth grant to run. Use `password` to log in with a username and password. The endpoint also accepts `refresh_token`, `authorization_code`, `mfa`, `google`, `office`, `apple`, `oidc`, `masquerade`, `delegated`, `guest` and `chat_guest`. Any other value returns `400`.

client_id.description: ID of your OAuth client. You can send it with `client_secret` as HTTP Basic credentials in the `Authorization` header instead. A Super User creates OAuth clients with `POST /oauth-clients`.

client_secret.description: Secret of the OAuth client named by `client_id`. You can send both as HTTP Basic credentials instead.

username.description: Login name of the user. It is matched against the user's login name, which is often `user@domain` but can be an email address.

AuthRequest.description: Request body for the OAuth password grant. The same body with a different `grant_type` runs the other grants.

username.description: Login name sent with the password grant. Present only for `grant_type` `password`.

user.description: Extension of the user. Omitted by the MFA grant.

domain.description: Domain of the user.

site.description: Site of the user. Omitted when the user has no site.

group.description: Same value as `site`, kept for older clients. Omitted when the user has no site.

uid.description: User ID in the form `extension@domain`.

login.description: Login name of the user. It can differ from `uid`, for example when it is an email address.

scope.description: User scope of the token, such as `Office Manager`. `mfa_required` means the login is not finished: send `access_token` and a passcode to `POST /tokens` with `grant_type` `mfa`.

displayName.description: First and last name of the user.

access_token.description: Bearer token for API requests. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`.

expires_in.description: Seconds until `access_token` expires. 3,600 by default, and 600 when `scope` is `mfa_required`.

refresh_token.description: Token for a new access token with `grant_type` `refresh_token`. Valid for 4 days by default. Omitted when `scope` is `mfa_required`.

client_id.description: Client ID of the OAuth client that requested the token.

apiversion.description: Version of the API package that answered, or `development` on an unversioned build.

mfa.description: MFA state of a login that is not finished: `mfa_required`, or `mfa_required_setup` when the domain requires an authenticator app the user has not set up.

mfa_vendor.description: MFA vendor of the user's MFA record, such as `google`. `setup_required` when the user has not set one up.

mfa_type.description: MFA type of the user's MFA record, such as `authenticator`. `setup_required` when the user has not set one up.

avatar.description: Path to the user's avatar image. Present only when the user has one.

AccessToken.description: Access token issued by `POST /tokens`. The fields depend on the grant: only the password grant returns `username`, the MFA grant omits `user`, and a login that still needs MFA carries `mfa`, `mfa_vendor` and `mfa_type` and no `refresh_token`.

description.description: Purpose of the key, shown in listings. At least 12 characters on create.

key-id.description: Key ID: the first 12 characters of the key. Identifies the key in paths, logs and audit records. The prefix shows the tier: `nss_`, `nsr_`, `nsd_` or `nsu_`. Set by the server.

key.description: Secret API key, 60 characters. Returned only in the `POST /apikeys` response. Store it securely: it cannot be read again.

reseller.description: Territory the key can reach. `*` for Super User keys. A Reseller key needs a specific territory.

user.description: Extension the key acts as. `*` when the key is not tied to one user. Required for user-level scopes.

domain.description: Domain the key can reach. `*` for Super User and Reseller keys. Required for Office Manager scope and lower.

user-scope.description: Scope that sets the key's permissions. A custom scope name is also accepted. `Site Manager` and `No Portal` are not supported. Required on create.

ip-address.description: Comma-separated IPv4 or IPv6 addresses and CIDR ranges the key can be used from. `*` allows any address. A request from any other address returns `403`.

readonly.description: `yes` limits the key to read, list and count actions, and any other action returns `403`. `no` allows every action the scope permits.

can-create-keys.description: `yes` lets the key create keys and update the keys it created. `no` blocks both. Revoking does not need it.

anyOf.description: A string with a specific model or "*" for all.

items.description: A string with a specific model or "*" for all. The specific models reference the API's scope defintions stored in the DB.

allowed-models.description: Objects the key can access. `*` allows every object. On create or update, send a string or an array of object names; reads return an array unless the value is `*`. A request for any other object returns `403`, but the key can always read itself. Object names come from the scope definitions and can differ from path names.

created-datetime.description: When the key was created.

lastused-datetime.description: When the key was last used. Updated during periodic token cleanup, not on every request, so it can lag behind the real last use. Null when the key has never been used.

notes.description: Reminder to store `key` now. Returned only by `POST /apikeys`.

ApiKey.description: API key for machine-to-machine access. Send the secret `key` as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. Every other field is readable; only `description`, `ip-address` and `allowed-models` can be changed after creation.

client_id.description: Not checked by the MFA grant. Send the same value as in the password login.

client_secret.description: Not checked by the MFA grant. Send the same value as in the password login.

username.description: Not read by the MFA grant. The user comes from `access_token`.

password.description: Must be present on `POST /jwt`, which uses it to pick the grant. Its value is not checked. Not read on `POST /tokens`.

mfa_type.description: Not read by the MFA grant

mfa_vendor.description: Not read by the MFA grant

ns_id_type.description: Which MFA record to check: `subscriber` for API and Portal logins, `level1` for Admin UI logins

passcode.description: 6-digit passcode from the user's authenticator app. Codes up to 2 time steps (about 60 seconds) old or ahead are accepted.

access_token.description: Limited token from the password login whose scope is `mfa_required`. Either the opaque token from `POST /tokens` or the JWT from `POST /jwt` works.

AuthRequestMFA.description: Request body for the MFA grant. Send it after a password login returns a limited token whose scope is `mfa_required`.

status.description: `healthy` when every check passed, `degraded` when any failed. The HTTP status is `200` either way.

timestamp.description: When the checks ran, in RFC 3339 UTC with a `Z` suffix. Up to 15 seconds old, because results are cached.

hostname.description: The hostname of the server that answered.

app_version.description: The API package version, such as `46.0.1234`. `dev` on a server without a version stamp.

environment.description: Only with a valid token. The deployment environment, such as `production`. `development` when unset.

php_version.description: Only with a valid token. The PHP version, such as `8.5.3`.

checks.description: Only with a valid token. The result of each dependency check: `cache`, `database`, and `sbus`.

cache.description: The cache check: a key is written, read back, and deleted.

status.description: `ok`, `error: read-back mismatch`, or `error: ` followed by the error the cache raised.

engine.description: The class name of the cache engine in use. Absent when the check raised an error.

database.description: One entry per database connection, keyed by connection name. A connection with no host configured is left out, so not every key is always present.

default.description: `ok`, or `error` followed by the database driver's numeric error code when there is one, such as `error (2002)`. Never any other text from the error.

nsapi.description: `ok`, or `error` followed by the database driver's numeric error code when there is one, such as `error (2002)`. Never any other text from the error.

sipbx.description: `ok`, or `error` followed by the database driver's numeric error code when there is one, such as `error (2002)`. Never any other text from the error.

cdr.description: `ok`, or `error` followed by the database driver's numeric error code when there is one, such as `error (2002)`. Never any other text from the error.

ndp.description: `ok`, or `error` followed by the database driver's numeric error code when there is one, such as `error (2002)`. Never any other text from the error.

voipmonitor.description: `ok`, or `error` followed by the database driver's numeric error code when there is one, such as `error (2002)`. Never any other text from the error.

sbus.description: The message bus check: the bus's status page is fetched with a 2-second timeout.

status.description: `ok` when the bus answered and lists at least one peer, `ok (no proxies)` when it answered with none, `unreachable` when it did not answer with `200`, and `error` when the check itself failed. `ok (no proxies)` still counts as healthy.

url.description: The bus URL that was checked. Absent when `status` is `error`.

proxies.description: The number of peers the bus reports. Present when `status` starts with `ok`.

reason.description: Why the check failed. Present when `status` is `unreachable` or `error`.

HealthResponse.description: The health report for the server that answered. Without a token, only `status`, `timestamp`, `hostname`, and `app_version` are present. With a valid token, `environment`, `php_version`, and `checks` are added.

total.description: Number of records that match the request's filters.

phonenumber.description: The phone number, digits with the country code, for example `15555550123`. 7 to 249 characters, and 16 at most when the number has an SMS assignment. The API stores it exactly as sent and does not convert it to E.164, so use the same form everywhere.

domain.description: The domain the number is assigned to. A write takes it from the path.

enabled.description: Whether the number routes calls. A disabled number is skipped when a call is matched.

dial-rule-application.description: The application that handles a call to the number, read together with the destination user and host. `available-number` keeps the number in the domain without routing it.

dial-rule-parameter.description: An extra setting for the application, such as the SIP header an `*-add-header` application adds. Send `<NULL>` to clear it. It reads back as an empty string.

dial-rule-translation-destination-user.description: Where the call goes, read together with `dial-rule-application`: a user's extension, a call queue's extension, or an off-net number. `[*]` keeps the dialed number.

dial-rule-translation-destination-host.description: The host part of the destination, usually your domain. `[*]` keeps the dialed host.

dial-rule-translation-source-name.description: The caller ID name sent with the call. `[*]` keeps the caller's name, and text around it is added to that name, for example `Sales_[*]`. Defaults to `[*]` on create.

dial-rule-description.description: A note on the number for your own tracking, up to 63 characters. Send an empty string to clear it.

sms-enabled.description: Present and `true` when the number has an SMS assignment. Absent means it has none.

sms-application.description: What receives the number's messages. `available` unassigns the number and clears `sms-dest`. Left out on a write, it is `user` when `sms-dest` is sent and `available` otherwise.

sms-carrier.description: The carrier the number sends and receives messages through, one of the platform's configured SMS carriers such as `bandwidth`. Not case-sensitive. Left out on an update, the current carrier is kept.

sms-dest.description: The extension of the user or call queue that receives the number's messages. Left out on an update, the current destination is kept.

sms-only.description: Present and `true` on a row for an SMS number that has no dial rule. These rows carry only `phonenumber`, `domain`, and the SMS fields. In a list they follow the dial-rule rows, and `/count` includes them.

mms-capable.description: Present and `true` when the number's carrier supports MMS, by the platform-wide carrier list. A per-domain carrier setting is not reflected: read `GET /domains/{domain}/smsnumbers` for that.

group-mms-capable.description: Present and `true` when the number's carrier supports group messaging, by the platform-wide carrier list. A per-domain carrier setting is not reflected.

domain-invalid.description: Present and `true` only on an SMS-only row whose domain no longer exists. Clean the number up, but do not link to the domain.

Phonenumber.description: A phone number in the domain's DID (direct inward dialing) table, with where calls to it go and its SMS assignment, if any. A row with `sms-only` set to `true` has no dial rule and carries only `phonenumber`, `domain`, and the SMS fields. Fields that do not apply are left out, not sent as `null`.

DialruleApplication.description: Application that routes the call, together with the destination user and host.

domain.description: Domain that owns the dial plan. `admin-only` for a platform-shared plan

dial-rule-dial-plan.description: Name of the dial plan the rule belongs to

dial-rule-matching-to-uri.description: Destination pattern the rule matches, as a SIP URI. `?` matches one character and `*` matches anything, so `sip:611@*` matches 611 dialed to any host

dialrule.description: Rule id. Use it to read, update, or delete the rule. It is the base64url encoding of the match fields joined with `||`, in this order: `dial-rule-matching-to-uri`, `dial-rule-matching-from-uri`, `dial-rule-matching-day-of-week`, `dial-rule-matching-start-time`, `dial-rule-matching-end-time`, `dial-rule-matching-start-date`, `dial-rule-matching-end-date`. When every field after the first is `*`, it encodes `dial-rule-matching-to-uri` alone. Read-only

enabled.description: Whether the rule is used for matching. A disabled rule is skipped

dial-rule-matching-from-uri.description: Caller pattern the rule also requires, as a SIP URI. `*` matches any caller

dial-rule-matching-day-of-week.description: Days the rule applies: one digit from `0` (Sunday) to `6` (Saturday), or a range in brackets such as `[1-5]`. `*` matches every day

dial-rule-matching-start-date.description: First day the rule applies, as `YYYY-MM-DD`. `*` means no start date

dial-rule-matching-end-date.description: Last day the rule applies, as `YYYY-MM-DD`. `*` means no end date

dial-rule-matching-start-time.description: Time of day the rule starts applying, as `HH:MM` from `00:00` to `23:59`. `*` means all day. Uses the time zone of the user the call passes through, when there is one

dial-rule-matching-end-time.description: Time of day the rule stops applying, as `HH:MM` from `00:00` to `23:59`. `*` means all day. Uses the time zone of the user the call passes through, when there is one

dial-rule-parameter.description: Extra setting for the application in `dial-rule-application`. Its meaning depends on the application. Empty by default

dial-rule-translation-destination-scheme.description: URI scheme of the destination. `[*]` keeps the scheme of the incoming request and is correct in most cases. `sip:` sets it to SIP

dial-rule-translation-destination-user.description: Where a matching call goes, read together with `dial-rule-application` and `dial-rule-translation-destination-host`. A user, a call queue, or an off-net number, depending on the application

dial-rule-translation-destination-host.description: Host of the destination: usually a domain, or a connection name for off-net routing. `[*]` keeps the incoming host

dial-rule-translation-source-name.description: Caller ID name passed on. `[*]` keeps the incoming value. Add text around it to change it, for example `sales_[*]`

dial-rule-translation-source-scheme.description: URI scheme of the caller. `[*]` keeps the scheme of the incoming request and is correct in most cases. `sip:` sets it to SIP

dial-rule-translation-source-user.description: Caller ID number passed on: the part of the caller's SIP URI before `@`. `[*]` keeps the incoming value. `<OwnCidNmbr>` substitutes the user's caller ID number

dial-rule-translation-source-host.description: Host part of the caller's SIP URI, after `@`. `[*]` keeps the incoming value. `<OwnDomain>` substitutes the user's domain

dial-rule-description.description: Free-text description of the rule

DialRule.description: A dial rule: one entry in a dial plan that matches a call and says where to send it.

domain.description: Domain that owns the dial plan. `admin-only` or `*` for a platform-shared plan

dial-rule-description.description: Free-text description of the dial plan. Defaults to `dialplan for <domain>` when created without one

Dialplan.description: A dial plan: a named set of dial rules owned by a domain.

description.description: New free-text description of the policy

DialpolicyUpdate.description: Body of a dial policy update. Only `description` can change.

permission-match.description: Destination pattern to match. `?` matches one character and `*` matches any run of characters

permission-mode.description: `permit` allows a matching call; `deny` blocks it

permission-reason.description: Short label for the rule, up to 31 characters

PermissionCreate.description: Body of a new dial policy rule.

permission-mode.description: `permit` allows a matching call; `deny` blocks it

permission-reason.description: Short label for the rule, up to 31 characters

PermissionUpdate.description: Body of a dial policy rule update. The match cannot change.

dialpolicy.description: Policy name. Unique within a domain; letters, digits, spaces, `.`, `&`, `-` and `_`

domain.description: Domain the policy is filed under. `*` or `admin-only` marks a shared policy that every domain can use; only a Super User can create or change one

description.description: Free-text description of the policy, up to 127 characters

Dialpolicy.description: A dial policy: a named set of permit and deny rules that decides which numbers a user may call.

dialpolicy.description: Name of the policy the rule belongs to

domain.description: Domain the rule is filed under: the policy's own domain, or `*` or `admin-only` for a shared policy

permission-match.description: Destination pattern the rule matches, up to 127 characters. `?` matches one character and `*` matches any run of characters, as in `sip:+1900???????@*`. `*` alone matches every call

permission-mode.description: What happens to a call that matches. `permit` allows it; `deny` blocks it

permission-reason.description: Short label for the rule, up to 31 characters. It is shown in the call trace when the rule denies a call

created-datetime.description: When the rule's row was last written, in RFC 3339

permission-id.description: Rule identifier for read, update and delete: the base64url encoding of `permission-match`, without `=` padding. Read-only

Permission.description: One rule of a dial policy. The rule matches a dialed destination and permits or denies the call.

RouteProfileCallRouting.description: The route of a route profile, as sent on create or update.

route-method.description: How the route picks a connection. On create it defaults to `percentage`; on update an omitted value keeps the stored one.

route-is-enabled.description: `no` stops the route from matching calls. On create it defaults to `yes`; on update an omitted value keeps the stored one.

description.description: Route description. On create it defaults to the profile's `description`; on update an omitted value keeps the stored one.

routecon.description: The route's connections, each written by `route-connection-ordinal-index`. The list is checked before anything is published.

route-connection-ordinal-index.description: Position of this connection in the route: a positive whole number, used once per request. Omitted, the connection takes the next free index, after the stored ones on update.

route-connection-translation-destination.description: Translation applied to the destination user. Defaults to `[*]`.
Host the call is sent to, such as `carrier1.example.com`. Required and not blank.

route-connection-integer-percentage.description: Share of calls, in percent, when `route-method` is `percentage`. Defaults to `0`.

route-connection-integer-cost.description: Cost of this connection when `route-method` is `cost`. Defaults to `0`.

RouteProfileCreate.description: Body for `POST /domains/{domain}/routeprofiles`. The domain comes from the path.

connection-orig-match-pattern.description: The profile's identifier. Unique across the platform. Also sets the route name.

description.description: Free-text description of the profile.

RouteProfileUpdate.description: Body for the route-profile `PUT` endpoints. Every field is optional.

description.description: Free-text description of the profile.

route-id.description: Read only. Key for `PUT` and `DELETE /routes/{route-id}` and the route's connections: base64url, without padding, of `route-destination-match-pattern` when the other 3 match fields are `*`, otherwise of all 4 joined by `||`.

route-destination-match-pattern.description: Destination pattern a call must match, such as `sip:1800*@*`. Required on create. Part of the route's identity.

route-source-match-pattern.description: Source pattern a call must match. `*`, the default, matches every caller. Part of the route's identity.

route-class.description: Call class the route applies to. `*`, the default, matches every class. Part of the route's identity.

route-match-server-hostname.description: Core server hostname the route is limited to, such as `core1.example.com`. `*`, the default, applies it on every core server. Part of the route's identity.

route-is-enabled.description: `no` stops the route from matching calls. Defaults to `yes`.

description.description: Free-text description of what the route is for.

route-method.description: How the route picks a connection: `fixed` tries them in `route-connection-ordinal-index` order, `cost` picks the lowest `route-connection-integer-cost`, and `percentage` splits calls by `route-connection-integer-percentage`. Defaults to `fixed`.

Route.description: A call route: the pattern a call must match, and how the route picks among its route connections. The 4 match fields identify the route, and `route-id` encodes them.

route-destination-match-pattern.description: Read only. The parent route's destination pattern.

route-source-match-pattern.description: Read only. The parent route's source pattern.

route-class.description: Read only. The parent route's class.

route-match-server-hostname.description: Read only. The parent route's core server hostname.

route-connection-ordinal-index.description: Position of this connection in the route, from `1`. With `route-method` `fixed`, connections are tried in this order. On `POST /routes/{route-id}/routecon` it defaults to one more than the highest index.

route-connection-translation-destination.description: Translation applied to the destination user when the call goes to this connection. Defaults to `[*]`.
Host the call is sent to, such as `carrier1.example.com`. Required and not blank on create. On update, an omitted host keeps the stored one.

route-connection-integer-percentage.description: Share of calls, in percent, for this connection when `route-method` is `percentage`.

route-connection-integer-cost.description: Cost of this connection, used when `route-method` is `cost`.

RouteConnection.description: One route connection: a next hop of a route. The 4 match fields are the parent route's and come from `route-id` on a write; `call-routing` in a route profile leaves them out.

RouteProfile.description: A route profile: a connection whose address names a route instead of a SIP peer. The SIP fields of a connection are left out, and `call-routing` carries the route.

domain.description: Domain that owns the profile.

description.description: Free-text description of the profile.
description.example: Primary SIP trunk connection for inbound and outbound calls

connection-id.description: Key for the route-profile endpoints: base64url, without padding, of `connection-orig-match-pattern`.

connection-orig-match-pattern.description: The profile's identifier, unique across the platform. Set on create and not changed afterward.

connection-usage-role.description: Connection role, such as `customer`. Defaults to `customer`.

last-modified-datetime.description: When the profile was last changed.

call-routing.description: The profile's route, with the fields of `Route` except `route-id`, and `routecon`, its connections in `RouteConnection` form without the 4 match fields. `route-destination-match-pattern` is `DOMAIN_name`: the domain in capitals, `_`, and the part of `connection-orig-match-pattern` after any `@`. Absent when the profile has no route.

route-id.description: This is an id that will be needed to edit, delete the route as well as manage its route connection rules.

route-destination-match-pattern.description: This is the main route match for the destination.

route-source-match-pattern.description: This is the source route, in most cases this should default to * and not be set otherwise.

route-class.description: This for jurisdictional routing of class. Leave as * for most cases.

route-match-server-hostname.description: This field will limit the route to only be effective on a matching hostname. This allow for localized routing to a closest carrier's POP or other special cases.

route-is-enabled.description: Ability to disable a route, when not enabled the route will not be used for any matching.

description.description: This is the route description, use to to give a plain english explanation as to what the route is intended to do.

route-method.description: This is the type of route to select the distribution method for the next hop/connection setting.

routecon.description: An ordered list of route container objects that define how calls are routed through this connection.

example.description: Primary SIP trunk connection for inbound and outbound calls

ConnectionCreate.description: Body for `POST /connections`. Read-only fields are ignored.

DomainConnectionCreate.description: Body for `POST /domains/{domain}/connections`. Read-only fields and `domain` are ignored.

ConnectionUpdate.description: Body for the connection `PUT` endpoints. Send only what changes. `connection-orig-match-pattern`, `domain`, and read-only fields are ignored.

connection-id.description: Read only. Key for the keyed connection paths: base64url, without padding, of `connection-orig-match-pattern`. Ignored in a request body.

connection-orig-match-pattern.description: The connection's key: the pattern the originating side of a call must match, such as `sip:*@192.0.2.10`. Unique across the platform. Required on create. It cannot change afterward: an update ignores it.

domain.description: Domain that owns the connection. Required on `POST /connections`; everywhere else the path supplies it.

description.description: Free-text description of the connection.

connection-term-match-pattern.description: The pattern the terminating side of a call must match. Defaults to `connection-orig-match-pattern`. The peak counters are kept for this value.

connection-audio-relay-enabled.description: Audio relay mode: `yes`, the default, `optional`, or `no`. They are stored as `automatic`, `none`, and `never`.

connection-address.description: Address of the far end, such as `192.0.2.10` or `carrier1.example.com`. The API reformats it to suit `connection-connectivity-type`: `inbound_registration` adds `sip:`, `route_profile` wraps it in angle brackets, and the other types strip both.

dial-plan.description: Name of the dial plan applied to calls on this connection.

dial-policy.description: Name of the dial policy applied to calls on this connection, such as `Permit All`.

limits-max-active-calls-orig.description: Most simultaneous originating calls on this connection.

limits-max-active-calls-term.description: Most simultaneous terminating calls on this connection.

limits-max-active-calls-total.description: Most simultaneous calls on this connection, in both directions.

connection-linked-billing-user.description: User the connection is linked to, such as `1001`. The API also treats that user as the connection's owner when it checks scope.

connection-sip-registration-username.description: Username for SIP digest authentication on this connection.

connection-sip-registration-password.description: Password for SIP digest authentication. Defaults to a random 8-character value on create. A read returns it in plain text.

connection-orig-enabled.description: `no` stops calls from originating on this connection. Reads `yes` when unset.

connection-term-enabled.description: `no` stops calls from terminating on this connection. Reads `yes` when unset.

connection-translation-request-host.description: Translation for the Request-URI host. Defaults to `connection-address`, as formatted for the connectivity type.

connection-translation-destination-host.description: Translation for the destination host. Defaults to `connection-address`, as formatted for the connectivity type.

connection-translation-request-user.description: Translation for the Request-URI user. Defaults to `[*]`.

connection-translation-destination-user.description: Translation for the destination user. Defaults to `[*]`.

connection-translation-source-user.description: Translation for the source user. Defaults to `[*]`.

connection-source-ip-checking-enabled.description: `yes` checks that calls come from the connection's address. Defaults to `no`.

connection-include-server-header-enabled.description: `yes` adds a `Server` header to SIP messages on this connection. Defaults to `no`.

connection-relay-comfort-noise-enabled.description: Comfort noise: `yes` relays it, `no` does not, and `system-default`, the default, follows the platform setting.

connection-pcmu-only-enabled.description: `yes` limits calls on this connection to the PCMU codec.

connection-bind-to-alternate-interface-e.description: `yes` sends this connection's traffic from the server's second address.

connection-block-video-in-sdp-enabled.description: `yes` removes video from the SDP of calls on this connection.

connection-sip-get-new-dialog-destinatio.description: Where a new SIP dialog is sent: `default-ip`, the default, uses `connection-address`, `contact-header` uses the `Contact` header, and `via-header` uses the `Via` header.

connection-sip-get-response-destination-.description: Where SIP responses are sent: `default-ip`, the default, uses `connection-address`, `contact-header` uses the `Contact` header, and `via-header` uses the `Via` header.

connection-require-encrypted-audio-enabl.description: Encrypted audio (SRTP): `yes` requires it, `optional` allows it, and `no`, the default, turns it off. Any other value returns `400`.

connection-check-orig-matching-sip-heade.description: SIP header matched against `connection-orig-match-pattern`: `from`, the default, `to`, `request` for the Request-URI, or `contact`.

connection-sip-session-timer-enabled.description: SIP session timers: `no` turns them off, and `system-default`, the default, follows the platform setting. `yes` is accepted and stored as `system-default`, with a `Warning` header. Any other value returns `400`.

connection-prevent-rtp-port-change-enabl.description: `yes` keeps the RTP port from changing during a call.

connection-hide-post-dial-delay-with-rin.description: `yes` answers a `100 Trying` from the far end with `180 Ringing`, so the caller hears ringback during post-dial delay.

connection-remote-ringback-handling.description: Ringback from the far end: `allowed`, the default, passes it through, `no-ringback` blocks `18x` responses, and `local-only` turns a `183` into a `180`.

connection-block-media-in-sip-180-ringin.description: `yes` removes the SDP from `180 Ringing` responses.

connection-allow-mid-call-uri-updates-en.description: `yes` lets the far end change the SIP URI during a call.

connection-record-all-calls-enabled.description: `yes` records every call on this connection.

connection-custom-p-asserted-id-format.description: Custom P-Asserted-Identity value for calls on this connection. Send an empty string to clear it.

connection-require-sip-authentication-en.description: `yes` requires calls from this connection to authenticate with SIP digest credentials.

connection-translation-source-host.description: Translation for the source host. Defaults to `<AppIP>`.

utc-offset.description: UTC offset of the connection's local time, in hours, such as `-7`.

time-zone.description: Time zone of the connection, as an IANA name such as `America/Phoenix`.

connection-usage-role.description: The connection's role: `customer`, the default, `vendor`, or `cluster`. The API stores the value as sent without checking it.

connection-connectivity-type.description: How the connection reaches the platform. `header_ip_match`, the default, is a peer identified by its address, with no registration. `inbound_registration` is a system that registers to the platform: `connection-address` is its SIP address, and a read attaches its registration. `outbound_registration` has the platform register upstream with the SIP credentials. `route_profile` is a route profile, managed with the route-profile endpoints; a route profile's type cannot change. Any other value returns `400`. A row stored as `header_ip_match` whose address or registration setting says otherwise reads back as the type it behaves as.

Connection.description: A connection: a SIP trunk or peer that carries calls between the platform and another system. `connection-orig-match-pattern` is its key, and `connection-id` encodes that key for use in a path. The call-processing fields, such as `connection-sip-transport-protocol`, are stored together and read back one field each.

Site.description: A site as the reads return it. A site is a system extension (`service-code` `system-site`) that holds settings for the users and call queues filed under it; members point at it by name through their own `site` field. The site's name is in `site`, and also in `user` for older clients. The list returns every stored setting. A single read, and the list with `site` or `billing`, return a shorter set plus live counts. `/sites/list` returns the name, `domain`, the name fields, `directory-name-number-dtmf-mapping`, and the emergency address fields. A site row never carries the extension's voicemail PIN, password hash, status message, or department.

model.description: Kind of event the subscription sends. One model per subscription: `call`, `call_origid` (latest state of each call only), `cdr`, `agent` (matched on the call queue), `voicemail`, `message`, `messagesession`, `presence`, `presense` (a misspelt presence model, still accepted), `subscriber`, `auditlog`, `auditlog_lite` (creates and deletes of main objects only), `domain`, or `device`. Your scope needs read access to the model. Any other value returns `400`.

post-url.description: URL each batch of events is sent to with `POST`. An `http://` or `https://` URL with a host, up to 256 characters, with no `user:password@` part. Unless a Super User sets it, it must resolve only to public addresses outside this platform.

domain.description: Domain whose events are sent. Defaults to your own domain. `*` means every domain and needs Super User (`403` otherwise). A domain that does not exist returns `404`. Ignored on `/domains/{domain}/subscriptions`, which takes the path domain.

user.description: User whose events are sent, or `*` for every user in the domain. `*` needs Office Manager, Reseller, or Super User; a Site Manager must name a user of its own site, and user-level scopes always get their own extension.

reseller.description: Ignored: the territory comes from the domain. A Super User sending it with `domain` `*` gets `400`.

subscription-geo-support.description: `yes` stores the subscription on every server and has one of them deliver it, with another taking over if that server stops. `no` stores it only on the server that handled the create, which alone delivers it. Defaults to `yes`.

subscription-expires-datetime.description: When delivery stops, as RFC 3339 or `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` in UTC. Stored in UTC. Defaults to the expiry of your token, or 20 years for a token that does not expire. Any other value returns `400`.

preferred-server.description: Hostname of the core server that should deliver a `subscription-geo-support: yes` subscription. It takes over after it has been up for 60 seconds. Defaults to the server that handled the create. Name a real core server: an unknown hostname can leave the subscription with no server delivering it.

post-url.description: New URL to send events to. Follows the create rules for `post-url`.

model.description: New kind of event to send. Must be a known model (`400`) that you can read (`403`).

subscription-expires-datetime.description: New expiry, as RFC 3339 or `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` in UTC. Leave it out to keep the current one.

subscription-geo-support.description: `yes` stores the subscription on every server and has one of them deliver it, with another taking over if that server stops. `no` stores it only on the server that handled the create, which alone delivers it. Defaults to `yes`. A switch from `yes` to `no` removes the copies on the other servers.

preferred-server.description: Hostname of the core server that should deliver a `subscription-geo-support: yes` subscription. It takes over after it has been up for 60 seconds. Defaults to the server that handled the create. Name a real core server: an unknown hostname can leave the subscription with no server delivering it.

error-count.description: Send `0` to reset the failed-delivery counter.

posts-count.description: Send `0` to reset the delivery counter.

domain.description: Accepted only when equal to the stored value. Any other value returns `400`.

user.description: Accepted only when equal to the stored value. Any other value returns `400`.

reseller.description: Accepted only when equal to the stored value. Any other value returns `400`.

SubscriptionUpdate.description: Fields a subscription update can change. Send only the ones to change.

id.description: Subscription identifier, and the key in `/subscriptions/{id}`. 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters, derived from the subscription's model, scope, territory, domain, user, `post-url`, and `subscription-geo-support`. Sent to your receiver as the `X-Correlation-ID` header.

model.description: Kind of event the subscription sends. One model per subscription: `call`, `call_origid` (latest state of each call only), `cdr`, `agent` (matched on the call queue), `voicemail`, `message`, `messagesession`, `presence`, `presense` (a misspelt presence model, still accepted), `subscriber`, `auditlog`, `auditlog_lite` (creates and deletes of main objects only), `domain`, or `device`. Your scope needs read access to the model. Any other value returns `400`.

post-url.description: URL each batch of events is sent to with `POST`. An `http://` or `https://` URL with a host, up to 256 characters, with no `user:password@` part. Unless a Super User sets it, it must resolve only to public addresses outside this platform. Returned in full only to a caller who can change the subscription; others get the query string and fragment masked.

subscription-geo-support.description: `yes` stores the subscription on every server and has one of them deliver it, with another taking over if that server stops. `no` stores it only on the server that handled the create, which alone delivers it. Defaults to `yes`.

user-scope.description: Scope of the token that created the subscription. Set by the API; a value in the request is ignored.

reseller.description: Territory of the subscription's domain, set by the API. It decides which Reseller can see and change the subscription, and does not filter events. A value in the request is ignored.

domain.description: Domain whose events are sent. `*` means every domain and only a Super User can set it. Defaults to your own domain. Cannot be changed after create.

user.description: User whose events are sent, or `*` for every user in the domain. A Site Manager cannot use `*`, and user-level scopes always get their own extension. Cannot be changed after create.

subscription-creation-datetime.description: When the subscription was created. It does not change afterward.

subscription-expires-datetime.description: When delivery stops. The subscription is deleted about 8 hours later. Defaults to the expiry of the token that created it, or 20 years for a token that does not expire. Send RFC 3339 or `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` in UTC; it is stored in UTC. Leaving it out of an update keeps the current value.

preferred-server.description: Hostname of the core server that should deliver a `subscription-geo-support: yes` subscription. It takes over after it has been up for 60 seconds. Defaults to the server that handled the create. Name a real core server: an unknown hostname can leave the subscription with no server delivering it.

current-active-server.description: Hostname of the server delivering the subscription now. `null` until a server takes it over.

status.description: Delivery state: `pending` until the first delivery, `active` when the last 5-second cycle delivered without errors, `error` when a delivery in the last cycle failed. It changes back to `active` at the next cycle without errors.

error-count.description: Failed deliveries: a response above `302`, a connection failure, or no answer in 15 seconds. Each failed batch counts once. Send `0` in an update to reset it; any other value is ignored.

posts-count.description: Delivery attempts, one per batch, failed ones included. Send `0` in an update to reset it; any other value is ignored.

Subscription.description: An event subscription: which events are sent (`model`, `domain`, `user`), where to (`post-url`), and how delivery is going (`status`, the counters, and the servers).

timeframe-name.description: Name of the time frame, unique for its owner. Letters, digits, spaces, and underscores, with at least one letter, digit, or underscore. It is also the name answer rules use, and it cannot be changed after the time frame is created.

timeframe-holiday-array.description: The holidays. Every holiday must use the same `timeframe-recurrence-type`, and each `timeframe-holiday-uuid` may appear once.

TimeframeCreateCustom.title: Custom
TimeframeCreateCustom.description: Any mix of date ranges, days of week entries, and holidays. The one-recurrence and one-entry rules of the other types do not apply.

timeframe-name.description: Name of the time frame, unique for its owner. Letters, digits, spaces, and underscores, with at least one letter, digit, or underscore. It is also the name answer rules use, and it cannot be changed after the time frame is created.

timeframe-days-of-week-array.description: Days of week entries. More than 1 is allowed.

timeframe-holiday-array.description: Holidays. The same holiday may appear more than once.

TimeframeCreateRequest.title: Create time frame
TimeframeCreateRequest.description: Body of a time frame create. `timeframe-type` selects the shape.

TimeframeAddEntriesRequest.title: Add entries
TimeframeAddEntriesRequest.description: Send the arrays the time frame type allows: date ranges for specific dates, holidays for holiday, any of the three for custom. A days of week time frame that already has its entry refuses more with `400`; change it with `PUT` instead. An `always` time frame has no entries.

timeframe-specific-dates-array.description: Date ranges to add. In a specific dates time frame, each must use the recurrence type the existing ranges use, `annual-month-day` or `doesNotRecur`.

timeframe-days-of-week-array.description: Days of week entries to add.

timeframe-holiday-array.description: Holidays to add. In a holiday time frame, each must use the existing recurrence type and must not repeat a holiday already there.

TimeframeConvertType.title: Convert type
TimeframeConvertType.description: Sets a new `timeframe-type`. Converting to `custom` keeps the entries. Converting to any other type deletes every entry; include the new type's arrays in the same request to fill it. A `custom` time frame cannot be converted.

timeframe-specific-dates-array.description: Date ranges for the new type.

timeframe-days-of-week-array.description: Days of week entry for the new type.

TimeframeReplaceEntries.title: Replace entries
TimeframeReplaceEntries.description: Every existing entry you do not list by `timeframe-id` is deleted. An entry with a `timeframe-id` is updated, and one without is created. An array you leave out deletes every entry of that kind.

timeframe-specific-dates-array.description: The date ranges to keep or create.

timeframe-days-of-week-array.description: The days of week entries to keep or create. A days of week time frame allows 1.

timeframe-holiday-array.description: The holidays to keep or create.

TimeframeUpdateEntries.title: Update entries
TimeframeUpdateEntries.description: With `update-only=yes`, only the entries you send change. An entry with a `timeframe-id` is updated, and one without is created. Nothing is deleted.

update-only.description: `yes` updates only the entries you send. Leave it out, or send any other value, to replace every entry instead. `update_only` is accepted as the same field.

timeframe-specific-dates-array.description: Date ranges to update, by `timeframe-id`, or to create.

timeframe-days-of-week-array.description: Days of week entries to update, by `timeframe-id`, or to create.

timeframe-holiday-array.description: Holidays to update, by `timeframe-id`, or to create. An update changes only the hours, observance options, workweek, and recurrence of a holiday; to change the holiday itself, delete it and add the new one.

TimeframeUpdateRequest.title: Update time frame
TimeframeUpdateRequest.description: Body of a time frame update. The shape is selected by which fields you send, not by a type field: `timeframe-type` that differs from the current type converts, `update-only=yes` updates, anything else replaces.

TimeframeDeleteRequest.title: Delete entry

child_id.description: `timeframe-id` of one entry to delete: a date range, days of week entry, or holiday. Leave it out to delete the whole time frame.

TimeframeDeleteRequest.description: Optional body of a time frame delete.

TimeframeReadResponse.description: One time frame. The shape depends on the form of `{id}`.

timeframe-id.description: Time frame ID: 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters, generated from the name and owner. Use it as `{id}`.

timeframe-name.description: Name of the time frame. Answer rules refer to it by this name.

user.description: Owner: `*` for a domain (shared) time frame, or the user, such as `1001`.

domain.description: Domain the time frame belongs to.

timeframe-specific-dates-array.description: Date ranges. Present on specific dates and custom time frames.

timeframe-holiday-array.description: Holidays. Present on holiday and custom time frames.

timeframe-days-of-week-array.description: Weekly schedules. Present on days of week and custom time frames.

end_on.description: Last day the time frame applies, as `YYYYMMDD`: the latest end of a date range or holiday, or the recurrence end date. `custom` for a custom time frame, and empty or absent when it never ends. Kept for existing clients; read `timeframe-end-date` instead.

timeframe-end-date.description: Last day the time frame applies, as `YYYYMMDD`, or `null` when it never ends, including `always` and `custom` time frames. Response only. Prefer it to `end_on`, which is kept unchanged and can also be `custom` or empty.

RecurringTimeframe.description: A time frame with its entries. The type decides which entry arrays it has.

RecurringTimeframeType.description:
Type of a time frame:

- `always`: matches at every moment
- `days-of-week`: one weekly schedule
- `specific-dates`: date ranges
- `holiday`: holidays from the holiday lookup
- `custom`: any mix of the three

On a request, `dow` and `sdate` are accepted for `days-of-week` and `specific-dates`.

timeframe-id.description: Entry ID, 13 hexadecimal characters. Generated on create; send it to update or delete this entry.

timeframe-parent-id.description: Id of the time frame this entry belongs to (32 lowercase hex characters).

ordinal-order.description: Position of this entry within its time frame, used to order the entries.

timeframe-weekly-sunday-begin-time-1.description: Start of the first period on Sundays. A time of day as `hhmm`, 24-hour, such as `0800`. Empty when the period is not used.

timeframe-weekly-sunday-end-time-1.description: End of the first period on Sundays. A time of day as `hhmm`, 24-hour, such as `0800`. Empty when the period is not used.

timeframe-weekly-sunday-end-time-2.description: End of the second period on Sundays. A time of day as `hhmm`, 24-hour, such as `0800`. Empty when the period is not used.

timeframe-weekly-monday-end-time-1.description: End of the first period on Mondays. A time of day as `hhmm`, 24-hour, such as `0800`. Empty when the period is not used.

timeframe-weekly-monday-end-time-2.description: End of the second period on Mondays. A time of day as `hhmm`, 24-hour, such as `0800`. Empty when the period is not used.

timeframe-weekly-tuesday-begin-time-1.description: Start of the first period on Tuesdays. A time of day as `hhmm`, 24-hour, such as `0800`. Empty when the period is not used.

timeframe-weekly-tuesday-end-time-1.description: End of the first period on Tuesdays. A time of day as `hhmm`, 24-hour, such as `0800`. Empty when the period is not used.

timeframe-weekly-tuesday-begin-time-2.description: Start of the second period on Tuesdays. A time of day as `hhmm`, 24-hour, such as `0800`. Empty when the period is not used.

timeframe-weekly-tuesday-end-time-2.description: End of the second period on Tuesdays. A time of day as `hhmm`, 24-hour, such as `0800`. Empty when the period is not used.

timeframe-weekly-wednesday-begin-time-1.description: Start of the first period on Wednesdays. A time of day as `hhmm`, 24-hour, such as `0800`. Empty when the period is not used.

timeframe-weekly-wednesday-end-time-1.description: End of the first period on Wednesdays. A time of day as `hhmm`, 24-hour, such as `0800`. Empty when the period is not used.

timeframe-weekly-wednesday-begin-time-2.description: Start of the second period on Wednesdays. A time of day as `hhmm`, 24-hour, such as `0800`. Empty when the period is not used.

timeframe-weekly-wednesday-end-time-2.description: End of the second period on Wednesdays. A time of day as `hhmm`, 24-hour, such as `0800`. Empty when the period is not used.

timeframe-weekly-thursday-begin-time-1.description: Start of the first period on Thursdays. A time of day as `hhmm`, 24-hour, such as `0800`. Empty when the period is not used.

timeframe-weekly-thursday-end-time-1.description: End of the first period on Thursdays. A time of day as `hhmm`, 24-hour, such as `0800`. Empty when the period is not used.

timeframe-weekly-thursday-begin-time-2.description: Start of the second period on Thursdays. A time of day as `hhmm`, 24-hour, such as `0800`. Empty when the period is not used.

timeframe-weekly-thursday-end-time-2.description: End of the second period on Thursdays. A time of day as `hhmm`, 24-hour, such as `0800`. Empty when the period is not used.

timeframe-weekly-friday-begin-time-1.description: Start of the first period on Fridays. A time of day as `hhmm`, 24-hour, such as `0800`. Empty when the period is not used.

timeframe-weekly-friday-end-time-1.description: End of the first period on Fridays. A time of day as `hhmm`, 24-hour, such as `0800`. Empty when the period is not used.

timeframe-weekly-friday-begin-time-2.description: Start of the second period on Fridays. A time of day as `hhmm`, 24-hour, such as `0800`. Empty when the period is not used.

timeframe-weekly-friday-end-time-2.description: End of the second period on Fridays. A time of day as `hhmm`, 24-hour, such as `0800`. Empty when the period is not used.

timeframe-weekly-saturday-begin-time-1.description: Start of the first period on Saturdays. A time of day as `hhmm`, 24-hour, such as `0800`. Empty when the period is not used.

timeframe-weekly-saturday-end-time-1.description: End of the first period on Saturdays. A time of day as `hhmm`, 24-hour, such as `0800`. Empty when the period is not used.

timeframe-weekly-saturday-begin-time-2.description: Start of the second period on Saturdays. A time of day as `hhmm`, 24-hour, such as `0800`. Empty when the period is not used.

timeframe-weekly-saturday-end-time-2.description: End of the second period on Saturdays. A time of day as `hhmm`, 24-hour, such as `0800`. Empty when the period is not used.

timeframe-recurrence-type.description: `weekly` repeats every week. `custom` repeats on the interval in `timeframe-recurrence-custom-interval` and `timeframe-recurrence-custom-interval-count`, from `timeframe-recurrence-begin-date`.

timeframe-recurrence-begin-date.description: First day of the schedule. A calendar date as `YYYYMMDD`, not an RFC 3339 timestamp: the day is read in the owner's time zone. Needed for `custom`.

timeframe-recurrence-custom-interval-cou.description: How many units between repeats of a `custom` recurrence, such as `2` for every 2 weeks. Ignored for `years`, which always repeats every year.

timeframe-recurrence-custom-interval-opt.description: For `months` or `years` only: which day of the month or year repeats. See `TimeframeSpecificDate`.

timeframe-recurrence-end-option.description: `onADate` stops the recurrence on `timeframe-recurrence-end-date`. Anything else repeats without end.

timeframe-recurrence-end-date.description: Last day of the recurrence, with `timeframe-recurrence-end-option=onADate`. A calendar date as `YYYYMMDD`, not an RFC 3339 timestamp: the day is read in the owner's time zone.

timeframe-expiry-datetime.description: Internal marker the platform uses to schedule regeneration of the time ranges, rendered as a timestamp. Kept for existing clients; read `timeframe-expiry-datetime-utc` instead.

domain.description: Domain of the time frame.

timeframe-next-observance-datetime.description: Start of each of the next weeks the schedule applies, as Unix timestamps in seconds. Up to 5. Kept for existing clients; `timeframe-next-observance-datetime-array` gives the same values as RFC 3339.

timeframe-recurrence-rrule.description: The recurrence as `KEY=value` pairs in the style of an iCalendar RRULE, such as `FREQ=WEEKLY;INTERVAL=2`. Not a complete RFC 5545 rule.

timeframe-is-v1.description: `true` on an entry converted on the fly from a legacy time frame that has no ID yet.

timeframe-next-observance-datetime-array.description: The same observances as `timeframe-next-observance-datetime`, as RFC 3339 timestamps in UTC, such as `2026-09-27T00:00:00+00:00`. Response only. Prefer it; the integer field is kept for existing clients.

timeframe-expiry-datetime-utc.description: The entry's expiry as an RFC 3339 timestamp in UTC, or `null` when `timeframe-expiry-datetime` holds an internal regeneration marker rather than a date, which is the usual case. Response only. `timeframe-expiry-datetime` is kept unchanged.

TimeframeDOW.description: A weekly schedule: up to 2 periods on each day of the week.

timeframe-id.description: Entry ID, 13 hexadecimal characters. Generated on create; send it to update or delete this range.

timeframe-parent-id.description: Id of the time frame this entry belongs to (32 lowercase hex characters).

ordinal-order.description: Position of this entry within its time frame, used to order the entries.

timeframe-specific-dates-begin-date.description: First day of the range. A calendar date as `YYYYMMDD`, not an RFC 3339 timestamp: the day is read in the owner's time zone. Required on a new range.

timeframe-specific-dates-begin-time.description: Time the range starts on its first day. A time of day as `hhmm`, 24-hour, such as `0800`. Empty when the period is not used.

timeframe-specific-dates-end-date.description: Last day of the range. A calendar date as `YYYYMMDD`, not an RFC 3339 timestamp: the day is read in the owner's time zone. Required on a new range.

timeframe-specific-dates-end-time.description: Time the range ends on its last day. A time of day as `hhmm`, 24-hour, such as `0800`. Empty when the period is not used.

timeframe-recurrence-type.description:
How the range repeats:

- `doesNotRecur`: once
- `annual-month-day` or `yearly-on-selected-dates`: every year on the same month and day
- `monthly-date`: every month on the same day; skipped in months without that day
- `monthly-on-last-day`: the last day of every month
- `monthly-on-ordinal-weekday`: the same weekday position every month, such as the third Friday
- `monthly-on-first-last`: the first or last of that weekday every month
- `yearly-first` or `yearly-last`: the first or last of that weekday in the same month every year
- `custom`: the interval in the custom fields

With more than 1 range in a specific dates time frame, only `annual-month-day` and `doesNotRecur` are allowed, and all ranges must use the same one.

timeframe-recurrence-custom-interval-cou.description: How many units between repeats of a `custom` recurrence, such as `3` for every 3 months. Ignored for `years`, which always repeats every year.

timeframe-recurrence-custom-interval-opt.description:
Which day repeats, for `months` or `years` only.

For `months`: `monthly-same-day`, `monthly-ordinal-weekday` (such as the third Friday), `monthly-first-last-weekday`, or `monthly-on-last-day`.

For `years`: `yearly-same-day`, `yearly-ordinal-weekday` (such as the second Tuesday of April), or `yearly-first-last-weekday`.

timeframe-recurrence-end-option.description: `onADate` stops the recurrence on `timeframe-recurrence-end-date`. Anything else repeats without end.

timeframe-recurrence-end-date.description: Last day of the recurrence, with `timeframe-recurrence-end-option=onADate`. A calendar date as `YYYYMMDD`, not an RFC 3339 timestamp: the day is read in the owner's time zone.

timeframe-expiry-datetime.description: Internal marker the platform uses to schedule regeneration of the time ranges, rendered as a timestamp. Kept for existing clients; read `timeframe-expiry-datetime-utc` instead.

domain.description: Domain of the time frame.

timeframe-recurrence-rrule.description: The recurrence as `KEY=value` pairs in the style of an iCalendar RRULE, including `DTSTART`, such as `DTSTART=20261224;FREQ=YEARLY;BYMONTH=12;BYMONTHDAY=24`. Not a complete RFC 5545 rule. `null` for a range that does not repeat.

timeframe-next-observance-datetime.description: Start of each of the next days the range applies, as Unix timestamps in seconds. Up to 5; empty once the range is over. Kept for existing clients; `timeframe-next-observance-datetime-array` gives the same values as RFC 3339.

timeframe-is-v1.description: Will be set to ```true``` if the specific date is part of a timeframe created before v44.1

timeframe-next-observance-datetime-array.description: The same observances as `timeframe-next-observance-datetime`, as RFC 3339 timestamps in UTC, such as `2026-09-27T00:00:00+00:00`. Response only. Prefer it; the integer field is kept for existing clients.

timeframe-expiry-datetime-utc.description: The entry's expiry as an RFC 3339 timestamp in UTC, or `null` when `timeframe-expiry-datetime` holds an internal regeneration marker rather than a date, which is the usual case. Response only. `timeframe-expiry-datetime` is kept unchanged.

TimeframeSpecificDate.description: A date range with a start and end time, optionally repeating.

timeframe-id.description: Entry ID, 13 hexadecimal characters. Generated on create; send it to update or delete this holiday.

timeframe-parent-id.description: Id of the time frame this entry belongs to (32 lowercase hex characters).

ordinal-order.description: Position of this entry within its time frame, used to order the entries.

timeframe-holiday-uuid.description: `uuid` of the holiday from `GET /holidays/{country}/{year}`. A holiday time frame may hold each once. Needed to find later years of a `yearlyOnHoliday` holiday.

timeframe-holiday-name.description: `name` of the holiday from the holiday lookup. Needed to find later years of a `yearlyOnHoliday` holiday.

timeframe-holiday-begin-date.description: Date of the first occurrence to observe, from the lookup's `date`. A calendar date as `YYYYMMDD`, not an RFC 3339 timestamp: the day is read in the owner's time zone. Required on a new holiday. A date that has already passed is dropped on create (`422`) and refused on update (`400`).

country-abbreviation.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country of the holiday, such as `US`. Stored uppercase.

state-province-abbreviation.description: ISO 3166-2 region of the holiday, such as `US-NY`, or empty for a nationwide holiday. Stored uppercase.

holiday-api-location-hint.description: `locations` of the holiday, exactly as the lookup sends it, such as `All`. Needed to find later years of a `yearlyOnHoliday` holiday.

timeframe-holiday-begin-time-1.description: Start of the first period on the holiday. A time of day as `hhmm`, 24-hour, such as `0800`. Empty when the period is not used.

timeframe-holiday-end-time-1.description: End of the first period on the holiday. A time of day as `hhmm`, 24-hour, such as `0800`. Empty when the period is not used.

timeframe-holiday-begin-time-2.description: Start of the second period on the holiday. A time of day as `hhmm`, 24-hour, such as `0800`. Empty when the period is not used.

timeframe-holiday-end-time-2.description: End of the second period on the holiday. A time of day as `hhmm`, 24-hour, such as `0800`. Empty when the period is not used.

timeframe-workweek-list.description: Days treated as workdays when a holiday moves to the next or prior workday, as a comma-separated list such as `M,T,W,Th,F`.

timeframe-recurrence-type.description: `never` observes the holiday once. `yearlyOnHoliday` observes it every year on the date the lookup gives for that year. All holidays in a holiday time frame use the same one.

timeframe-recurrence-end-option.description: `onDate` stops a `yearlyOnHoliday` recurrence after `timeframe-recurrence-end-date`. Anything else repeats without end.

timeframe-recurrence-end-date.description: Last day of the recurrence, with `timeframe-recurrence-end-option=onDate`. A calendar date as `YYYYMMDD`, not an RFC 3339 timestamp: the day is read in the owner's time zone.

timeframe-expiry-datetime.description: Internal marker the platform uses to schedule regeneration of the time ranges, rendered as a timestamp. Kept for existing clients; read `timeframe-expiry-datetime-utc` instead.

domain.description: Domain of the time frame.

timeframe-next-observance-datetime.description: Each of the next dates the holiday is observed, as Unix timestamps in seconds. Up to 5. Kept for existing clients; `timeframe-next-observance-datetime-array` gives the same values as RFC 3339.

timeframe-next-observance-datetime-array.description: The same observances as `timeframe-next-observance-datetime`, as RFC 3339 timestamps in UTC, such as `2026-09-27T00:00:00+00:00`. Response only. Prefer it; the integer field is kept for existing clients.

timeframe-expiry-datetime-utc.description: The entry's expiry as an RFC 3339 timestamp in UTC, or `null` when `timeframe-expiry-datetime` holds an internal regeneration marker rather than a date, which is the usual case. Response only. `timeframe-expiry-datetime` is kept unchanged.

TimeframeHoliday.description: A holiday from the holiday lookup, with the hours it applies and how a weekend holiday is observed.

domain.description: Domain of the time frame.

user.description: Owner: `*` for a domain (shared) time frame, or the user.

time-range-data.description: The generated time ranges, one per day and period.

Timeframe.description: Legacy view of a time frame, returned when `{id}` is a name: the time ranges generated for it.

uuid.description: Holiday ID from the lookup. Copy it to `timeframe-holiday-uuid`.

name.description: Holiday name, in `language` when you sent it. Copy it to `timeframe-holiday-name`.

description.description: Short description from the lookup.

date.description: Date of the holiday in the requested year, as an integer `YYYYMMDD`. Copy it to `timeframe-holiday-begin-date` as a string.

type.description: Holiday types from the lookup, such as `National holiday`.

primary_type.description: Main holiday type from the lookup, such as `Federal Holiday`.

locations.description: Where the holiday applies, as text, such as `All` or `NY`. Copy it to `holiday-api-location-hint`.

states.description: `All` for a nationwide holiday, or a list of the region codes it applies in.

Holiday.description: A holiday from the holiday lookup service, as `GET /holidays/{country}/{year}` returns it.

filename.description: File name on the server, `moh-` and the two-digit index.

ordinal-order.description: Index of the file. Files play in index order. Use it as `{index}` in the path.

file-duration-seconds.description: Length in seconds, worked out from the file size at 8,000 bytes a second.

file-size-kilobytes.description: File size as a formatted string with its unit, `B`, `KB`, `MB`, or `GB`, despite the name.

created-datetime.description: When the file was last written.

file-access-url.description: Signed link that plays this file with no token: `GET /domains/{domain}/moh/{index}/play (or the user path for a user's file)` with `expires` and `signature` added. Put it straight in an `<audio>` element. It works for that one file only and expires after 24 hours by default; read the file again for a fresh link. Anyone holding it can play the file, so do not log or share it. Left out only when the server cannot sign links.

file-script-text.description: The words spoken for a text-to-speech file, or the description sent with an upload. Empty when none was sent. Stored on one line: line breaks become spaces and double quotes become single quotes.
file-script-text.example: Hold music, instrumental

file-source.description: How the file was made, as the client that created it said. Empty unless one was sent.

text-to-speech-voice-id.description: Voice used for a text-to-speech file. Empty for an upload.

text-to-speech-language.description: Language of the voice for a text-to-speech file. Empty for an upload.

size.description: Total size in bytes of the counted MoH audio files. `0` when there are no files.

MohCount.description: MoH file count and folder size.

file.description: The audio file. The part's `Content-Type` picks the decoder: `audio/mpeg` or `audio/mp3` for MP3, `audio/ogg`, `audio/webm`, `video/ogg`, `video/webm`, or `application/ogg` for Ogg or WebM, and anything else is read as WAV. The part may also be named `File`.

index.description: Index to store the file at. Omit it to take the next free index; an index that is already used is overwritten. `0` is stored as `moh-00.wav`. It is `ordinal-order` in the response.

file-script-text.description: Description of the audio, returned as `file-script-text`. Optional.
file-script-text.example: Hold music, instrumental

file.description: The audio file. The part's `Content-Type` picks the decoder: `audio/mpeg` or `audio/mp3` for MP3, `audio/ogg`, `audio/webm`, `video/ogg`, `video/webm`, or `application/ogg` for Ogg or WebM, and anything else is read as WAV. The part may also be named `File`.

file-script-text.description: Description of the audio, returned as `file-script-text`. Optional.
file-script-text.example: Hold music, instrumental

file-base64.description: The audio as base64, with no line breaks or spaces, in the format `file-encoding` names. Base64 that does not decode returns `400`.

file-encoding.description: Format of the audio in `file-base64`: `audio/wav` (the default), `audio/mpeg` for MP3, `audio/ogg`, or `audio/webm`. Another value returns `400`.

index.description: Index to store the file at. Omit it to take the next free index; an index that is already used is overwritten. `0` is stored as `moh-00.wav`. It is `ordinal-order` in the response.

file-script-text.description: Description of the audio, returned as `file-script-text`. Optional.
file-script-text.example: Hold music, instrumental

MohCreateTextToSpeech.title: Text to speech
MohCreateTextToSpeech.description: Words to speak in `file-script-text`, and no `file-base64`.

file-script-text.description: Words to speak. Stored and returned as `file-script-text`.
file-script-text.example: Thank you for holding. Your call is important to us.

text-to-speech-voice-id.description: Voice to speak with, by id, name, or gender, as `GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/voices/{language}` lists them. Omit it to use the domain's default voice. A voice the language does not offer falls back to the language's first voice.

text-to-speech-language.description: Language of the voice, such as `en-US`. Omit it to use the domain's default language.

index.description: Index to store the file at. Omit it to take the next free index; an index that is already used is overwritten. `0` is stored as `moh-00.wav`. It is `ordinal-order` in the response.

MohCreateJson.description: Create a MoH file from JSON: a base64 file or text to speech.

file-base64.description: The audio as base64, with no line breaks or spaces, in the format `file-encoding` names. Base64 that does not decode returns `400`.

file-encoding.description: Format of the audio in `file-base64`: `audio/wav` (the default), `audio/mpeg` for MP3, `audio/ogg`, or `audio/webm`. Another value returns `400`.

file-script-text.description: Description of the audio, returned as `file-script-text`. Optional.
file-script-text.example: Hold music, instrumental

MohUpdateJson.description: Replace a MoH file from a base64 file, or change only its description.

ordinal-order.description: Current indexes, in the order you want them to play. The listed files take the same indexes, sorted.

filename.description: This is the filename without and path or folder. Should end in .wav

ordinal-order.description: This is the index of the audio file.

file-duration-seconds.description: This value is the length of the file in seconds.

file-size-kilobytes.description: This value will be a formated filesize of the file in kilobytes

created-datetime.description: This is the timestamp of create time fo the file

file-access-url.description: This will be URL of the file for remote playback.

file-script-text.description: This is the script that was used for text to speech and also used to create a new file.

file-source.description: This is the source of the file, it will show how the file was created originally.

text-to-speech-voice-id.description: This is the voice id used when using text to speech.

text-to-speech-language.description: This is the voice language when using TTS.

recorded-datetime.description: This is the timestamp of record time fo the file

Contact.description: A contact as the contact endpoints return it: a personal contact, a shared contact of the domain, or, with `includeDomain=yes`, an on-net user from the domain directory.

unique-id.description: The contact's ID: 1 to 32 letters, digits, `-`, or `_`. Assigned by the server as 32 hexadecimal characters unless the client sent one on create. A directory row has none unless a personal contact was merged into it; use `user` for those. `groups`, `list`, and `count` are reserved

email.description: The contact's email address

company.description: The company or organization the contact belongs to

user.description: Extension of an on-net contact. Present only on directory rows from `includeDomain=yes`; personal and shared contacts have none

department.description: Department of an on-net contact. Present only on directory rows

site.description: Site of an on-net contact. Present only on directory rows

phonenumber-work.description: The contact's work phone number, as entered

phonenumber-cell.description: The contact's mobile phone number, as entered

phonenumber-fax.description: The contact's fax number, as entered

phonenumber-home.description: The contact's home phone number, as entered

created-datetime.description: When the contact was stored, in RFC 3339. `null` when not set

avatar.description: Filename of the contact's avatar, or empty when it has none. On a directory row it is the user's own avatar unless a merged personal contact has one. The image is at `/ns-api/v2/avatar/{filename}` (48 by 48 pixels) and `/ns-api/v2/avatar/256/{filename}`. Ignored on create and update: set it with the contact avatar endpoints

notes.description: Free-text notes about the contact, up to 256 characters

is-shared.description: `true` for a contact from the domain's shared address book. Change shared contacts through `/domains/{domain}/contacts`, which needs domain tier or above

is-favorite.description: `true` when the user marked the contact as a favorite

items.description: Name of a contact group. Can't contain a comma

groups.description: Contact groups the contact is filed in. On an update, the groups you send replace the stored ones. List a user's groups with `GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/contacts/groups`

domain.description: Domain of the address book the contact is in

uid.description: `user@domain` of an on-net contact. Present only on directory rows

user-presence-status.description: Presence of an on-net contact. Present only on directory rows

status-message.description: Status message an on-net contact set. Present only on directory rows that have one

iotum-contact-id.description: ID of the copy in the video meeting service's contact list, when there is one. Returned by the single read only

matrix-user-id.description: Chat user ID of an on-net contact. Present only on directory rows; empty when chat is not set up

callqueue.description: Extension of the call queue. The queue's key in paths

domain.description: Domain that owns the queue

description.description: Name of the queue, shown in the portal and used as the system user's name
