callqueue-dispatch-type.description: How calls are offered to agents: `Round-robin` (longest idle first), `Tiered Round-robin`, `Ring All` (all at once), `Linear Cascade` (in order, adding agents each round), `Linear Hunt` (in order, one at a time), or `Call Park`. `-` for a call park with no dispatch settings

callqueue-calculate-statistics.description: `yes` when the platform keeps queue statistics for this queue

active-queued-calls-total-current.description: Calls waiting in the queue now

callqueue-agent-dispatch-timeout-seconds.description: Seconds an agent is rung before the queue moves on

callqueue-count-agents-available.description: Agents available to take a call now

callqueue-debug.description: `yes` when debug logging is on for the queue

callqueue-force-full-intro-playback.description: `yes` makes callers hear the whole intro message before they are offered to an agent

callqueue-max-callback-queueing-hours.description: Hours a caller-requested callback stays queued. `0` turns callbacks off

callqueue-max-current-callers-to-accept-.description: Callers allowed to wait before new callers follow the busy forward. `0` is unlimited

callqueue-max-current-wait-to-accept-new.description: Expected wait, in seconds, above which new callers follow the busy forward. `0` is unlimited

callqueue-max-wait-timeout-minutes.description: Minutes a caller can wait before leaving the queue by the no-answer forward. `0` is unlimited

callqueue-require-available-agents-to-ac.description: `yes` sends new callers to the busy forward when no agent is logged in

callqueue-source-match.description: Caller ID sent to the agent on the dispatched leg, such as `<Queue>`. `null` when the default is used

callqueue-sms-enable.description: `yes` when the queue takes SMS conversations

callqueue-sms-phrase-initiate-chat.description: Keyword a texter sends to start a queued SMS conversation. Reserved words such as `STOP` and `HELP` are refused

callqueue-sms-phrase-initiate-success.description: Reply sent when a conversation starts

callqueue-sms-phrase-no-agents-available.description: Reply sent when no agent can take a conversation

callqueue-sms-phrase-terminate-chat.description: Keyword that ends a conversation. Reserved words such as `STOP` and `HELP` are refused

callqueue-sms-phrase-terminate-success.description: Reply sent when a conversation ends by keyword

callqueue-agent-auto-logout-after-missed.description: `yes` logs out an agent who misses a dispatched call

callqueue-sim-ring-1st-round.description: Agents rung together in the first round, for `Linear Cascade` and `Ring All`

callqueue-sim-ring-increment.description: Agents added to each later round, for `Linear Cascade`

recording-configuration.description: Call recording for the queue: `yes`, `yes-with-transcription`, `yes-with-transcription-and-sentiment`, or `no`

voicemail-enabled.description: `yes` when the queue's extension has voicemail. Left out until the queue's system user exists

phone-number.description: Phone number routed to the queue, or `""` when none

callqueue-hold-audio-type.description: What callers hear while they wait: `moh` (music on hold) or `ringback`. Returned by the single-queue read only

forward-on-busy.description: Where new callers go when the queue is full or needs an agent and has none, such as `vmail_4000`. `""` when off

forward-when-unregistered.description: Where callers go when no agent device is registered. `""` when off

forward-no-answer.description: Where callers go when the wait limit runs out, such as `vmail_4000`. `""` when off

callqueue-ring-timeout-seconds.description: Seconds the queue rings agents before following the no-answer forward. Left out until the queue's system user exists

callqueue-local-only.description: `yes` dispatches only to agents registered on the same core server as the call

department.description: Department of the queue's system user, or `""`. Left out until that user exists

site.description: Site of the queue's system user, or `""`. Left out until that user exists

agent_loggedin_count.description: Agents logged in, available or not. Collection reads only. The name is literal: it has no v2 spelling yet

activecall_count.description: Calls in progress, from the last 30 seconds of statistics. Only with `callqueue-calculate-statistics=yes` on a collection read

gau_queue_max_wait.description: Longest current wait in seconds, from the last 30 seconds of statistics. Only with `callqueue-calculate-statistics=yes` on a collection read

callqueue-sms-phrase-initiation-fail.description: Reply sent when a text arrives without the start keyword

CallQueue.description: A call queue as the reads return it: its settings, its dispatch settings, the fields kept on its system user, its routing, and live counts.

callqueue-agent-id.description: The agent: `user@domain` for a user agent, which rings every device of the user, or `sip:` and the device address for a device agent. Offnet agents are a `sip:` address with no owning user

callqueue.description: Extension of the queue this entry is on

domain.description: Domain of the queue

callqueue-agent-availability-type.description: `automatic` (logged in), `manual` (offline, or single call mode), `disabled`, or `offnet-automatic` (an offnet agent that is logged in)

callqueue-agent-wrap-up-allowance-second.description: Seconds the agent stays unavailable after a call before the next one is offered

auto-answer-enabled.description: `yes` answers dispatched calls automatically on devices that support it

callqueue-agent-dispatch-order-ordinal.description: Position in the ring order for `Linear Hunt` and `Linear Cascade` queues. Lower rings first

callqueue-agent-dispatch-queue-priority-.description: Priority of this queue among the agent's queues. Lower is offered first when the agent becomes available

limits-max-active-calls-total.description: Most calls offered to the agent at once. Usually `1`

callqueue-agent-answer-confirmation-enab.description: `yes` makes the agent press a key to accept a dispatched call

callqueue-agent-has-registered-devices.description: Whether the agent can be reached: `yes` (a device is registered), `no`, `push-enabled` (reachable by push notification), or `offnet`

callqueue-agent-availability-for-dispatc.description: The platform's live dispatch state for the agent, such as `available` or `unavailable`

active-calls-total-current.description: Calls the agent is on now, across all queues

callqueue-agent-max-concurrent-sms-conve.description: Most SMS conversations offered to the agent at once. `0` offers none

last-callqueue-dispatch-datetime.description: When a call was last offered to the agent. `null` when never

login-username.description: Login of the user behind the agent

name-full-name.description: Full name of the user behind the agent. `Offnet Agent` for an offnet agent

agent-department.description: Department of the user behind the agent

name-first-name.description: First name of the user behind the agent

name-last-name.description: Last name of the user behind the agent

site.description: Site of the user behind the agent

user-scope.description: Scope of the user behind the agent, such as `Call Center Agent`

status-message.description: The user's status message. An offline reason set through Agent Actions shows here

queue_list.description: Comma-separated extensions of every queue the agent is on. `GET /domains/{domain}/agents` only; the name is literal

queue_list_status.description: The agent's availability on each queue in `queue_list`, in the same order, with the values of `callqueue-agent-availability-type`. `GET /domains/{domain}/agents` only; the name is literal

callqueue-agent-state.description: The call center status of the user behind this agent, as the agent log stores it: `Auto` (Online), `Manual-avail` (Single Call), `Manual` (Offline), `Logout` (End shift), `Manual-unavail`, `Lunch`, `Break`, `Meeting`, `Web`, `Other`, or `cust1` to `cust8`. One value for the user, not per queue: only an agent action on every queue (`all`) sets it. A device agent shows its owner's status. Empty until the user's first such action, and left out for an offnet agent or one with no user in the domain. Read a queue's own login state from `callqueue-agent-availability-type`.

Agent.description: A call queue agent entry as the reads return it: the agent's settings on one queue, its live state, and the user behind it.

index.description: The index of the file, Example "2" for greeting 2. In create (POST) requests index cab be omitted and the API will select a new index automatically.

script.description: This is a simple explanation of what the audio is and can include what is said in the audio file for explanation.

convert.description: Setting yes will allow the API to attempt to convert the file from accepted formats into the correct format for media playback

encoding.description: Used when providing base64 encoded data to give the content tupe of the file.

base64_file.description: This is a base64 encoded string formated without line breaks or spaces.

voice_language.description: This is the language that can be requested when using TTS feature. Leave of to have API lookup configs from the defaults or domain specific configs.

voice_id.description: This value will allow you to select the voice to be used for TTS applications. Value must be valid or will cause errors. leave off request to have the API lookup defaults from system and/or domain.

CodeApplication.description: One package, with the version installed on each cluster server that answered.

application.description: Package name with any release channel suffix removed, or `repo` for the repository entry

description.description: Package description, taken from the first server that reported one

servers.description: One entry for each server that has the package installed

CodeApplicationServer.description: The version of one package on one server.

hostname.description: Server the package is installed on

version.description: Installed version with the Debian epoch and the Ubuntu codename removed

upgradable.description: Whether apt has a newer version of this package on this server

details.description: The full package record from that server, without `all_options`

CodeApplicationServerDetails.description: One installed NetSapiens package on one server. The list also holds one entry with `application` set to `repo`, which reports the highest repository version configured on the server instead of a package.

hostname.description: Server the package is installed on

application.description: Package name with any release channel suffix removed, or `repo` for the repository entry

name.description: Package name as apt knows it, including the release channel suffix

version.description: Installed version with the Debian epoch and the Ubuntu codename removed. For the `repo` entry, the highest configured repository version

type.description: Release channel, taken from the package name suffix: `ga` (no suffix), `alpha`, `beta` or `staging`

version_full.description: Installed version exactly as apt reports it

version_index.description: Number for ordering versions: higher is newer. Compare it with `upgradable_index` and with the entries in `all_options`

architecture.description: CPU architecture the package is built for

upgradable.description: Whether apt has a newer version of this package from the configured repositories

upgradable_to.description: Version apt would upgrade to, in the same form as `version`. `null` when `upgradable` is `false`

upgradable_full.description: Version apt would upgrade to, exactly as apt reports it. `null` when `upgradable` is `false`

description.description: Package description from apt. Present on the `repo` entry and when apt reports one

all_options.description: Every version you can install, across every release channel, newest first. Returned by `GET /apt/installed/{hostname}` only: the cluster-wide list leaves it out

PackageRepositoryList.description: The NetSapiens apt repositories on one server: those configured, and those published but not configured.

hostname.description: Server the list was read from

maxVersion.description: Highest repository version configured on the server, as `<major>.<minor>`

maxAvailableVersion.description: Highest repository version published for the server's Ubuntu release, as `<major>.<minor>`. The number `0` when none is

codename.description: Ubuntu release codename of the server

repos.description: Configured repositories first (`enabled: true`), then published ones that are not configured (`enabled: false`)

version.description: Repository version. Pass it as `version` to add or remove the repository

filePath.description: apt source list file for this version on the server

type.description: apt source type. Configured repositories only

signedBy.description: GPG keyring apt checks this repository against

distribution.description: Ubuntu codename in the source line. Configured repositories only

components.description: Repository components in the source line. Configured repositories only

codename.description: Ubuntu release codename of the server

enabled.description: Whether the server has a source list for this version

available.description: Whether this version is still published

supported.description: Whether this version is published for the server's Ubuntu release. Always `true` for a configured repository

os.description: Ubuntu codenames this version is published for. Missing on a configured repository that is no longer published

domain.description: Domain of the user

user.description: User the rule belongs to. `*` marks a rule that applies to every user in the domain

time-frame.description: Time frame the rule applies to, and the key used to address the rule. `*` is the default rule, which applies when no other rule matches

enabled.description: Whether the rule is used at all. A disabled rule is skipped when calls are matched

is-active.description: Whether this rule is the one handling calls right now, in the user's time zone. The default rule is active only when no other enabled rule matches

simultaneous-ring.description: Rings every destination in `parameters` at the same time as the user's own devices. Each entry is an extension, a device such as `1001wp`, or a phone number.

do-not-disturb.description: Stops the user's devices from ringing. Calls go to `forward-on-dnd` when that is enabled, otherwise to voicemail.

enabled.description: This settings will control if the the parent feature is enabled.

forward-always.description: Forwards every call to the first destination in `parameters`, without ringing the user.

forward-on-active.description: Forwards a call to the destination in `parameters` when the user is already on a call.

forward-on-busy.description: Forwards a call to the destination in `parameters` when the user's devices answer busy.

forward-no-answer.description: Forwards a call to the destination in `parameters` when the user does not answer.

forward-when-unregistered.description: Forwards a call to the destination in `parameters` when none of the user's devices is registered.

forward-on-dnd.description: Forwards a call to the destination in `parameters` while `do-not-disturb` is enabled.

forward-on-spam-call.description: Forwards a call flagged as spam to the destination in `parameters`.

call-screening.description: Asks the caller to record their name, then plays it to the user before the call connects.

enabled.description: This settings will control if the the parent feature is enabled.

phone-numbers-to-allow.description: Caller numbers that bypass `do-not-disturb` and `call-screening` and always ring the user.

phone-numbers-to-reject.description: Caller numbers that are refused. `anonymous` matches a caller who withheld caller ID.

time_range_data.description: The time ranges of the rule's time frame

ordinal-priority.description: Position of the rule in the order rules are checked. Lower is checked first

prompt-no-answer.description: A no-answer feature kept alongside `forward-no-answer`, which is set up and switched together with it. Takes its destination in `parameters`.

Answerrule.description: An answer rule: how calls to a user are handled while one time frame applies.

enabled.description: Whether the feature is on

parameters.description: Destination of the feature: an extension such as `1002`, a voicemail box such as `vmail_1001`, or a phone number. A numeric value can come back as a number rather than a string

AnswerruleFeature.description: An answer rule feature that sends calls to a destination.

enabled.description: Whether the feature is on

parameters.description: Destinations rung at the same time: extensions, devices such as `1001wp`, or phone numbers. A numeric value can come back as a number rather than a string

AnswerruleFeatureSimRing.description: The simultaneous ring feature of an answer rule.

enabled.description: Whether the list is applied

parameters.description: Caller numbers on the list, such as `15555550142`

remove.description: On an update, `yes` removes the numbers in `parameters` from the list instead of adding them

AnswerruleFeatureWithRemove.description: An answer rule list of caller numbers.

ordinal-order.description: Position of the range within its time frame

start-date.description: First day the range applies, as `YYYY-MM-DD`. `now` means it has no start date

end-date.description: Last day the range applies, as `YYYY-MM-DD`. `never` means it has no end date

anyOf.description: Integer can be used 0-6 for day in week.
String of * can be used for all days.

day-of-week-number.description: Days of the week the range applies, `0` (Sunday) to `6` (Saturday). `*` means every day

start-time.description: Start of the range each day, as `HH:MM` in the user's time zone

end-time.description: End of the range each day, as `HH:MM` in the user's time zone

invert-match.description: `yes` makes the range apply outside these dates and times instead of inside them

Timerange.description: One time range of a time frame.

device-provisioning-mac-address.description: MAC address of the phone, and the key you address it by. Returned as 12 hex digits with no separators. On create you can send `:`, `-`, or `.` separators, which are removed. Anything else returns `400`.

domain.description: Domain the phone belongs to. Required on create, unless the path names the domain.

reseller.description: Reseller (territory) the phone's domain belongs to. Taken from the domain when you leave it out.

device-models-brand-and-model.description: Brand and model, separated by a space, as listed by `GET /phones/models`. Required on create. On an update that changes a line, the stored model is used when you leave it out. A soft phone (`Manual or Softphone`) or a blank model returns `400`.

device-provisioning-registration-core-se.description: Hostname of the core server the phone registers to. Defaults to the platform's configured core server on create.

device-provisioning-sip-uri-1.description: Device on line 1, as `sip:<device>@<domain>`. `n/a` or `sip:@<domain>` means the line is unassigned. The user who owns this device is the phone's user. Basic User and the other user scopes can assign only their own device here, and Site Manager only a device of a user in its site.

device-provisioning-line-1-enabled.description: Whether line 1 is provisioned on the phone. When you assign line 1 and leave this out, it is set to `yes`, or `no` for an unassigned line. Returned on single-phone reads.

device-provisioning-sip-uri-1-shared-lin.description: Whether line 1 is a shared line (`shared`) or not (`private`).

device-provisioning-sip-uri-2.description: Device on line 2, as `sip:<device>@<domain>`. `n/a` or `sip:@<domain>` means the line is unassigned.

device-provisioning-line-2-enabled.description: Whether line 2 is provisioned on the phone. When you assign line 2 and leave this out, it is set to `yes`, or `no` for an unassigned line. Returned on single-phone reads.

device-provisioning-sip-uri-2-shared-lin.description: Whether line 2 is a shared line (`shared`) or not (`private`).

device-provisioning-sip-transport-protoc.description: SIP transport the phone is configured to use.

device-provisioning-username.description: Username the phone uses to download its configuration file from the Endpoints server.

device-provisioning-password.description: Password the phone uses to download its configuration file. Masked unless the phone is your own, or you are a Super User sending `include-secrets=yes`. Sending the masked value back keeps the stored password.

device-models-count-buttons.description: Read-only. Number of line keys the model has, from its model definition. Returned on single-phone reads.

device-models-fxs-support-enabled.description: Read-only. Number of FXS (analog) ports the model has, from its model definition. Returned on single-phone reads.

device-provisioning-overrides-blob.description: This phone's own configuration overrides, as `key="value"` pairs separated by spaces, applied on top of the model and domain defaults. Stored as text with no practical length limit. Replaces the deprecated `device-models-overrides-blob`.

device-models-overrides-blob.description: Deprecated: use `device-provisioning-overrides-blob`. Holds the same value, this phone's own overrides, and will be removed in the next release. Still accepted on write, where it sets `device-provisioning-overrides-blob`.

device-models-resync-support-enabled.description: Read-only. Whether the model supports a remote resync, from its model definition. Returned on single-phone reads.

device-models-shared-line-support-enable.description: Read-only. Whether the model supports shared lines, from its model definition. Returned on single-phone reads.

device-models-sidecar-support-enabled.description: Whether the phone's model supports a sidecar (expansion module), from its model definition. Returned on single-phone reads. On a write, this name sets the phone's own `device-provisioning-sidecar`.

device-provisioning-sidecar.description: Whether this phone has a sidecar (expansion module) configured. Returned on single-phone reads. Whether its model supports one is `device-models-sidecar-support-enabled`.

device-provisioning-last-retrieved-datet.description: Read-only. When the phone last downloaded its configuration, RFC 3339. `null` until it has, and again after any change to the phone.

device-provisioning-directory.description: Phone directory setting for the phone. `disabled` turns the directory off.

device-provisioning-directory-support.description: Read-only. Whether the model supports a phone directory, from its model definition. Returned on single-phone reads.

device-provisioning-line-1-extensions.description: Read-only. Device name on line 1, without the `sip:` prefix and domain. Set from `device-provisioning-sip-uri-1`. Returned on single-phone reads.

device-provisioning-line-2-extensions.description: Read-only. Device name on line 2, without the `sip:` prefix and domain. Set from `device-provisioning-sip-uri-2`. Returned on single-phone reads.

device-provisioning-line-3-extensions.description: Read-only. Device name on line 3, without the `sip:` prefix and domain. Returned on single-phone reads.

device-provisioning-line-4-extensions.description: Read-only. Device name on line 4, without the `sip:` prefix and domain. Returned on single-phone reads.

device-provisioning-ndp-hostname.description: Read-only. Hostname of the Endpoints server that holds the phone's record. Returned on single-phone reads.

device-provisioning-presence.description: Whether the phone shows presence (busy lamp field) for other users.

created-datetime.description: Read-only. When the phone was added, RFC 3339. Updates never change it.

global-one-time-pass.description: Whether the phone may download its configuration once with the system-wide global password instead of its own credentials. The Endpoints server sets it back to `no` after the phone's next successful download. While it is `yes`, the configuration file endpoints return `409`.

last-modified-datetime.description: Read-only. When the phone's per-phone configuration (`/domains/{domain}/phoneconfiguration/{mac}`) last changed, RFC 3339. Absent when the phone has none.

redundency.description: How the phone fails over between core servers. The field name is spelled `redundency`.

device-provisioning-sip-uri-3.description: Device on line 3, as `sip:<device>@<domain>`. `n/a` or `sip:@<domain>` means the line is unassigned.

device-provisioning-line-3-enabled.description: Whether line 3 is provisioned on the phone. When you assign line 3 and leave this out, it is set to `yes`, or `no` for an unassigned line. Returned on single-phone reads.

device-provisioning-sip-uri-3-shared-lin.description: Whether line 3 is a shared line (`shared`) or not (`private`).

device-provisioning-sip-uri-4.description: Device on line 4, as `sip:<device>@<domain>`. `n/a` or `sip:@<domain>` means the line is unassigned.

device-provisioning-line-4-enabled.description: Whether line 4 is provisioned on the phone. When you assign line 4 and leave this out, it is set to `yes`, or `no` for an unassigned line. Returned on single-phone reads.

device-provisioning-sip-uri-4-shared-lin.description: Whether line 4 is a shared line (`shared`) or not (`private`).

device-provisioning-sip-uri-5.description: Device on line 5, as `sip:<device>@<domain>`. `n/a` or `sip:@<domain>` means the line is unassigned.

device-provisioning-line-5-enabled.description: Whether line 5 is provisioned on the phone. When you assign line 5 and leave this out, it is set to `yes`, or `no` for an unassigned line. Returned on single-phone reads.

device-provisioning-sip-uri-5-shared-lin.description: Whether line 5 is a shared line (`shared`) or not (`private`).

device-provisioning-sip-uri-6.description: Device on line 6, as `sip:<device>@<domain>`. `n/a` or `sip:@<domain>` means the line is unassigned.

device-provisioning-line-6-enabled.description: Whether line 6 is provisioned on the phone. When you assign line 6 and leave this out, it is set to `yes`, or `no` for an unassigned line. Returned on single-phone reads.

device-provisioning-sip-uri-6-shared-lin.description: Whether line 6 is a shared line (`shared`) or not (`private`).

device-provisioning-sip-uri-7.description: Device on line 7, as `sip:<device>@<domain>`. `n/a` or `sip:@<domain>` means the line is unassigned.

device-provisioning-line-7-enabled.description: Whether line 7 is provisioned on the phone. When you assign line 7 and leave this out, it is set to `yes`, or `no` for an unassigned line. Returned on single-phone reads.

device-provisioning-sip-uri-7-shared-lin.description: Whether line 7 is a shared line (`shared`) or not (`private`).

device-provisioning-sip-uri-8.description: Device on line 8, as `sip:<device>@<domain>`. `n/a` or `sip:@<domain>` means the line is unassigned.

device-provisioning-line-8-enabled.description: Whether line 8 is provisioned on the phone. When you assign line 8 and leave this out, it is set to `yes`, or `no` for an unassigned line. Returned on single-phone reads.

device-provisioning-sip-uri-8-shared-lin.description: Whether line 8 is a shared line (`shared`) or not (`private`).

device-provisioning-line-1-name.description: Label shown for line 1 on the phone. Returned on single-phone reads.

device-provisioning-line-2-name.description: Label shown for line 2 on the phone. Returned on single-phone reads.

device-provisioning-line-3-name.description: Label shown for line 3 on the phone. Returned on single-phone reads.

device-provisioning-line-4-name.description: Label shown for line 4 on the phone. Returned on single-phone reads.

device-provisioning-line-1-password.description: Password for line 1. Returned only to a Super User sending `include-secrets=yes`, and left out otherwise.

device-provisioning-line-2-password.description: Password for line 2. Returned only to a Super User sending `include-secrets=yes`, and left out otherwise.

device-provisioning-line-3-password.description: Password for line 3. Returned only to a Super User sending `include-secrets=yes`, and left out otherwise.

device-provisioning-line-4-password.description: Password for line 4. Returned only to a Super User sending `include-secrets=yes`, and left out otherwise.

device-provisioning-config-filename.description: Configuration file name the Endpoints server serves this phone. Returned on single-phone reads.

device-provisioning-outbound-proxy.description: Outbound proxy the phone sends SIP through. Returned on single-phone reads.

device-provisioning-outbound-proxy-port.description: Port of the outbound proxy. Returned on single-phone reads.

device-provisioning-local-port.description: Local SIP port on the phone. Returned on single-phone reads.

device-provisioning-codec.description: Codec preference for the phone. Returned on single-phone reads.

device-provisioning-time-zone.description: Time zone the phone displays. Returned on single-phone reads.

device-provisioning-gmt-offset.description: Offset from GMT in hours, for models that take an offset instead of a time zone. Returned on single-phone reads.

device-provisioning-firmware.description: Firmware the phone is told to load. Returned on single-phone reads.

device-provisioning-encryption.description: Whether the configuration file is encrypted. Returned on single-phone reads.

device-provisioning-srtp.description: Whether the phone uses SRTP for media. Returned on single-phone reads.

device-provisioning-full-provisioning.description: Full-provisioning setting for the phone. Returned on single-phone reads.

device-sip-registration-contact.description: Read-only. Contact header from line 1's last registration. Returned on single-phone reads.

device-sip-registration-datetime.description: Read-only. When line 1 last registered, RFC 3339. Returned on single-phone reads.

device-sip-registration-expires-datetime.description: Read-only. When line 1's current registration expires, RFC 3339. A time in the past means line 1 is not registered.

device-sip-registration-state.description: Read-only. `registered` while line 1's last registration has not expired, allowing about 2 minutes of grace. Otherwise `unregistered`. `null` when line 1 is unassigned.

device-sip-registration-user-agent.description: Read-only. User agent of line 1's last registration. Returned on single-phone reads.

user.description: Read-only. User that owns line 1 (`device-provisioning-sip-uri-1`).

dirs.description: Read-only. The domain's phone directories. Returned on a single-phone read through `/domains/{domain}/phones/{mac}` when the model supports a directory.

api-note.description: Read-only. Present when line slots 9 and above were left out of the response because they are unassigned or disabled.

NdpPhone.description: A phone in the Endpoints server inventory, keyed by MAC address. List reads return a subset of these fields. Single-phone reads add the model's capabilities, line 1's registration detail, and the per-phone provisioning settings. Line slots 9 and above, up to the platform's configured maximum, are returned as `device-provisioning-sip-uri-N` and `device-provisioning-line-N-enabled` when assigned. `device-models-overrides-blob` is deprecated: read `device-provisioning-overrides-blob`, which holds the same value.

PhoneListItem.title: PhoneListItem
PhoneListItem.description: A reduced phone row, returned by `GET /phones/list` and `GET /domains/{domain}/phones/list`.

device-provisioning-mac-address.description: MAC address of the phone: 12 hex digits with no separators. The key you address the phone by.

device-models-brand-and-model.description: Brand and model, separated by a space.

domain.description: Domain the phone belongs to.

device-provisioning-line-1-extensions.description: Device name on line 1, without the `sip:` prefix and domain. Empty when line 1 is unassigned.

PushR.description: A push registration: one push token, the device it notifies, and the user who owns it.

push-device-token.description: Push token the app got from its push service. A credential: in clear only to the registration's own user, masked for everyone else.

domain.description: Domain of the user who owns the registration.

user.description: User (extension) who owns the registration.

push-device.description: AOR of the device that gets the notifications, as `sip:<device>@<domain>`.

push-network.description: Push service the token belongs to: `firebase` (Firebase Cloud Messaging, Android), `apns` (Apple Push Notification service, iOS), `apns_chat` (an Apple token used for chat and messages only), or `pwa` (a web push subscription for a progressive web app).

push-test.description: `yes` sends Apple notifications through Apple's development (sandbox) service, for a development build of the app. Applies to `apns` only.

BackupResponse.description: Result of a manual domain backup.

backup-hostname.description: Hostname of the server that ran the backup. Send it as `hostname` when you restore from this backup.

backup-index.description: Index of the new restore point: the server's local date and time as year, month, day, hour, and minute. Send it as `index` when you restore from this backup.

type.description: Kind of backup. Always `manual` for this endpoint.

backup-log-link.description: Link to the backup log dashboard for this server and domain, covering the last 2 hours. Absent when the platform has no backup log dashboard.

data-sync-results.description: Result of copying the domain's stored files, or `false` when the copy produced no result.

complete-file-backup-time-ms.description: Time the file copy took, in milliseconds.

uploaded.description: Number of files created or changed since the previous backup.

upload-size.description: Size of the newly created files, in bytes.

note.description: Fixed note that the counts cover changes since the previous backup.
note.example: This numbers are since last backup/sync

deleted.description: Number of files removed since the previous backup.

status.description: Result of the database backup.

duration-main-loop-ms.description: Time spent writing the database files, in milliseconds.

manual-index.description: Index of the new restore point. Same value as `backup-index`.

complete-database-backup-time-ms.description: Total time the database backup took, in milliseconds.

hostname.description: Server that holds the backup, as keyed in the restore-point list.

domain.description: Domain to restore, such as `example.com`. Send it in the body: a `domain` in the query string is ignored.

type.description: Kind of backup, from the restore point's `type`.

index.description: Restore point to restore, from its `day`. Nightly backups use `0` to `6`. Manual backups use the `backup-index` the backup returned.

confirmation-value.description: The restore point's `confirmation-value`, from the restore-point list. It proves you picked the point that exists now.

geo.description: `yes` queues the restore and answers at once, without waiting for it to finish.

Restore.description: Restore point to restore a domain from.

common-name.description: Hostname the certificate is issued for, and the key that addresses it. Use a fully qualified domain name whose CNAME or A record points at this cluster. Wildcards are not allowed here: put them in `subject-alternative-name`.

subject-alternative-name.description: Comma-separated list of extra hostnames the certificate covers. Each entry is a hostname, or a wildcard with a single leading `*.` label such as `*.example.com`. Empty when there are none.

reseller.description: Territory that owns the certificate, or `*` for a system-level certificate.

account-email-address.description: Email address registered with Let's Encrypt for this certificate. Expiry notices go here.

status.description: Read only. Progress of the request, set by the certificate manager. `OK` means the certificate is issued and installed. Other values include `pending`, `Requesting Cert`, `Validating Challenge [http-01]`, `Certificate Received`, `pending delete`, and `Error:` followed by the reason.

generate-datetime.description: Read only. When the current certificate was issued. `null` until the first one is issued.

expiration-datetime.description: When the current certificate expires. The certificate manager renews it before then. `null` until the first one is issued.

challenge-type.description: How Let's Encrypt confirms you control the hostnames. `http-01` fetches a file from each hostname over HTTP and suits most certificates. `dns-01` checks a DNS TXT record and is required when `subject-alternative-name` has a wildcard. Defaults to `http-01`.

default-ssl-cert.description: `yes` makes this the web server's default certificate, served for any hostname that has no certificate of its own.

replicate-ssl-cert.description: Where the certificate is installed. `yes` installs it on every server in the cluster. `ndp` installs it on the Endpoints server, for phone provisioning. `no` keeps it on the server that issued it.

Certficate.description: An SSL certificate that the certificate manager issues and renews for a hostname.

number.description: SMS number: digits with the country code and no `+`, such as `15555550100`. A number belongs to one domain only.

application.description: What the number delivers to: `user` for a user's extension, `callqueue` for a call queue, or `available` for the domain's pool of unassigned numbers.

carrier.description: SMS carrier that sends and receives messages for this number, such as `bandwidth`. MMS and group MMS support are decided from this name.

dest.description: Extension or call queue that receives messages to this number when `application` is `user` or `callqueue`. Empty for an available number.

notes.description: Free-text note, for example why the number was released.

mms-capable.description: Present, and `true`, when the number's carrier is one the domain's settings mark as supporting MMS. Absent otherwise.

group-mms-capable.description: Present, and `true`, when the number's carrier is one the domain's settings mark as supporting group MMS. Absent otherwise.

SmsNumber.description: An SMS number in a domain and where its messages go.

call-term-user.description: For a blind transfer, the destination: an extension, a number, or a SIP URI. For answer, the device that answers, such as `sip:1001wp@example.com`. Leave it out for an attended transfer.

hostname.description: For an attended transfer, the core server that holds the call to merge in, from that call's `core-server`. Send it with `call-destination-session-id`.

call-destination-session-id.description: For an attended transfer, the `call-session-id` of the call to merge in. Send it with `hostname`.

CallActions.description: Body of a transfer or answer request on an active call.

uid.description: Read-only. The user the settings belong to, as `user@domain`.

domain.description: Read-only. Domain of the user.

user.description: Read-only. Extension of the user.

voicemail-reminder-phonecall-enabled.description: Whether reminders are sent as phone calls to the numbers in `voicemail-reminder-phonecall-phonenumber-array`.

voicemail-reminder-phonecall-phonenumber.description: Phone numbers to call. Returned as numbers, not strings, so a leading `+` is not shown. Empty when none are set.

voicemail-reminder-sms-enabled.description: Whether reminders are sent as SMS messages to the numbers in `voicemail-reminder-sms-phonenumber-array`.

voicemail-reminder-sms-phonenumber-array.description: Numbers to text. Returned as numbers, not strings, so a leading `+` is not shown. Empty when none are set.

voicemail-reminder-email-enabled.description: Whether reminders are sent by email to the addresses in `voicemail-reminder-email-address-array`.

voicemail-reminder-email-address-array.description: Email addresses to notify. Empty when none are set.

voicemail-reminder-interval-minutes.description: Minutes between reminders while the user has unheard voicemail.

voicemail-reminder-last-sent.description: Read-only. When the last reminder was sent, as the reminder service records it. Set by the platform; a value sent in a request is ignored.

voicemail-reminder-control-server.description: Read-only. Hostname of the server that sends this user's reminders. Returned only to Super User tokens. Set by the platform; a value sent in a request is ignored.

Vmailnag.description: A user's voicemail reminder settings: which channels repeat a reminder about unheard voicemail, where each goes, and how often.

user.description: Extension that answers as the auto attendant.

starting-prompt.description: Starting tier of the menu, such as `Prompt_100`. Use it as `{prompt}` in the attendant's path.

time-frame.description: Time frame of the answering rule that sends calls to the attendant. `*` is the default time frame.

intro-greetings.description: Intro greetings played before the menu, one per time frame. Present only when the attendant has any.

time-frame.description: Time frame whose calls hear this greeting first.

audio.description: The intro greeting. An empty array when no recording has that number.
Greeting of the starting tier. An empty array when the tier has no greeting.

auto-attendant.description: The starting tier: what each key does.

AutoAttendant.description: An auto attendant as **Read auto attendant** returns it, with every tier of its menu.

3-digit-dial-by-extension.description: `yes` when callers can dial a 3-digit extension from this tier.

4-digit-dial-by-extension.description: `yes` when callers can dial a 4-digit extension from this tier.

5-digit-dial-by-extension.description: `yes` when callers can dial a 5-digit extension from this tier.

no-key-press.description: What happens when the caller presses nothing. Empty when it is not set.

unassigned-key-press.description: What happens when the caller presses a key with no destination. Empty when it is not set.

option-1.description: What key `1` does. Present only when the key has a destination.

option-2.description: What key `2` does. Present only when the key has a destination.

option-3.description: What key `3` does. Present only when the key has a destination.

option-4.description: What key `4` does. Present only when the key has a destination.

option-5.description: What key `5` does. Present only when the key has a destination.

option-6.description: What key `6` does. Present only when the key has a destination.

option-7.description: What key `7` does. Present only when the key has a destination.

option-8.description: What key `8` does. Present only when the key has a destination.

option-9.description: What key `9` does. Present only when the key has a destination.

option-0.description: What key `0` does. Present only when the key has a destination.

option-*.description: What key `*` does. Present only when the key has a destination.

option-#.description: What key `#` does. Present only when the key has a destination.

AutoAttendantTier.description: One tier of an auto attendant menu as a read returns it.

description.description: Label of the key, as it was last sent, such as `Sales`.

destination-application.description: Where the key sends the call. `repeat-tier` plays the tier again, and `play-message` plays `audio`. Left out when the key opens a submenu.

destination-user.description: Destination of the call. Present when `destination-application` routes the call.

caller-name-translation.description: Caller name the destination sees. Present only when it replaces the caller's name.

audio.description: Greeting of the submenu, or the message a `play-message` key plays. An empty array when there is none.

remove.description: If set to yes it will remove the option from the menu.

AutoAttendantTierOption.description: What one key of an auto attendant tier does, as a read returns it.

AutoAttendantFailOptions.description: What a tier does when the caller presses nothing or a key with no destination. `repeat` plays the tier again, `hangup` ends the call, and `option-<key>` does what that key does. An empty string means not set.

id.description: Meeting ID: 9 digits, as a string. Also the key used in paths.

domain.description: Domain of the meeting's owner.

user.description: Extension of the meeting's owner.

description.description: Longer text about the meeting.

current_timestamp.description: When the meeting row was last written, as stored.

meeting-calendar-invite-id.description: Read-only. ID of the calendar invitation, kept so updates and cancellations replace the same calendar entry.

meeting-ordinal-sequence.description: Read-only. Revision number of the calendar invitation. It goes up by 1 with each change.

core-server.description: Read-only. Core server the meeting was created on.

chat-session-id.description: Read-only. ID of the meeting's chat session.

meeting-registration-id.description: Registration ID guests use to register for a `presentation` meeting. Empty for other meeting types.

meeting-instance-id.description: ID of the current instance, set while the meeting is running. Empty when it is not running.

meeting-status.description: State of the meeting, such as `active` while an instance runs or `ended`. Empty for a meeting that has not started.

meeting-schedule-start-datetime.description: When the meeting is scheduled to start.

timezone.description: Time zone the meeting was scheduled in.

meeting-schedule-recurrence-rule.description: RFC 5545 repeat rule for a recurring meeting, with any cancelled occurrences as `EXDATE`. Empty for a one-time meeting.

meeting-chat-history-enabled.description: `1` when the chat history is kept.

meeting-question-answer-enabled.description: `1` when questions and answers are on.

meeting-join-require-invite-enabled.description: `1` when only invited attendees can join. `0` lets anyone with the meeting ID join while the meeting is not locked.

meeting-require-host-to-begin-enabled.description: `1` when attendees wait until a host joins.

meeting-allow-changes-from-hosts-enabled.description: `1` when hosts other than the owner may change the meeting in the app. The API lets every host make changes whatever this is set to.

meeting-hide-attendee-list-enabled.description: `1` when attendees who are not hosts or presenters cannot see the attendee list.

meeting-lock-allowed.description: Comma-separated attendee IDs that were connected when the meeting was locked and can stay or rejoin.

meeting-dial-in-number-blob.description: Phone numbers audio-only attendees dial to join.

meeting-passcode.description: Passcode attendees enter to join. Shown only to the meeting's owner, its hosts, and Office Manager or higher for its domain. Everyone else gets it masked with asterisks, and `include-secret=yes` does not change that.

meeting-previous-presenter-attendee-id.description: Read-only. Attendee ID of the previous presenter.

meeting-presenter-attendee-id.description: Attendee ID of the attendee presenting now.

last-modified-datetime.description: When the meeting was last changed.

meeting-instance-actual-start-datetime.description: When the current instance started. `null` when the meeting is not running.

meeting-video-layout.description: Default video layout for the meeting.

attendees.description: The meeting's attendees, as a JSON-encoded array string. Each item carries the raw attendee fields: `meeting_id`, `domain`, `name`, `email`, `role` (`host`, `presenter`, or `attendee`), `uid`, `phonenumber`, `audio_id`, `contact_id`, `status`, `status_video`, `attendee_id`, and `join_source`. Present on a read of one meeting, or with `include_attendees`.

active_attendee_count.description: Attendees connecting or connected now. Present with `attendees`.

meeting-instance-schedule-start-datetime.description: Scheduled start of this occurrence of a recurring meeting. Present on list rows for recurring meetings.

attendee_id.description: Present with `attendee_id` in the request: that attendee's ID.

attendee_name.description: Present with `attendee_id` in the request: that attendee's display name.

attendee_email.description: Present with `attendee_id` in the request: that attendee's email address.

attendee_audio_id.description: Present with `attendee_id` in the request: that attendee's audio ID in the meeting.

attendee_role.description: Present with `attendee_id` in the request: that attendee's role.

Meeting.description: A meeting or permanent room, as the meeting reads return it. IDs, passcodes, names, users, and dial-in numbers are strings; flags, counts, and durations are numbers.

name.description: Name shown for the host. Defaults to the user's first and last name.

email.description: Email address of the host. Defaults to the user's first email address.

password.description: Write-only. Password for signing in to the video portal directly. Leave it out for a host that signs in only through the platform.

role.description: Role of the host in the domain's video account, as the video service defines it. Office Manager scope or higher only.

auto_record.description: Whether the host's conferences are recorded automatically.

plan_slug.description: Plan to give the host, by its product slug. `use-domain-default` gives the domain's default plan, and `no-plan` gives none. Leave it out for no plan. Office Manager scope or higher only. List the domain's plans with `GET /domains/{domain}/video/products`.

auto_stream.description: Whether the host's conferences are streamed automatically.

host_initiated_recording.description: Whether only the host can start a recording.

waiting_room.description: Whether participants wait until the host admits them.

no_welcome_email.description: Whether to skip the video service's welcome email. Defaults to `true`.

IotumHost.description: Body of a request that creates a user's video host. Every field is optional: what you leave out is filled from the user. Each value goes to the video service, which validates it.

name.description: Name of the contact.

email.description: Email address of the contact. Conference invitations go here.

business_phone.description: Business phone number of the contact.

mobile_phone.description: Mobile phone number of the contact.

home_phone.description: Home phone number of the contact.

other_phone.description: Another phone number for the contact.

time_zone.description: Time zone of the contact, as an IANA time zone name such as `America/Chicago` or `Europe/London`.

contact_id.description: Unique ID (`unique-id`) of the matching contact in the user's platform contacts. The two are linked shortly after.

IotumContact.description: One contact to add to a user's video address book. Fields other than `contact_id` go to the video service, which validates them.

id.description: Read-only. ID of the dashboard. Use it as `dashboard_id` on the charts endpoints.

name.description: Name of the dashboard.

domain.description: Domain the dashboard belongs to. `*` for a stock dashboard offered across the platform.

favorite.description: Whether the user marked the dashboard a favorite.

owner_id.description: Extension of the user who owns the dashboard, such as `1001`.

owner_type.description: Kind of owner. `1` is a user.

Dashboard.description: A dashboard as listed: its ID, name, owner, and whether the user marked it a favorite.

id.description: Read-only. ID of the chart.

name.description: Name of the chart.

type.description: How the chart is drawn, such as `ResponsiveLine`, `ResponsiveStat`, or `ResponsiveTable`.

data_token.description: Read-only. Access token for loading the chart's data, issued to you for every request. Every chart in one response carries the same token. It has no refresh token.

access_token.description: Bearer token with `Call Center Data` scope, issued to you.

expires_in.description: Seconds until `access_token` expires. A day, `86400`, by default.

token_type.description: How to send the token: in an `Authorization: Bearer` header.

refresh_token.description: Not returned. A data token cannot be refreshed: read the charts again for a new one.

Chart.description: A chart as listed: its ID, name, and type, with the token for loading its data.

by-ip.description: IP address the change was made from.

timestamp-datetime.description: When the change was made, in UTC.

by-domain.description: Domain of the user who made the change.

by-user.description: Who made the change: an extension, or an API key ID for a change made with an API key.

by-client.description: Client the change came through: `api`, or `api-` followed by the OAuth client ID.

action-type.description: What was done, such as `create`, `update`, or `delete` for a change, or `login` or `logout` for a sign-in or sign-out.

target-user.description: User that was changed, by extension. Empty when the change was not to a user.

target-object.description: Kind of object that was changed, such as `Subscriber`, `Call Queue`, `Domain`, `Dial Plan`, or `Registrar`.

auditlog-details.description: The values the change set, keyed by field name. Credentials such as passwords and keys are shown as `********`. Absent when none were recorded. Long changes are cut at 511 characters, so the last values may be missing.

event-category.description: Kind of entry: `change` for a configuration change, `session` for a sign-in or sign-out. Present when the request names `event-category`, except `session` alone.

Auditlog.description: One audit log entry: a configuration change, or a sign-in or sign-out. When it was made, by whom and from where, and what it changed.

LicenseR.description: One license record of a server. The authorization keys are masked unless a Super User sends `include-secret=yes`.

license-mac-address.description: MAC address the license is bound to.

license-remaining-days.description: Days left before the license expires.

license-authorized-endpoints.description: Number of endpoints the license allows.

license-authorized-sessions.description: Number of concurrent sessions the license allows.

license-authorization-key.description: Secret. Authorization key of the active license. Masked, as the first and last 2 characters around `*`, unless a Super User sends `include-secret=yes`.

license-authorization-data.description: Authorization data of the active license.

license-pending-key.description: Secret. Authorization key of a license waiting to replace the active one, masked like `license-authorization-key`. Empty when none is pending.

license-pending-data.description: Authorization data of the pending license. Empty when none is pending.

license-status.description: Status of the license, such as `active`.

license-update-status.description: Status of a license update, such as `idle`.

Limit.description: Maximum number of records to return. Defaults to `100`. Use it with `start` to page.

domain.description: The domain name.

description.description: The display name of the domain.

reseller.description: The reseller (territory) the domain belongs to.

limits-max-active-calls-total.description: Maximum number of simultaneous calls in the domain.

count-users-total.description: Users in the domain, not counting departments and the system users that features create.

count-call-center-agents.description: Distinct agent devices assigned to the domain's call queues.

count-conferences.description: Conference bridges in the domain, not counting monitoring and video bridges.

count-phone-numbers.description: Phone numbers routed to the domain.

count-phone-numbers-toll-free.description: Toll-free phone numbers routed to the domain: numbers starting 1800, 1888, 1877, 1866, 1855, 1844, or 1833.

count-devices-registered.description: Devices currently registered in the domain, including mobile apps that receive calls by push notification.

count-devices-total.description: Devices configured in the domain, registered or not.

stats-calculation-duration-milliseconds.description: How long counting the domain's objects took, in milliseconds.

active-calls-onnet-last-month.description: Peak number of simultaneous calls in the domain last month.

active-calls-offnet-last-month.description: Peak number of simultaneous off-net calls in the domain last month.

active-calls-onnet-this-month.description: Peak number of simultaneous calls in the domain this month.

active-calls-offnet-this-month.description: Peak number of simultaneous off-net calls in the domain this month.

sms-received-last-month.description: SMS messages received in the domain last month.

sms-received-this-month.description: SMS messages received in the domain this month.

sms-received-today.description: SMS messages received in the domain today.

sms-sent-today.description: SMS messages sent from the domain today.

sms-sent-this-month.description: SMS messages sent from the domain this month.

sms-sent-last-month.description: SMS messages sent from the domain last month.

count-user-scopes-basic-users.description: Users with the Basic User scope, system users included. Present only when not zero.

count-user-scopes-call-center-agents.description: Users with the Call Center Agent scope, system users included. Present only when not zero.

count-user-scopes-call-center-supervisor.description: Users with the Call Center Supervisor scope, system users included. Present only when not zero.

count-user-scopes-no-portal.description: Users with the No Portal scope, system users included. Present only when not zero.

count-user-scopes-office-manager.description: Users with the Office Manager scope, system users included. Present only when not zero.

count-user-scopes-reseller.description: Users with the Reseller scope, system users included. Present only when not zero.

count-user-scopes-super-user.description: Users with the Super User scope, system users included. Present only when not zero.

count-user-scopes-route-manager.description: Users with the Route Manager scope, system users included. Present only when not zero.

count-user-scopes-site-manager.description: Users with the Site Manager scope, system users included. Present only when not zero.

count-user-scopes-ndp-users.description: Users with the NDP scope, system users included. Present only when not zero.

count-service-codes-auto-attendant.description: Users with the `system-aa` service code (auto attendant users). Present only when not zero.

count-service-codes-call-queue.description: Users with the `system-queue` service code (call queue users). Present only when not zero.

count-service-codes-conference.description: Users with the `system-conf` service code (conference users). Present only when not zero.

count-service-codes-department.description: Users with the `system-department` service code (department users). Present only when not zero.

count-service-codes-ring-group.description: Users with the `system-ringgroup` service code (ring group users). Present only when not zero.

count-service-codes-site.description: Users with the `system-site` service code (site users). Present only when not zero.

count-service-codes-time-frame.description: Users with the `system-tod` service code (time frame users). Present only when not zero.

count-service-codes-trunk.description: Users with the `system-trunk` service code (SIP trunk users). Present only when not zero.

count-service-codes-system-user.description: Users with the `system-user` service code (generic system users). Present only when not zero.

count-users-configured-voicemail-transcr.description: Users whose voicemail is transcribed by `google`. Present only when not zero.
Users whose voicemail is transcribed by `mutare`. Present only when not zero.
Users whose voicemail is transcribed by `nuance`. Present only when not zero.
Users whose voicemail is transcribed by `voicebase`. Present only when not zero.

allow-video-conference.description: The domain's video conferencing setting. Present only when video conferencing is licensed.

DomainBilling.description: Usage counters and main limits of one domain. Counters by user scope, service code, and transcription vendor are present only when not zero. Video usage counters are added when video conferencing is licensed.

user.description: The user's extension.

domain.description: The user's domain.

site.description: The user's site. Empty when the user has none.

department.description: The user's department. Empty when the user has none.

directory-name-number-dtmf-mapping.description: The digits a caller dials to find the user in the auto attendant directory, up to 3.

PublicUserInfo.description: One user in the domain directory returned by `GET /domains/{domain}/users/list`. Only the fields named in `fields` are returned.

Brand.description:
A brand: the colors, fonts, spacing, footer text, and images the app uses for one hostname, reseller, and domain.

A brand is identified by its `hostname`, `reseller`, `domain`, and `brand-name`. `*` in `hostname` or `domain` means every hostname or every domain. Each combination of hostname, reseller, and domain has at most one active brand, and the active-brand endpoints fall back through `*` levels to find one.

`/list` endpoints return only `reseller`, `hostname`, `brand-name`, `description`, and `currently-active` (see `BrandListItem`). The active-brand endpoints add `matched-hostname`, and their `assets` entries add the `source-` fields.

id.description: The brand ID: the MD5 hash of `hostname`, `reseller`, `domain`, and `brand-name` joined together. Set by the server.

hostname.description: The hostname the brand applies to, such as `portal.example.com`, or `*` for every hostname.

reseller.description: The reseller that owns the brand.

domain.description: The domain the brand applies to, or `*` for every domain of the reseller.

brand-name.description: The brand name, unique for its hostname, reseller, and domain.

description.description: Notes about the brand.
description.example: Blue theme for the main portal

currently-active.description: `1` when this is the active brand for its hostname, reseller, and domain, otherwise `0`.

font-family.description: The CSS font family, also the fallback when `font-family-url` is set.

font-family-url.description: The URL of a custom font file, `http` or `https`.

font-size-pixels.description: The base font size in pixels, 8 to 32.

margin-pixels.description: The default margin in pixels, 0 to 100.

padding-pixels.description: The default padding in pixels, 0 to 100.

border-radius.description: The corner rounding: a preset (`none`, `subtle`, `rounded`, `soft`, or `pill`, from square to fully rounded) or a number of pixels from 0 to 100.

oneOf.description: Named preset
Pixel value

powered-by.description: The footer text shown in the app.

email-sender.description: The sender address for email the app sends under this brand.

matched-hostname.description: Active-brand reads only: the hostname of the brand returned, `*` when a hostname-wide brand matched.

created.description: When the brand was created, as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`.

modified.description: When the brand was last changed, as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`.

items.description: An image of the brand, as brand reads return it. These entries keep the stored names for most keys (`asset_type`, `brand_id`, `file_size`, `download_url`), unlike the asset endpoints.

id.description: The asset ID.

brand_id.description: The ID of the brand the asset belongs to.

filename.description: The stored file name.

created.description: When the asset was created, as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`.

modified.description: When the asset was last changed, as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`.

download_url.description: The absolute URL of the asset's download endpoint. Fetching it needs an access token.

source-hostname.description: Active-brand reads only: the hostname of the brand the asset came from.

source-reseller.description: Active-brand reads only: the reseller of the brand the asset came from.

source-domain.description: Active-brand reads only: the domain of the brand the asset came from.

source-brand-name.description: Active-brand reads only: the name of the brand the asset came from.

assets.description: The brand's images, as metadata. Not returned by `/list`. The entries use the stored names for most keys, such as `asset_type` and `download_url`; the asset endpoints return the same data under `asset-type` and `file-access-url`. Active-brand reads merge the entries from every level of the lookup and add the `source-` fields.

BrandAsset.description: An image of a brand, as the asset endpoints return it: metadata only. Fetch the image itself from `file-access-url`. A brand has one asset of each `asset-type`.

id.description: The asset ID: the MD5 hash of `brand-id` and `asset-type` joined together. Set by the server.

brand-id.description: The ID of the brand the asset belongs to.

asset-type.description: The asset type, such as `logo` or `favicon`. Any name of letters, digits, `-`, and `_`.

filename.description: The stored file name, used when the image is downloaded.

mime-type.description: The image type, read from the image: `image/png`, `image/jpeg`, or `image/svg+xml`.

width.description: The image width in pixels, read from the image.

height.description: The image height in pixels, read from the image.

file-size-bytes.description: The image size in bytes, up to 5,242,880.

file-access-url.description: The absolute URL of the asset's download endpoint. Fetching it needs an access token.

created.description: When the asset was created, as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`.

modified.description: When the asset was last changed, as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`.

domain.description: The domain of the call queue.

call-orig-call-id.description: The call ID of the caller's leg.

agent-term-uri.description: The SIP URI the call was last offered to. Empty when no agent was offered the call.

agent-term-user.description: The extension of the agent the call was last offered to.

agent-talking-duration-seconds.description: Talk time with an agent, in seconds. `0` on an abandoned call.

agent-call-duration-seconds.description: Time the call spent with the agent leg, in seconds.

queue-duration-seconds.description: Time the caller waited in the queue before leaving, in seconds.

agent-call-start-datetime.description: When the call was offered to the agent.

queue-call-start-datetime.description: When the call entered the queue.

queue-call-disconnect-datetime.description: When the call left the queue.

agent-call-answer-datetime.description: When an agent answered. Empty on an abandoned call.

call-orig-from-user.description: The caller's number. A string, so leading zeros and `+` are kept.

domain.description: The domain the disposition belongs to.

disposition.description: The outcome an agent picks, such as `Sale`.

DispositionReason.description: One reason under one call disposition in a domain.

emergency-address-id.description: The address ID. IDs the API generates are `a-` followed by 13 hexadecimal characters. Paths accept only letters, digits, spaces, and `* . - _ '`.

domain.description: The domain that owns the address.

user.description: Who the address belongs to: `*` for a domain-level address, a site name for a site address, or an extension for a personal address. Endpoint rows have `address_endpoint`.

address-name.description: A label for the address, shown when users pick one.

caller-name.description: The caller name stored with the address.

address-line-1.description: The house number and street. The house number is the text up to the first space.

address-state-province-abbreviation.description: The state or province code, such as `CA`.

address-postal-code.description: The postal code. Send it as a string to keep leading zeros.

address-country-abbreviation.description: The country code, such as `US` or `CA`.

address-location-description.description: Where in the building, such as a room or desk.

ip-address-public.description: A public IP address stored with the address, as sent. The API does not detect it.

address-formatted-pidflo.description: The address in PIDF-LO form, the XML the platform sends on emergency calls. Empty when the address was saved without a supported `carrier`.
