carrier.description: The emergency calling carrier the address was checked with.

count-users-configured.description: The number of users assigned this address. Returned by the lists only.

address-formatted-pretty.description: The address on three lines, for display.
address-formatted-pretty.example:
123 Example St
Suite 100 Front desk
Example City, CA 90210, US

address-is-default-for-site.description: `true` when a site uses this address as its own. Present only when `true`.

domain_default.description: `true` when the domain uses this address as its own. Present only when `true`.

site_address.description: `true` on an address a site owns that is not the site's own address. Present only when `true`.

shared.description: `true` on a site or domain-level row in a user's list. Present only there.

site_level.description: `true` on a site row in a user's list. Present only there.

domain_level.description: `true` on a domain-level row in a user's list. Present only there.

Address.description: An emergency (E911) address. An address is one of three kinds, set by its `user` field: `*` for a domain-level address that every user in the domain can see, a site name for a site address, or an extension for a personal address. The lists add `count-users-configured` and the default flags.

domain.description: The domain that owns the endpoint.

user.description: Always `address_endpoint`.

address-name.description: A label for the address, shown when users pick one.

caller-name.description: The caller name registered with the carrier.

address-line-1.description: The house number and street. The house number is the text up to the first space.

address-state-province-abbreviation.description: The state or province code, such as `CA`.

address-postal-code.description: The postal code. Send it as a string to keep leading zeros.

address-country-abbreviation.description: The country code, such as `US` or `CA`.

carrier.description: The carrier the number is registered with.

count-users-configured.description: The number of users whose `caller-id-number-emergency` is this number.

sub_count_total.description: The number of users in the domain.

multiple.description: `true` when the number appears more than once in this response.

address-formatted-pretty.description: The address on three lines, for display.
address-formatted-pretty.example:
123 EXAMPLE ST
Suite 100 
EXAMPLE CITY, CA 90210, US

AddressEndpoint.description: An endpoint: a callback number registered with the emergency calling carrier against an address. `emergency-address-id` is the callback number and `user` is always `address_endpoint`.

domain.description: The domain in the path.

emergency-address-id.description: The ID to save the address under: the one you sent, or a new one, `a-` followed by 13 hexadecimal characters.

valid.description: `false` when the carrier rejected the address. Absent when the address is valid.

reason.description: Why the carrier rejected the address. Present only with `valid: false`.
reason.example: The address could not be found.

carrier.description: The carrier that checked the address. Send it with the address when you save it.

address-formatted-pidflo.description: The standardized address, as an object whose keys depend on the carrier. Send it unchanged to `POST /domains/{domain}/addresses`. Absent when `valid` is `false`.

AddressValidate.description: The result of an address check: the request as sent, plus `emergency-address-id`, and either `address-formatted-pidflo` and `carrier` or `valid: false` and `reason`.

phoneconfiguration-name.description: The template name, unique in its domain. 1 to 32 characters: letters, digits, spaces, and `* . - _ '`.

phoneconfiguration-mac-address.description: The phone's MAC address: 12 hexadecimal digits with no separators.

phoneconfiguration-description.description: A description of the layout. Up to 255 characters.
phoneconfiguration-description.example: Front desk layout with queue toggle

phoneconfiguration-brand.description: The phone brand, as `device-models-brand` spells it in the device profiles. Up to 127 characters.

phoneconfiguration-model.description: The phone model, as `device-models-model` spells it in the device profiles. Up to 127 characters.

phoneconfiguration-domain.description: The domain that owns the configuration, or `*` for a platform-wide template.

phoneconfiguration-sidecars.description: The sidecars attached to the phone, in order. Allowed models are in the phone's device profile, in `profile-sidecar-support`.

phoneconfiguration-brand.description: The sidecar brand. Up to 127 characters.

phoneconfiguration-model.description: The sidecar model, as its device profile spells it. Up to 127 characters.

phoneconfiguration-extra.description: Extra settings for the layout, as a JSON object. Stored as sent. `{}` when there are none.

phoneconfiguration-directory.description: How the phone's directory is built: which contacts it lists, their order, and who is left out. Stored as sent.

group.description: The contacts to list: `All`, `Coworkers`, or a department name.

group-type.description: The kind of contact set: `Standard` or `department`.

exclusions.description: Contacts left out of the directory.

id.description: The user to leave out, as `user@domain`.

type.description: The kind of contact. Usually `onnet`.

phoneconfiguration-buttons.description: The buttons, in any order. Every button you send is saved, and the buttons belong to this configuration in this domain only. On an update, the list replaces every button: an update without it deletes every button.

Phoneconfiguration.description: A phone template or a phone configuration, as a single read returns it. A template has `phoneconfiguration-name`; a phone configuration has `phoneconfiguration-mac-address`. Every button you send is saved, and the buttons belong to this configuration in this domain only.

phoneconfiguration-button-order.description: The button's position: `profile-button-index` in the device profile. Numbering continues across sidecar buttons. Use each value once per button type.

phoneconfiguration-button-type.description: The kind of key, such as `line_only` or `mpk`. Allowed values are the model's button types from `GET /deviceprofiles/{brand}/{model}`. Up to 50 characters.

phoneconfiguration-button-feature.description: What the key does, such as `line`, `blf`, `park`, `speed_dial`, `queue_status`, or `timeframe_status`. Allowed values depend on the button type. Two button features also write a dial rule. It goes in the dial plan of the user on the first `line` button, or in the domain's dial plan when there is no `line` button. A `queue_status` button toggles the user's call queue availability: its target is ignored, and reads return it empty. A `timeframe_status` button toggles a time frame: its target is the time frame name, and `Default` means the default time frame. Add `targetUser` to the button's `phoneconfiguration-extra` to toggle another user's time frame. The dial rules appear with the dial plan's other dial rules. Up to 127 characters.

phoneconfiguration-button-target.description: What the key acts on, such as an extension for `line` or `blf`, or a time frame name for `timeframe_status`. Ignored for `queue_status`. Up to 127 characters.

phoneconfiguration-button-label.description: The text shown on the key, replacing the default label. Up to 127 characters.

phoneconfiguration-button-locked.description: `1` stops users changing the key in the portal. `0` leaves it editable.

phoneconfiguration-extra.description: Extra settings for the key. `{}` when there are none.

timeframe.description: For `timeframe_status`: the time frame name. The API fills it from the target.

targetUser.description: For `timeframe_status`: the user whose time frame the key toggles, when it is not the phone's own user.

dynamic.description: For `blf`: `true` makes the key a dynamic busy lamp field.

PhoneConfigBtn.description: One button of a phone template or phone configuration. The button types and features a model supports come from `GET /deviceprofiles/{brand}/{model}`, in `devicemodel`.

locales.description: Every locale that has at least one translation, sorted alphabetically.

namespaces.description: Every namespace in use across all locales, sorted alphabetically.

id.description: The translation ID.

common_entry_created.description: `true` when a copy of this key was also created in the `common` namespace. `false` when the namespace is `common` or `common` already had the key.

id.description: The translation ID.

description.description: Context for translators. `null` when none is set.
description.example: Placeholder text in the translation search box

created_at.description: When the record was created, as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`.

updated_at.description: When the record last changed, as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`.

availability.description: Which locales have this key, to find missing translations.

available_locales.description: The locales that have a translation for this `namespace` and `key`.

all_locales.description: Every locale in use. The same on every record.

TranslationRawRecord.description: One translation record with its metadata, as `GET /translations/raw` returns it.

success.description: One entry per item that succeeded: the same fields as the single-item response. A delete entry has `id`, `locale`, and `namespace` only.

errors.description: One entry per item that failed.

index.description: The position of the item in the request's `translations` array, starting at 0.

translation.description: The item as it was sent.

error.example: Translation already exists for this locale, namespace, and key combination

created.description: Items created. Present on a create.

updated.description: Items changed. Present on a change.

deleted.description: Items deleted. Present on a delete.

BulkTranslationResponse.description: The result of a bulk create, change, or delete. Always returned with `200`: check `errors` and `summary.failed` for items that did not succeed.

user.description: The extension the session belongs to. Each participant has their own copy of a session.

domain.description: The domain of that user.

messagesession-id.description: The session ID. Every participant's copy shares it. Use it in the path of the session endpoints. Chat, SMS, and MMS sessions use 32 lowercase hex characters.

messagesession-remote.description: Read-only. Who the user talks to: a user ID such as `1002@example.com` for a chat, or a phone number for an SMS. A group lists every other party, comma-separated. A number comes back as an integer.

messagesession-sms-number.description: Read-only. Your SMS number the session sends from. Empty for a chat session. A number comes back as an integer.

messagesession-last-datetime.description: When the session last sent or received a message.

messagesession-start-datetime.description: When this user's view of the session starts. Messages before it are not returned to this user. Deleting the session moves it to the time of the delete.

messagesession-last-message.description: Read-only. The text of the last message. Text made only of digits comes back as an integer.
messagesession-last-message.example: Can you cover the front desk at 3?

messagesession-last-sender.description: Read-only. Who sent the last message: a user ID, or a phone number for an inbound SMS.

messagesession-last-status.description: Whether the user has read the last message: `read` or `unread`. A new inbound message sets it to `unread`.

messagesession-muted.description: Whether the user muted the session: `yes` or `no`.

messagesession-last-email-reminder-datet.description: When the user was last emailed about an unread message in the session.

messagesession-receiver-hostname.description: Read-only. The server that last handled a message in the session.

messagesession-queue-termination.description: Read-only. For an SMS conversation routed to a call queue, the queue's user ID. Empty otherwise.

messagesession-queue-status.description: Read-only. Where a call queue conversation stands, such as `queued`, `dispatching`, `active`, or `complete`. Empty otherwise.

messagesession-queue-session-id.description: Read-only. The ID of the call queue conversation. Empty otherwise.

messagesession-agent-start-datetime.description: When an agent accepted the call queue conversation.

messagesession-last-type.description: Read-only. The type of the last message, such as `chat`, `sms`, or `mms`.

messagesession-last-media-type.description: Read-only. The MIME type of the last message's file. Empty when it had none.

messagesession-last-media-size.description: Read-only. The size in bytes of the last message's file. `0` when it had none.

session-name.description: The name of a group session. Empty for an unnamed session.

messagesession-participants.description: Every participant of a group chat, as comma-separated user IDs. Empty for a one-to-one session.

Messagesession.description: One user's copy of a conversation. Every participant has their own copy with the same `messagesession-id`, so read status, mute, and history start are per user. A number-only value, such as a phone number, comes back as an integer.

id.description: Read-only. The message ID: `m-` and 13 hex characters for a text message, the file ID for a message with a file, or the carrier's ID for an inbound SMS.

timestamp.description: Read-only. When the message was sent or received, in UTC, in the form `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`. Not RFC 3339.

type.description: Read-only. The message type, such as `chat`, `chat-media`, `sms`, or `mms`.

domain.description: Read-only. The domain of the session.

direction.description: Read-only. `term` for a message sent from the platform, `orig` for an inbound SMS or MMS.

from-number.description: Read-only. The phone number the SMS or MMS came from. Empty for a chat. Comes back as an integer.

from-user-id.description: Read-only. The user ID that sent the message. Empty for an inbound SMS.

from-video-attendee-id.description: Read-only. The video meeting attendee that sent the message, for a meeting chat.

from-user-agent.description: Read-only. The `User-Agent` of the app that sent the message.

dialed.description: Read-only. The number or numbers an SMS or MMS was sent to, comma-separated. Empty for a chat.

text.description: Read-only. The message text. Text made only of digits comes back as an integer.
text.example: Can you cover the front desk at 3?

terminating-user-id.description: Read-only. The user ID or IDs the chat was sent to, comma-separated.

terminating-number.description: Read-only. The number or numbers the SMS or MMS was sent to, comma-separated.

status.description: Read-only. The delivery status, such as `sending`, `error`, or `deleted`.

meeting-instance-id.description: Read-only. The video meeting the message was sent in, for a meeting chat.

media-type.description: Read-only. The MIME type of the attached file. Empty when there is none.

media-size.description: Read-only. The size in bytes of the attached file. `0` when there is none.

file-access-url.description: Read-only. A signed link that downloads the attached file. Present only on a message with a file. The link expires.

deleted-datetime.description: When the message was deleted. `null` when it was not.

messagesession-receiver-hostname.description: Read-only. The server that handled the message.

messagesession-id.description: Read-only. The session the message belongs to.

messagesession-participants.description: Read-only. For a group chat, every participant when the message was sent, comma-separated.

Message.description: One message in a session. A number-only value, such as a phone number or a text of digits, comes back as an integer. `timestamp` is UTC in the form `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`.

id.description: Read-only. The block ID, made from the two numbers and the domain: 40 lowercase hex characters.

requesting-number.description: The off-net number that asked to stop receiving messages, normalized to `+` and the country code. A 10-digit number gets `+1`.

blocked-number.description: Your number that may no longer message `requesting-number`, normalized the same way. An SMS or MMS from it to that number is refused with `409`.

domain.description: Read-only. The domain that owns the block. Taken from the path.

status.description: `active` blocks messages. `inactive` keeps the record but no longer blocks. Reads return only `active` blocks unless you filter on `status`.

created-datetime.description: When the block was created.

SmsBlock.description: An SMS opt-out: `requesting-number` asked not to receive messages from `blocked-number`. The platform adds one when an off-net number texts STOP, and removes it on START. While it is `active`, an SMS or MMS from `blocked-number` to `requesting-number` is refused with `409`.

domain.description: The domain the provider is offered to, or `*` for every domain. Defaults to `*`. On `/domains/{domain}/oidc-providers`, the path sets it.

provider-id.description: A short identifier used in login and logo URLs, unique across the platform. Omit it to have `idp_` and 12 hexadecimal characters generated. Use letters, digits, `_`, and `-` so the logo URL can address it.

provider-name.description: The name shown on the login button.

client-id.description: The client ID the identity provider issued for this platform.

client-secret.description: The client secret the identity provider issued. Never returned by a read. On an update, omit it to keep the stored secret.

discovery-url.description: The OpenID Connect discovery document URL, ending in `/.well-known/openid-configuration`. Used for any endpoint you leave empty.

authorization-endpoint.description: The authorization endpoint. Overrides the discovery document.

token-endpoint.description: The token endpoint. Overrides the discovery document.

userinfo-endpoint.description: The UserInfo endpoint. Overrides the discovery document.

jwks-uri.description: The JSON Web Key Set URL used to check ID token signatures. Overrides the discovery document.

issuer.description: The issuer value ID tokens must carry. Overrides the discovery document.

scope.description: The scopes requested from the identity provider, separated by spaces. Defaults to `openid email profile`.

logo-url.description: The logo shown on the login button. An uploaded logo sets it for you.

allowed-cidrs.description: Addresses that see the provider, as IPv4 or IPv6 addresses or CIDR ranges separated by commas. Empty means everyone. A bad entry is a `400`. It is a display filter, not access control: the address is read from forwarding headers.

enabled.description: `yes` offers the provider on login pages. `no` hides it and refuses logins through it. Defaults to `yes`.

display-order.description: The position on the login page, lowest first. Defaults to `0`.

OIDCProvider.description: The body of an OIDC provider create. Send `provider-name`, `client-id`, and `client-secret`, plus a `discovery-url` or the endpoints themselves.

smtp-host.description: The SMTP server's host name or IP address. A `tls://`, `ssl://`, or `smtps://` prefix is accepted and sets the encryption when `smtp-encryption` is `auto`.

smtp-encryption.description: `auto`, the default, uses implicit TLS on ports 465 and 2465 and STARTTLS elsewhere, and retries without encryption only when the server refuses STARTTLS. `tls` is implicit TLS, `starttls` upgrades the connection, and `none` stays unencrypted.

smtp-username.description: The login for SMTP authentication. Omit it or send it empty to test a relay that needs no login.

smtp-password.description: The password for SMTP authentication. Never returned.

test-email.description: `true` also sends a test message to `destination-email`. You can also send the destination address itself here. Defaults to `false`.

destination-email.description: Where to send the test message. Required when `test-email` is `true`.

source-email.description: The From address of the test message. Defaults to your own email address. Most servers refuse a From address that is not the login's own.

EmailValidate.description: SMTP settings to test. Nothing is stored.

AppinfoR.description: One application on one server. Every field is a string; a value the server did not report is an empty string. `appinfo-start-time` and `appinfo-status-update-time` are text as each server reported them, not RFC 3339 date-times.

appinfo-element-id.description: The application on the server, such as `sipbx`. With `appinfo-mac-address`, it identifies the row.

appinfo-hostname.description: The hostname of the server the application runs on.

appinfo-mac-address.description: The MAC address of the server. With `appinfo-element-id`, it identifies the row.

appinfo-ip-address.description: The internal IP address of the server. Empty when not reported.

appinfo-domain-db.description: The `domain_db` value the server reports. Empty when not reported.

appinfo-element-type.description: The type of the application, as the server reports it.

appinfo-status.description: The status the server reports for the application, such as `Running`.

appinfo-start-time.description: When the application last started, as the server reported it. Text such as `Tue, 01 Sep 2026 14:30:14 GMT`, not an RFC 3339 date-time.

appinfo-status-update-time.description: When the server last reported the application. Text such as `Tue, 06 Oct 2026 09:15:41 GMT`, not an RFC 3339 date-time.

appinfo-app-address.description: The address and port the application listens on, as `ip:port`. Empty when not reported.

appinfo-app-address-v6.description: The IPv6 address and port the application listens on, as `[ipv6]:port`. Empty when not reported.

appinfo-wan-address.description: The public address and port of the application, as `ip:port`. Empty when not reported.

appinfo-subnet-mask.description: The subnet mask of the server's interface. Empty when not reported.

RejectlogR.description: One rejected SIP request source. A row is identified by `reject-received-from`, `reject-method`, and `reject-address-of-record`, and repeats of the same request update it.

reject-received-from.description: The source address the rejected request came from.

reject-hostname.description: The core server that rejected the request.

reject-method.description: The SIP method of the request, such as `REGISTER` or `INVITE`.

reject-address-of-record.description: The address of record (AOR) the request was for.

reject-last-datetime.description: When the request was last received. RFC 3339 when the core server stored a standard date and time; otherwise the stored text. `null` when empty.

reject-user-agent.description: The `User-Agent` header of the request, as received.

reject-contact.description: The `Contact` header of the request, as received.

reject-result.description: The result the core server recorded for the request.

reject-action.description: The action the core server took on the request.

reject-count.description: How many times this request has been rejected.

reject-rate.description: The rate at which this request is being rejected, as the core server computes it.

server.description: Only in a per-server or reseller series: the server the point belongs to, as the metrics service names it. Can be empty.

ts.description: The time of the point, as a Unix timestamp in seconds, on a multiple of the step. Not an RFC 3339 date-time.

query.description: The query that was sent to the metrics service.

start.description: The start of the window, as a Unix timestamp in seconds.

end.description: The end of the window, as a Unix timestamp in seconds.

debug-parameters.description: Only on the first point: the parameters the query was sent with, for troubleshooting.

InsightValue.description: One point of an iNSight series. The response is an array of points in time order; a per-server read returns each server's points in turn.

status.description: Always `success`. A failed upstream call returns `500` instead.

endpoint.description: The alerting service path that was read: `/api/v2/alerts` for `active_alerts`.

annotations.description: Text the alert rule attaches to the alert. The keys vary by rule; these are the common ones.

__dashboardUid__.description: The dashboard the alert belongs to, with its organization ID.

description.description: What was detected and why it matters.
description.example: A critical Core Module security vulnerability has been detected. Take immediate action to remedy the affected configurations.

runbook_url.description: Where to read how to fix it.

summary.description: A one-line summary of the alert.
summary.example: 2 critical severity security misconfigurations have been found on your Core servers.

endsAt.description: When the alert expires unless it fires again, in RFC 3339 UTC with a `Z` suffix and milliseconds.

fingerprint.description: A hash that identifies this alert.

name.description: The receiver's name, such as `Logging` or `Email`.

startsAt.description: When the alert first fired, in RFC 3339 UTC with a `Z` suffix and milliseconds.

status.description: Whether the alert is active, silenced, or inhibited.

inhibitedBy.description: Fingerprints of the alerts inhibiting this one. Empty when none.

silencedBy.description: IDs of the silences muting this alert. Empty when none.

updatedAt.description: When the alert was last updated, in RFC 3339 UTC with a `Z` suffix and milliseconds.

generatorURL.description: The relative link to the expression that raised the alert.

labels.description: The labels that identify and route the alert. The keys vary by rule.

alertname.description: The name of the alert rule.

data.description: The alerts, as the alerting service returns them. Empty when nothing is firing.

InsightAlertResponse.description: The alert envelope. The alerting service's answer is passed through in `data` unchanged, wrapped with its source and a count.

Vcon.description: A vCon document in the IETF vCon core format. Empty optional members are omitted. Platform-specific values are under `x-netsapiens`.

uuid.description: A UUID derived from the CDR ID, so the same call always has the same UUID.

created_at.description: When the first leg started, in UTC with a `Z` suffix.

updated_at.description: When the last leg ended, in UTC with a `Z` suffix.

subject.description: A one-line subject: the first sentence of the AI summary when there is one, else the disposition and reason, else `Call from <caller> to <destination>`. At most 200 characters when taken from the summary.
subject.example: The caller asked about a delayed order and the agent confirmed the ship date.

extensions.description: The vCon extensions the document uses: `CC` (contact center) and `x-netsapiens`.

parties.description: The people on the call, one entry each, referred to elsewhere by their position in this array. An external caller has `role` `customer`, `tel`, and `sip`. An internal user has `role` `agent`, `sip`, and from their user profile `name` and `mailto`; their extension, site, department, and IP address are under `x-netsapiens`.

dialog.description: One `recording` entry per leg with media: `start`, `duration` in seconds, `parties`, `mediatype` `audio/wav`, and when recorded `filename`, a signed playback `url`, and `content_hash`. A `transfer` entry between two legs names `transferee`, `transferor`, `transfer_target`, `original`, and `target_dialog` by index.

analysis.description: The results of call analysis, each with `type`, `dialog` (the recording entries covered), `mediatype`, `vendor`, `body`, and `encoding`. Types are `transcript` (diarized segments with `party`, `text`, `start` and `end` in seconds, and `sentiment`), `summary`, `sentiment` (overall percentages), and `tags` (disposition, reason, notes, and whether the call was transferred). Empty when the call was not analyzed.

attachments.description: One `cdr` attachment per leg. Its `body` is the CDR row with the stored column names, not the API field names.

x-netsapiens.description: Platform details: `generator` (always `netsapiens-api-v2`), `domain` and `tenant` (both the path domain), `territory` (the domain's reseller, when known), and `notes` (gaps found while building, such as a leg with no recording).

call-intelligence-job-id.description: The transcription job ID. It links every analysis result for the recording.

call-intelligence-processing-status.description: The job's status, such as `finished`. Results can be incomplete until it is `finished`.

created-datetime.description: When the transcription was requested.

call-id.description: The SIP call ID of the recorded leg: the originating or terminating call ID, depending on who was recorded.

call-intelligence-features-enabled.description: The analysis features run for this job, separated by commas.

call-intelligence-summary.description: The AI summary of the call. Empty when summaries are off or not finished.
call-intelligence-summary.example: The caller inquired about their account balance and was assisted by a support agent.

call-intelligence-topics-top.description: The most frequent topics detected on the call.

call-intelligence-duration-seconds.description: The total seconds of detected speech.

call-intelligence-duration-seconds-negat.description: The seconds of speech with negative sentiment.

call-intelligence-duration-seconds-neutr.description: The seconds of speech with neutral sentiment.

call-intelligence-duration-seconds-posit.description: The seconds of speech with positive sentiment.

call-intelligence-ending-duration-second.description: The seconds of speech analyzed in the ending segment of the call.
The seconds of the ending segment with negative sentiment.
The seconds of the ending segment with neutral sentiment.
The seconds of the ending segment with positive sentiment.

call-intelligence-ending-percent-negativ.description: The percentage of the ending segment with negative sentiment. Not returned under this name today: the value arrives as `ending_negative_percentage`.

call-intelligence-ending-percent-neutral.description: The percentage of the ending segment with neutral sentiment.

call-intelligence-ending-percent-positiv.description: The percentage of the ending segment with positive sentiment.

call-intelligence-ending-sentiment-scale.description: A score for the sentiment of the ending segment of the call.

call-intelligence-percent-negative.description: The percentage of the call with negative sentiment.

call-intelligence-percent-neutral.description: The percentage of the call with neutral sentiment.

call-intelligence-percent-positive.description: The percentage of the call with positive sentiment.

call-intelligence-segments.description: The transcript, one entry per spoken segment in order, with the speaker, the text, its sentiment, and its start and end within the recording.

speaker.description: The speaker, as a SIP address such as `sip:1001@example.com`.

comment.description: The words spoken in this segment.
comment.example: Hello, and thanks for calling. How can I help you today?

sentiment.description: The sentiment of the segment: `Positive`, `Neutral`, or `Negative`.

start-time.description: Where the segment starts in the recording, as `HH:MM:SS,ff` (hundredths after the comma).

end-time.description: Where the segment ends in the recording, as `HH:MM:SS,ff`.

example.speaker: Agent
example.comment: Thank you for calling, how can I help you?

call-intelligence-summary-status.description: The status of the summary, such as `completed`.

call-intelligence-topics-all.description: Every topic detected on the call, including less frequent ones.

errors.description: Error details when processing failed. Empty otherwise.

last-modified-datetime.description: When the job last changed. The gap from `created-datetime` is roughly the processing time.

Transcription.description: One call transcription with its analysis. Fields from analysis features that were not enabled, or have not finished, are empty or absent.

call-id.description: The SIP call ID of the recorded call leg.

call-recording-match-pattern.description: The case the recording was made for: a user as `user@domain`, `*@domain` for a domain-wide rule, or `recording`.

call-recording-status.description: The recording's conversion status, such as `archived` once the file is in remote storage. Recordings whose status is empty, `empty media`, `conversion error`, or `archive error` are never returned.

call-recording-started-datetime.description: When the recording started, in RFC 3339. Null when not recorded.

call-recording-ended-datetime.description: When the recording stopped, in RFC 3339. Null when not recorded.

file-duration-seconds.description: The length of the recording in seconds.

file-size-kilobytes.description: The size of the recording file. Despite the name, for a file stored on the Recording server the value is in bytes. For an archived file it is `call-recording-remote-wav-size-kilobytes`. `0` when the file is not available yet.

file-access-url.description: A signed link that streams the recording with `GET /recordings/play`. It needs no access token and expires 180 minutes after `call-recording-retrieved-datetime` by default. Treat it like a password: anyone who has it can play the recording until it expires.

call-recording-retrieved-datetime.description: When this response was built, in RFC 3339. `file-access-url` expires a fixed time after it.

call-recording-remote-wav.description: The path of the file in remote storage. Empty when the recording has not been archived.

call-recording-remote-wav-size-kilobytes.description: The size of the archived copy, as remote storage reported it. A value above `0` means the file is in remote storage.

call-recording-remote-storage-config-id.description: The ID of the remote storage configuration that holds the archived copy. See `GET /domains/{domain}/recording-storage`.

geo-call-id.description: The originating call ID when this leg was tunneled between geographic sites. `na` when not.

sha512_3.description: The SHA-512 of the archived file, as 128 hexadecimal characters. Present only for recordings archived since version 46.

Recording.description: One recording of one call leg. A call can have several: one per case it matched, such as the user's own rule and a domain-wide rule.

user.description: The user's extension.

uid.description: The user's ID: extension `@` domain.

domain.description: The user's domain.

site.description: The user's site. Empty when the user has none.

department.description: The user's department. Empty when the user has none.

user-presence-status.description: The user's presence, for example `open` or `inactive`.

status-message.description: The user's status message. Left out when the user has never set one.

email.description: The user's email address, or several separated by commas.

Presence.description: One user's presence, as the presence lists return it.

CallqueuePath.description: Extension of the call queue, such as `4000`: the `callqueue` value returned by `GET /domains/{domain}/callqueues`.

AgentPath.description: The agent, as `callqueue-agent-id` returns it: `user@domain` for a user agent (`1001@example.com`), or `sip:` and the device address for a device agent (`sip:1001wp@example.com`). `~` means you. URL-encode it if your client does not.

Start.description: Number of records to skip before the first one returned. Defaults to `0`. Use it with `limit` to page.

UserAddressCreateRequest.title: UserAddressCreateRequest
UserAddressCreateRequest.description: Request body for creating an emergency (E911) address scoped to a single user/extension within a domain (POST /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/addresses). Distinct from the domain-level and endpoint-level address-create variants.

emergency-address-id.description: Client-assigned unique identifier for the address. Observed format: `a-{hex}`.

caller-id-number.description: Caller ID name/number presented to the PSAP for 911 calls originating from this address.

address-provisioned-carrier-name.description: Carrier the address will be provisioned with for E911 dispatch.

address-formatted-pidflo.description: Structured PIDF-LO record from the carrier's address validator. Sub-object keys use PascalCase, unlike the surrounding kebab-case request body.

HouseNumber.description: Numeric portion of the street address.

StreetName.description: Street name without the suffix; typically uppercase.

StreetSuffix.description: Street suffix abbreviation (LN, ST, AVE, BLVD, etc.).

City.description: City name (typically uppercase in PIDF-LO form).

Zip.description: Five-digit ZIP, encoded as integer (not string).

County.description: County information from the carrier's address validator. Often empty when not resolved.

LocationId.description: Carrier-assigned location ID after MSAG validation.

ValidationStatus.description: Result of MSAG validation against the carrier's address database.

Adjusted.description: Boolean-as-string. "true" when the carrier adjusted/normalized the address during validation.

ip-address-public.description: Public IP observed for the user at submission time. Used by the carrier to map the address to a known site/subnet.

UserAddressCreateReturn.title: UserAddressCreateReturn
UserAddressCreateReturn.description: Response payload returned after successfully creating an emergency (E911) address scoped to a single user/extension within a domain (POST /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/addresses). Address fields are emitted in kebab-case via the FieldMap pass in `responseWithV2Json`; envelope/identity fields are framework-set and remain in their original casing.

address-provisioned-carrier-name.description: Carrier the address was provisioned with for E911 dispatch.

object.description: Object type identifier; always "address" for this endpoint.

domain.description: Domain the address belongs to (echoes the path parameter).

user.description: User/extension the address is associated with (echoes the path parameter).

singular.description: Boolean-as-integer (0/1). Indicates whether this is the user's singular E911 address.

action.description: Action performed; always "create" for this endpoint.

apiVer.description: API version that served the request.

uid.description: Fully-qualified subscriber identifier in the form `user@domain`.

carrier.description: Carrier the address was provisioned with (typically matches `address-provisioned-carrier-name`). Present for compatibility with v1-shaped consumers.

emergency-address-id.description: Unique identifier for the address record. Echoes the value supplied on the request.

caller-id-number.description: Caller ID name/number presented to the PSAP for 911 calls originating from this address.

address-location-description.description: Free-form location detail within the address (room, desk, floor).

ip-address-public.description: Public IP observed at the time of address creation. Used by the E911 vendor to map the address to a known site/subnet.

title.description: Echo of the request `title` (null if omitted).

qrCodeUrl.description: qrserver.com URL whose `data=` param contains a URL-encoded otpauth:// URI.

apiversion.description: Server build version. `Version: 0.0.0` in dev, `BUILD_NUMBER` in a packaged build.

hostname.description: The core server the series was read from.

range.description: The `range` used, or `null` when `datetime-start` and `datetime-end` were sent.

interval-seconds.description: The bucket width in seconds: 60, 600, or 3600.

gauge-aggregate.description: How gauge samples inside one bucket were combined.

start-datetime.description: The start of the first bucket, aligned to the interval.

end-datetime.description: The start of the last bucket, aligned to the interval. The last bucket can still be filling.

timestamps.description: The start of each bucket, in Unix seconds (UTC). This is the shared time axis for every metric's `values`.

metrics.description: The series for each requested metric, keyed by metric ID.

NmsStatusSeries.description: A time-bucketed series of one core server's status counters.

type.description: `gauge` is a reading at one moment. `counter` is a running total, reported as a rate per second.

unit.description: The unit of `values`. For a counter it ends in `/s`.

label.description: A display label for the metric.

group.description: The group the metric belongs to, for building pickers.

current.description: For a gauge, the latest raw sample. For a counter, the rate in the latest bucket that has one. `null` when the window has no data.

first.description: The first bucket value in the window that is not `null`. `null` when the window has no data.

min.description: The lowest bucket value in the window. `null` when the window has no data.

max.description: The highest bucket value in the window. `null` when the window has no data.

avg.description: The average of the bucket values, rounded to 3 decimal places. `null` when the window has no data.

change-percent.description: The change from `first` to `current` as a percentage, rounded to 2 decimal places. `null` when `first` is 0 or the window has no data.

samples.description: The number of buckets that have a value.

total.description: Counters only. The total increase over the window, not counting resets.

values.description: One value per entry in `timestamps`. `null` where the bucket had no samples or, for a counter, where the counter reset.

NmsStatusMetricSeries.description: The series and summary figures for one metric.

metric.description: The metric ID. Use it in the `metrics` parameter of `GET /nmsstatus`; it is also the key in that response.

column.description: The underlying column name. `GET /nmsstatus` also accepts it in `metrics`.

type.description: `gauge` is a reading at one moment, averaged per bucket. `counter` is a running total, reported as a rate per second.

unit.description: The base unit of the metric.

series-unit.description: The unit `GET /nmsstatus` reports. For a counter it is the base unit followed by `/s`.

group.description: The group the metric belongs to, for building pickers. Use it in the `group` filter.

label.description: A display label for the metric.

NmsStatusMetric.description: One metric in the status catalog.

hostname.description: The core server's hostname. Use it as `hostname` in `GET /nmsstatus`.

local.description: `yes` when this is the server that answered the request.

reachable.description: `yes` when the server answered in time. `no` when it did not answer, so its other fields are empty.

last-status-datetime.description: When the server recorded its newest sample. `null` when it has none or did not answer.

last-status-age-sec.description: Seconds since the newest sample. `null` when it has none or did not answer.

stale.description: `yes` when the newest sample is more than 45 seconds old, which is more than two missed samples, or when the server has none or did not answer.

NmsStatusServer.description: One core server a status series can be read from.

CustomScope.description: A custom scope, or with `include-built-in=yes` a built-in catalog entry. A custom scope takes a built-in parent scope and removes rights from it, so it can never do more than its parent. Users and API keys are assigned it by name. Its rights come from these settings:

name.description: The scope name, assigned to users and API keys and carried by their tokens. 1 to 32 characters: letters, digits, spaces, `.`, `_`, and `-`, starting with a letter or digit. It cannot be the name of a built-in scope.

parent-scope.description: The built-in scope this one takes its rights from. Empty on a built-in catalog entry. A scope created before the current parent list can still name a parent outside it.

description.description: A note about the scope, up to 256 characters.
description.example: Operations admin with no platform configuration or routing changes

read-only.description: `yes` refuses every write the parent would allow. `no` keeps the parent's writes, less `modifications`.

enabled.description: `no` refuses every token issued under the scope, as a delete would, until it is set back to `yes`.

hidden.description: `yes` leaves the scope out of `GET /scopes` unless `include-hidden=yes` is sent. It changes nothing about what the scope can do.

built-in.description: `yes` on a built-in catalog entry, which you cannot redefine. `no` on a custom scope.

default-hidden.description: Built-in catalog entries only. `yes` when the scope is hidden unless you show it. Only the eight scopes you can derive from are shown by default.

assignable-parent.description: Built-in catalog entries only. `yes` when a custom scope can name this scope as its parent.

CustomScopeModifications.description:
Rights removed from the parent scope, per object. Each key is an API object name, such as `phonenumber`, `device`, `route`, or `nsconfig`, and an unknown name is refused. Each value is one of these limits:

- `none`: the object is refused.
- `ro`: reads, lists, and counts only.
- `update-only`: reads, lists, counts, and updates.
- `no-delete`: everything but deletes.

An object not listed keeps the parent's rights.

CdrDBase.description: A domain call detail record (CDR), base shape, returned when `limit` is over 100 or `0`. It lacks `id`, the SIP Call-IDs, `core-server`, and the other full-record fields. Empty fields are left out.

domain.description: Domain the row is filed under

reseller.description: Territory of `domain`

call-direction.description: Kind of call, from this row's point of view: `0` outbound, `1` inbound and answered, `2` inbound and missed, `3` on-net (extension to extension)

call-parent-cdr-id.description: Id of the call record. It is on every row, and it is the id the keyed paths and `/quality` take.

call-orig-user.description: Originating user or extension, such as `1001`

call-orig-from-uri.description: SIP From URI of the originating leg

call-orig-from-name.description: Display name in the originating leg's From header

call-orig-to-user.description: User part of the originating leg's To header: the number dialed

call-orig-request-uri.description: SIP Request-URI of the originating leg

call-orig-request-user.description: User part of the originating leg's Request-URI

call-through-user.description: User the call was routed through, such as a forwarding user or a call queue

call-term-to-uri.description: SIP To URI of the terminating leg

call-answer-datetime.description: When the call was answered. Left out for an unanswered call.

call-total-duration-seconds.description: Length of the call, in seconds

hide-from-results.description: `1` hides the row from reads unless they send `showhidden`

privacy.description: `true` when the caller asked for privacy. Name and number fields then read `Anonymous` for scopes below Reseller. Returned under this v1 name.

call-orig-match-uri.description: Connection or route the originating leg matched

call-intelligence-job-id.description: Id of the call's transcription job

call-intelligence-percent-positive.description: Share of the transcript with positive sentiment, as a percent

call-intelligence-percent-neutral.description: Share of the transcript with neutral sentiment, as a percent

call-intelligence-percent-negative.description: Share of the transcript with negative sentiment, as a percent

ending_sentiment.description: Sentiment at the end of the call. Returned under this v1 name.

call-intelligence-topics-top.description: Main topics found in the transcript

call-disposition.description: Disposition set on the call, such as a wrap-up code

call-disposition-notes.description: Notes recorded with the disposition. Stored as text with no practical length limit.

call-account-code.description: Account code entered for the call

call-disconnect-reason-text.description: Why the call ended, as text

call-recording-status.description: Recording state of the call, as a number. `0` is the default.

call-audio-quality-orig-mos.description: Summary MOS of the originating leg, on the 1 to 5 scale: the worse of its two audio directions. Left out until quality scanning has seen the call. `GET /cdrs/{id}/quality` has each direction.

call-audio-quality-term-mos.description: Summary MOS of the terminating leg, on the 1 to 5 scale: the worse of its two audio directions. Left out until quality scanning has seen the call. `GET /cdrs/{id}/quality` has each direction.

call-intelligence-summary.description: Summary of the call written by call intelligence. Stored as text with no practical length limit.

call-last-updated-datetime.description: When the row last changed, in UTC

call-term-to-name.description: Display name in the terminating leg's To header

is-trace-expected.description: `true` when a SIP trace should still exist for this call

prefilled-transcription-api.description: Ready-made `/transcriptions` request for this call. Present only when the call has a transcription job and the read named a domain.

CdrUBase.description: A user's call detail record (CDR), base shape, returned when `limit` is over 100 or `0`. It lacks `id`, the SIP Call-IDs, `core-server`, and the other full-record fields. Empty fields are left out.

uid.description: User the row is filed under, as `user@domain`. Returned under this v1 name.

domain.description: Domain the row is filed under

call-parent-cdr-id.description: Id of the call record. It is on every row, and it is the id the keyed paths and `/quality` take.

call-direction.description: Kind of call, from this row's point of view: `0` outbound, `1` inbound and answered, `2` inbound and missed, `3` on-net (extension to extension)

call-answer-datetime.description: When the call was answered. Left out for an unanswered call.

call-total-duration-seconds.description: Length of the call, in seconds

call-orig-to-uri.description: SIP To URI of the originating leg

number.description: Number of the other party on the call. Returned under this v1 name.

name.description: Name of the other party on the call. Returned under this v1 name.

onnet.description: On-net marker for the call. Returned under this v1 name.

hide-from-results.description: `1` hides the row from reads unless they send `showhidden`

privacy.description: `true` when the caller asked for privacy. Name and number fields then read `Anonymous` for scopes below Reseller. Returned under this v1 name.

call-intelligence-job-id.description: Id of the call's transcription job

call-intelligence-percent-positive.description: Share of the transcript with positive sentiment, as a percent

call-intelligence-percent-neutral.description: Share of the transcript with neutral sentiment, as a percent

call-intelligence-percent-negative.description: Share of the transcript with negative sentiment, as a percent

ending_sentiment.description: Sentiment at the end of the call. Returned under this v1 name.

call-intelligence-topics-top.description: Main topics found in the transcript

call-disposition.description: Disposition set on the call, such as a wrap-up code

call-disposition-notes.description: Notes recorded with the disposition. Stored as text with no practical length limit.

call-account-code.description: Account code entered for the call

call-disconnect-reason-text.description: Why the call ended, as text

call-recording-status.description: Recording state of the call, as a number. `0` is the default.

call-audio-quality-orig-mos.description: Summary MOS of the originating leg, on the 1 to 5 scale: the worse of its two audio directions. Left out until quality scanning has seen the call. `GET /cdrs/{id}/quality` has each direction.

call-audio-quality-term-mos.description: Summary MOS of the terminating leg, on the 1 to 5 scale: the worse of its two audio directions. Left out until quality scanning has seen the call. `GET /cdrs/{id}/quality` has each direction.

call-intelligence-summary.description: Summary of the call written by call intelligence. Stored as text with no practical length limit.

CdrG.description: A site or department call detail record (CDR), expanded shape, returned when a read names `site` or `group`. It carries the full call record when `limit` is 100 or less or `raw` is sent. Empty fields are left out.

grp.description: Site or department the row is filed under. Returned under this v1 name.

grp_type.description: `1` when `grp` is a site. Any other value is a department. Returned under this v1 name.

call-direction.description: Kind of call, from this row's point of view: `0` outbound, `1` inbound and answered, `2` inbound and missed, `3` on-net (extension to extension)

NdpCoreServerUpdate.description: Body for `PUT /phones/servers/{server}`. Every field is optional, and the server comes from the path. Send a credential as an empty string to leave it unchanged. A non-blank `core-server-api-key` blanks the 4 OAuth fields and sets `status` to `APIkey enabled`.

core-server-hostname.description: SIP proxy FQDN handed to devices. Required on create. Super User and Super User Read Only only on read.

core-server-db-hostname.description: Host of this server's SiPbx database. Super User and Super User Read Only only on read.

core-server-port.description: SIP port, as a string. Super User and Super User Read Only only on read.

device-provisioning-core-server-tcp-port.description: SIP TCP port, as a string.

device-provisioning-core-server-tls-port.description: SIP TLS port, as a string.

core-server-sipbx-db.description: Name of this server's SiPbx database. Super User and Super User Read Only only on read.

core-server-user.description: SiPbx database user. Super User and Super User Read Only only on read.

core-server-tac-url.description: TAC endpoint URL. Super User and Super User Read Only only on read.

core-server-tac-username.description: TAC endpoint user name. Super User and Super User Read Only only on read.

core-server-active.description: Not used. Present in the table, read by nothing.

device-provisioning-redundancy-group.description: Failover group (`geo_group`). Servers sharing a group are failover peers.

backup_ok.description: May this server be chosen as a failover target. NDP treats NULL as `yes`. This raw column name is the one to send on a write.

core-server-lat.description: Latitude, a decimal with 4 places, as a string.

core-server-lon.description: Longitude, a decimal with 4 places, as a string.

address-location-description.description: Free-text location (`location`). This spelling is the one to send on a write.

device-provisioning-core-server-postfix-.description: DNS suffix appended when building the device registrar (`postfix`).

device-provisioning-core-server-api-fqdn.description: NsApi FQDN NDP calls for subscriber/device data (`ns_api_hostname`).

core-server-client-id.description: OAuth client ID NDP uses. Defaults to `ndp`. Blanked when an API key is set. Super User and Super User Read Only only on read.

core-server-oauth-username.description: OAuth user NDP logs in as. Blanked when an API key is set. Super User and Super User Read Only only on read.

core-server-access-expires-datetime.description: When NDP's OAuth access token expires. Written by NDP. Super User and Super User Read Only only on read.

core-server-refresh-expires-datetime.description: When NDP's OAuth refresh token expires. Written by NDP. Super User and Super User Read Only only on read.

core-server-pass.description: SiPbx database password. Secret: returned only with `include-secrets=yes` and Super User scope. Send an empty string on update to leave it unchanged.

core-server-tac-password.description: TAC endpoint password. Secret: returned only with `include-secrets=yes` and Super User scope. Send an empty string on update to leave it unchanged.

core-server-client-secret.description: OAuth client secret. Secret: returned only with `include-secrets=yes` and Super User scope. Blanked when an API key is set.

core-server-oauth-password.description: OAuth password. Secret: returned only with `include-secrets=yes` and Super User scope. Blanked when an API key is set.

core-server-access-token.description: OAuth access token, written by NDP. Secret: returned only with `include-secrets=yes` and Super User scope.

core-server-refresh-token.description: OAuth refresh token, written by NDP. Secret: returned only with `include-secrets=yes` and Super User scope.

core-server-api-key.description: API key NDP uses instead of OAuth. When it is not blank, the 4 OAuth fields are blanked and `status` becomes `APIkey enabled`. Secret: returned only with `include-secrets=yes` and Super User scope.

core-server-cert.description: PEM certificate. Returned only with `include-certs=yes` and a Super User or Super User Read Only scope.

core-server-ca.description: PEM CA certificate. Returned only with `include-certs=yes` and a Super User or Super User Read Only scope.

DeviceModelUpdate.description: Body for `PUT /phones/models/{brand}/{model}`. Every field is optional, and the brand and model come from the path.

device-models-type.description: `Device` for a phone, `AnalogGW` for an analog gateway, or `DigitalGW` for a digital gateway. The list shows `Device` and `AnalogGW` by default.

device-models-config-format.description: The NDP config builder that renders this model, such as `Polycom`, `CiscoSPA`, or `SnomM3`, or a custom template name. Models with `Counterpath` never appear in the list. Up to 128 characters.

device-models-count-buttons.description: A whole number of 0 or more. Stored as `phone_ext`.

device-models-fxs-support-enabled.description: Number of FXS ports. A whole number of 0 or more. The value is a count, even though the name ends in `-enabled`.

device-models-fxo-support-enabled.description: Number of FXO ports. A whole number of 0 or more.

device-models-trunk-support-enabled.description: Number of trunk ports. A whole number of 0 or more.

device-models-directory-support-enabled.description: `yes` when the model supports a directory, otherwise `no`.

device-models-presence-support-enabled.description: `yes` when the model supports presence, otherwise `no`. Stored in the misspelled column `presense`.

device-models-shared-line-support-enable.description: `yes` when the model supports shared line appearances (SLA), otherwise `no`.

device-models-sidecar-support-enabled.description: `yes` when the model supports an expansion module (sidecar), otherwise `no`.

device-models-resync-support-enabled.description: `yes` when the model supports resync, otherwise `no`.

device-models-encryption-support-enabled.description: `yes` when the model supports encryption, otherwise `no`.

device-models-firmware-support-enabled.description: `yes` when the model supports firmware management, otherwise `no`.

device-models-firmware-options.description: Firmware choices for this model, as stored. Up to 255 characters.

device-models-overrides-blob.description: Model-level provisioning overrides as `key="value"` pairs separated by spaces. Checked with NDP's parser on write. To edit one option at a time, use `/phones/models/{brand}/{model}/overrides`.

device-models-visible-in-portal.description: `yes` when the model is offered in the portal, otherwise `no`. The list returns only `yes` models by default.

DeviceModelOverrideUpdate.description: Body for `PUT /phones/models/{brand}/{model}/overrides/{option-name}`. The option name comes from the path.

option-value.description: The option value. May contain spaces and `=`. Cannot contain `"` or the texts `SPACE`, `EQUALQUOTE`, or `EQUALINVALUE`. An empty value is stored as `<null>`.

default-value.description: New parameter value, stored as text.

default-description.description: New free-text note, up to 255 characters.

BrandDefaultUpdate.description: Body for `PUT /brand-defaults/{brand}/{server}/{default-name}`. Send `default-value`, `default-description`, or both; sending neither answers `400`.

option-value.description: New option value. May contain spaces and `=`. Cannot contain `"` or the literal `<null>`.

ProvisioningOptionUpdate.description: Body for `PUT .../provisioning-defaults/{server}/{option-name}`. The option name and server tier come from the path.

domain.description: Domain written.

site.description: Site written. Site defaults only.

default-applied.description: `yes` when this API server's NDP database showed the write within `synchronous-timeout`. `no` when it did not yet, which is not a rejection. Other NDP servers are not checked.

ProvisioningDefaultsRawApplied.description: The `synchronous=yes` report for a raw row write or delete.

NdpConfigUpdate.description: Body for `PUT /ndpconfig/{config-name}`. The key comes from the path, and a `config-name` in the body is ignored.

config-value.description: The new value, stored as text. The API applies no length limit. A value that repeats the masked placeholder a read returned for this key returns `400`.

code.description: HTTP status, repeated in the body.

message.description: What went wrong, and which field when one is at fault.

NdpErrorResponse.description: Error body. `message` says what went wrong and, where it can, which field.

code.description: HTTP status. `202` on a standard install.

message.description: `Accepted` for `202`, or `Success` for `200`.

warnings.description: Notes about the request that did not stop it. Present only when there are any.

NdpSuccessResponse.description: Answer to a write that was published on the service bus. Each NDP server applies the change after this response, so a `202` does not mean the change is live yet.

config-name.description: The configuration key. Up to 127 characters.

config-value.description: The stored value, as text. Never converted to a number. Masked when the key looks like a credential and the request did not get `include-secrets=yes`.

config-value-redacted.description: `yes` when `config-value` is a mask, not the stored text. Present only on masked rows.

config-timestamp-datetime.description: When the row last changed on that server, in RFC 3339. `null` when the server stores no time.

config-server.description: Hostname of the NDP server this row came from.

config-in-sync.description: `yes` when every expected server answered and holds the same value. `no` when this response shows servers holding different values. `unknown` when not every server answered, a masked value cannot be compared, or the values differ only as text, such as `1.10` and `1.1`.

config-servers-reporting.description: How many NDP servers answered this request.

config-servers-expected.description: How many NDP servers the inventory lists, from `NsNdpApiHosts` or the `ndp` rows in the process list. When this is larger than `config-servers-reporting`, `config-in-sync` cannot be `yes`.

NdpConfig.description: One configuration key as one Endpoints server (NDP) holds it, from `config_config`. A fanned-out read returns one of these per key per server. The sync fields are repeated on every row because the response is a bare list.

config-name.description: The configuration key. Up to 127 characters. Letters, digits, `.`, `_`, and `-` only, so `/ndpconfig/{config-name}` can reach it.

config-value.description: The value, stored as text. The API applies no length limit. A value that repeats the masked placeholder a read returned for this key is refused. Saving `PerDevicePasswordGlobalAllowOnce` stores the value only and does not change the `phones_config` column default.

NdpConfigWrite.description: Body for `POST /ndpconfig`. Adds one key on every Endpoints server (NDP), or on the server named in `config-server`.

config-name.description: The key that was written.

config-server.description: Hostname of the NDP server this row describes.

config-applied.description: `yes` when the server showed the written value, or for a delete showed the key gone, before the wait ended. `no` when it answered but did not show it yet. `unknown` when it did not answer.

NdpConfigApplied.description: What one Endpoints server (NDP) showed when a `synchronous=yes` write stopped waiting. The write is still asynchronous, so `no` means not yet seen, never rejected.

config-server.description: Hostname from the inventory. Every server the inventory lists appears, whether or not it answered.

config-server-local.description: `yes` when this is the server that handled your request, otherwise `no`.

config-server-reachable.description: `yes` when the server answered. For the server handling your request, `yes` when it could read its own table. Otherwise `no`.

config-server-config-count.description: Configuration rows the server returned. `null` when it did not answer, never `0`.

config-server-out-of-sync-count.description: Rows on the server marked `config-in-sync: no`. `null` when it did not answer.

NdpConfigServer.description: One Endpoints server (NDP) from the inventory, with how much configuration it holds and how much of it differs from another server.

NdpCoreServer.description: A core server that the Endpoints server (NDP) provisions devices against, from `servers_config`. A Reseller gets `name`, `address-location-description`, `device-provisioning-redundancy-group`, both ports, `backup_ok`, both FQDNs, and `status`, plus their aliases. Every other field is for Super User and Super User Read Only only. Credentials and certificates appear only on request.

core-server-oauth-username.description: OAuth user NDP logs in as. Blanked when an API key is set. Super User and Super User Read Only only on read.

core-server-access-expires-datetime.description: When NDP's OAuth access token expires. Written by NDP. Super User and Super User Read Only only on read.

core-server-refresh-expires-datetime.description: When NDP's OAuth refresh token expires. Written by NDP. Super User and Super User Read Only only on read.

core-server-tac-password.description: TAC endpoint password. Secret: returned only with `include-secrets=yes` and Super User scope. Send an empty string on update to leave it unchanged.

core-server-client-secret.description: OAuth client secret. Secret: returned only with `include-secrets=yes` and Super User scope. Blanked when an API key is set.

core-server-oauth-password.description: OAuth password. Secret: returned only with `include-secrets=yes` and Super User scope. Blanked when an API key is set.

core-server-refresh-token.description: OAuth refresh token, written by NDP. Secret: returned only with `include-secrets=yes` and Super User scope.

core-server-api-key.description: API key NDP uses instead of OAuth. When it is not blank, the 4 OAuth fields are blanked and `status` becomes `APIkey enabled`. Secret: returned only with `include-secrets=yes` and Super User scope.

core-server-cert.description: PEM certificate. Returned only with `include-certs=yes` and a Super User or Super User Read Only scope.

core-server-refresh-expires-datetime.description: When NDP's OAuth refresh token expires. Written by NDP. Super User and Super User Read Only only on read.

core-server-pass.description: SiPbx database password. Secret: returned only with `include-secrets=yes` and Super User scope. Send an empty string on update to leave it unchanged.

core-server-tac-password.description: TAC endpoint password. Secret: returned only with `include-secrets=yes` and Super User scope. Send an empty string on update to leave it unchanged.

core-server-client-secret.description: OAuth client secret. Secret: returned only with `include-secrets=yes` and Super User scope. Blanked when an API key is set.

core-server-oauth-password.description: OAuth password. Secret: returned only with `include-secrets=yes` and Super User scope. Blanked when an API key is set.

core-server-access-token.description: OAuth access token, written by NDP. Secret: returned only with `include-secrets=yes` and Super User scope.

core-server-refresh-token.description: OAuth refresh token, written by NDP. Secret: returned only with `include-secrets=yes` and Super User scope.

core-server-api-key.description: API key NDP uses instead of OAuth. When it is not blank, the 4 OAuth fields are blanked and `status` becomes `APIkey enabled`. Secret: returned only with `include-secrets=yes` and Super User scope.

core-server-cert.description: PEM certificate. Returned only with `include-certs=yes` and a Super User or Super User Read Only scope.

core-server-ca.description: PEM CA certificate. Returned only with `include-certs=yes` and a Super User or Super User Read Only scope.

NdpServerConfig.description: The Endpoints server (NDP) connection this API instance is configured with. Not a `servers_config` row.

name.description: Always `ndpConfig`.

hostname.description: Host of this API's NDP database connection, or this server's own name when that connection is local.

device-models-brand.description: Vendor-cased brand, such as `Polycom`. Part of the key.

device-models-model.description: Model name, such as `VVX 400`. Part of the key. Up to 127 characters.

device-models-brand-and-model.description: Brand and model separated by one space. Computed on read.

device-models-type.description: `Device` for a phone, `AnalogGW` for an analog gateway, or `DigitalGW` for a digital gateway. The list shows `Device` and `AnalogGW` by default.

device-models-config-format.description: The NDP config builder that renders this model, such as `Polycom`, `CiscoSPA`, or `SnomM3`, or a custom template name. Models with `Counterpath` never appear in the list. Up to 128 characters.

device-models-count-buttons.description: A whole number of 0 or more. Stored as `phone_ext`.

device-models-fxs-support-enabled.description: Number of FXS ports. A whole number of 0 or more. The value is a count, even though the name ends in `-enabled`.

device-models-fxo-support-enabled.description: Number of FXO ports. A whole number of 0 or more.

device-models-trunk-support-enabled.description: Number of trunk ports. A whole number of 0 or more.

device-models-directory-support-enabled.description: `yes` when the model supports a directory, otherwise `no`.

device-models-presence-support-enabled.description: `yes` when the model supports presence, otherwise `no`. Stored in the misspelled column `presense`.

device-models-shared-line-support-enable.description: `yes` when the model supports shared line appearances (SLA), otherwise `no`.

device-models-sidecar-support-enabled.description: `yes` when the model supports an expansion module (sidecar), otherwise `no`.

device-models-resync-support-enabled.description: `yes` when the model supports resync, otherwise `no`.

device-models-encryption-support-enabled.description: `yes` when the model supports encryption, otherwise `no`.

device-models-firmware-support-enabled.description: `yes` when the model supports firmware management, otherwise `no`.

device-models-firmware-options.description: Firmware choices for this model, as stored. Up to 255 characters.

device-models-overrides-blob.description: Model-level provisioning overrides as `key="value"` pairs separated by spaces. Checked with NDP's parser on write. To edit one option at a time, use `/phones/models/{brand}/{model}/overrides`.

device-models-visible-in-portal.description: `yes` when the model is offered in the portal, otherwise `no`. The list returns only `yes` models by default.

DeviceModelRow.description: One phone or gateway model that the Endpoints server (NDP) can provision, from `device_models`. The brand and model together are the key.

device-models-brand.description: Vendor-cased brand, such as `Polycom`. Part of the key.

device-models-model.description: Model name, such as `VVX 400`. Part of the key. Up to 127 characters.

device-models-type.description: `Device` for a phone, `AnalogGW` for an analog gateway, or `DigitalGW` for a digital gateway. The list shows `Device` and `AnalogGW` by default.

device-models-config-format.description: The NDP config builder that renders this model, such as `Polycom`, `CiscoSPA`, or `SnomM3`, or a custom template name. Models with `Counterpath` never appear in the list. Up to 128 characters.

device-models-count-buttons.description: A whole number of 0 or more. Stored as `phone_ext`.

device-models-fxs-support-enabled.description: Number of FXS ports. A whole number of 0 or more. The value is a count, even though the name ends in `-enabled`.

device-models-fxo-support-enabled.description: Number of FXO ports. A whole number of 0 or more.

device-models-trunk-support-enabled.description: Number of trunk ports. A whole number of 0 or more.

device-models-directory-support-enabled.description: `yes` when the model supports a directory, otherwise `no`.

device-models-presence-support-enabled.description: `yes` when the model supports presence, otherwise `no`. Stored in the misspelled column `presense`.

device-models-shared-line-support-enable.description: `yes` when the model supports shared line appearances (SLA), otherwise `no`.

device-models-sidecar-support-enabled.description: `yes` when the model supports an expansion module (sidecar), otherwise `no`.

device-models-resync-support-enabled.description: `yes` when the model supports resync, otherwise `no`.

device-models-encryption-support-enabled.description: `yes` when the model supports encryption, otherwise `no`.

device-models-firmware-support-enabled.description: `yes` when the model supports firmware management, otherwise `no`.

device-models-firmware-options.description: Firmware choices for this model, as stored. Up to 255 characters.

device-models-overrides-blob.description: Model-level provisioning overrides as `key="value"` pairs separated by spaces. Checked with NDP's parser on write. To edit one option at a time, use `/phones/models/{brand}/{model}/overrides`.

device-models-visible-in-portal.description: `yes` when the model is offered in the portal, otherwise `no`. The list returns only `yes` models by default.

DeviceModelWrite.description: Body for `POST /phones/models`. `device-models-brand-and-model` is computed and ignored if sent.

DeviceProfileRow.description: A device profile, as a read returns it. A device profile describes one phone or sidecar model for the phone template builder: its picture, where each button sits on it, how many button pages it has, and which sidecars it takes. Device profiles are shared by every domain.

device-models-brand.description: The device brand. 1 to 32 characters: letters, digits, `-`, and `_`.

device-models-model.description: The device model. 1 to 64 characters: letters, digits, spaces, `-`, and `_`.

device-models-type.description: Whether the profile is a phone or a sidecar. Defaults to `phone`.

profile-page-count.description: How many pages of buttons the model has. Defaults to `1`.

profile-sidecar-support.description: The sidecars the model takes. An empty array when it takes none.

limit.description: How many of this sidecar the phone can take.

buttons.description: Where each button sits on the picture, one entry per button.

image.description: The profile's picture. The picture itself is at `file`.

file.description: The URL of the picture. It needs no token.

file-size-kilobytes.description: The size of the picture file, in bytes.

default_position.description: Where the phone template builder places and zooms the picture by default.

x.description: Offset from the left edge, in pixels.

y.description: Offset from the top edge, in pixels.

devicemodel.description: Single-profile reads only: the matching device model, with its `device-models-*` fields. `device-models-button-types` lists the button types the model supports and, for each, the features it can take.

profile-button-index.description: The button number, unique in the profile. Phone templates use it as `phoneconfiguration-button-order`.

profile-button-type.description: The kind of key, such as `line_only` or `mpk`. Up to 50 characters.

profile-button-position.description: Where the button sits on the picture, as a JSON pair of pixel coordinates `[x,y]`. Up to 127 characters.

profile-button-settings.description: Extra settings for the button. Often empty.

DeviceProfileButtonRow.description: One button of a device profile: its number, its kind, and where it sits on the picture.

device-models-brand.description: The device brand. 1 to 32 characters: letters, digits, `-`, and `_`.

device-models-model.description: The device model. 1 to 64 characters: letters, digits, spaces, `-`, and `_`.

device-models-type.description: Whether the profile is a phone or a sidecar. Defaults to `phone`.

profile-page-count.description: How many pages of buttons the model has. Defaults to `1`.

profile-sidecar-support.description: The sidecars the model takes, as a JSON array of `{"model": "<sidecar model>", "limit": <count>}`. Send `[]` for none.

buttons.description: The buttons. When sent and not empty, they replace every button of the profile.

device_image.description: The picture: `0x` followed by the image bytes in hexadecimal. Up to 16 MB of image data.

device_image_filetype.description: The picture's media type. Up to 50 characters.

device_image_filesize.description: The picture file size, in bytes.

device_image_default_position.description: Where the phone template builder places and zooms the picture by default, as a JSON object `{"x": <px>, "y": <px>, "zoom": <factor>}`. Up to 127 characters.

DeviceProfileWrite.description: The body of a device profile create. `device-models-brand` and `device-models-model` are required. An existing profile for the same brand and model is overwritten.

default-brand.description: Lowercase brand slug, such as `polycom`, or `*` for the general defaults. Never `domain` or `site` on this resource.

default-server.description: Server tier: `default` (fallback), `*` (stored as written, treated like `default`) or a server name from `/phones/servers`.

default-name.description: Vendor parameter name, up to 127 characters.

default-value.description: Parameter value, stored as text. Numeric-looking values such as `0123` stay strings.

default-description.description: Free-text note about the row, up to 255 characters.

default-timestamp-datetime.description: When the row last changed, in RFC 3339.

BrandDefault.description: One brand default: a vendor parameter the Endpoints server (NDP) writes into the config of every device of that brand, for one server tier.

default-server.description: Server tier. Omitted means `default`. A named server must exist in `/phones/servers`, and `all` is refused.

default-name.description: Vendor parameter name, up to 127 characters.

default-value.description: Parameter value, stored as text. Numeric-looking values such as `0123` stay strings.

default-description.description: Free-text note about the row, up to 255 characters.

default-brand.description: Lowercase brand slug, such as `polycom`, or `*`. Required on `POST /brand-defaults`; on `POST /brand-defaults/{brand}` the path supplies it.

BrandDefaultWrite.description: Body for creating a brand default. On `POST /brand-defaults` send `default-brand` as well; on `POST /brand-defaults/{brand}` the brand comes from the path.

default-name.description: Vendor parameter name of the row written.

default-brand.description: Brand slug of the row written.

default-server.description: Server tier of the row written.

default-applied.description: `yes` when this API server's NDP database showed the write within `synchronous-timeout`. `no` when it did not yet, which is not a rejection. Other NDP servers are not checked.

BrandDefaultApplied.description: The `synchronous=yes` report for a brand default write: whether this API server's NDP database shows the change yet.
