default-brand.description: Lowercase brand slug, or `*` for the general defaults.

default-count.description: Number of rows for the brand across every server tier.

BrandDefaultBrand.description: One brand that has at least one brand default, with how many it has.

domain.description: Domain the option belongs to.

site.description: Site the option belongs to. Site defaults only.

default-server.description: Server tier: `default`, `*` or a server name.

option-value.description: Option value. May contain spaces and `=`. An empty value is stored as `<null>` and returned as an empty string.

default-timestamp-datetime.description: When the row (the whole stored string) last changed, in RFC 3339.

ProvisioningOption.description: One provisioning option from a domain or site row, for one server tier.

ProvisioningOptionWrite.description: Validated against NDP's own parser before publishing. A `400` names the reason: a double quote, the literal text `SPACE`, `EQUALQUOTE`, `EQUALINVALUE` or `<null>`, a character outside NDP's key or value class, or a row that would exceed 2,000 options.

default-server.description: Server tier. Omitted means `default`. A named server must exist in `/phones/servers`, and `all` is refused.

option-name.description: Option name. Letters, digits and `_ * ; : - ( ) [ ] . / |`, with no spaces.

option-value.description: Option value. May contain spaces and `=`. Cannot contain `"` or the literal `<null>`. Send an empty string for an empty value. Leading and trailing spaces are trimmed.

default-description.description: Sets the row's description, whether the row is new or already exists.

default-applied.description: `yes` when this API server's NDP database showed the write within `synchronous-timeout`. `no` when it did not yet, which is not a rejection. Other NDP servers are not checked.

domain.description: Domain written.

site.description: Site written. Site defaults only.

ProvisioningOptionApplied.description: The `synchronous=yes` report for a provisioning option write: whether this API server's NDP database shows the change yet.

ProvisioningDefaultsRaw.description: The whole stored row: the option string NDP parses, as stored.

domain.description: Domain the row belongs to.

site.description: Site the row belongs to. Site rows only.

default-value.description: The stored string: `key="value"` pairs separated by spaces. `<null>` is an empty value.

option-count.description: Number of options NDP's parser finds in the string.

default-timestamp-datetime.description: When the row last changed, in RFC 3339.

ProvisioningDefaultsRawWrite.description: Replaces the whole stored string. Any text NDP would drop is reported in a `400`.

default-value.description: The whole option string: `key="value"` pairs separated by spaces. Must parse cleanly, hold 1 to 2,000 options and not be empty.

default-description.description: Free-text note on the row, up to 255 characters. Replaces the current note when sent.

NdpPhoneAdditionalFields.description: Fields of `phones_config` (`GET /phones/{mac}`, object `mac`) that API-3162 mapped for the first time. They are additive to the existing `NdpPhone` schema; nothing existing was renamed. They appear on a single-MAC read (a list read selects an explicit subset) and are accepted on writes.

device-provisioning-line-1-password.description: Per-line SIP credential. Omitted unless a Super User sends `include-secrets=yes`.

DeviceModelOverride.description: One provisioning option from a device model's overrides.

option-value.description: The option value. May contain spaces and `=`, but not `"`. An empty value is stored as `<null>`.

DeviceModelOverrideWrite.description: Body for `POST /phones/models/{brand}/{model}/overrides`. Checked with NDP's own parser before publishing. A `400` gives the reason, in the same words as domain provisioning defaults.

option-name.description: The option name. Letters, digits, and `_ * ; : - ( ) [ ] . / |`. Cannot contain the texts `SPACE`, `EQUALQUOTE`, or `EQUALINVALUE`.

option-value.description: The option value. May contain spaces and `=`. Cannot contain `"` or the texts `SPACE`, `EQUALQUOTE`, or `EQUALINVALUE`. An empty value is stored as `<null>`.

DeviceModelOverridesRaw.description: All of a device model's overrides as one stored value.

device-models-overrides-blob.description: Every override as `key="value"` pairs separated by spaces. Empty when the model has no overrides.

option-count.description: Number of options NDP's parser reads from the stored value.

DeviceModelOverridesRawWrite.description: Replaces every override on a device model. The value must pass NDP's parser cleanly, and every fragment the parser would drop is listed in a `400`. An empty value clears the overrides.

device-models-overrides-blob.description: Every override as `key="value"` pairs separated by spaces. At most 2,000 options. Send an empty string to clear every override.

ProvisioningDefaultsDomain.description: One domain or site that holds provisioning defaults, with how many options it has.

domain.description: Domain that holds the defaults.

site.description: Site name. Present on site rows only.

option-count.description: Number of options NDP's parser finds, summed across every server tier's row.

default-server-count.description: Number of server-tier rows (`default`, `*` or named servers) for this domain or site.

default-timestamp-datetime.description: Newest change among those rows, in RFC 3339.

CdrExport.description: One file a CDR schedule produced: one run of the schedule over one export window. Times are in UTC (`+00:00`).

export-id.description: Identifies the export within its schedule: the start of the export window in UTC. Use it in the export's own path.

schedule-name.description: The schedule that produced the export.

domain.description: Domain the export covers. `*` for a platform-wide schedule.

reseller.description: Reseller (territory) the schedule belongs to. Empty when the schedule has none.

user.description: User the schedule belongs to. Empty for a domain-wide schedule.

export-cdr-format.description: The CDR format the file was written in, as set on the schedule.

data-lookup-window.description: The schedule's lookup window when the export ran, for example `day` or `custom`.

export-window-start-datetime.description: Start of the period of calls in the file.

export-window-end-datetime.description: End of the period of calls in the file.

cdr-count.description: Number of call records in the file. Left out when it was not recorded.

export-core-server.description: Hostname of the server that ran the export and holds the file.

file-name.description: The file's name, as the download sends it.

file-access-url.description: A signed download link for this export. Anyone holding it can download the file with no token until `file-access-url-expires-datetime`, so treat it like the file itself. Every read returns a fresh link. Left out when a link cannot be signed.

file-access-url-expires-datetime.description: When `file-access-url` stops working: 60 minutes after the read by default.

LicfConfigApplied.description: What one recording server reports after a write with `synchronous=yes`.

config-name.description: The key written.

config-applied.description: `yes`: the server holds the written value, or for a delete no longer holds the key. `no`: it answered but does not hold it yet; this means not seen yet, never rejected. `unknown`: the server did not answer.

DomainTemplate.description: A template domain. Carries the ordinary domain fields plus, unless `include-counts=no`, one `element-*` count per resource provisioning would clone. Only the template-specific fields are listed here; every other domain field is present as usual.

reseller.description: The territory the template belongs to.

element-users.description: Subscribers, excluding the domain user and system accounts.

element-callparks.description: Call parks, which are queues with a dispatch type of `-`.

element-agents.description: Queue membership rows across all queues.

element-phonetemplates.description: Phone provisioning templates — configurations with no MAC.

element-scope.description: Only present under `debug-counts=yes`: the domain string the counts were scoped to.

DomainTemplateProvisionRequest.description:
The template-specific fields accepted by `POST /domains`. Supplying `domain-template-source` switches the ordinary create into provisioning mode; the rest of the normal domain create fields still apply.

For each resource, pass either a `*-list` (explicit items) or a `*-count` (the first N from the template), or neither to clone every one the template has. A `*-list` entry is merged over the template item at the same index. With `user-count`, extensions are assigned sequentially from the greater of the template's lowest extension and 1000.

domain.description: The new domain to create.

domain-template-source.description: The template domain to clone from. Must be flagged as a template.

main-number.description: A DID to assign as the new domain's main number. It is routed to the destination the template names, remapped onto the cloned attendant or queue. Omit it and no number is assigned — the API cannot allocate a DID.

user-list.description: Explicit users; each item may carry any subscriber field.

user-count.description: Clone the first N template users, renumbering extensions.

DomainTemplateProvisionResponse.description: What `POST /domains` returns when provisioning from a template: the new domain record plus a report of the clone. The counts are what was attempted — read the new domain's resources to confirm.

provisioned_skipped.description: Resources the run declined to create, each with the reason. Present only when something was skipped. A resource missing from a provisioned domain and named here is recoverable; one missing silently is not.

site.description: The site name. Required on create; taken from the path on update, where it cannot be changed.

SiteWrite.description: Writes take the same v2 names the read returns; `site` is the one exception, being the name rather than a field of the row.

DomainSetting.description: One setting as stored on one tier.

reseller.description: The territory of a reseller setting. `*` on a system or domain setting.

domain.description: The domain of a domain setting. `*` on a system or reseller setting.

domain-editable.description: `no` locks the setting for the domain tier: Office Manager tokens cannot override it on a domain. Always `yes` on a domain setting.

reseller-editable.description: `no` locks a system setting for the reseller tier: Reseller tokens cannot override it. Always `yes` on a reseller or domain setting.

updated-by.description: The user who last changed the setting.

updated-datetime.description: When the setting was last changed.

source.description: The tier the setting is stored on: `system`, `reseller`, or `domain`.

DomainSettingCatalog.description: Every setting the platform reads, as an object keyed by setting name.

description.description: What the setting does.

type.description: The kind of value the platform expects: `boolean`, `number`, `string`, `enum`, `json`, or `key`. Advisory: the API does not check values against it.

default.description: The built-in value the platform uses when no tier sets the setting. `null` when there is none.

values.description: The allowed values. Present when `type` is `enum`.

ref.description: The kind of object the value names, such as `dialplan` or `ndpserver`. Present when `type` is `key`.

legacy.description: The legacy UI configuration names this setting replaces.

min.description: The smallest allowed value. Present on some `number` settings.

max.description: The largest allowed value. Present on some `number` settings.

shape.description: The expected structure of a `json` value.

dynamic.description: `true` when the name is a prefix for a family of settings rather than one setting.

used-in.description: The apps that read the setting, such as `api`.

DomainSettingEffective.description: One setting in effect for a domain, and the tier its value came from.

domain.description: The domain the settings are in effect for, from the path.

reseller.description: The territory the domain belongs to.

source.description: The tier the value came from: `system`, `reseller`, or `domain`.

domain-editable.description: Whether an Office Manager token can change this setting on the domain. `no` when the reseller setting, or the system setting if there is no reseller setting, is locked.

reseller-editable.description: Whether a Reseller token can change this setting. `no` when the system setting is locked.

description.description: What the setting does, from the catalog. Empty for a setting the catalog does not list.

DomainSettingValue.description: The setting value: any JSON value, including `null`, `false`, `0`, and an empty string. It is returned with the type it was sent with. At most 65,536 bytes as JSON. The API does not check it against the catalog type.

DomainSettingWrite.description: The setting to store. The path decides the tier: a `reseller` or `domain` in the body is ignored.

setting.description: The setting name. Required on `POST` to a collection, and ignored on `PUT`, where the path names it. Letters, digits, and `. - _`, case-sensitive. A name that contains a credential word such as `password`, `secret`, or `token` is refused.

domain-editable.description: On a system or reseller setting, `no` stops Office Manager tokens from overriding it on a domain. Ignored on a domain setting. Defaults to `yes`.

reseller-editable.description: System settings only. `no` stops Reseller tokens from overriding the setting. Sending it to a reseller or domain setting returns `400`. Defaults to `yes`.

config-name.description: The configuration key.

config-value.description: The stored value, exactly as stored. Masked when the key looks like a credential, unless `include-secrets=yes` was accepted.

config-timestamp-datetime.description: When this server last wrote the row.

config-server.description: The recording server this row came from. With `local-only=yes` on a core server, the serving server's hostname.

config-in-sync.description: Whether the recording servers agree on this key: `yes` (every expected server answered and all agree), `no` (they differ, visibly in this response, or some hold the key and others do not), or `unknown` (agreement cannot be shown).

config-servers-reporting.description: How many servers' rows are in this response. On every row, because a list is a bare array.

config-servers-expected.description: How many recording servers the inventory holds. When it exceeds `config-servers-reporting`, a server did not answer and no `yes` is given; the `/servers` path says which.

LicfConfig.description: One configuration entry as held by one recording server.

NmcConfig.description: One `nmc_config_config` entry as held by one recording server. Same fields as `LicfConfig`, with different limits: `config-name` is at most 31 characters here (127 in `config_config`) and `config-value` at most 255 (127 there). A longer write returns `400`.

config-name.description: The key: letters, digits, `.`, `_`, and `-`, up to 127 characters.

config-server.description: Writes this recording server only, with nothing published. Leave it out to publish to every recording server.

overwrite.description: `yes` lets the create replace an existing key instead of returning `409`. Also accepted as a query parameter.

synchronous.description: `yes` waits for the write to reach each recording server and answers `200` with one row per server. Also accepted as a query parameter.

LicfConfigWrite.description: Body for creating a recording-server configuration key.

config-value.description: The new value, up to 127 characters. A mask sent back is dropped from the write, so every server keeps its stored value.

config-server.description: Writes this recording server only, with nothing published.

synchronous.description: `yes` waits for the write to reach each recording server. Also accepted as a query parameter.

LicfConfigUpdate.description: Body for changing a recording-server configuration key.

config-server-local.description: `yes` when this recording server took the request itself.

config-server-reachable.description: `no` when the server is in the inventory but did not answer, or when it is the serving server and could not read its own table.

config-server-config-count.description: Rows the server holds. `null`, not `0`, when it did not answer.

config-server-out-of-sync-count.description: The server's rows whose `config-in-sync` is `no`. `null` when the server did not answer.

LicfConfigServer.description: One recording server's view of a configuration key.

acc-elm.description: First part of the policy's key. `*` is a stored value.

case-id.description: Second part of the key: the recording's case ID, such as `1001@example.com`.

status.description: Third part of the key: the recording status the policy applies to, or `*` for every status.

enabled.description: Whether the policy is active.

delete-rtp.description: Whether the raw RTP capture is deleted after archiving.

delete-wav.description: Whether the converted WAV file is deleted after archiving.

delete-all.description: Whether everything is deleted after archiving.

hold-period.description: How long archived media is held, as stored text.

last-date-datetime.description: This server's last archive run. `null` when it has never run.

last-poll-datetime.description: This server's last poll. `null` when it has never polled.

archive-config-server.description: The recording server this row came from.

archive-config-in-sync.description: Whether the recording servers agree on this policy, comparing the policy fields only: `yes` (every expected server answered and all agree), `no` (they differ, or some hold the policy and others do not), or `unknown` (not every server answered).

archive-config-servers-reporting.description: How many servers' rows are in this response.

archive-config-servers-expected.description: How many recording servers the inventory holds. When it exceeds `archive-config-servers-reporting`, no `yes` is given.

ArchiveConfig.description: A lawful-intercept archive policy on a recording server.

acc-elm.description: First part of the key. Letters, digits, spaces, `.`, `_`, `-`, `@`, and `*`.

case-id.description: Second part of the key: the case ID, such as `1001@example.com`.

status.description: Third part of the key. Send `*` for a policy that applies whatever the status; it is not filled in for you.

enabled.description: Whether the policy is active. Defaults to `yes`.

delete-rtp.description: Delete the raw RTP capture after archiving. Defaults to `no`.

delete-wav.description: Delete the converted WAV file after archiving. Defaults to `no`.

delete-all.description: Delete everything after archiving. Defaults to `no`.

hold-period.description: How long archived media is held. Defaults to `0`.

ArchiveConfigWrite.description: Body for creating an archive policy.

enabled.description: Whether the policy is active.

delete-rtp.description: Delete the raw RTP capture after archiving.

delete-wav.description: Delete the converted WAV file after archiving.

hold-period.description: How long archived media is held.

ArchiveConfigUpdate.description: Body for changing an archive policy.

service-id.description: The service's id. The API generates it on create from `service-name`, `service-type`, `service-value`, and `service-vendor`, as 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters. It does not change when those fields are updated later.

service-type.description: The level the service applies to: `domain` for one domain, `reseller` for a territory, or `system` for the whole platform.

service-value.description: The subject of `service-type`: the domain for `domain`, the territory for `reseller`. For `system`, the value is stored as sent.

service-vendor.description: Where recordings are archived, matched without regard to case: `awss3` (Amazon S3), `wasabi`, `oracle`, and `awsglacier` are S3-compatible; `dropbox`; `ftp` and `ftps`; `sftp`.

service-url.description: For an S3-compatible vendor, the region, such as `us-east-1`. For `ftp`, `ftps`, and `sftp`, the server's host name.

service-path.description: For an S3-compatible vendor, the bucket. For `ftp`, `ftps`, and `sftp`, the directory recordings are written to.

service-login.description: The account the service signs in as: the access key ID for an S3-compatible vendor, or the user name. Returned on every read; it is not a secret on its own.

service-password.description: The secret: the secret access key for an S3-compatible vendor, or the password. Left out of every read unless a Super User asks with `include-secrets=yes`.

service-password-redacted.description: `yes` when a `service-password` is stored but was left out of this read. Absent when none is stored or when the value is included.

access-token.description: An OAuth access token for vendors that use one. For `oracle`, the object storage namespace. Left out of every read unless a Super User asks with `include-secrets=yes`.

access-token-redacted.description: `yes` when an `access-token` is stored but was left out of this read. Absent otherwise.

refresh-token.description: An OAuth refresh token for vendors that use one. Left out of every read unless a Super User asks with `include-secrets=yes`.

refresh-token-redacted.description: `yes` when a `refresh-token` is stored but was left out of this read. Absent otherwise.

admin-email.description: The address notified when archiving to this service fails.

enabled.description: Whether recordings are archived to this service: `yes` archives to it, `no` keeps it configured but unused. Defaults to `yes` on create.

status.description: The archiver's last result for this service. It is cleared whenever the service is updated.

parameter.description: Free-form text stored with the service.

created-datetime.description: When the service was created. Sent as RFC 3339 in UTC (`+00:00`), and `null` when the column holds the zero date.

updated-datetime.description: When the service was last changed. Sent as RFC 3339 in UTC (`+00:00`), and `null` when the column holds the zero date.

emailed-datetime.description: When `admin-email` was last notified of a failure. Sent as RFC 3339 in UTC (`+00:00`), and `null` when the column holds the zero date. It is `null` until the first notice.

bytes.description: Only with `report=yes`: the total size, in bytes, of the recordings archived to this service.

cnt.description: Only with `report=yes`: the number of recordings archived to this service.

RecordingStorage.description: A recording storage service: a remote destination where call recordings are archived, for one domain, one territory, or the whole platform. `service-password`, `access-token`, and `refresh-token` are left out of every read, and a matching `*-redacted` field says which are stored. A Super User gets them with `include-secrets=yes`.

service-name.description: The service's display name. Part of the generated `service-id`.

service-type.description: The level the service applies to: `domain` for one domain, `reseller` for a territory, or `system` for the whole platform. Optional: defaults to `domain`. Any other value returns `403`. Part of the generated `service-id`.

service-value.description: The subject of `service-type`: the domain for `domain`, the territory for `reseller`. For `system`, the value is stored as sent. Optional: defaults to the domain in the path. Any other value returns `403`. Part of the generated `service-id`.

service-vendor.description: Where recordings are archived, matched without regard to case: `awss3` (Amazon S3), `wasabi`, `oracle`, and `awsglacier` are S3-compatible; `dropbox`; `ftp` and `ftps`; `sftp`. Part of the generated `service-id`.

service-url.description: For an S3-compatible vendor, the region, such as `us-east-1`. For `ftp`, `ftps`, and `sftp`, the server's host name.

service-path.description: For an S3-compatible vendor, the bucket. For `ftp`, `ftps`, and `sftp`, the directory recordings are written to.

service-login.description: The account the service signs in as: the access key ID for an S3-compatible vendor, or the user name. Returned on every read; it is not a secret on its own.

service-password.description: The secret: the secret access key for an S3-compatible vendor, or the password.

access-token.description: An OAuth access token for vendors that use one. For `oracle`, the object storage namespace.

refresh-token.description: An OAuth refresh token for vendors that use one.

admin-email.description: The address notified when archiving to this service fails.

enabled.description: Whether recordings are archived to this service: `yes` archives to it, `no` keeps it configured but unused. Defaults to `yes` on create.

parameter.description: Free-form text stored with the service.

RecordingStorageWrite.description: The body of a recording storage service create. `service-name`, `service-vendor`, and `admin-email` are required. The service always belongs to the domain in the path, so `service-type` and `service-value` default to it. The API generates `service-id`.

RecordingStorageUpdate.description: The body of a recording storage service change. Every field is optional; send only the fields to change. A read leaves the credentials out, so a read-modify-write round trip keeps them.

service-name.description: The service's display name. Leave it out to keep the current value. Changing it does not change `service-id`.

service-type.description: The level the service applies to: `domain` for one domain, `reseller` for a territory, or `system` for the whole platform. Leave it out to keep the current value. Changing it does not change `service-id`.

service-value.description: The subject of `service-type`: the domain for `domain`, the territory for `reseller`. For `system`, the value is stored as sent. Leave it out to keep the current value. Changing it does not change `service-id`.

service-vendor.description: Where recordings are archived, matched without regard to case: `awss3` (Amazon S3), `wasabi`, `oracle`, and `awsglacier` are S3-compatible; `dropbox`; `ftp` and `ftps`; `sftp`. Leave it out to keep the current value. Changing it does not change `service-id`.

service-url.description: For an S3-compatible vendor, the region, such as `us-east-1`. For `ftp`, `ftps`, and `sftp`, the server's host name. Leave it out to keep the current value.

service-path.description: For an S3-compatible vendor, the bucket. For `ftp`, `ftps`, and `sftp`, the directory recordings are written to. Leave it out to keep the current value.

service-login.description: The account the service signs in as: the access key ID for an S3-compatible vendor, or the user name. Returned on every read; it is not a secret on its own. Leave it out to keep the current value.

service-password.description: The secret: the secret access key for an S3-compatible vendor, or the password. Leave it out, or send it empty, to keep the stored value.

access-token.description: An OAuth access token for vendors that use one. For `oracle`, the object storage namespace. Leave it out, or send it empty, to keep the stored value.

refresh-token.description: An OAuth refresh token for vendors that use one. Leave it out, or send it empty, to keep the stored value.

admin-email.description: The address notified when archiving to this service fails. Leave it out to keep the current value.

enabled.description: Whether recordings are archived to this service: `yes` archives to it, `no` keeps it configured but unused. Leave it out to keep the current value.

parameter.description: Free-form text stored with the service. Leave it out to keep the current value.

domain.description: Domain the quota belongs to. `*` is the platform default.

count-limit.description: Maximum number of recordings the domain can keep. `0` means unlimited.

size-limit.description: Maximum total size of the domain's recordings, in kilobytes. `0` means unlimited.

time-limit.description: Maximum total length of the domain's recordings, in seconds. `0` means unlimited.

age-limit.description: Number of days a recording is kept before it can be removed. `0` means unlimited.

quota-server.description: Read-only. Hostname of the Recording server this copy of the quota was read from.

quota-in-sync.description: Read-only. Whether the Recording servers agree about this domain's quota. `yes` means every Recording server answered, there are at least 2, and they all hold the same limits. `no` means two of them hold different limits, or the quota is missing from some of them. `unknown` means not every Recording server was asked or answered, which is normal with one Recording server, with `local-only=yes`, and on the domain and reseller paths.

quota-servers-reporting.description: Read-only. Number of Recording servers that answered this request.

quota-servers-expected.description: Read-only. Number of Recording servers on the platform. Fewer reporting than expected makes `quota-in-sync` `unknown`, unless a difference is already visible.

Quota.description: A recording quota for one domain, as stored on one Recording server. A domain without a quota of its own uses the platform default, returned with `domain` set to `*`. `count-limit` is a number of recordings, `size-limit` is in kilobytes, `time-limit` is in seconds, and `age-limit` is in days. `0` means unlimited.

count-limit.description: Maximum number of recordings the domain can keep. `0` means unlimited.

size-limit.description: Maximum total size of the domain's recordings, in kilobytes. `0` means unlimited.

time-limit.description: Maximum total length of the domain's recordings, in seconds. `0` means unlimited.

age-limit.description: Number of days a recording is kept before it can be removed. `0` means unlimited.

QuotaWrite.description: Limits to set on a recording quota. Every field is optional on update; a limit you leave out keeps its value. Each is a whole number of 0 or more, and `0` means unlimited.

code.description: HTTP status code of the response.

message.description: Short status text, such as `Accepted`.
What went wrong.

LicfErrorResponse.description: Error returned by a recording-server endpoint.

ProcessR.description: One process on one server. A process is identified by `process-element-id` and `process-hostname`. Every field is a string; a value the server did not report is an empty string. `process-start-time` and `process-status-update-time` are returned as each server reported them, as text such as `Tue, 06 Oct 2026 09:15:41 GMT`. They are not RFC 3339 date-times.

process-element-id.description: The process identifier, such as `sipbx`, `ncs`, `nfr`, or `sbus` on a core server, or `licf` and `nmc` on a recording server. With `process-hostname`, it identifies the row.

process-application.description: The application the process belongs to. When the server reports none, this is the `process-element-type` value.

process-element-type.description: The type of the process, as the server reports it.

process-element-version.description: The software version, as text. It is never converted to a number.

process-status.description: The status the server reports for the process, such as `Running`.

process-start-time.description: When the process last started, as the server reported it. Text such as `Tue, 01 Sep 2026 14:30:14 GMT`, not an RFC 3339 date-time.

process-status-update-time.description: When the server last reported the process. Text such as `Tue, 06 Oct 2026 09:15:41 GMT`, not an RFC 3339 date-time. Sorting by it orders the text, not the time, so parse it to compare times.

process-hostname.description: The hostname of the server the process runs on. With `process-element-id`, it identifies the row.

process-ip-address.description: The internal IP address of the server. Empty when not reported.

process-mac-address.description: The MAC address of the server. Empty when not reported, as for `sbus`.

process-app-address.description: The address and port the process listens on, as `ip:port`. Empty when not reported.

process-app-address-v6.description: The IPv6 address and port the process listens on, as `[ipv6]:port`. Empty when not reported.

process-wan-address.description: The public address and port of the process, as `ip:port`. Empty when not reported.

process-subnet-mask.description: The subnet mask of the server's interface. Empty when not reported.

process-domain-db.description: The `domain_db` value the server reports. Empty when not reported.

total.description: Number of rows matching the request's filters.

domain.description: Domain to set the quota for, such as `example.com`. `default` or `*` sets the platform default, which requires Super User scope and is refused under a reseller.

QuotaCreate.description: Body of a request that sets a recording quota on a collection path, which has no domain in the URL. Carries `domain` and the limits to set.

DeviceListItem.title: DeviceListItem
DeviceListItem.description: Short view of a device, returned by the `/list` suffix: identity, owner, and registration state. It carries no provisioning fields and no credentials.

device.description: Device name, such as `1001a`: the user part of `device-sip-registration-uri`.

device-sip-registration-uri.description: SIP address the device registers as: `sip:<device>@<domain>`.

user.description: User who owns the device, such as `1001`. `domain` for a device no user owns.

domain.description: Domain the device belongs to.

device-sip-registration-user-agent.description: User agent of the device's last registration. `null` when it has never registered.

device-sip-registration-state.description: `registered` while the device's last registration has not expired, allowing about 2 minutes of grace. Otherwise `unregistered`.

code.description: HTTP status code of the response, repeated in the body.

message.description: Why the request failed. Read it for troubleshooting; it is not a stable value to match on.

ErrorResponse.description: Error body returned with every 4xx and 5xx status. The same text is also sent in the `Warning` response header.

code.description: HTTP status code of the response: `200` or `202`.

message.description: `Success` for `200`, `Accepted` for `202`.

warnings.description: Present only when the request was accepted but stored differently from what was sent, for example a value normalized to a supported range. Each entry is also sent as a `Warning: 299` header

SuccessResponse.description: Body returned by a write that has no resource to return. A `202` means the change was accepted and is applied shortly after.

PhonenumberListItem.title: PhonenumberListItem
PhonenumberListItem.description: One row of `GET /domains/{domain}/phonenumbers/list`. An SMS-only number carries only `phonenumber` and `domain`.

phonenumber.description: The phone number, digits with the country code, for example `15555550123`. 7 to 249 characters, and 16 at most when the number has an SMS assignment. The API stores it exactly as sent and does not convert it to E.164, so use the same form everywhere.

domain.description: The domain the number is assigned to.

dial-rule-description.description: The note on the number. Absent on an SMS-only row.

dial-rule-translation-destination-user.description: Where calls to the number go. `[*]` on an available number. Absent on an SMS-only row.

DialruleListItem.title: DialruleListItem
DialruleListItem.description: The reduced dial rule returned by `/dialrules/list`: the fields that identify a rule, without its full routing.

dial-rule-description.description: Free-text description of the rule

dial-rule-dial-plan.description: Name of the dial plan the rule belongs to

domain.description: Domain that owns the dial plan

DialpolicyListItem.title: DialpolicyListItem
DialpolicyListItem.description: The reduced dial policy returned by `/dialpolicy/list` and `/domains/{domain}/dialpolicy/list`.

dialpolicy.description: Name of the dial policy. Use it as `{policy}` in `/domains/{domain}/dialpolicy/{policy}`.

domain.description: Domain the policy is filed under. `*` or `admin-only` for a shared policy

description.description: Free-text description of the policy

PermissionListItem.title: PermissionListItem
PermissionListItem.description: The reduced dial policy rule returned by `/permission/list`.

permission-id.description: Rule identifier: the base64url encoding of `permission-match`, without `=` padding

dialpolicy.description: Name of the policy the rule belongs to

permission-mode.description: `permit` allows a matching call; `deny` blocks it

domain.description: Domain the rule is filed under, or `*` or `admin-only` for a shared policy

ConnectionListItem.title: ConnectionListItem
ConnectionListItem.description: The reduced connection that `/list` returns: identity fields only.

domain.description: Domain that owns the connection.

connection-connectivity-type.description: How the connection reaches the platform: `header_ip_match`, `inbound_registration`, `outbound_registration`, or `route_profile`.

connection-usage-role.description: The connection's role, such as `customer` or `vendor`.

connection-id.description: Key for the keyed connection paths: base64url, without padding, of `connection-orig-match-pattern`.

schedule-name.description: Schedule name, unique across the platform

domain.description: Domain whose calls are exported. `*` covers every domain of `reseller`, or the whole platform when `reseller` is also `*`.

reseller.description: Territory that owns the schedule. A domain schedule carries the territory that owns its domain. `*` with `domain` `*` is a platform-wide schedule.

user.description: Extension the export is limited to. Empty exports every user in `domain`.

email.description: Where the export or its notification is emailed

schedule-user-export-scope.description: Scope of whoever created the schedule. Set by the API and read-only. When it is `Office Manager`, calls marked private are anonymized in the export.

data-lookup-window.description: Length of the export window: calls that ended in the last window before each run are exported

schedule-preset.description: Recurrence preset. `Daily`, `Weekly`, and `Monthly` fix the window and repeat interval. `Custom` uses `data-lookup-window` and `schedule-repeat-interval` as stored.

schedule-start-time.description: Time of day for `Daily` and `Weekly` runs, as `HH:MM` in `time-zone`

time-zone.description: IANA time zone the start time and first run were given in, such as `America/New_York`

schedule-monthly-day-of-month.description: Day of the month for a `Monthly` schedule, as sent

schedule-weekly-day-of-week.description: Day of the week for a `Weekly` schedule, such as `Monday`

schedule-repeat-interval.description: Time added to both window ends after each run, such as `1 Day`, `4 hours`, or `1 Month`. `No Repeat` runs once.

schedule-next-run-datetime.description: End of the next export window and the time of the next run, in UTC. Empty for a finished `No Repeat` schedule.

schedule-last-run-datetime.description: Start of the next export window, in UTC. It is one `data-lookup-window` before `schedule-next-run-datetime`, not the time of the last run.

schedule-status.description: `waiting` until due, `processing` while a server exports it, and `completed` once a `No Repeat` schedule has run

schedule-core-server.description: Server that last claimed the schedule

schedule-processing-start-datetime.description: When the current run started, in UTC

schedule-kill-datetime.description: When another server may take over a run that has stalled, in UTC

schedule-previous-export-datetime.description: When the previous export was written, in UTC

schedule-attempt-count.description: Export attempts in the current run. Reset to `0` after a successful run.

schedule-error-info.description: Why the last scheduled export failed, as `<utc timestamp> <export method>: <message> (<n> attempts)`. Cleared on the next successful run. Written by the export service and ignored on a create or update.
schedule-error-info.example: 2026-09-01 14:30:00 sftp: Timeout while connecting to server (3 attempts)

schedule-error-backoff-datetime.description: When the failed export window may be retried, in UTC. While set, the schedule waits and the same window is replayed rather than skipped. Cleared on the next successful run. Written by the export service and ignored on a create or update.

export-method.description: How the file is delivered. `email` attaches it, `ftp upload` and `sftp` upload it to `export-hostname`, `backup locally` keeps it on the server that ran it, and `do nothing` writes it and delivers nothing. Older schedules can still show `scp copy`, which the export service never ran and the API now refuses.

export-cdr-format.description: CSV layout. `Advanced` is the short layout of 13 columns. `Standard` is the full layout with every CDR column.

export-include-headers-enabled.description: Whether the CSV starts with a header row. Stored as sent. Send lowercase `yes` or `no`: the export service compares against lowercase `yes`.

export-inbound-calls-enabled.description: Whether inbound calls are exported. Stored as sent. Send lowercase `yes` or `no`: the export service compares against lowercase `yes`.

export-outbound-calls-enabled.description: Whether outbound calls are exported. Stored as sent. Send lowercase `yes` or `no`: the export service compares against lowercase `yes`.

export-offnet-calls-enabled.description: Whether off-net calls are exported. Stored as sent. Send lowercase `yes` or `no`: the export service compares against lowercase `yes`.

export-notify-email-enabled.description: Whether `email` is sent a notice after an upload. Always `yes` when `export-method` is `email`.

export-hostname.description: Host for `ftp upload` or `sftp`, with an optional `:port`. The port defaults to `22` for `sftp`.

export-password.description: Password for `ftp upload` or `sftp`, masked: values of 8 characters or fewer are all `*`, longer ones keep their first 2 and last 2 characters. Super User can send `include-secrets=yes` for the plain text.

export-remote-path.description: Directory on the remote host. A trailing `/` is added when missing.

export-last-sequence-number.description: Stored for older clients. The export service does not use it.

post-export-script-enabled.description: Stored for older clients. The export service does not run a script.

post-export-script-path.description: Stored for older clients. `n/a` when unset.

language-token.description: Language of the notification email, such as `en_us`

schedule-run-immediately.description: `yes` while a run-now request is pending

CdrSchedule.description: A CDR export schedule: which calls to export, how often, and where to deliver the file. Returned by the schedule reads. Fields that are empty in the database are left out of the response.

schedule-name.description: Schedule name. Must be unique across the whole platform: a name already in use returns `409`. Letters, digits, spaces, `.`, `-`, `_`, and `'` only, 127 characters at most, or the create returns `400`.

domain.description: Domain whose calls are exported. `*`, or leaving it out on `POST /schedule` or `POST /resellers/{reseller}/schedule`, covers every domain of `reseller`. Ignored on the domain paths, where the path sets it.

reseller.description: Territory that owns the schedule. Leave it out: the API fills in the territory that owns `domain`, or the path territory on the reseller paths. A territory that does not own `domain` returns `400`. `*` with `domain` `*` is a platform-wide schedule.

user.description: Extension to limit the export to. Leave it out to export every user in `domain`. A scope limited to its own schedules always gets its own extension, and naming another returns `403`.

schedule-preset.description: Recurrence preset. Required. `Daily`, `Weekly`, and `Monthly` set `data-lookup-window` and `schedule-repeat-interval` for you. `Custom` needs `time-zone`, `data-lookup-window`, and `schedule-repeat-interval`.

data-lookup-window.description: Length of the export window. Required unless `schedule-preset` is `Daily`, `Weekly`, or `Monthly`, which set it to `1 day`, `1 week`, or `1 month`.

schedule-next-run-datetime.description: First run, in RFC 3339 (`2026-09-02T09:00:00-04:00` or `...Z`) or as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` read in `time-zone` (UTC when there is none). Stored in UTC. With `Daily`, `Weekly`, or `Monthly` and a `time-zone`, only the date is used: the time comes from `schedule-start-time`, or is midnight for `Monthly`. Leave it out to start now. An unparseable value returns `400`.

time-zone.description: IANA time zone name, such as `America/New_York`. Required for `Custom`. An unknown name returns `400`.

schedule-start-time.description: Time of day as `HH:MM` in `time-zone`. Required for `Weekly`, and used by `Daily` when `time-zone` is set. A value that is not a time returns `400`.

schedule-monthly-day-of-month.description: Day of the month, `1` to `31`. Required for `Monthly`. The API stores it without checking the range.

schedule-weekly-day-of-week.description: Day of the week, such as `Monday`. Required for `Weekly`.

schedule-repeat-interval.description: Time between runs, such as `1 hour`, `1 Day`, or `1 Month`. `No Repeat` runs once. Set by the `Daily`, `Weekly`, and `Monthly` presets. Defaults to `1 day`.

export-method.description: How the file is delivered. `email` attaches it (9 MB or smaller; larger files get a download link), `ftp upload` and `sftp` upload it, `backup locally` keeps it on the server that ran it, and `do nothing` delivers nothing. `scp copy` returns `400`.

email.description: Where the export or its notification is emailed. Required in practice when `export-method` is `email`.

export-notify-email-enabled.description: Send `yes` to have `email` notified after an upload. Defaults to `no`, and is always `yes` when `export-method` is `email`.

export-offnet-calls-enabled.description: Whether off-net calls are exported. Defaults to `No`. Stored as sent. Send lowercase `yes` or `no`: the export service compares against lowercase `yes`.

export-inbound-calls-enabled.description: Whether inbound calls are exported. Defaults to `No`. Stored as sent. Send lowercase `yes` or `no`: the export service compares against lowercase `yes`.

export-outbound-calls-enabled.description: Whether outbound calls are exported. Defaults to `No`. Stored as sent. Send lowercase `yes` or `no`: the export service compares against lowercase `yes`.

export-include-headers-enabled.description: Whether the CSV starts with a header row. Defaults to `No`. Stored as sent. Send lowercase `yes` or `no`: the export service compares against lowercase `yes`.

export-cdr-format.description: CSV layout. Defaults to `Advanced`, the short layout of 13 columns. `Standard` is the full layout.

export-hostname.description: Host for `ftp upload` or `sftp`, with an optional `:port`. Required for those methods.

export-username.description: Login for `ftp upload` or `sftp`. Required for those methods.

export-password.description: Password for `ftp upload` or `sftp`. Stored in plain text and masked on read. A value that looks masked returns `400` on create.

export-remote-path.description: Directory on the remote host. Defaults to empty.

export-last-sequence-number.description: Stored for older clients. The export service does not use it.

post-export-script-enabled.description: Stored for older clients. The export service does not run a script. Defaults to `No`.

post-export-script-path.description: Stored for older clients. Defaults to `n/a`.

schedule-user-export-scope.description: Read-only. Ignored if sent: the API records your scope on create and never changes it on update.

schedule-status.description: Leave it out. Defaults to `waiting`, and the export service manages it after that.

schedule-run-immediately.description: Send `yes` to run the schedule now, over the window that ends now, without moving its regular times.

language-token.description: Language of the notification email, such as `en_us`. Defaults to `en_us` when empty.

CdrScheduleInput.description: Body of a schedule create. `schedule-name`, `schedule-preset`, and `export-method` are required.

schedule-name.description: Ignored: the path names the schedule, and a schedule cannot be renamed.

domain.description: Leave it out. On `PUT /schedule/{schedule_name}` and the reseller form it must equal the schedule's domain, or the update returns `404`. On the domain form the path sets it.

reseller.description: Leave it out. On the reseller form it must equal the path territory. An older schedule stored with `*` is given its domain's territory on update.

user.description: Extension to limit the export to. A scope limited to its own schedules cannot name another extension: that returns `403`.

schedule-preset.description: Recurrence preset. Send one: a schedule without a preset is never run. `Daily`, `Weekly`, and `Monthly` set `data-lookup-window` and `schedule-repeat-interval` for you. `Custom` needs `time-zone`, `data-lookup-window`, and `schedule-repeat-interval`.

data-lookup-window.description: New window length. Ignored when `schedule-preset` is `Daily`, `Weekly`, or `Monthly`, which set it.

schedule-next-run-datetime.description: New next run, in RFC 3339 or as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` read in `time-zone` (UTC when there is none). Stored in UTC. `schedule-last-run-datetime` is reset to one `data-lookup-window` earlier. An unparseable value returns `400`.

time-zone.description: IANA time zone name, such as `America/New_York`. Required for `Custom`. An unknown name returns `400`.

schedule-start-time.description: Time of day as `HH:MM` in `time-zone`. Required for `Weekly`, and used by `Daily` when `time-zone` is set. A value that is not a time returns `400`.

schedule-monthly-day-of-month.description: Day of the month, `1` to `31`. Required for `Monthly`. The API stores it without checking the range.

schedule-weekly-day-of-week.description: Day of the week, such as `Monday`. Required for `Weekly`.

schedule-repeat-interval.description: Time between runs, such as `1 hour`, `1 Day`, or `1 Month`. `No Repeat` runs once. Set by the `Daily`, `Weekly`, and `Monthly` presets. Defaults to `1 day`.

export-method.description: How the file is delivered. `email` attaches it (9 MB or smaller; larger files get a download link), `ftp upload` and `sftp` upload it, `backup locally` keeps it on the server that ran it, and `do nothing` delivers nothing. `scp copy` returns `400`.

email.description: Where the export or its notification is emailed. Required in practice when `export-method` is `email`.

export-notify-email-enabled.description: Send `yes` to have `email` notified after an upload. Defaults to `no`, and is always `yes` when `export-method` is `email`.

export-offnet-calls-enabled.description: Whether off-net calls are exported. Defaults to `No`. Stored as sent. Send lowercase `yes` or `no`: the export service compares against lowercase `yes`.

export-inbound-calls-enabled.description: Whether inbound calls are exported. Defaults to `No`. Stored as sent. Send lowercase `yes` or `no`: the export service compares against lowercase `yes`.

export-outbound-calls-enabled.description: Whether outbound calls are exported. Defaults to `No`. Stored as sent. Send lowercase `yes` or `no`: the export service compares against lowercase `yes`.

export-include-headers-enabled.description: Whether the CSV starts with a header row. Defaults to `No`. Stored as sent. Send lowercase `yes` or `no`: the export service compares against lowercase `yes`.

export-cdr-format.description: CSV layout. Defaults to `Advanced`, the short layout of 13 columns. `Standard` is the full layout.

export-hostname.description: Host for `ftp upload` or `sftp`, with an optional `:port`. Required for those methods.

export-username.description: Login for `ftp upload` or `sftp`. Required for those methods.

export-password.description: Password for `ftp upload` or `sftp`. Stored in plain text and masked on read. A value that looks masked returns `400`, except the exact mask a read returned for this schedule, which keeps the stored password.

export-remote-path.description: Directory on the remote host. Defaults to empty.

export-last-sequence-number.description: Stored for older clients. The export service does not use it.

post-export-script-enabled.description: Stored for older clients. The export service does not run a script. Defaults to `No`.

post-export-script-path.description: Stored for older clients. Defaults to `n/a`.

schedule-user-export-scope.description: Read-only. Ignored if sent: the API records your scope on create and never changes it on update.

schedule-status.description: Leave it out. Defaults to `waiting`, and the export service manages it after that.

schedule-run-immediately.description: Send `yes` to run the schedule now, over the window that ends now, without moving its regular times.

language-token.description: Language of the notification email, such as `en_us`. Defaults to `en_us` when empty.

CdrScheduleUpdate.description: Body of a schedule update. Every field is optional: send only what changes.

RecordingentryWrite.description: Recording entry create, update, and delete body. The interception fields are set by the server and are not accepted here.

device-aor.description:
Address of record to record. Use one of these forms:

- `user@domain` for a user or call queue, such as `1001@example.com`
- `sip:device@domain` for a device, such as `sip:1001wp@example.com`
- `*@domain` for every call in the domain, such as `*@example.com`

`*` is allowed only as the whole part before the `@`. These return `400`: an empty value, a bare `*`, `*@`, a partial wildcard such as `10*@example.com`, and any `*` after the `@`.

case-id.description: Case ID that identifies the entry on its recording server. Defaults to `device-aor`. A blank value is the same as leaving it out.

recording-server-id.description: Write to this recording server only. Leave it out, or send `*`, to write to every recording server. On a create or update, a recording server that does not exist returns `404`. A delete accepts one that no longer exists, to remove the entries it left behind.

transcription.description: Whether recordings for this entry are transcribed: `yes` or `no`. An unrecognized value returns `400`. Leave it out to keep the current value.

sentiment.description: Whether recordings for this entry get sentiment analysis: `yes` or `no`. An unrecognized value returns `400`. Leave it out to keep the current value.

Department.description: A department, with its member count. The fields use the spellings a user carries, so a department read and a user read agree.

department.description: Department name, and the key in `/domains/{domain}/departments/{department}`. It is the value of a user's own `department` field. Always a string, even when it is all digits.

domain.description: Domain the department belongs to

count-users-total.description: Users filed under the department. It does not count the department's own row, call queues, sites, or other system extensions. `0` for a declared department with no users.

SubscriptionListItem.title: SubscriptionListItem
SubscriptionListItem.description: The reduced event subscription returned by `/subscriptions/list`: what it sends and where to.

id.description: Subscription identifier, and the key in `/subscriptions/{id}`

model.description: Kind of event the subscription sends. See `Subscription.model`.

post-url.description: URL each batch of events is sent to. Masked like `Subscription.post-url` when you cannot change the subscription.

domain.description: Domain whose events are sent, or `*` for every domain

user.description: User whose events are sent, or `*` for every user in the domain

status.description: Delivery state: `pending`, `active`, or `error`

domain.description: Domain of the time frame.

user.description: Owner: `*` for a domain (shared) time frame, or the user, such as `1001`. Empty when the owner is not recorded.

selected.description: `yes` when an answer rule of the owner uses the time frame, otherwise `no`.

expired.description: `yes` when every time range of the time frame ended before today. Always `no` when `selected` is `yes`.

ContactListItem.title: ContactListItem
ContactListItem.description: The reduced contact returned by `/contacts/list`: identity, name, and where it is filed.

unique-id.description: The contact's ID. A directory row has none unless a personal contact was merged into it

company.description: The company or organization the contact belongs to

domain.description: Domain of the address book the contact is in

user.description: Extension of an on-net contact. Present only on directory rows from `includeDomain=yes`; personal and shared contacts have none

AgentListItem.title: AgentListItem
AgentListItem.description: The reduced call queue agent entry returned by `/agents/list`: who the agent is, the queue, and the user behind it.

callqueue-agent-id.description: The agent: `user@domain` for a user agent, or `sip:` and the device address for a device agent. The key used to address the agent

callqueue.description: Extension of the queue this entry is on. On `GET /domains/{domain}/agents/list`, the first of the agent's queues

domain.description: Domain of the queue

callqueue-agent-dispatch-queue-priority-.description: Priority of this queue among the agent's queues. Lower is offered first

name-full-name.description: Full name of the user behind the agent. `Offnet Agent` for an offnet agent

site.description: Site of the user behind the agent

agent-department.description: Department of the user behind the agent

callqueue-agent-availability-for-dispatc.description: The platform's live dispatch state for the agent, such as `available`

domain.description: The domain the answer is for.

preferred-server.description: The preferred server's name. `SiPbx` means any server, used when no preferred server is set.

preferred-server-source.description: Where `preferred-server` came from: the `domain`, `reseller`, or `system` setting, the `legacy` portal setting, or the platform `default`.

redundancy.description: The `provisioning.redundancy` setting in effect, in lowercase, such as `none`, `geography`, or `force primary`. `system default` when neither the setting nor the platform names one.

redundancy-group.description: The preferred server's geographic group. `null` when it has none, or when the preferred server is not one named server.

preferred-transport.description: The `provisioning.preferred-transport` setting, or the legacy portal setting when it holds a transport. `tls` when neither does.

preferred-transport-source.description: Where `preferred-transport` came from: the `domain`, `reseller`, or `system` setting, the `legacy` portal setting, or `default` when neither held a transport.

srv.description: DNS SRV names and records of each server group. Omitted when no server in the list has SRV names.

preferred-srv.description: The `srv` entry to use: the `preferred-transport` name of the first server in `servers` that has SRV names. Returned even when its `records` are empty. `null` when no server has SRV names.

servers.description: The servers in the order to try them. Empty when the preferred server does not exist.

SipServers.description: Where a domain's SIP clients connect, and in what order.

name.description: The server name.

hostname.description: The server's fully qualified domain name.

priority.description: Position in the failover order, starting at `1`. Try `1` first.

weight.description: `100` for the first server, `90` for the second, and so on, down to `0`.

wss-uri.description: WebSocket URI for a web phone, on the platform's WebSocket port (`9002` unless configured otherwise).

sip-port.description: SIP UDP port. `null` when not set.

sip-port-tcp.description: SIP TCP port. `null` when not set.

sip-port-tls.description: SIP TLS port. `null` when not set.

location.description: Free-text site label. `null` when not set.

backup-allowed.description: Whether the server may be used as a backup. Only the preferred server can be `no` in this list.

status.description: The status the Endpoints server last recorded for this server. `null` when not set.

SipServer.description: One SIP server in the failover order.

name.description: SRV record name, built from the server's `postfix`.

transport.description: The transport the SRV name is for.

records.description: The resolved records, lowest priority first, then highest weight. Empty when the name does not resolve.

target.description: Host name the record points to.

priority.description: SRV priority. Lower is tried first.

weight.description: SRV weight among records of equal priority. Higher is chosen more often.

SipServerSrv.description: One DNS SRV name for a server group and transport, with its resolved records.

DefaultC.description: Body of a default create: the row's key and its value.

default-object.description: Object the default applies to: `domain`, `user`, `device`, or `*` for any of them. Stored lowercase

default-field.description: v2 field the default sets, as `GET /defaults/objects/{object}/fields` lists it. Credentials, `scope`, and key fields are refused

reseller.description: Territory the row applies to, or `*`. Defaults to `*`. On `/resellers/{reseller}/defaults` the path wins

domain.description: Domain the row applies to, or `*`. Defaults to `*`. On `/domains/{domain}/defaults` the path wins

default-value.description: Value filled into the field, up to 255 characters. A number is stored as its string form; any other non-string returns `400`

DefaultU.description: Body of a default update: the key of the row to change and its new value.

default-object.description: Object of the row to change: `domain`, `user`, `device`, or `*`. Left out means `*`

default-field.description: v2 field of the row to change. Must be a catalog field of the object

reseller.description: Territory of the row to change, or `*`. Left out means `*`. On `/resellers/{reseller}/defaults` the path wins

domain.description: Domain of the row to change, or `*`. Left out means `*`. On `/domains/{domain}/defaults` the path wins

default-value.description: New value, up to 255 characters. Left out, only the row's `updated-datetime` changes. `created-datetime` can't be set

DefaultListItem.title: DefaultListItem
DefaultListItem.description: A default reduced to its key, as the `/list` suffix returns it. The value is on the full read.

default-object.description: Object the default applies to, or `*` for any

domain.description: Domain the row applies to, or `*`

reseller.description: Territory the row applies to, or `*`

default-object.description: API object the default applies to ('*' = any)

default-field.description: v2 API field name the default sets

reseller.description: Reseller scope ('*' = global)

domain.description: Domain scope ('*' = global)

created.description: Unix timestamp the row was created

updated.description: Unix timestamp the row was last updated

NmsConfig.description: One configuration entry as held by one core server.

config-name.description: The configuration key.

config-value.description: The stored value, exactly as stored. Masked when the key looks like a credential, unless `include-secrets=yes` was accepted.

config-timestamp-datetime.description: When this server last wrote the entry.

config-server.description: The core server this row came from.

config-in-sync.description: Whether the servers agree on this key: `yes` (every expected server answered and all agree), `no` (they differ, visibly in this response), `unknown` (agreement cannot be shown), or `not-expected` (a per-server key listed in `NsNmsconfigPerServer`).

config-servers-reporting.description: How many servers' rows are in this response. On every row, because a list is a bare array.

config-servers-expected.description: How many core servers the inventory holds. When it exceeds `config-servers-reporting`, a server did not answer and no `yes` is given.

config-name.description: The key: letters, digits, `.`, `_`, and `-`.

config-value.description: The value. A credential-shaped key with a mask-shaped value returns `400`.

config-geo.description: The geo flag. Defaults to the column default.

config-server.description: Writes this core server only, with nothing published. Leave it out, or send `*`, `all`, `any`, or `geo`, to replicate to every server.

config-value.description: The new value. A mask sent back is dropped from the write, so every server keeps its stored value.

config-server.description: Writes this core server only, with nothing published.

NmsConfigListItem.description: The `/list` projection: key and server, no value.

config-name.description: The configuration key.

config-server.description: The core server this row came from.

config-in-sync.description: Whether the servers agree on this key; see `NmsConfig`.

config-server-local.description: `yes` on the server that took this request.

config-server-reachable.description: `no` when the server is in the inventory but did not answer.

config-server-config-count.description: Entries the server holds. `null`, not `0`, when it did not answer.

config-server-out-of-sync-count.description: The server's keys whose `config-in-sync` is `no`. `not-expected` and `unknown` keys are left out. `null` when the server did not answer.

total.description: Matching entries on the server that took the request.

NmsConfigVerify.description: What one core server reports after a write with `synchronous=yes`.

config-name.description: The key written.

config-applied.description: `yes`: the server holds the written value, or for a delete no longer holds the key. `no`: it answered but does not hold it yet; this means not seen yet, never rejected. `unknown`: the server did not answer.

message.description: `Accepted`.
What went wrong.

AnswerruleListItem.title: AnswerruleListItem
AnswerruleListItem.description: The reduced answer rule returned by `/answerrules/list`.

time-frame.description: Time frame of the rule, and the key used to address it. `*` is the default rule

user.description: User the rule belongs to. `*` marks a rule that applies to every user in the domain

domain.description: Domain of the user

ordinal-priority.description: Position of the rule in the order rules are checked. Lower is checked first

enabled.description: Whether the rule is used at all. `yes` or `no`

Park.description: A call park: an extension that holds calls until someone retrieves them, and its label. A park has none of a call queue's dispatch settings or agents.

park.description: Extension of the call park. Callers dial it to park and retrieve calls, and it is the park's key in paths.

description.description: Label of the park, shown in the portal. Defaults to the extension.

domain.description: Domain the park belongs to.

site.description: Site the park is filed under, or `""` for none. Always `""` on `GET /parks`, which spans domains.

department.description: Department the park is filed under, or `""` for none. Always `""` on `GET /parks`.

parked-calls-total-current.description: Number of calls parked on this extension right now. Always `0` on `GET /parks`, which does not look up live calls.

ParkListItem.title: ParkListItem
ParkListItem.description: The reduced call park returned by `GET /domains/{domain}/parks/list`: identity and filing, without the live call count.

park.description: Extension of the call park, and its key in paths.

description.description: Label of the park.

domain.description: Domain the park belongs to.

site.description: Site the park is filed under, or `""` for none.

department.description: Department the park is filed under, or `""` for none.

park.description: Extension of the new park. Letters, digits, `.`, `-`, and `_` only, so the park can be addressed by path. `all`, `list`, and `count` are reserved. An extension already used by a call queue, a call park, or a user returns `409`.

description.description: Label of the park. Also names the park's system user. Defaults to the extension.

domain.description: Domain to create the park in. Required on `POST /parks`. On `POST /domains/{domain}/parks` the path names the domain, and this field is ignored.

site.description: Site to file the park under. For a Site Manager, left out means its own site, and any other site returns `403`.

department.description: Department to file the park under.

synchronous.description: `yes` waits up to 2 seconds for the park to be created and answers `200` with it. If it is not there in time, the answer is `202` as for `no`. `no`, the default, answers `202` as soon as the request is accepted. Send it in the body or the query string.

ParkWrite.description: Body of a request that creates a call park.

SpeechWordR.description: A speech word: a short recorded prompt the platform plays, such as a number or a menu phrase. A system speech word (`domain` `*`) applies to every domain; a domain can override it. Writes return the stored fields only; `recorded`, `file-size`, `recorded-datetime`, `inherited`, and `media-path` come with reads.

filename.description: Name of the speech word, without the `.wav` extension.

domain.description: Domain the row belongs to. `*` for a system speech word.

language.description: Language of the speech word, such as `en_us` or `fr_ca`.

script.description: Words the audio says. Rendering speaks this text. No practical length limit.

voice-engine.description: Voice type that recorded the audio, as the text-to-speech service names it, or `upload` for uploaded audio. Empty for audio shipped with the platform.

voice-id.description: Id or name of the text-to-speech voice. Empty until the speech word is rendered.

voice-language.description: Language of the text-to-speech voice, as a BCP 47 tag such as `en-US`. Rendering uses `en-US` when it is empty.

source-type.description: Where the audio came from: `default` (shipped with the platform, or not recorded yet), `tts` (rendered with text to speech), or `upload` (uploaded).

content-hash.description: Fingerprint of the recorded audio: of the text, voice, and silence that rendered it, or of the uploaded file. Rendering is skipped while the stored values still match it. Empty until the speech word is rendered or uploaded.

created-datetime.description: When the row was created. Empty for speech words shipped with the platform.

updated-datetime.description: When the row last changed. Empty for speech words shipped with the platform.

pre-silence-ms.description: Silence before the words, in milliseconds. Defaults to `500`.

post-silence-ms.description: Silence after the words, in milliseconds. Defaults to `200`.

recorded.description: Read only. Whether this row's own audio file exists. A domain override that is not recorded yet is `false` while the domain still plays the system audio.

file-size.description: Read only. Size of the audio file in bytes. `0` when not recorded.

recorded-datetime.description: Read only. When the audio file was last written. Empty when not recorded.

inherited.description: Read only. `true` when a domain read answers with the system speech word because the domain has no override. Always `false` on system reads.

media-path.description: Read only. Signed link, relative to the API host, that plays the audio with no access token. Expires after one day by default. See the `/play` endpoints.

SpeechWordU.description: Body that creates or changes a speech word. Fields you leave out keep their stored value, or take the system speech word's value on a new override.

script.description: Words the audio should say. Required only when the speech word is new and has no system speech word to take them from. No practical length limit.

language.description: Language of the speech word, such as `en_us` or `fr_ca`. Defaults to `en_us`.

voice-engine.description: Voice type, as the text-to-speech service names it. Rendering fills it in when empty.

voice-id.description: Id or name of the text-to-speech voice, such as `en-US-Wavenet-C`. List voices with `GET /domains/{domain}/users/{user}/voices/{language}`.

voice-language.description: Language of the voice, as a BCP 47 tag such as `en-US`.

pre-silence-ms.description: Silence before the words, in milliseconds, added when the speech word is rendered. Defaults to `500`.

post-silence-ms.description: Silence after the words, in milliseconds, added when the speech word is rendered. Defaults to `200`.

SpeechWordRender.description: Body of a single render. Every field is optional; a field you leave out uses the stored value. The values used are stored with the new audio.

script.description: Words to speak instead of the stored text. Stored as the new text. No practical length limit.

language.description: Language of the speech word, such as `en_us` or `fr_ca`. Defaults to `en_us`.

voice-id.description: Id or name of the voice to use, such as `en-US-Wavenet-C`. When the language has no such voice, its first voice is used.

voice-engine.description: Voice type to store with the audio. Taken from the voice when empty.

voice-language.description: Language of the voice, as a BCP 47 tag such as `en-US`. Defaults to the stored value, then `en-US`.

pre-silence-ms.description: Silence before the words, in milliseconds. Defaults to the stored value, then `500`.

post-silence-ms.description: Silence after the words, in milliseconds. Defaults to the stored value, then `200`.

SpeechWordUpload.description: JSON body of an audio upload: the audio as base64.

language.description: Language of the speech word, such as `en_us` or `fr_ca`. Defaults to `en_us`.

script.description: New text for the speech word, describing what the audio says. The stored text is kept when you leave it out.

file-base64.description: The audio file, base64-encoded. WAV, MP3, Ogg, or WebM.

file-encoding.description: Format of the audio in `file-base64`. Without it, MP3 is recognized by its header and anything else is read as WAV.

SpeechWordBulkRender.description: Body of a bulk render. Each speech word uses its own stored text and voice; a voice or silence field you send applies to every word in the list.

filenames.description: Names of the speech words to render, without `.wav`. Duplicates and blank names are ignored. An invalid name is reported as an error for that entry.

language.description: Language of the speech words, such as `en_us` or `fr_ca`. Defaults to `en_us`.

voice-id.description: Id or name of the voice to use for every word, such as `en-US-Wavenet-C`.

voice-engine.description: Voice type to store with every word. Taken from the voice when empty.

voice-language.description: Language of the voice for every word, as a BCP 47 tag such as `en-US`.

pre-silence-ms.description: Silence before the words, in milliseconds, for every word.

post-silence-ms.description: Silence after the words, in milliseconds, for every word.

SpeechWordBulkResult.description: Outcome of a bulk render: totals, and one entry per speech word in the order sent.

message.description: Always `Bulk re-record complete`.

skipped.description: Number of speech words whose recording was already current.

failed.description: Number of speech words that could not be recorded.

filename.description: Name of the speech word, as sent.

status.description: `rendered`: new audio was recorded. `skipped`: the recording was already current. `error`: see `reason`.

reason.description: Why the word was skipped (`up-to-date`) or failed, such as `No script to render for 'hour-99'.`, `Invalid filename`, or `Text-to-speech synthesis failed`. Absent on `rendered`.

content-hash.description: Fingerprint of the recording. Absent on `error`.

results.description: One entry per speech word, in the order sent.

SpeechwordListItem.title: SpeechwordListItem
SpeechwordListItem.description: A speech word as `/list` returns it: name, domain, and language only.

filename.description: Name of the speech word, without the `.wav` extension.

domain.description: Domain the row belongs to. `*` for a system speech word.

error.description: Why the service refused the request. Read it for troubleshooting; it is not a stable value to match on.

IpawareError.description: Error body from the IP rules service, passed through unchanged.

IpawareValidationError.description: Configuration change refused. Nothing was written.

cidr.description: The allowed address or CIDR range, normalized.

source.description: Where the entry comes from. `builtin` is the platform's own addresses. `local` is stored on this server only. `db` is this server's allow table. `url` is a remote list the server is set up to read. `vendor` is curated centrally. You can remove only `local` and `db` entries with this API.

comment.description: Note stored with the entry. For a `url` entry, the list it came from.

addedBy.description: Who added the entry. For an entry added through this API, the acting user and the credential, as `<user> key=<key id>`.

addedAt.description: When the entry was added, RFC 3339 in UTC, with a `Z` suffix. Not returned for `db` entries.

expiresAt.description: When the entry expires, RFC 3339 in UTC, with a `Z` suffix. `null` for a permanent entry.

country.description: Country of the address, as a 2-letter code, when known.

city.description: City of the address, when known.

domain.description: Domain from the address's reverse DNS name, when known.

vendor.description: `vendor` entries only. Who curates the entry.

IpawareAllowEntry.description: One allow-list entry. An address on the allow list is always allowed and never blocked by the firewall.

status.description: Allow-list status on this server: entry counts per source, whether the allow table is in use, when each source last synced, and the last sync error.

IpawareAllowedIpsList.description: The allow list on one server: its status, and every entry from every source.

IpawareAllowedIpAdd.description: Entry to add. Send the address as `cidr` or `ip`, as one value or an array. A single IPv4 or IPv6 address and a CIDR range are both accepted; match-all ranges such as `0.0.0.0/0` are refused.

oneOf.description: One address or CIDR range.
Several, up to the server's `api_batch_max` setting (100 unless changed).

cidr.description: Address or CIDR range to allow, or an array of them.

oneOf.description: One address or CIDR range.
Several, up to the server's `api_batch_max` setting (100 unless changed).

ip.description: Same as `cidr`. Used only when `cidr` is not sent.

comment.description: Note stored with the entry. Longer text is cut to 255 characters. Applies to every item of a batch.

ttl.description: Seconds until the entry expires. `0`, the default, makes it permanent. Applies to every item of a batch.

oneOf.description: One address or CIDR range.
Several, up to the server's `api_batch_max` setting (100 unless changed).

cidr.description: Address or CIDR range to remove, or an array of them.

oneOf.description: One address or CIDR range.
Several, up to the server's `api_batch_max` setting (100 unless changed).

ip.description: Same as `cidr`. Used only when `cidr` is not sent.

IpawareAllowedIpRemove.description: Entry to remove. Send the address as `cidr` or `ip`, as one value or an array. The address must match the entry as stored.
