status.description: `added` when the entry was stored, new or updated. `removed` when it was deleted. `not_found` when there was no such entry, which is still a `200`.

store.description: Where the entry is stored on this server: `db` for its allow table, `local` for its local file. Either way, the other servers in the cluster receive the change shortly after.

removed.description: Removals only. Whether an entry existed and was deleted.

IpawareAllowedIpMutationResult.description: Result of adding or removing one entry.

running.description: Value the service is running with.

file.description: Value in the configuration file, which applies after a restart.

IpawarePendingChange.description: A key whose value in the configuration file is not yet in effect.

path.description: Path of the configuration file on the server.

exists.description: Whether the configuration file exists. When `false`, every key is at its default.

config.description: Every key with the value the configuration file gives it, defaults included.

overrides.description: Only the keys set in the configuration file, with their values as written.

warnings.description: Problems found reading the file, such as an unknown key or an invalid value that fell back to its default.

pending.description: Keys whose file value is not yet in effect. Restart the service to apply them.

liveKeys.description: Keys a change puts into effect at once, without a restart.

replicableKeys.description: Keys a change also copies to the other servers in the cluster. A change to any other key applies to this server only.

replication.description: Cluster copy status: whether copying is on, and in `drift`, the servers whose values differ from this one.

IpawareConfigState.description: Configuration of the IP rules service on one server.

value.description: Value the configuration file gives the key, or its default when the file does not set it.

running.description: Value the service is running with.

source.description: `file` when the configuration file sets the key, `default` when it does not.

restartRequired.description: `true` when the file value is not yet in effect.

applyMode.description: How a change to this key takes effect: `live` at once, or `process_restart` after the service restarts. `component_restart` is reserved for keys applied by restarting one part of the service.

replicable.description: Whether a change to this key is also copied to the other servers in the cluster.

IpawareConfigKeyState.description: One configuration key on one server.

status.description: Always `updated`.

updated.description: Keys set by this request, with their values as stored.

removed.description: Keys this request reset to their defaults.

pending.description: Every key on this server whose file value is not yet in effect, including keys changed earlier by other requests.

restartRequired.description: `true` when at least one key in this request needs a restart to take effect.

effects.description: One entry per key in this request.

key.description: Configuration key name, as you sent it.

value.description: Value set. For a reset key, its default.

removed.description: Present and `true` for a key reset to its default.

effect.description: `live` when the value is already in effect, `restart` when it applies after a restart.

applied.description: Keys from this request already in effect.

IpawareConfigUpdateResult.description: Result of a configuration change. The file is written, and each key is reported as in effect or waiting for a restart.

IpawareStatusZ.description: Runtime status of the IP rules service on one server. The top-level fields below are stable; the objects inside them change between releases, so treat any field you do not recognize as information only.

requests.description: Requests the service has screened since it started.

decisions.description: Counters of allow and deny decisions.

cache.description: Decision cache size and hit counters.

cloud.description: Cloud scoring status. `null` when cloud scoring is not set up.

firewall.description: Firewall status, as in `GET /ipaware/{hostname}/firewall`. `null` when the firewall is not set up.

apiAuth.description: Counters of credential checks made by the service.

coreScan.description: Core scanner status, as in `GET /ipaware/{hostname}/core`. `null` on a server that does not scan.

ajpPool.description: Status of the service's backend connection pool.

memoryRssBytes.description: Memory the service is using, in bytes.

ip.description: Blocked address. Always a single IPv4 or IPv6 address.

reason.description: Why the address was blocked: the reason given by whoever blocked it by hand, or the detection that blocked it.

score.description: Risk score recorded with the block. `null` when none was given.

type.description: Request type recorded with the block. `null` when none was given.

addedAt.description: When the block was made, RFC 3339 in UTC, with a `Z` suffix.

expiresAt.description: When the block expires, RFC 3339 in UTC, with a `Z` suffix. `null` for a permanent block.

origin.description: `manual` for a block made by hand, on this server or another. Absent for an automatic block.

country.description: Country of the address, as a 2-letter code, when known.

city.description: City of the address, when known.

domain.description: Domain from the address's reverse DNS name, when known.

status.description: Firewall status. `enabled` is whether automatic blocking is on, `manualEnabled` whether blocking by hand is allowed, and `active` whether the firewall is running at all. `{"enabled": false}` on a server without one.

blocks.description: Every active block. Empty on a server without a firewall.

IpawareFirewallState.description: Firewall status and active blocks on one server.

oneOf.description: One IPv4 or IPv6 address.
Several, up to the server's `api_batch_max` setting (100 unless changed).

ip.description: Address to block, or an array of them.

reason.description: Why you are blocking the address, recorded with the block. Defaults to `manual`.

score.description: Risk score to record with the block. For information only.

type.description: Request type to record with the block. For information only.

ttl.description: Seconds until the block expires. Defaults to the server's `firewall_block_ttl` setting, 7 days unless changed. `0` makes the block permanent.

IpawareFirewallBlockRequest.description: Address to block. Send `ip` as one value or an array. Only single addresses can be blocked, not CIDR ranges.

oneOf.description: One IPv4 or IPv6 address.
Several, up to the server's `api_batch_max` setting (100 unless changed).

ip.description: Address to unblock, or an array of them.

reset.description: Also clear the address's scan history, so it is judged afresh. Defaults to `false`.

IpawareFirewallUnblockRequest.description: Address to unblock. Send `ip` as one value or an array.

IpawareFirewallOpResult.description: Result of blocking or unblocking one address.

status.description: What happened. `blocked`. `duplicate` when the address is already blocked. `skipped` when it is on the allow list or the never-block list, or is one of the platform's own addresses. `unblocked`. `not_blocked` when there was no block to remove.

cachePurged.description: Unblock only. Whether a cached refusal for the address was also cleared.

historyForgotten.description: Unblock only. Whether the address's scan history was cleared, which happens only with `reset`.

expiresAt.description: Block only, with `blocked`. When the block expires, RFC 3339 in UTC, with a `Z` suffix. `null` for a permanent block.

reason.description: Only with `skipped`, when the address is one of the platform's own.

PushListItem.title: PushListItem
PushListItem.description: A registered device as `/push/list` returns it. Never includes the token.

push-device.description: AOR of the device that gets the notifications, as `sip:<device>@<domain>`.

push-network.description: Push service the token belongs to: `firebase` (Firebase Cloud Messaging, Android), `apns` (Apple Push Notification service, iOS), `apns_chat` (an Apple token used for chat and messages only), or `pwa` (a web push subscription for a progressive web app).

domain.description: Domain of the user who owns the registration.

user.description: User (extension) who owns the registration.

UsersettingR.description: A user setting as it is read.

domain.description: Domain the user belongs to.

user.description: User the setting belongs to.

setting.description: Name of the setting, and the key used to address it.

updated-datetime.description: Read-only. When the setting was last created or changed, in RFC 3339 format.

UsersettingC.description: A user setting to create or update, named in the body.

setting.description: Name of the setting, such as `dashboard.timeWindow`. 1 to 191 characters: letters, digits, `.`, `-`, and `_`. Sending a name the user already has replaces that setting's value.

UsersettingU.description: The new value of a user setting named in the path.

UsersettingListItem.title: UsersettingListItem
UsersettingListItem.description: A user setting as `/settings/list` returns it: which settings exist, not their values.

domain.description: Domain the user belongs to.

user.description: User the setting belongs to.

setting.description: Name of the setting, and the key used to address it.

UsersettingValue.description: Value of the setting. Send a string, a number, a boolean, an object, or an array. An object, an array, or a boolean is returned as you sent it. Anything else, a number included, is stored and returned as a string, exactly as written: `42` reads back as `"42"` and `"0800"` as `"0800"`. A string that holds a JSON object or array, or the text `true` or `false`, is returned parsed. Up to 65,536 bytes, measured on the string or on the JSON text of an object, array, or boolean. `null` is not accepted.

ConferenceListItem.title: ConferenceListItem
ConferenceListItem.description: The reduced conference returned by `/conferences/list`: its address and name only.

conference-sip-uri.description: SIP address of the bridge, `sip:<conference>.<domain>@conference-bridge`. The part before the domain is the conference's `{conference}` key.

ParticipantListItem.title: ParticipantListItem
ParticipantListItem.description: The reduced participant returned by `/participants/list`: who is on the bridge.

participant_match.description: SIP address of the participant on the bridge.

name.description: Display name of the participant.

conference-participant-mode.description: Call state of the participant. `active` while the participant is connected.

ActiveCall.description: A call in progress. A field the platform has no value for is left out of the response.

call-orig-call-id.description: Call ID of the originating leg.

call-term-call-id.description: Call ID of the terminating leg.

call-orig-user.description: User or number that placed the call.

call-orig-domain.description: Domain of the party that placed the call.

call-orig-name.description: Caller name of the party that placed the call.

call-orig-uri.description: SIP URI of the party that placed the call.

call-orig-match-uri.description: URI the platform matched the originating party on.

call-through-action.description: Application the call passed through, such as `CallRequest` for a call started through the API, or a call queue or auto attendant.

call-through-user.description: User the call passed through, such as a call queue or an auto attendant.

call-through-domain.description: Domain of the user the call passed through.

call-through-name.description: Name of the user the call passed through.

call-through-call-id.description: Call ID of the leg through that user.

call-term-user.description: User or number that received the call.

call-term-domain.description: Domain of the party that received the call.

call-term-name.description: Name of the party that received the call.

call-term-uri.description: SIP URI of the party that received the call.

caller-id-number.description: Caller ID number of the call.

call-dialed-number.description: Number or extension that was dialed.

call-answer-datetime.description: When the call was answered. `null` while the call is still ringing.

call-orig-info.description: State of the originating leg, as reported by the switch.

call-term-info.description: State of the terminating leg, as reported by the switch.

call-session-id.description: Session ID of the call on its core server. Use it with `hostname` to merge the call into an attended transfer.

call-audio-codec.description: Audio codec in use, such as `PCMU`.

Recordingserver.description: A recording server as one core server sees it. A list returns the same recording server once per core server, so read `enabled` together with `hostname`.

hostname.description: Hostname of the core server this row comes from.

name.description: Display name of the recording server.

address.description: Address of the recording server's operator. Free text.

contact.description: Contact person or team for the recording server.

phone.description: Contact phone number. Free text, returned as a string.

email.description: Contact email address. Free text, not validated.

ccc-ip.description: Host or IP address that receives call content (the media) for recording.

ccc-port.description: Port that receives call content on `ccc-ip`.

cdc-url.description: URL that receives call data (the signaling events) for recording.

cdc-type.description: Protocol for `cdc-url`, such as `http`. Free text.

enabled.description: Whether the core server in `hostname` records to this recording server: `yes` or `no`.

entry-count.description: Read-only. Number of distinct addresses of record recorded on this recording server. One address of record can hold several entries, so this can be lower than the number of entries. Ignored on a write.

RecordingserverWrite.description: Recording server create and update body. On an update, send only the fields to change.

recording-server-id.description: Recording server id, such as `Recording-Server2`. Up to 127 letters, digits, `.`, `-`, and `_`; anything else returns `400`. Lists and entry writes to every recording server cover the ids that start with `Recording-Server`. Required on create. On an update, the id in the path is used.

name.description: Display name of the recording server.

address.description: Address of the recording server's operator. Free text.

contact.description: Contact person or team for the recording server.

email.description: Contact email address. Free text, not validated.

ccc-ip.description: Host or IP address that receives call content (the media) for recording.

ccc-port.description: Port that receives call content on `ccc-ip`.

cdc-url.description: URL that receives call data (the signaling events) for recording.

cdc-type.description: Protocol for `cdc-url`, such as `http`. Free text.

enabled.description: Whether core servers record to this recording server: `yes` or `no`. An unrecognized value returns `400`. On create, a core server that `enabled-hosts` does not name takes this value, and it defaults to `yes`. On an update without `enabled-hosts`, it sets every core server. Leave it out on an update to keep each core server's current value.

enabled-hosts.description:
Per core server value, as a map of core server hostname to `yes` or `no`, or as the text `core1.example.com:yes,core2.example.com:no`. It is not stored: each core server applies its own entry when the write arrives.

On an update, a core server the map does not name keeps its current value, even when `enabled` is sent. On a create, it takes `enabled`. A core server is never disabled by being left out. A value other than `yes` or `no` returns `400`. To change one core server, use `PUT /recordings/coreservers/{hostname}`.

Recordingentry.description: A recording entry: call recording turned on for one address of record (AOR) on one recording server.

recording-server-id.description: Recording server that holds this entry.

device-aor.description: Address of record that is recorded: `user@domain`, `sip:device@domain`, or `*@domain` for a whole domain.

case-id.description: Case ID that identifies the entry on its recording server. Usually the same as `device-aor`.

valid-from.description: Read-only. Start of the recording window. Always `0000-00-00 00:00:00`, meaning no start limit, on entries written through the API.

valid-to.description: Read-only. End of the recording window. Always `0000-00-00 00:00:00`, meaning no end limit, on entries written through the API.

ccc-intercept.description: Read-only. Whether call content (the media) is recorded. Always `yes` on entries written through the API.

cdc-intercept.description: Read-only. Whether call data (the signaling events) is recorded. Always `yes` on entries written through the API.

transcription.description: Whether recordings for this entry are transcribed: `yes` or `no`.

sentiment.description: Whether recordings for this entry get sentiment analysis: `yes` or `no`. `null` when never set.

RecordingCoreserver.description: Whether one core server records to one recording server.

hostname.description: Hostname of the core server.

enabled.description: Whether this core server records to this recording server: `yes` or `no`.

RecordingentrySyncRequest.description: Entry copy request. The target is the recording server in the path.

source-recording-server-id.description: Recording server to copy entries from. It must exist and differ from the recording server in the path.

synchronous.description: `yes` waits for the copy and returns the result with `200`. Too many entries to copy in one request run in the background anyway and return `202`, so handle `202` even when you send `yes`. An unrecognized value returns `400`.

dry-run.description: `yes` copies nothing and returns the counts a copy would give. Use it for a confirmation prompt. An unrecognized value returns `400`.

overwrite-existing.description: `yes` also updates `transcription` and `sentiment` on entries the target already has when they differ from the source. `no`, the default, leaves those entries alone. An unrecognized value returns `400`.

RecordingentrySyncResult.description: Result of a finished copy, or the counts a copy would give for `dry-run=yes`.

source-recording-server-id.description: Recording server the entries are copied from.

recording-server-id.description: Recording server the entries are copied to.

source-total.description: Number of entries on the source recording server.

copied.description: Number of entries copied to the target. For a dry run, the number that would be copied.

overwritten.description: Number of existing entries updated. Always `0` unless `overwrite-existing` is `yes`.

skipped.description: Number of source entries already on the target and left alone.

failed.description: Number of entries that were not copied. Can be larger than the length of `failures`.

failures.description: Entries that were not copied, and why. Holds at most 100. See `failures-truncated`.

failures-truncated.description: Present, and `yes`, when `failed` is larger than the number of entries in `failures`.

processed.description: Number of entries the copy attempted. Absent on a dry run.

total.description: Number of entries the copy set out to write: copies plus updates. Absent on a dry run.

dry-run.description: Present, and `yes`, when nothing was written.

message.description: Present when the copy stopped at its time limit. Run the copy again to finish it.

device-aor.description: Address of record of the entry.

message.description: Why the entry was not copied, such as an address of record the API does not accept.

RecordingentrySyncFailure.description: An entry that was not copied, and why.

RecordingentrySyncAccepted.description: Returned with `202` when the copy runs in the background.

job-id.description: Job ID to poll. The part after the first `.` is the core server running the job, which is the only core server that knows it.

source-recording-server-id.description: Recording server the entries are copied from.

recording-server-id.description: Recording server the entries are copied to.

total.description: Number of entries the copy sets out to write, or `null` when it is not counted yet. The job reports it once the copy starts.

poll.description: Request to poll this job with.

downgraded-to-async.description: Present, and `yes`, when you sent `synchronous=yes` but there were too many entries to wait for.

message.description: Present with `downgraded-to-async`. Says why the copy runs in the background.

RecordingentrySyncJob.description: Progress of a background entry copy and, once it ends, the same counts a finished copy returns. Kept for 24 hours.

state.description: Where the job is: `running` while it copies, `complete` when it finished, `incomplete` when it stopped at its time limit (run the copy again to finish it), `cancelled` after a cancel, or `failed` when the copy itself failed, with `message`.

processed.description: Number of entries attempted so far. Updated every 25 entries.

total.description: Number of entries the copy sets out to write. `null` until the copy starts.

source-recording-server-id.description: Recording server the entries are copied from.

recording-server-id.description: Recording server the entries are copied to.

source-total.description: Number of entries on the source recording server. Present once the job ends.

skipped.description: Number of source entries already on the target and left alone.

failed.description: Number of entries that were not copied.

failures.description: Entries that were not copied, and why. Holds at most 100.

failures-truncated.description: Present, and `yes`, when `failed` is larger than the number of entries in `failures`.

started.description: Deprecated. Use `started-datetime`. When the job started, in UTC, as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`.

updated.description: Deprecated. Use `updated-datetime`. When the job last reported progress, in UTC, as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`.

message.description: Present when the job stopped at its time limit or failed. Says what happened.

started-datetime.description: When the job started, in RFC 3339.

updated-datetime.description: When the job last reported progress, in RFC 3339.

AttendantListItem.title: AttendantListItem
AttendantListItem.description: An auto attendant as the lists return it: its name and where to read it.

user.description: Extension that answers as the auto attendant.

starting-prompt.description: Starting tier of the menu, such as `Prompt_100`.

read-path.description: Path that reads the attendant in full with **Read auto attendant**.

timeframes.description: Time frames whose answering rule sends calls to the attendant. `Default` is the default time frame.

id.description: Meeting ID: 9 digits, as a string.

domain.description: Domain of the meeting's owner.

user.description: Extension of the meeting's owner.

meeting-schedule-start-datetime.description: When the meeting is scheduled to start. For a recurring meeting this is the first occurrence; each upcoming occurrence is its own item.

NetworktestR.description: Summary of one network test report, as lists return it. The figures are copied from the report when it is stored. A figure the report did not include is `null`. Read the full report by its `test-id`. Reports are kept for 90 days after they are stored, then deleted automatically.

test-id.description: ID of the report, from its `metadata.reportId`.

timestamp.description: When the test ran, in epoch milliseconds, taken from the report's `metadata.timestamp`. `null` when the report gave none.

territory.description: Reseller territory of the domain, such as `example-reseller`.

domain.description: Domain the report belongs to.

user.description: Extension of the user the report is attributed to, such as `1001`.

source-ip.description: Public IP address the test ran from, IPv4 or IPv6.

location.description: Approximate location of that address, such as `San Diego, California, US`.

carrier.description: Internet service provider of that address.

cf-download.description: Download speed from the speed test, in Mbps.

cf-upload.description: Upload speed from the speed test, in Mbps.

cf-packetloss.description: Packet loss during the speed test, as a percentage.

aim-rtc.description: Aggregated Internet Measurement (AIM) rating for real-time communication, such as `great`.

nms-hostname.description: Hostname of the server the test calls connected to, such as `core1.example.com`.

mos.description: Average MOS score of the test calls.

jitter.description: Average jitter of the test calls, in milliseconds.

packet-loss.description: Packet loss on the test calls, as a percentage.

rtt.description: Average round-trip time of the test calls, in milliseconds.

calls.description: Number of call legs in the test, two per call pair.

duration.description: Test length in seconds: the planned duration, or the measured time rounded when no plan was sent.

NetworktestReport.description: A network test report, as the app's network test tool produces it. It is stored and returned exactly as sent. Only the fields below are read when it is stored, to build the summary that lists return; other blocks, such as per-call time series or an event log, are kept as they are. A field that feeds the summary must fit the summary field it becomes: a value above its maximum, or of the wrong type, such as text where a number is expected, returns `400`. Fields marked as stored only have no limit of their own beyond the 1 MB body. `metadata.reportId` is required. Reports are kept for 90 days after they are stored, then deleted automatically.

version.description: Version of the report format, such as `1.0`. Stored only.

reportId.description: Unique ID for the report, usually a UUID. Becomes the report's `test_id` and must be unique across the platform. 1 to 36 letters, digits, dots, hyphens, and underscores; anything else returns `400`.

timestamp.description: When the test ran, in RFC 3339, such as `2026-09-01T14:30:00+00:00`. Becomes the summary's `timestamp`, in epoch milliseconds, which the `start_date` and `end_date` filters match. A digits-only value is read as epoch milliseconds. Must be text or a number; an object or array returns `400`. Leave it out, or send a value that can't be parsed, and the report has no run time.

user.description: Extension of the user who ran the test, such as `1001`. A `user@domain` value is stored as the extension. Must be text or a number; an object or array returns `400`. Basic User, Advanced User, Simple User, Call Center Agent, Site Manager, and Route Manager can name only themselves. On a user path it must match the path user. Defaults to you.

domain.description: Domain the test ran in. When sent, it must match the path domain exactly, or the request returns `400`. An object or array also returns `400`.

reseller.description: Reseller territory of the domain. The summary's `territory` is looked up from the domain; this value is used only when that lookup finds nothing, and then must be at most 255 characters.

userScope.description: User scope of whoever ran the test, such as `Basic User`. Stored only; it does not change access.

nmsHostname.description: Hostname of the server the test calls connected to, such as `core1.example.com`. Becomes the summary's `nms-hostname`. When left out, `speedTest.nms-hostname` or the host of `config.wsUri` is used. A value that is not text is ignored.

metadata.description: Who ran the test, where, and when. Required.

mode.description: Test mode, such as `loopback`. Stored only.

duration.description: Planned test length, in seconds. Becomes the summary's `duration`.

maxPairs.description: Most test call pairs run at once. When `results.legs` is missing, the summary's `calls` is twice this value, so it must be at most 1,073,741,823.

codec.description: Audio codec of the test calls, such as `opus`. Stored only.

wsUri.description: WebSocket address the test calls connected to, such as `wss://core1.example.com/ws`. Its host becomes the summary's `nms-hostname` when no hostname is sent. A value that is not text is ignored.

downloadMbps.description: Download speed, in Mbps. Becomes the summary's `cf-download`.

uploadMbps.description: Upload speed, in Mbps. Becomes the summary's `cf-upload`.

packetLossPct.description: Packet loss during the speed test, as a percentage. Becomes the summary's `cf-packetloss`.

aim.description: Aggregated Internet Measurement (AIM) ratings from the speed test, one per use.

rtc.description: Rating for real-time communication, such as calls and video meetings, such as `great`. Becomes the summary's `aim-rtc`. A value that is not text is ignored.

streaming.description: Rating for streaming, such as `good`. Stored only.

gaming.description: Rating for gaming, such as `average`. Stored only.

nms-hostname.description: Hostname of the server the test calls connected to. Used for the summary when `metadata.nmsHostname` is missing.

ip.description: Public IP address the test ran from, IPv4 or IPv6. Becomes the summary's `source-ip`.

provider.description: Internet service provider of that address. Becomes the summary's `carrier`.

location.description: Approximate location of that address, such as `San Diego, California, US`. Becomes the summary's `location`.

speedTest.description: Results of the speed test run before the test calls.

elapsed.description: How long the test actually ran, in seconds. Rounded into the summary's `duration` when `config.duration` is missing.

legs.description: Number of call legs in the test, two per call pair. Becomes the summary's `calls`.

totalSent.description: Media packets sent across all legs. With `totalLost`, gives the summary's `packet-loss` when `aggregate` has no loss values.

totalLost.description: Media packets lost across all legs.

aggregate.description: Averages across all test call legs. `avgMos` becomes the summary's `mos`, the mean of the two jitter values becomes `jitter`, `avgRtt` becomes `rtt`, and the mean of the two loss values becomes `packet-loss`. Each mean must fit its summary field: at most 99,999,999.99 for `jitter` and 999.99 for `packet-loss`. A value that is not a number is left out of its mean.

avgMos.description: Average MOS score, on the 1 to 5 scale.

avgFwdLoss.description: Average forward-direction packet loss, as a percentage.

avgRetLoss.description: Average return-direction packet loss, as a percentage.

ServiceCode.description: A service code. Its key is the combination of `srvcode-item`, `srvcode-code`, and `domain`.

srvcode-code.description: The service code. A user's `service-code` field names it. Codes that start with `system-` are the platform's own. 1 to 31 characters: letters, digits, and `* # . - _`.

srvcode-item.description: The type of the code: a grouping key you choose when you create it. `*`, the default, means no particular type. 1 to 31 characters: letters, digits, and `* # . - _`.

domain.description: The domain that owns the code, or `*` for a system-wide code that every domain shares.

srvcode-description.description: A label for the code, shown in admin screens. Up to 255 characters.

srvcode-code.description: The service code. A user's `service-code` field names it. Codes that start with `system-` are the platform's own. 1 to 31 characters: letters, digits, and `* # . - _`.

srvcode-item.description: The type of the code: a grouping key you choose when you create it. `*`, the default, means no particular type. 1 to 31 characters: letters, digits, and `* # . - _`.

domain.description: The domain the code is for, or `*` for a system-wide code that every domain shares. `~` means the domain of your token. `domain` is required: a write without it returns `400`. Send `"domain": "*"` to address a system-wide code, which needs Super User scope. Up to 63 characters.

srvcode-description.description: A label for the code, shown in admin screens. Up to 255 characters.

ServiceCodeCreate.description: The body of a service code create. `srvcode-code` is required. `domain` is required: a write without it returns `400`. Send `"domain": "*"` to address a system-wide code, which needs Super User scope.

DomainServiceCodeCreate.description: The body of a domain service code create. The domain comes from the path. `srvcode-code` is required.

srvcode-code.description: The service code. A user's `service-code` field names it. Codes that start with `system-` are the platform's own. 1 to 31 characters: letters, digits, and `* # . - _`.

srvcode-item.description: The type of the code: a grouping key you choose when you create it. `*`, the default, means no particular type. 1 to 31 characters: letters, digits, and `* # . - _`.

srvcode-description.description: A label for the code, shown in admin screens. Up to 255 characters.

ServiceCodeKeyedUpdate.description: The body of a service code change. The type and code come from the path. `domain` is required: a write without it returns `400`. Send `"domain": "*"` to address a system-wide code, which needs Super User scope.

domain.description: The domain of the code to change, or `*` for a system-wide code. `~` means the domain of your token. `domain` is required: a write without it returns `400`. Send `"domain": "*"` to address a system-wide code, which needs Super User scope. Read from the body only.

srvcode-description.description: The new label for the code. Up to 255 characters.

srvcode-item.description: Optional. If sent, it must equal `{type}` in the path, or the answer is `400`.

srvcode-code.description: Optional. If sent, it must equal `{code}` in the path, or the answer is `400`.

DomainServiceCodeKeyedUpdate.description: The body of a domain service code change. The domain, type, and code come from the path.

srvcode-description.description: The new label for the code. Up to 255 characters.

srvcode-item.description: Optional. If sent, it must equal `{type}` in the path, or the answer is `400`.

srvcode-code.description: Optional. If sent, it must equal `{code}` in the path, or the answer is `400`.

ServiceCodeKeyedDelete.description: The body of a service code delete. The type and code come from the path. `domain` is required: a write without it returns `400`. Send `"domain": "*"` to address a system-wide code, which needs Super User scope.

domain.description: The domain of the code to delete, or `*` for a system-wide code. `~` means the domain of your token. `domain` is required: a write without it returns `400`. Send `"domain": "*"` to address a system-wide code, which needs Super User scope. Read from the body only.

ServicecodeListItem.title: ServicecodeListItem
ServicecodeListItem.description: A service code as `/list` returns it. For service codes it has the same fields as a full read.

srvcode-code.description: The service code. A user's `service-code` field names it. Codes that start with `system-` are the platform's own. 1 to 31 characters: letters, digits, and `* # . - _`.

srvcode-item.description: The type of the code: a grouping key you choose when you create it. `*`, the default, means no particular type. 1 to 31 characters: letters, digits, and `* # . - _`.

domain.description: The domain that owns the code, or `*` for a system-wide code that every domain shares.

srvcode-description.description: A label for the code, shown in admin screens. Up to 255 characters.

DispositionListItem.title: DispositionListItem
DispositionListItem.description: The short disposition row returned by `/dispositions/list`.

disposition.description: The outcome an agent picks, such as `Sale`.

disposition_type.description: The category the disposition is listed under. The portal groups dispositions by it.

reason.description: One reason listed under the disposition.

domain.description: The domain the disposition belongs to.

OauthClient.description: An OAuth client, as a read returns it. `client-secret` is returned masked: the first 2 and last 2 characters, with asterisks between. A secret of 8 characters or fewer is all asterisks. Send `include-secret=yes` to get the whole value; that read is recorded in the access log. `client-secret-set` says whether a secret is stored.

client-id.description: The client identifier. Letters, digits, `.`, `-`, and `_`.

client-secret.description: The client secret, masked: the first 2 and last 2 characters, with asterisks between. Whole when you send `include-secret=yes`. `null` when no secret is stored.

client-secret-set.description: `yes` when a secret is stored for the client, `no` when none is.

redirect-uri.description: The redirect URI stored for your reference. No grant flow checks it. Empty or `null` when none is set.

client-id.description: The client identifier, 1 to 64 characters: letters, digits, `.`, `-`, and `_`. It must not already exist.

client-secret.description: The client secret, 1 to 64 characters. Omit it to have a 32-character hexadecimal secret generated. A masked value is refused.

redirect-uri.description: A redirect URI to store for your reference, up to 256 characters. It must start with a scheme and `://`, such as `https://` or `com.example.app://`. No grant flow checks it.

OauthClientCreate.description: The body of an OAuth client create. `client-id` is required. A secret is generated when you do not send one.

OauthClientUpdate.description: The body of an OAuth client change. Send at least one change. The stored secret is kept unless you send `regenerate-secret` or a new `client-secret`.

redirect-uri.description: A new redirect URI, up to 256 characters, starting with a scheme and `://`. Send an empty string to clear it.

regenerate-secret.description: `yes` generates a new 32-character secret and returns it in the response. `true` and `1` also work.

client-secret.description: A new secret, 1 to 64 characters. Ignored when `regenerate-secret` is `yes`. A masked value or an empty string leaves the stored secret unchanged.

OauthClientWithSecret.description: An OAuth client with its whole secret, as a create or a secret rotation returns it.

client-secret.description: The whole client secret. Store it now: reads return it masked.

redirect-uri.description: The stored redirect URI. Present on a create that sent one; absent on a secret rotation.

notes.description: A reminder of how the secret is returned from now on.
notes.example: The client secret is shown here on create. It is returned masked from now on; include-secret=yes reads it back whole.

AddressListItem.title: AddressListItem
AddressListItem.description: An address as `/list` returns it: its ID, name, owner, and city.

emergency-address-id.description: The address ID. IDs the API generates are `a-` followed by 13 hexadecimal characters. Paths accept only letters, digits, spaces, and `* . - _ '`.

address-name.description: A label for the address, shown when users pick one.

domain.description: The domain that owns the address.

user.description: Who the address belongs to: `*` for a domain-level address, a site name for a site address, or an extension for a personal address. Endpoint rows have `address_endpoint`.

address-state-province-abbreviation.description: The state or province code, such as `CA`.

FlowSdkExtension.description: A registered extension, as the management endpoints return it. `enabled` and the `verification_*` fields are computed for the caller.

id.description: The extension `id`, derived from `webpack_module` at registration.

name.description: Display name of the extension.

reseller.description: Owning reseller. `*` means the extension is platform-wide.

webpack_module.description: Module Federation container name. Unique across the platform; cannot be changed.

version.description: Version of the live bundle. Only a deploy changes it.

enabled.description: State for the caller. `yes`: on. `no`: the master switch is off. `restricted`: on, but an access rule hides it from you.

description.description: What the extension does.
description.example: Adds a notes panel to the inbound call view.

integrity_hash.description: Subresource integrity hash of the live entry, computed by the platform at deploy.

active_version.description: The `version_id` of the live version. See `GET /ui-extensions/registry/{id}/versions`.

active_verification_status.description: Verdict the live version had when it was deployed. This is what decides whether it loads, so a later reanalysis does not unload it. `dev` is a local development build, on development servers only.

verification_status.description: Current verdict of the live version. A reanalysis can change it; `active_verification_status` stays as deployed.

verification_report.description: Analysis report of the live version. Null before the first deploy.

verification_declared.description: Zones, routes, and capabilities the bundle declares, read from its source. Null when unknown.

allowed_hostnames.description: Origins the remote authentication callbacks may use, comma-separated. No length limit.

remote_auth_enabled.description: `yes` when the extension uses remote authentication with its vendor; `no` when it does not.

remote_callback_secret.description: Shared secret used to sign the remote authentication webhook, masked: the first 2 and last 2 characters, with asterisks between; 8 characters or fewer is all asterisks, at least 4. A Super User gets it whole with `include-secret=yes`.

remote_timeout_seconds.description: Seconds to wait for the vendor during remote authentication.

created_by.description: Login of the user who registered the extension.

created_at.description: When the extension was registered, in UTC, as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`.

updated_at.description: When the extension last changed, in UTC, as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`.

remote_callback_url.description: Vendor endpoints that receive the remote authentication webhook, comma-separated, in failover order. No length limit.

FlowSdkExtensionRuntime.description: An extension the caller's browser may load, as `GET /ui-extensions` returns it. It carries only what the app needs to load the extension.

id.description: The extension `id`, derived from `webpack_module`.

name.description: Display name of the extension.

webpack_module.description: Module Federation container name the bundle was built with.

integrity_hash.description: Subresource integrity hash of the live entry, for the `integrity` attribute. Null only for a `dev` build. Absent on a platform app.

verification_status.description: Verdict of the live version. `dev` is a local development build served without analysis, on development servers only. Absent on a platform app.

enabled.description: Always `yes`: only extensions on for this caller are returned.

remote_auth_enabled.description: `yes` when the extension uses remote authentication with its vendor; `no` when it does not.

remote_timeout_seconds.description: Seconds to wait for the vendor during remote authentication.

builtin.description: Present and `true` only on an app the platform provides. Such an app has no `integrity_hash` and no `verification_status`.

FlowSdkExtensionVersion.description: One deployed version of an extension, with its verdict.

status.description: Current verdict. A reanalysis can change it; whether the version loads depends on the verdict it had when deployed. `dev` is a local development build, on development servers only.

has_chunk_sri.description: `yes` when the bundle's chunks carry integrity hashes.

integrity_hash.description: Subresource integrity hash of this version's entry. Null when it could not be fetched.

verified_at.description: When the current verdict was issued.

ruleset_fingerprint.description: Rule set that produced the verdict. When it differs from the settings' `analysis-ruleset-fingerprint`, the rules have changed since.

report.description: Analysis report for this version. Null when none was stored.

FlowSdkSettings.description: The platform-wide Flow SDK settings. Reseller, Super User, Super User Read Only, and Admin Super User receive every field. Other scopes receive only `disabled-zones`, `disabled-capabilities`, `api-read-deny-resources`, `api-write-deny-resources`, and `approved-cdn-origins`, which is all the app needs to decide what to load. Every field you receive is always present; unset values fall back to the defaults.

disabled-zones.description: Zones no extension may mount into, such as `sidetray` or `table-row-actions`.

disabled-capabilities.description: Capabilities withheld from every extension, whatever it declares.

api-read-deny-resources.description: API resources extensions may not read.

api-write-deny-resources.description: API resources extensions may not change.

approved-cdn-origins.description: Hosts extension bundles may be served from: bare hostnames or `*.example.com` wildcards. An empty list approves no host. Approving a host here does not change the portal's Content Security Policy; see `csp-coverage`.

analysis-settings.description: Administrators only. Bundle-analysis limits in force.

analysis-denylist.description: Administrators only. Denied packages and suppressed findings in force.

analysis-rule-policy.description: Administrators only. Every analysis rule with the mode and severity in force.

analysis-ruleset-fingerprint.description: Administrators only. Fingerprint a verdict issued now would carry. A version whose `ruleset_fingerprint` differs was judged under older rules.

csp-coverage.description: Administrators only. Whether the portal's Content Security Policy allows scripts from every approved host.

FlowSdkAccessRule.description: An access rule that shows or hides an extension for callers that match it. The most specific matching rule wins, in this order: user, scope, domain, reseller, hostname. With no matching rule, the extension is shown. A matching `enabled: no` makes the extension `restricted` for that caller.

rule_id.description: Handle of the rule, for `PUT` and `DELETE`.

extension_id.description: The extension the rule belongs to.

hostname.description: Portal hostname the rule applies to. `*` matches every hostname.

reseller.description: Reseller the rule applies to. `*` matches every reseller.

domain.description: Domain the rule applies to. `*` matches every domain.

role.description: User scope the rule applies to, by scope name. `*` matches every scope.

user.description: Reserved. Always `*`.

enabled.description: `yes` shows the extension to matching callers. `no` hides it.

created_at.description: When the rule was created, in UTC, as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`.

updated_at.description: When the rule last changed, in UTC, as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`.

FlowSdkAnalysisSettings.description: Bundle-analysis limits. Reads always return every key. On write, an unknown key, a numeric string, or a value out of range returns `400`.

max_total_bytes.description: Largest total of the entry and all chunks, in bytes.

max_chunk_count.description: Most chunks a bundle may have.

max_fetch_seconds.description: Time allowed to fetch the bundle, in seconds.

obfuscation_string_array_max.description: Largest string array allowed before code counts as obfuscated.

obfuscation_string_array_share_max.description: Largest share of the file a string array may take, from 0 to 1.

obfuscation_hex_ratio_max.description: Largest share of hex-escaped identifiers allowed, from 0 to 1.

obfuscation_bracket_ratio_max.description: Largest share of bracket property access allowed, from 0 to 1.

size_delta_flag_ratio.description: Growth over the live version that flags a deploy. `2` means twice the size.

FlowSdkAnalysisDenylist.description: Denied packages and suppressed findings. Reads include the built-in suppressions, which always apply. On write, an unknown key returns `400`.

bad_packages.description: Package names whose presence rejects a bundle.

benign.description: Findings to ignore: a rule firing under a known-safe path.

rule.description: Id of the rule to ignore, such as `document-cookie`.

path.description: Source path prefix where the rule is ignored, such as a package folder.

FlowSdkRulePolicy.description: Every analysis rule with the mode, severity, and bucket severities in force, keyed by rule id. To change it, send overrides in `PUT /ui-extensions/settings`.

FlowSdkRulePolicyEntry.description: The policy in force for one analysis rule.

mode.description: `enforce` counts toward the verdict. `monitor` reports only. `off` does not run the rule.

severity.description: Verdict the rule produces when it fires.

buckets.description: Severity for hits in dependency code (`vendored`) or code the build tool added (`build-injected`).

FlowSdkCspCoverage.description: Whether the portal's Content Security Policy allows scripts from every approved host. The policy is part of the web server configuration, so approving a host does not update it. Update the policy as well, or extensions from that host are blocked by the browser.

status.description: `ok`: every approved host is allowed. `diverged`: at least one is not; see `uncovered`. `no-csp`: the policy sets no script sources. `unknown`: the policy could not be read.

uncovered.description: Approved hosts the policy does not allow. Empty unless `status` is `diverged`.

source.description: Which configuration the check read. Null when `status` is `unknown`.

FlowSdkReanalyzeResult.description: Result of a reanalysis run. A reanalysis records new verdicts but never changes which version is live.

analyzer_version.description: Version of the analyzer that ran.

processed.description: Versions handled in this call. Call again while `remaining` is above 0.

remaining.description: Versions still judged under older rules after this call. A dry run leaves it unchanged.

live_rejections.description: Live versions that now fail. They are still live and still loading. Review each one and deploy a fixed version or turn the extension off.

FlowSdkReanalyzeEntry.description: One version a reanalysis handled. When `result` is `unfetchable`, `was` and `is_active` are absent and the earlier verdict stands.

extension_id.description: The extension the version belongs to.

result.description: `changed`: the verdict moved. `unchanged`: it did not. `unfetchable`: the bundle could not be fetched, so the earlier verdict stands.

status.description: Verdict after the reanalysis: `approved`, `flagged`, or `rejected`.

is_active.description: `true` when this is the live version.

OauthToken.description: An issued token. `token` is returned masked: the first 2 and last 2 characters, with asterisks between. Send `include-secret=yes` to get the whole value; that read is recorded in the access log. Every row also carries `token-hash`, the SHA-256 of the token, which you can use in place of the token to read or revoke it.

token.description: The token, masked unless you sent `include-secret=yes`.

token-hash.description: The SHA-256 of the token, in lowercase hex. Use it in place of the token to read or revoke it.

client-id.description: The OAuth client the token was issued to.

reseller.description: The territory the token was issued in.

domain.description: The domain of the user the token was issued to.

user-id.description: The user the token was issued to, as `user@domain`.

expired.description: `yes` when `expires-datetime` has passed, `no` while the token is live.

user-scope.description: The scope the token was issued with, such as `Office Manager` or a custom scope name.

token-type.description: `access` authenticates requests. `refresh` gets new access tokens.

mask-chain.description: The masquerade chain when the token was issued while masquerading. Empty otherwise.

SmscarrierFields.description: The configurable fields of a custom SMS carrier. Text fields have no length limit but must not contain a line break. Boolean fields take `true` or `false`; the strings `true`, `yes`, `on`, and `1` also mean true, and anything else means false.

url.description: The carrier endpoint the platform posts outbound messages to.

auth.description: The carrier credential. With `set-http-header` and `outbound-include-auth-header` both `true`, it is sent in the header `auth-type` names, exactly as stored, so store a Basic credential already base64-encoded. Read back masked; a masked value sent back is ignored.

auth-type.description: Which header carries `auth`: `Basic Auth` sends `Authorization: Basic`, `Bearer Token` sends `Authorization: Bearer`, and `API Key` sends `X-API-Key`. Defaults to `Basic Auth`.

inbound-to.description: Name of the field that holds the destination number in the carrier's inbound webhook.

inbound-to-plus.description: Whether inbound destination numbers carry a `+` prefix.

inbound-from.description: Name of the field that holds the source number in the carrier's inbound webhook.

inbound-from-plus.description: Whether inbound source numbers carry a `+` prefix.

inbound-text.description: Name of the field that holds the message text in the carrier's inbound webhook.

inbound-media-field.description: Name of the field that holds media URLs in the carrier's inbound MMS webhook.

custom-nested-inbound-fields.description: The path of keys under which the message sits in the carrier's inbound webhook, for example `[0, "message"]`. Send an array, or the same array as a JSON string. A plain string becomes a path of one key.

response.description: The body to answer the carrier's inbound webhook with, when `response-param` is in the webhook.

response-param.description: Name of the inbound webhook field whose presence makes the platform answer with `response`.

response-header-type.description: The whole header line sent with `response`, for example `Content-Type: application/json`.

outbound-to.description: Name of the field for the destination number in the outbound request.

outbound-to-plus.description: Whether to send outbound destination numbers with a `+` prefix.

outbound-to-array-format.description: Whether to send the outbound destination as a JSON array.

outbound-from.description: Name of the field for the source number in the outbound request.

outbound-from-plus.description: Whether to send the outbound source number with a `+` prefix.

outbound-from-array-format.description: Whether to send the outbound source as a JSON array.

outbound-text.description: Name of the field for the message text in the outbound request.

json-encode.description: Whether to send the outbound body as JSON instead of form-encoded.

content-type.description: The `Content-Type` of the outbound request, sent when `set-http-header` is `true`, for example `application/json` or `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`. Defaults to `application/json`.

outbound-include-auth-header.description: Whether to send `auth` in the header `auth-type` names. Takes effect only when `set-http-header` is `true`.

set-http-header.description: Whether to send the `Content-Type` header, and the credential header when `outbound-include-auth-header` is `true`.

custom-outbound-json-fields.description: Fixed fields added to every outbound request, as a map of field name to string value. Sending it replaces the whole map, and an empty value removes it. Each value reads back masked, so a carrier that authenticates in the body can keep its credential here.

outbound-media-keep-text.description: Whether to keep the message text alongside media in an outbound MMS.

outbound-media-field.description: Name of the field for media URLs in the outbound MMS request.

outbound-mms-array-format.description: Whether to send outbound MMS media as a JSON array.

ssl-verify.description: Whether to verify the carrier's TLS certificate on outbound requests. Leave it out to verify. Set `false` only for a carrier that cannot present a valid certificate: the requests carry the carrier credential.

allOf.description: An SMS carrier as Super User and Super User Read Only read it.

type.description: `builtin` for a carrier the platform ships with, `custom` for one added with `POST /smscarriers`.

enabled.description: Whether the portal shows the carrier. Read-only on a custom carrier, which is always `true`. A builtin carrier is `true` until hidden. It does not change how messages are sent.

mms-capable.description: Read-only. Whether the platform's MMS carrier list names this carrier.

group-mms-capable.description: Read-only. Whether the platform's group MMS carrier list names this carrier.

SmscarrierR.description: An SMS carrier as Super User and Super User Read Only read it. A builtin carrier has only the first five fields; a custom carrier also has every field it was given.

SmscarrierPortalR.description: The portal view of an SMS carrier, returned to every scope other than Super User and Super User Read Only. Disabled carriers are left out.

mms-capable.description: Whether the platform's MMS carrier list names this carrier.

group-mms-capable.description: Whether the platform's group MMS carrier list names this carrier.

carrier.description: The new carrier name: letters, digits, `-`, and `_`. It must not be a builtin carrier, `twillio`, `nullResponseFields`, or an existing custom carrier.

SmscarrierC.description: The body of a custom SMS carrier create. `carrier` and `url` are required.

SmscarrierCustomU.description: The body of a custom SMS carrier change. Send at least one field. Fields you leave out keep their values; an empty string removes a field.

SmscarrierBuiltinU.description: The body of a builtin SMS carrier change. Only `enabled` is used.

enabled.description: Whether the portal shows this builtin carrier. It does not change how messages are sent. `true`, `yes`, `on`, and `1` mean true; anything else means false.

FaxNumber.description: A fax number and how it sends and receives.

user.description: The user the number belongs to.

vendor.description: The fax vendor holding the number. Set by the platform, never by the client.

enable-email.description: The number may send faxes by email.

enable-portal.description: The number may send faxes from the portal and the API.

enable-ata.description: The number may send faxes from a fax adapter (ATA).

inbound-email.description: Email a received fax: `yes` sends a link, `attachment` attaches the PDF.

inbound-portal.description: Keep received faxes in the mailbox.

inbound-ata.description: Deliver received faxes to the fax adapter.

notify-success-email.description: Email the sender when a fax is sent.

notify-success-ata.description: Print a confirmation on the fax adapter when a fax is sent.

notify-failure-email.description: Email the sender when a fax fails.

notify-failure-ata.description: Print a notice on the fax adapter when a fax fails.

sharing.description: Who else may send from the number: `no`, `all`, `site:<site>`, `dept:<department>`, or `user:<user>,<user>`.

ata-mac.description: MAC address of the fax adapter, 12 hex digits.

serial-number.description: Serial number of the fax adapter (Faxback).

ata-status.description: Whether the fax adapter is registered (Pangea).

vendor-data.description: The vendor's own identifiers for the number. Informational; the keys differ by vendor.

FaxNumberWrite.description: Fields of a fax number a client may set. On an update send only the fields to change.

phonenumber.description: The fax number, 7 to 15 digits. Create only.

user.description: The user the number belongs to. Required on create.

enable-email.description: The number may send faxes by email.

enable-portal.description: The number may send faxes from the portal and the API.

enable-ata.description: The number may send faxes from a fax adapter (ATA).

inbound-email.description: Email a received fax: `yes` sends a link, `attachment` attaches the PDF.

inbound-portal.description: Keep received faxes in the mailbox.

inbound-ata.description: Deliver received faxes to the fax adapter.

notify-success-email.description: Email the sender when a fax is sent.

notify-success-ata.description: Print a confirmation on the fax adapter when a fax is sent.

notify-failure-email.description: Email the sender when a fax fails.

notify-failure-ata.description: Print a notice on the fax adapter when a fax fails.

sharing.description: Who else may send from the number: `no`, `all`, `site:<site>`, `dept:<department>`, or `user:<user>,<user>`.

ata-mac.description: MAC address of the fax adapter, 12 hex digits.

serial-number.description: Serial number of the fax adapter (Faxback).

status.description: `pending` is still sending; `retrying` failed and will be tried again.

error-message.description: Why the fax failed or is being retried. Empty otherwise.

remote-number.description: The other party: the sender of a received fax, the destination of a sent one.

local-number.description: Your fax number the fax came in on or went out from.

remote-name.description: The sender's name, when the vendor reported one.

datetime.description: When the fax was received or completed, in UTC.

file-access-url.description: Signed link to the PDF that works without a token until it expires. Empty when there is no document yet.

thumbnail-url.description: Signed link to a small image of the first page. Empty when there is none.

FaxCoverPageFields.description: Text for the cover page placeholders. `$(Date)`, `$(SenderNumber)` and `$(ReceiverNumber)` are filled automatically.

source-level.description: The level the template came from.

inherited.description: `yes` when the template comes from a level below the one asked for (`resolved=yes`).

size.description: Size of the template in bytes.

file.description: The cover page: a Word .docx of at most 1 MB with `$(Placeholder)` tokens.
The document: pdf, doc, docx, odt, txt, html, jpg, png or tif, up to 20 MB.

caller-id.description: One of your fax numbers, or one shared with you. The fax is sent through the vendor holding it.

destination.description: The fax number to send to, 7 to 15 digits. A 10-digit number is dialed as North American.

vendor.description: The vendor a new fax number in this domain is created on.

source.description: `setting` when the `fax.vendor` setting chose it; `default` when the first configured vendor did.

setting.description: The `fax.vendor` setting, when one is set.

ApnsApp.description: An APNs app on the server, as a read returns it. The key is never returned.

app-id.description: The app's ID: the first word of its SIP User-Agent.

key-file.description: Where the server reads the key from.

key-file-present.description: `yes` when the key file exists and can be read.

key-fingerprint.description: SHA-256 of the public key, in hex. Empty when the key file is missing or unreadable.

managed.description: `yes` when this endpoint stored the key; `no` for an app added by hand.

valid.description: `yes` when the key loads and `key-id`, `team-id` and `bundle-id` are all set.

ApnsAppCreate.description: The body of an APNs app add.

app-id.description: The app's ID: the first word of its SIP User-Agent, exactly. Letters, digits, `-` and `_`.

key.description: The contents of the `.p8` file Apple issued, with its line breaks. Never returned by a read.

key-id.description: The 10-character Key ID Apple shows for the key.

ApnsAppUpdate.description: The body of an APNs app change. Send at least one field; the others keep their values.

key.description: A new `.p8` key, with its line breaks. Never returned by a read.

EmailReportType.description: `summary` (all queues totalled), `queue` (one row per call queue), `agent` (one row per agent), `dialed` (one row per dialed number).

EmailReportQueueStatistic.description: A column in the queue or dialed number report table.

EmailReportAgentStatistic.description: A column in the agent report table.

EmailReportUpdate.description: Every field is optional; a field left out keeps its current value.

report-types.description: Reports to send. Empty stops every report.

frequencies.description: How often each selected report is sent. At least one is required when `report-types` is not empty.

monthly-send-day.description: Day of the month monthly reports are sent, at the start of that day.

weekly-send-day.description: Day of the week weekly reports are sent: `0` Sunday, `1` Monday, `2` Tuesday, `3` Wednesday, `4` Thursday, `5` Friday, `6` Saturday.

send-time.description: Time of day (`HH:MM`, 24-hour, in the user's time zone) daily and weekly reports are sent. Monthly reports ignore it.

attach-csv.description: Attach the report data as a CSV file.

cc-email-addresses.description: Extra recipients. The user's own email address always receives the report and is not listed here.

queue-statistics.description: Columns in the queue report, in order.

agent-statistics.description: Columns in the agent report, in order.

dialed-number-statistics.description: Columns in the dialed number report, in order.

callqueues.description: Limit the reports to these call queues. Empty reports on every call queue the user can see.

departments.description: Limit the agent report to these departments. Empty reports on every department the user can see.

time-zone.description: The time zone send days and times are in: the user's, or the domain's when the user has none.

schedules.description: One entry per report being sent (report type × frequency).

status.description: `ready` (waiting for its next send), `pending` or `running` (being sent now), or `api error` (the last send failed and will be retried).

next-send-datetime.description: When this report is next sent.

status-datetime.description: When `status` last changed; after a successful send, when it was sent.

status-seconds.description: Seconds per status name, the sum of the periods below. Only statuses that occur in the window are present. For a window that has ended, `available` and `unavailable` equal the minutes `GET /domains/{domain}/statistics/agentLog` reports for the same agent and window (times 60).

periods.description: The status periods, oldest first. Empty when the agent has no status in the window.

status.description: The status the agent was in: `available` (online, single call mode, or on a call), `unavailable` (offline or unavailable), `break`, `lunch`, `meeting`, `other`, `web`, `custom1` to `custom8`, `logged-in` (logged in without becoming available) or `logged-out`. A status not in this list is reported under its own stored name, lower-cased.

status-code.description: The status as stored, for example `Auto`, `Manual-avail`, `Manual`, `Lunch`, `cust3`, `Login` or `Logout`. Several codes share one `status`.

start-datetime.description: When the period started, or the window start if it started earlier. UTC.

end-datetime.description: When the period ended, or the window end if it ended later. UTC. `null` when the period is still open.

duration-seconds.description: Length of the period inside the window. For an open period, up to now.

open.description: `true` only for the last period of a window that has not ended yet: the agent is still in this status.

StockReportId.description: The stock report a saved report was built from.

ReportVisibility.description: Who else can read the report. `private`: only the owner (and Office Managers and above). `domain`: every Call Center Agent, Call Center Supervisor, Site Manager and Office Manager in the domain. `roles`: users of the domain whose scope is listed in `roles`. `users`: the users listed in `users`. Only Call Center Agents, Call Center Supervisors, Site Managers and Office Managers of the domain are ever shared a report.

ReportRole.description: A scope the report is shared with.

ReportName.description: Unique among the owner's reports. Leading and trailing spaces are removed.

ReportDefinition.description: The report's widgets, filters and columns, as the call center reports screen builds them. Must be a JSON object, at most 64 KB as JSON. Stored and returned exactly as sent, keys and values unchanged. The emailed summary reads its `widgets` to decide what the email shows.

owner-user.description: The user who owns the report, or `null` for a domain report; `~` means you. Defaults to you on create (to `null` for an Office Manager, Reseller or Super User who is not a user of this domain). Must be a user of the domain. Only Office Managers and above can set it to someone else or to `null`.

roles.description: Scopes the report is shared with when `visibility` is `roles`; otherwise ignored.

users.description: Users (extensions) the report is shared with when `visibility` is `users`; otherwise ignored.

can-edit.description: `yes` lets the Call Center Supervisors and Office Managers the report is shared with change its name, description, definition and email. Call Center Agents and Site Managers can never change it.

based-on-id.description: The stock report it was built from. Send it with `based-on-version`, or neither for a report started from a blank canvas; send both as `null` to clear them.

based-on-version.description: Version of the stock report it was built from.

EmailMetric.description: A statistic for the email. Counts: `VOL` total calls, `CO` offered, `CH` answered, `AST` assisted, `AC` abandoned, `AAC` abandoned (adjusted), `VM` voicemails, `FWD` forwarded, `CB` callback requests. Percent: `AR` abandon rate, `AAR` abandon rate (adjusted), `SL` service level. Durations, shown as minutes:seconds: `AWT` average wait, `AHT` average handle time, `ATT` average talk time, `TT` total talk time, `AH` average hold.

email-enabled.description: Whether the email is sent. Turning it on needs at least one recipient.

email-time.description: When it is sent, HH:MM, 24-hour, in the domain's time zone.

email-range.description: The period the email reports on. Weeks start on Monday. Send it empty to use the frequency's default: `yesterday` (daily), `last-week` (weekly) or `last-month` (monthly). Every figure, table and chart in the email covers this period, whatever period the report's own widgets show.

email-metrics.description: No longer used. The email shows what the report shows: its figures, charts and tables, in the report's order. Still accepted and returned, so older clients keep working.

email-filters.description: Limit the figures to these queues and, at most one, dialed number. Empty lists mean no limit.

email-include-queue-table.description: No longer used. The email carries the report's own tables. Still accepted and returned, so older clients keep working.

email-attach-csv.description: Attach the report's first table as a CSV file, every row of it. A report without a table attaches the per-queue figures.

email-recipient-users.description: Users of the domain (extensions), sent to their email address on file at send time.

email-next-send-datetime.description: When the email is next sent; `null` while it is off.

email-last-status.description: How the last scheduled send went: `ok`, `ok; <n> of <m> charts not included`, or `failed: <reason>` / `skipped: <reason>`. `null` before the first send.

revision.description: The `revision` you read. If the report has changed since, the change is refused with `409`. Leave it out to skip the check.

owner-user.description: The owner's extension; `null` for a domain report.

based-on-id.description: The stock report it was built from; `null` for a report started from a blank canvas.

revision.description: Goes up by one each time the report changes. A new report starts at 1.

email-enabled.description: Whether the report's emailed summary is on. Always present, `no` for a report that was never scheduled.

start.description: Unix seconds of the first point.

end.description: Unix seconds of the last point, the current minute.

oldest-available.description: Unix seconds from which every core still holds samples (the latest of the cores' oldest samples). Points before it may carry no queue values. Null when there are none at all.

data-points.description: One per minute from `start` to `end`, oldest first.

timestamp.description: Unix seconds of the start of the minute.

queues.description: Keyed by queue extension. A queue with no known value yet for this minute is absent; read it as 0 for callers and sessions. An empty object when no queue has a value.

longest-wait-seconds.description: How long the longest-waiting caller had waited, in seconds.

sessions.description: Calls in the queue, waiting or with an agent.

CallqueueLiveHistoryAll.description: Across the covered queues: callers and sessions are summed, the wait is the longest. One agent can be on several queues, so agent counts cannot be added up; the `-max` fields give the highest single-queue value. Every field is 0 when no queue has a value for the minute.

start.description: Unix seconds of the first bucket's start.

end.description: Unix seconds where the last bucket ends (the current quarter hour, hour or day starts).

timezone.description: Daily only. The time zone the days follow (UTC when the domain has none).

oldest-available.description: Unix seconds of the oldest bucket held for this domain and period (for `15m`, of the oldest raw sample the server holds); null when none.

timestamp.description: Unix seconds of the bucket's start.

date.description: Daily only. The bucket's local date.

queues.description: Keyed by queue extension. An empty object when no queue has history for the bucket.

avg.description: Time-weighted average over the bucket, rounded to 3 decimals.

seconds-known.description: Seconds of the bucket with a recorded value (900 for a full quarter hour, 3600 for a full hour, the length of the local day for a full day). Less means the statistics cover only part of the bucket.

CallqueueHistoryAll.description: Across the covered queues. Callers waiting and sessions are added (for min and max this is a bound, since queues need not peak together); the wait is the longest. One agent can be on several queues, so agent counts are not added: the `-max` fields give the largest single-queue value. An empty object when no queue has history for the bucket.

CodeType.description: `disposition`: how a call ended. `call-reason`: why the customer called.

name.description: Trimmed; no control characters. Unique per domain and type, ignoring case.

active.description: `no` hides the code from selection but keeps its name.

system-applied.description: Dispositions only. `yes` means the system applies it, not an agent. A call reason is always `no`.

CodeClassification.description: The outcome a disposition records. Dispositions only; a call reason is always `none`.

used.description: `yes` once a call carries this code; it then cannot be deleted.

example.name: Resolved
example.description: The caller's issue or request was fully handled on this call.

end.description: The window end, Unix seconds. An end given on second `:59` is moved to the next second.

agents.description: The agent extensions whose figures are summed: the same set the read without `interval` would list. Empty when none are visible to you.

data-points.description: One entry per completed bucket, oldest first.

AgentLogIntervalPoint.description: One bucket. Only the fields named in `fields` are present. Each status field is the minutes the listed agents spent in that status during the bucket, summed over the agents. Each agent's share is capped at the bucket length, so `minutes / (seconds / 60)` is the average number of agents in that status.

seconds.description: The bucket length after clipping to the window: 900 or 3600 except for a first or last bucket that the window cuts short.

status-unavailable-duration-minutes.description: `UM`. Every logged-in status other than available: unavailable, break, lunch, meeting, other, web and CUST1 to CUST8.

status-login-duration-minutes.description: `LI`. The sum of all the status minutes.

calls-unanswered-count.description: `MC`. Calls that rang one of the agents and that the agent did not answer, counted once per call and agent, in the bucket where the call first rang. A call that was later retrieved is not counted. Months whose call history has been archived are not counted.

Forbidden.description: Your token does not have the scope this request needs.

Record_not_found.description: The resource does not exist, or your token cannot see it.

Bad_Request.description: The request is malformed or a field value is invalid. The message names the field.

Authentication_Required.description: The access token is missing, expired, or invalid. Get a new token and retry.
